## Dense label store (denselab): every training label rendered once, on the NAS, read instead of recomputed (2026-11-19, branch denselab-20261119, mergeflag) -- DESIGN, step 1

User (via lead, 11-19): render all training labels to dense 3-D volumes once, store them compressed on the NAS (forlinnas
/srv/nas/ufsm, ~/nas), and have the sampler read them instead of computing them on the fly. NAS only, no dl.ash2txt upload.

Inventory: what a training window's labels are made of today (try9's sources-scratch1-ph80-ho.json, 32 sources):

| plane | made from | where | cached today |
|---|---|---|---|
| phase (u8 0..251, 255 unknown) | winding codes rasters / stamped meshes -> pair rule (band_onfly.c), per (codes set, rmax, level; pool2 pooled) | GPU or CPU | yes: dcache, key = codes path + stat + rmax + cell (~/.cache/ufsm/derived, zstd cells) |
| codes (winding mod 14 x 18) | GT rasters (datafix-20261114/raster, volcomp lossless) or meshes (stamped per window) | stored / CPU | stored; meshes: only their vertex pack (.meshcodes-*.pack) |
| ink (prob254, 255 unknown) | segments json (meshes + label rasters) splatted along the normal at the open face (inksplat.c) | GPU or CPU | yes: dcache level L (cell 128) + index.bin; L+1 pooled in memory |
| ink MIL rays {p, n, y} | mesh points + signed normals (inkfly_rays), no plane | CPU | the tile index only |
| fibre H / V (prob254) | AFV / .fib polylines (+ extra, map) rasterised (fiberraster.c) | GPU or CPU | NO (a 2-box reuse pool) |
| band / side / w4 / wcomp | the phase (or band codes) per window | CPU / GPU | no (derived from phase) |
| normals (6) + density + rv targets | the phase + papyrus per window, after augmentation | GPU | no |
| papyrus / pm / rv papyrus / air mask | CT thresholds (iso) per window | CPU / GPU | no |

So the derived cache already holds most of it: 170 GB on the desk today, all phase (P4 A48 / B48 at 3 levels 112 GB, 1667 A / B at
3 levels 29 GB, 0172 15 GB, 1299 10 GB, 0139 7 GB) and ink (1.6 GB over 8 scrolls), but only the cells training has touched, local to
the desk's /home disk, evicted LRU at 200 GB, and keyed by local paths + mtimes.

What gets stored (one dense array per derived spec, the same values the on-the-fly path computes):
- phase: per onfly spec x level, exactly the dcache array (its key hex). Every cell of the codes' support (+ rmax), not just the touched
  ones. u8.
- ink: per u2ink source, level L, the inkfly array (prob254 incl. 255 unknown = the known channel: known = v != 255, weight from the
  sampler's existing rules); the MIL tile index (index.bin) beside it. Level L+1 stays a memory pooling of L (exact, cheap).
- fibre H / V: per fibre source x level x plane: new, needs a dcache key (afv / extra / map files stat + cfg + CT key + level + plane
  + a label version LBL_FIBRE). Today recomputed for every window: the main compute saved.
- codes: archived beside (labcomp kind 1, 6-24x smaller than the volcomp-lossless rasters: 1667 A+B 9.4 GB -> ~0.5-1.5 GB, P4 107 GB
  -> ~5-15 GB): not read by training once the phase is stored, kept so any phase variant can be rendered again from the NAS alone.
- NOT stored: normals / density / rv / band / side / w4 / papyrus. They are cheap per-window functions of the phase and the CT that
  must be evaluated after the window's spatial augmentation (a stored normal would have to be rotated, and its rounding would break
  byte identity with today's targets). Storing their input (phase) removes all the expensive work.
- Ink "signed band distance" for the MIL loss: today MIL works on rays (mesh point, signed normal, label) sampled along t in [-R, R];
  there is no voxel plane. A dense equivalent (per voxel: signed distance along the nearest labelled mesh point's normal, int8 in level-L
  voxels, 127 = none; plus that point's label bit) would be a NEW loss input, not byte-identical to the ray path. Proposal: store the
  rays' tile index as today (exact) now; the dense signed-distance plane as a separate opt-in plane + loss variant, its own A/B.

Format and read path:
- Store = a zarr v3 array per key under ~/nas/denselab/<24-hex key>/ (inputs.txt with the key text, zarr.json), chunk = the dcache
  cell (128 / 256), sharded 4^3 cells per shard file (NAS file counts: P4 phase would be ~150k cell files otherwise), inner codec zstd
  (the dcache's own cell coding; byte-exact; volcomp lossless as the alternative where it wins: phase is smooth mod 252, measured on
  1667 before choosing). labcomp only for codes (55 Mvox/s read: archive format).
- dcache gets a read-only tier: on a cell miss (memory, local disk) it reads the cell from $UFSM_DENSELAB/<hex> (opt-in: unset = off,
  as before; the default flips to ~/nas/denselab once 1667 is complete and a batch-hash A/B on real 1667 windows passes) before computing, and writes it to the local disk cache as today. The NAS is never read hot: rclone FUSE does
  147 MB/s sequential (measured, one 223 MB file) but per-file latency is high, so the local dcache stays the hot tier and the NAS
  replaces the compute. Nothing changes in the sources json: same specs, same keys, same bytes; a store missing a cell falls back to
  the compute (logged once per key).
- `ufsm denselab-render SOURCES.json [--source NAME] [--kind phase,ink,fibre] --out ROOT [--threads N] [--gpu D]`: opens each source's
  derived arrays exactly as the sampler does (sources.c), enumerates the cells of the label support (codes chunk map dilated by rmax;
  ink index tiles; fibre polyline boxes + radius), computes them (GPU allowed on a free card; CPU otherwise) and writes the shards.
  Resumable per shard; a store is marked complete (done file with cell count, bytes, seconds).
- Keys stay the dcache keys (local paths + mtimes): a re-raster or a moved file changes the key and the store is simply not found
  (compute fallback), never stale. Pods cannot use these keys (different paths): out of scope (NAS only).

Expected sizes (zstd, from today's dcache cells; the full support is larger than the touched part, ~1-2x):

| scroll | phase (all specs, all levels) | ink | fibre | codes (labcomp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paris 4 | ~110-200 GB | 0.9 GB | to measure (4 fibre sources) | ~5-15 GB |
| 1667 | ~30-55 GB | 0.4 GB | none in try9's set | ~0.5-1.5 GB |
| 0172 / 1299 / 0139 / 0500P2 / 1218 | ~35-60 GB | 0.3 GB (0139, 0814, MAN5, 0009B, 0841, 0500P2) | 1447 / 0175A / 0125 / 0139 / 1451 / 0332: to measure | ~1-3 GB |

Total ~0.2-0.35 TB on a 30 TB NAS (23 TB free). Step 2 (1667 end to end) measures the real 1667 numbers and the fibre per-source size
before anything else is rendered.

Test (step 2, new test_denselab, CPU): a fixture scroll with codes, an ink segment and an AFV fibre: render the store, then sample
windows (several levels, augmentation off and on) once with the store and once on the fly with an empty cache: label planes byte for
byte equal; a store with a missing shard falls back to the compute and is still equal.

## How much GT does the global count need? Sparse GT anchors in count-field; P4 phase misses by normal gap (2026-11-18/19, branch anchors-20261118, mergeflag)

User (via lead): "how much ground truth do we actually need?" Test: feed count-field's least-squares ref sparse GT anchors and score
GT ids on boxes that got none. `ufsm gt-anchors CODES KEY FIELDS --boxes B.tsv --hold N,.. --kind pin|pair --p P` samples labelled
GT voxels (a hash per voxel, rate P) outside the held-out boxes:
- pin (A): the GT winding at a voxel, as U' = W + dir theta / 2 pi, lifted to the ref's 14-turn period after a per-box gauge pass
  (mode of U'_ref - code / 18);
- pair (R): from a sampled voxel, along the radial ray to the k-th distinct GT sheet (k 1..3, ~17 % each of dU +-1/2/3, median
  47 native voxels apart): only the turn difference dU.
Records are merged per 16-voxel cell. count-field `--anchor-pins F` / `--anchor-pairs F` add them as cf_pairs rows (pins: the a half
only), weight `--anchor-w 10` x min(n, `--anchor-ncap 4`), never IRLS-reweighted, and kept in no-data cells (17 % of pairs were
dropped there before 5220bf2b). test_countfield: GT pairs / pins restore a cut band sector (err 0.000), wrong dU does not (1.000).

1667 q2 (u1-13790 fields, podun PHerc1667-q2pod; mf-weighted ref `--mf-w 1`, CPU, pass 1 from a pool cache: ~7-10 min / run, 7-11 GB), 54 GT boxes split
27 held out / 27 anchor boxes (3.20 cm^3, 1.18 G labelled voxels), seed 1, GT ids right:

| kind | p | anchors | per cm^3 | anchor boxes | held-out boxes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.8876 | 0.8916 |
| pair | 1e-5 | 10.1 k | 3.2 k | 0.8988 | 0.8907 |
| pair | 1e-4 | 100 k | 31 k | 0.9351 | 0.8923 |
| pair | 1e-3 | 1.0 M | 314 k | 0.9699 | 0.8926 |
| pair | 1e-2 | 10 M | 3.1 M | 0.9736 | 0.8923 |
| pair | 1e-1 | 101 M | 31 M | 0.9714 | 0.8923 |
| pin | 1e-5 | 11.9 k | 3.7 k | 0.9178 | 0.8999 |
| pin | 1e-4 | 117 k | 37 k | 0.9517 | 0.9006 |
| pin | 1e-3 | 1.2 M | 369 k | 0.9692 | 0.9014 |
| pin | 1e-2 | 11.8 M | 3.7 M | 0.9709 | 0.9003 |
| pin | 1e-1 | 118 M | 37 M | 0.9711 | 0.9001 |

- Locally anchors work: pins 3.7 k / cm^3 (~12 k points over the 27 boxes) already take the anchor boxes 0.888 -> 0.918, 37 k /
  cm^3 -> 0.952, and both kinds saturate at ~0.97 from ~300 k / cm^3 (the rest is the per-box id scoring / label noise floor).
  Pairs need ~10x the pins' density for the same local gain.
- They do not carry: held-out boxes gain +0.008-0.010 with pins at any density (the absolute gauge spreads), pairs +0.000-0.001.
  The ref's errors are local (merged / packed regions, C19-type cores) and the anchors' constraints die out within a box or two:
  GT helps where it is, not around it. "How much GT": ~10^4 pins per cm^3 where counting fails, nothing gained elsewhere.
- Seed 2 skipped (lead). Data: /vesuvius/ufsm/mergeflag/anc (sweep.sh, sweep.out, hold.txt).

P4 phase misses (`merge-flag --eval --gap-report G [--thr T]`): per GT one-turn interval along radial rays (eval's truth: the net's
phase misses the turn), the flag's P / R, the miss share by radial gap and by NORMAL gap (in-slice GT sheet normal from the
covariance of the same-code label voxels, gap x |cos ray,normal|). 38 P4 GT boxes, identical intervals for both nets (same axis):

| net | all 38 | PH1-3 | J1-34 | HOLD | PH1-3 at normal gap >= 150 um | J at >= 150 um | HOLD at >= 150 um |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| u1 13790 | 0.436 | 0.752 | 0.437 | 0.176 | 0.58 | 0.36 | 0.07 |
| try9 16000 live | 0.379 | 0.606 | 0.381 | 0.174 | 0.38 | 0.29 | 0.08 |

1667 (9 boxes): u1 0.183, try9 EMA 12750 0.234 (EMA understates try9; P4 EMA 0.514 vs live 0.379), >= 150 um 0.08 / 0.11.
PH1-3 is oblique to the radial rays (median |cos| 0.63 vs 0.93-0.98 elsewhere: radial gaps overstate spacing 1.6x) and denser
(52 % of normal gaps < 100 um vs 21 % in HOLD), but at the same normal gap it still misses 4-8x more than HOLD / 1667: a genuine
phase failure on P4 (J boxes are not oblique), reduced by try9. The flag at mf >= 179 on u1 P4 fields: 38 % flagged, P 0.90 R 0.80
vs the misses (1667 5.6 %, P 0.82 R 0.34): unrollperf's 42 % mf on P4 is real. Data: /vesuvius/ufsm/mergeflag/gapchk.

## Recto / verso and fibre direction do not separate touching sheets either: try9's heads count fewer boundaries than the CT (2026-11-18, branch rvsep-20261118, unrollperf)

**Question (user via lead).** Each sheet is a recto layer (horizontal fibres) on a verso layer (vertical fibres). Along a ray through a
stack the sequence is R V | R V | R V, so every sheet boundary is a V -> R (V-fibre -> H-fibre) step, even at zero gap. Could counting
those steps count the touching sheets that the CT and the phase merge?

**Tool.** `ufsm gt-trans` (src/gttrans.c) ports pseudolab's / fix0332's ctgt.py to C: the same boxes, rays, GT intervals, normal-gap rule
and CT detector (section "Packed sheets are not resolved by finer CT"). Its CT row reproduces ctgt's on Paris 4: 48882 vs 48897 intervals,
per turn 0.523 / 0.740 / 0.871 / 0.970, 1.044 overall.

Per GT interval it also counts, on the same samples:
- **rv state flips**, with hysteresis +-8 around 128 on `predict --heads rv` (1 + 254 (1 + p_r - p_v) / 2).
- **Fibre state flips** from fib/H vs fib/V: state set where max >= 8 and the difference >= 4.
- **Peaks** of the rv signal and of H - V, using the CT detector. These are recto-ruler's "peaks of the fused signal".

A sheet's GT centre lies at its R | V interface, so the boundary direction should give 1 per turn. test_gttrans builds a synthetic stack
of packed (38 um) and spaced (115 um) sheets and gets rv / fibre V -> R 0.94 / 1.06 per turn there, while the CT peaks merge (0.47).

**Predictions.** try9 snap 16000, live weights (`--ema 0 --gn-live 1`), `--heads rv,c14,c15` (c14 / c15 = fib/H / fib/V), every wbench GT
box of paris4 (PH1-3, HOLD), paris4j (J1-34) and 1667 (70). Window 256 / halo 64 and CT decoded on the CPU, to stay at 2.9 GB beside the
ink trainer on desk card 1. Outputs and logs: /vesuvius/ufsm/unrollperf/rvsep/.

**Per GT turn.** All columns are on the same intervals. "Flips" is the boundary direction (V -> R, V -> H) going outward; the reverse
direction is within +-0.1 of it except on 1667's rv.

| | gap 0-70 um | 70-85 | 85-100 | 100-115 | all |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paris 4 (PH1-3, HOLD): CT peaks | 0.52 | 0.74 | 0.87 | 0.97 | 1.04 |
| rv flips V -> R | 0.25 | 0.34 | 0.43 | 0.56 | 0.60 |
| rv peaks | 0.45 | 0.62 | 0.77 | 0.88 | 0.87 |
| fibre flips V -> H | 0.17 | 0.28 | 0.36 | 0.47 | 0.47 |
| (H - V) peaks | 0.36 | 0.55 | 0.64 | 0.74 | 0.80 |
| Paris 4 July (J1-34): CT peaks | 0.35 | 0.68 | 0.79 | 0.92 | 1.20 |
| rv flips / rv peaks | 0.16 / 0.28 | 0.38 / 0.60 | 0.47 / 0.72 | 0.57 / 0.84 | 0.64 / 0.99 |
| fibre flips / (H - V) peaks | 0.12 / 0.23 | 0.30 / 0.49 | 0.38 / 0.59 | 0.44 / 0.68 | 0.50 / 0.88 |
| 1667 (70 boxes): CT peaks | 0.45 | 0.67 | 0.78 | 0.88 | 1.54 |
| rv flips / rv peaks | 0.26 / 0.41 | 0.37 / 0.63 | 0.42 / 0.72 | 0.48 / 0.79 | 0.65 / 1.07 |
| fibre flips / (H - V) peaks | 0.21 / 0.37 | 0.33 / 0.50 | 0.39 / 0.60 | 0.46 / 0.67 | 0.53 / 1.04 |

**Gate: not met.** No rv or fibre measure reaches 0.9 per turn below 70 um. Every one stays at or below the CT peaks (0.52 / 0.35 /
0.45). They also fall short at wide gaps: rv flips are 0.6-0.9 per turn above 115 um.

**Reading.** try9's side and fibre heads merge the touching sheets as the trunk does. The heads cannot add separation the trunk lacks.
- The latent net sees 4-voxel cells (38 um at 9.6).
- A packed pair (< 70 um) is two sheets, four layers of ~15-35 um each, inside two cells.
- An R V R V alternation at that scale is below the representation. The heads come off the same cells through the sub-cell head.

The fibre head marks tubes, not layer orientation. Its probabilities are mostly below 0.13 between fibres, so its states are sparse. This
is a test of try9's heads, not of the physics. The CT itself does not separate the layers either: at 2.4 um, 0.60 per turn below 70 um
(section above).

**Remaining lever (not run).** A full-resolution recto / verso net:
- rv1d2, whose recto-ruler counted 1.06 per GT turn on 1667 overall, is deleted.
- A model whose rv output at 2.4-4.8 um keeps the layer alternation could be gated with this tool unchanged: `--rv` takes any store on
  the CT key's grid.

**The latent codec keeps the sheet separation (lead's question, 2026-11-18).** `gt-trans --lat-rt klt1.lcb --lat-c C --lat-step S
--lat-norm CENTRE,SCALE` runs each 4^3 cell (global 4-aligned grid) of the CT through the cell transform before the peak detector:
- the normalised values (try9's scan-norm: P4 85.8 / 37.95, 1667 62.9 / 37.59) projected on the first C basis rows;
- quantised exactly as `input_latc_k` does: `rint(c / S) * S`, |q| <= 127, the mean <= 32767;
- decoded back to voxels as the sum of q_c b_c, then to uint8 CT.

CT peaks per GT turn by normal gap (um):

| arm | P4 0-70 | 70-85 | 85-100 | 100-115 | all | P4 July 0-70 | 70-85 | all | 1667 0-70 | 70-85 | all |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| raw 9.6 CT | 0.523 | 0.740 | 0.871 | 0.970 | 1.044 | 0.352 | 0.680 | 1.199 | 0.454 | 0.674 | 1.541 |
| 64 coefs, unquantised (check) | 0.523 | 0.740 | 0.871 | 0.970 | 1.044 | 0.352 | 0.680 | 1.199 | 0.454 | 0.674 | 1.541 |
| 61, step 0.05 (R1-like) | 0.521 | 0.742 | 0.870 | 0.971 | 1.044 | 0.353 | 0.681 | 1.200 | 0.452 | 0.671 | 1.539 |
| 29, unquantised | 0.520 | 0.736 | 0.869 | 0.966 | 1.040 | 0.352 | 0.678 | 1.197 | 0.451 | 0.669 | 1.537 |
| 29, step 0.125 | 0.524 | 0.739 | 0.861 | 0.969 | 1.042 | 0.354 | 0.682 | 1.199 | 0.449 | 0.669 | 1.535 |
| **29, step 0.25 (try9)** | **0.519** | **0.739** | **0.864** | **0.967** | **1.040** | **0.355** | **0.681** | **1.197** | **0.441** | **0.667** | **1.517** |
| 13, step 0.25 | 0.507 | 0.720 | 0.848 | 0.948 | 1.023 | 0.348 | 0.669 | 1.176 | 0.432 | 0.655 | 1.495 |

- The 64-coefficient decode is bit-exact to the raw CT, which validates the path.
- try9's codec costs -0.004 / +0.003 / -0.013 peaks per turn below 70 um on P4 / P4 July / 1667.
  - That is small next to the rv heads' gap to the CT: 0.45 vs 0.52, 0.28 vs 0.35, 0.41 vs 0.45.
  - So the codec is not what throws the separation away. The loss is in the net (38 um cells, the trunk), not in its input.
- 61 coefficients at step 0.02 (R1's plan) lose: below 70 um 0.515 / 0.347 / 0.438. The |q| <= 127 clamp caps AC coefficients at 2.54
  normalised units and clips strong edges. A step that fine needs a wider code.
- A lossless latent (61 coefficients, small step) gains nothing this detector sees. Only 13 coefficients start to lose (-0.016 on P4 below 70 um).
- Caveats:
  - The detector smooths at sigma 1.2 voxels in the plane, so it cannot see detail finer than ~2 voxels.
  - A first version decoded to float. Its sub-LSB residue broke the ties of flat masked runs, giving a 1667 64-coefficient "check" of 0.37
    and a spurious try9 drop. The decode now rounds to uint8.
- Setup: `/vesuvius/ufsm/unrollperf/rvsep/lat/run2.sh`, outputs `{p4,p4j,c7}.<arm>.out` (CPU, ~1 min per arm).

## Ink retrain from try9 on the 2-D teachers; ink-teach --extra (B2) (2026-11-18, branches inkteach / inkteachx-20261118, inksdk)

User (via lead, 11-18): retrain the latent ink head from try9 (scratch2) on the 2-D teachers (reader3 + ink9um soft targets via
ink-teach) plus the human labels, not from u1 and not human-only. Numbers that led here:
- Pod smoke at P 1024 (u1 init, 4 scrolls, arm A): step-10 gate failed, 0.02 fresh samples/s, trainer RSS 23.6 GB at 2 workers / 3
  slots. The sampler worker is one CPU thread, ~42 s per P 1024 window (desk dry run), so the arm was sampler-bound by ~15x.
- Same smoke at P 512: step 10 0.27, step-50 mean 0.350 fresh samples/s (0.21-0.43 steady, 32-55 Mvox/s), 3.2 s/step, RSS 8.2 GB;
  200 steps in 11 min. P 512 windows still carry 55-65k ink rays (the 65,536 cap at times), so ink supervision per step is ~unchanged.
- The CT prefetch's `--levels 1,2` meant max level 1: level 2 was never prefetched before 11-18 (podq now passes `--levels 2`).
- inkpod-15000 live (`--ema 0`) vs EMA on the 1667 held-out wraps: heldout 0.5824 vs 0.5824 (n 1,296,287), hold 0.5998 vs 0.6040,
  valonly 0.5517 vs 0.5481 (reader3 0.858 / 0.862 / 0.856): the memorisation verdict is not a stale-EMA artefact.
- try9's own ink head trains on the validation rasters (ink onfly `"validation": "off"`): of the eval's held-out split
  (VAL | HOLD) only HOLD is clean for it (all 28 1667 ink holdout boxes lie inside its holdouts-20261114 boxes).
  /vesuvius/ufsm/inksdk/pairwrap2.py adds the `hold` / `valonly` splits. inknorm's 3-D audit: try9-15000 EMA held-out 0.52-0.56,
  no better than raw CT intensity.
- Scoring try9-class nets: predict at window 640 / halo 64 (nlev 6) peaked 8.8 GB; 512 / 64 fits ~4.5 GB. Binaries before
  a8babaff need an explicit `--gn-live 1` (try9's running GN statistics were never trained). latink.sh: LATINK_X, LATWIN / LATHALO.

Pod run (podq FULL=1 SKIPA=1, /root/ink/FULL.sh): init try9 16000 weights-only (header muon_mom 0 + the p and EMA arrays, 832 MB;
--init-from copies p -> p, ema -> ema, training runs on p), try9's architecture flags (TARCH / TXTRA / TUW in trainarm.sh), P 512;
teach on every labelled mesh (27 meshes over 6 scrolls), then arm B for 6000 steps, refitted at step 100 to the measured step time so
the run ends inside the 11 h slot (BUDGET_END; one restart, so the wsd cooldown still runs); B1000 held-out <= 0.60 stops it.

**ink-teach --extra (B2).** ink-teach labelled only the human-labelled meshes (the whole mesh, outside held-out boxes and human px).
`--extra NAME=TIFXYZ` / `--extra-list FILE` adds meshes without human labels (unroll wraps, unlabelled segments): their raster is the
teacher's own px grid (label_scale = px_um / mesh voxel um, 4 at 9.596 / 2.399), calibrated with the labelled meshes' ensemble weights
and Platt fit, gated the same way, held-out boxes removed, and px within --extra-clear (48) level-0 voxels of any labelled-mesh vertex
dropped (there the human labels and the labelled mesh's own teacher px rule; it also keeps the 1667 validation rasters, which lie on
labelled meshes, free of teacher labels). teach.sh reads KIT/kit/extra-SCROLL.tsv. Test: tests/test_ink_teach.py (CPU: a labelled
mesh, an extra mesh 400 voxels away gets ~88k teacher px at 48.8 % ink on the half-ink stripes, one 10 voxels away is cleared).

**Result (11-18/19, desk card 1 instead of the pod: pod money ran out).** The same arm B (try9-16000 weights-only init, teacher-first
targets on 6 scrolls, P 512, 1 worker / 2 slots, UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB 6.5 so try9 keeps 4.5 GB) ran beside try9 on its second card:
try9's on-the-fly phase + fibre held card 1 at 55-98 % SM, the ink trainer got 0-44 % (pmon), wait 0 %: GPU-bound at 0.04-0.10
samples/s (mean 0.09; 1000 steps 18:18 -> 22:02, vs 0.27-0.35 on the pod), planner lean 2 with 0.75 GB host offloads each way, card
peak 7.6 GB, host RSS 18.4 GB. Ink bce 0.450 -> 0.455, MIL 0.475 -> 0.453 over the 1000 steps. Scored at B1000 (live weights,
`--gn-live 1`, window 512 / halo 64, 1667 held-out wraps, pairwrap2): heldout AUC **0.541** (n 1,296,287; reader3 -0.317
[-0.355, -0.282]), hold 0.524, valonly 0.569 (reader3 0.86 on all three): below the 0.60 gate, early stop 00:07. Verdict:
try9 init + 2-D teachers at 1000 steps on a contended card = 0.54 held-out, no better than try9's untrained head (0.52-0.56) or raw
CT. 1000 steps at P 512 is ~1000 windows: too few to say the recipe fails, too slow to find out on a shared card (6000 steps ~ 22 h).
Not retried until a dedicated GPU (or a pod) is available; the kit (/vesuvius/ufsm/inksdk/desk9: teach rasters for 4 scrolls,
sources-B, run3.sh driver with the B1000 gate) is ready to rerun as is.

## HerculeX exact integer levels: one-sided votes on our fitter and on patch-solve (2026-11-18, branch levelsolve-20261118)

HerculeX (github adambetka2/HerculeX, MIT; README "Exact integer levels") gives patches integer turns f by an exact solve of
min sum w rho(f_b - f_a - k): sheet edges have k = 0, and rays along the normal have k = the sheets crossed. A ray can miss a faint sheet,
so its count is a lower bound: a residual on the permitted side costs half (one-sided). It solves both senses and keeps the cheaper, and
keeps only the edges that all of 8 Exp-reweighted re-solves agree on. Our exact L1 machinery already does the symmetric half:
src/l1pot (PUMA graph cuts, BK) in the fitter's slip repair (--uw-repair) and in patch-solve. New on this branch:
- l1_vote.wn: the weight below d (0 = w, so every old caller is unchanged). Merging swaps w / wn when it flips a vote. The solve and the
  energy use the asymmetric cost; the convexity that makes +-1 cut moves exact still holds. test_repair: 300 exhaustive one-sided
  5-node trials (shifts -10..10; one-sided chains reach past the old +-6). UFSM_L1_DUMP records grow 24 -> 32 B.
- fit --uw-rep-hidden H: a touching slip-repair vote between two pieces whose axis lies along the model normal (|n_ax| >= 1/2) is
  one-sided. More turns outward cost H, fewer cost the whole.
- patch-solve --hidden H: gap votes are one-sided. --hidden-room R makes a crossing one-sided only when dr >= (d + R) x pitch.
  --hidden-pitch P makes the box's votes one-sided only when its pitch < P voxels.
  --draws K is HerculeX's consensus: K Exp(1)-reweighted re-solves; only the largest comp of the edges every draw keeps stays active.
  test_patchsolve has a merged-contact case: sheet 2 is hidden in sheet 3 for theta < -0.1, so most 1 -> 3 crossings count d 1.
  Symmetric ray votes put 8 of 10 nodes off their sheet (score 0.886); --hidden 0.5 puts 0 of 9 active off (score 1.0; s1_0 pruned).
  Pair votes keep only each pair's mode, so the minority count is gone before the solve; there --hidden changes nothing.

**The phase route cannot carry a packed count (oracle).** Run: u1-fd615 fields, CPU fit, master ba6fdf77. The label-phase ceiling fit is
passed as --ref-model with --uw-rep-ref 1000, so every slip-repair piece takes the GT integer. That is the best any patch-level integer
solve on our phase can do.

| box | base ids0 | pieces at the GT integer, 8^3 / 4^3 tiles | per-voxel GT integer (--ref-snap 1) | ceil |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PH1 | 0.222 | 0.238 / 0.237 | 0.931 | 0.967 |
| PH2 | 0.277 | 0.246 / 0.243 | 0.965 | 0.963 |
| PH3 | 0.219 | 0.201 / 0.202 | 0.702 | 0.812 |
| HOLD | 0.810 | 0.919 / 0.917 | 0.882 | 0.996 |

- In PH1-3 the phase counts 1.79 / 1.61 / 1.33 turns too few per 0.5 mm radial segment (2.79 reference turns). One piece of net phase
  spans 2-3 GT sheets, so only per-voxel integers (new local evidence) recover them.
- HOLD's slips are piece-level: +0.11 is available there.
- --uw-rep-hidden 0.5 over 34 boxes (PH1-3, HOLD, 21 J, 9 C): mean ids0 delta +0.0001 (PH1 +0.006, J19 -0.003, J24 -0.002, the rest
  within +-0.0006). On a phase field a skipped sheet is a slower phase, not a loop residual, so there is nothing for a one-sided cut to act on.
  Not a fitter option worth using. (The 1667 label phase was deleted in the 11-17 cleanup, so there are no 1667 oracles.)

**patch-solve (unroll v3) on the 1667 GT bed.** The 11-06 bed was gone. It is rebuilt in /vesuvius/ufsm/levelsolve/v3bed (mkbox.sh: m7 L2
prob + 1667 wind codes max-pooled 4.8 -> 9.6 um, 512^3; ev.sh / ev2.sh = scripts/v3/ev_box.sh with sheet-trace --tile 16). C7
reproduces the 11-06 rec .576 / solve .934. Metric: right sheet+turn x matched area kept (pruning and --draws drop area), per box.

| set | sym | --hidden 0.5 | --hidden 0.25 | GT-oracle edges |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 bed boxes (C1-4, 7, 9, 11, 19, 21, 24) | 0.696 | 0.730 (+0.034 [-0.035, +0.114]) | 0.735 (+0.039 [-0.032, +0.114]) | 0.932 |
| 20 more clean boxes (C10-C57, mostly open) | 0.729 | 0.723 (-0.006 [-0.030, +0.018]) | 0.681 (-0.048 [-0.099, -0.001]) | |
| all 30 | 0.718 | 0.725 (+0.007) | 0.699 (-0.019) | |

- Over the 30 boxes the gain follows packing: corr(packed share, delta at H 0.5) 0.43, corr(box pitch, delta) -0.40.
  - The 8 boxes with patch-solve pitch < 18 voxels (C1-3, C19, C21, C22, C24, C29): +0.091, 7 of 8 up.
  - The 22 others: -0.020 (C26 -0.142, C4 -0.133, C35 -0.088).

- Packed boxes gain: C2 0.513 -> 0.712, C19 0.579 -> 0.719, C3 0.454 -> 0.686 (0.767 at H 0.5), C1 0.494 -> 0.586.
- Others lose: C24 0.752 -> 0.617, C9 0.835 -> 0.723, C4 0.556 -> 0.423 (H 0.5).
- --cross-tsv vote errors vs GT: C2 15.7 % under / 6.1 % over and C19 13.6 / 10.7, which the lower-bound model fits. C4 is 6.4 / 27.3
  (duplicate / double-face crossings) and C9 4.0 / 4.2; one-sided votes amplify the overcounts.
- Refinements that do not help:
  - --hidden-room 0.5 / 0.25 brings C2 / C19 back to sym (0.579 / 0.582): the undercounted gaps have ordinary dr (as 11-06 found).
  - --dup-frac 0.5 lowers sym itself to 0.646; with --hidden 0.25 it is 0.729.
  - --votes ray is the same as pair (ray + H 0.5 0.735).
  - --draws 8 (C2, H 0.25): right 0.831 -> 0.844 at area 0.857 -> 0.817, a precision knob only.

Verdict: one-sided votes are the right model where the counter undercounts (merged contacts), and wrong where it overcounts
(duplicates). Which error dominates differs by box, and the per-crossing guards tried here do not tell them apart. The box pitch does
(above). --hidden-pitch P makes the votes one-sided only when the box pitch < P. The rule (H 0.5, P 18) was chosen on these 30 boxes,
so it is checked held out on the other 1667 boxes of boxes.tsv. Of 40 scored, none has pitch < 18 (lowest C55 19.0). The rule is
inert there (40 / 40 identical scores, sym mean 0.788), but that says nothing about the gain: the packed-annotated held-out boxes C5 /
C20 / C23 trace only their open parts (recall 0.10-0.44, pitch 24-26). Held-out #2 used the z-neighbours of the 8 packed selection boxes (11 boxes; 8 have pitch < 18).
- Switched boxes: -0.001 [-0.047, +0.033], 5 up / 3 down: CN2b +0.063, CN2a +0.049, CN1a +0.031, CN29b -0.141.
- FAIL (pre-registered: CI > 0). The selection set's +0.091 does not hold up. Even in packed boxes the one-sided votes sometimes flip
  which gauge wins the largest comp (C29 / CN29b, C24 / C4 in selection). This is the single-gauge instability 11-06 already saw
  (C3 .77 / .50), and the half-price over-side makes it easier. Nothing is switched on by default.
The fitter option is null. patch-solve --hidden is not a default either: with pitch gating it fails held out. It would need an overcount
guard (a detector that separates double faces / duplicates) and a gauge-stable score first. The 1667-unroll step of the plan was not run,
since no route passed its gate. Scripts and rows: /vesuvius/ufsm/levelsolve/{orc,hid,v3bed}.

## merge-flag on the GPU, count-field --mf-w: 1667 in 34 s on the shared desk card (was 716 s on the pod's CPUs) (2026-11-18, branch mfgpu-20261118)

MFREF put merge-flag in front of the ref, and the pod e2e measured it at 716 s (6904 CPU s; +454 s of critical path even in the
background). perf on the CPU version: 71 % box3 (float box means with double prefix sums, strided y / z passes), 14 % mf_block, 5 %
atan2f; decode 0.9 %, encode 0.6 %. So the work is the filters, and the I/O (4 planes in, 1 out) is small.

**Exact integer sums (src/mf_core.h).** The 12 box sums behind the three features are integers: amp_q = round(65536 |(pc, ps)| / 127)
on material, the material count, sp and its known count (9-box), sp / known (5-box), and the neighbour products' numerators
(pc1 - 128)(pc0 - 128) + (ps1 - 128)(ps0 - 128) and the cross term per axis (5-box; the 127^2 cancels in atan2). Sums of integers are
the same in any order, so CPU threads, GPU tiles and slab borders agree exactly; only mf_final's few double operations per cell remain.
The CPU mf_block now uses the same sums (int64 prefix lines): against the previous float version, 3634 of 932 M interior cells differ,
178 by more than 1 (atan2 near +-pi of a near-zero imaginary sum), 13 threshold flips at 179: the eval / GT numbers above stand.

**GPU (src/nn_mf.cu).** Tiles of 32 output rows x YS columns (full x; YS from --gpu-mem) with a 4-cell halo in z / y. Three kernels,
4 sums each (G0: the r 4 sums; G1: sp / known r 2 and the z products; G2: the y / x products + the final), each a 32 x 8 block
column sliding along z: per plane the bytes of its (8 + 2r + 1) x (32 + 2r + 1) region into shared memory (fetched into registers one
plane ahead), the cell values, x sums, y sums (the plane's box face), and the z window as a running sum over a register ring of the
last 2r + 1 faces. G0 / G1 store their 8 sums, G2 adds its 4 and writes mf: in fp32, and where 255 p lands within a bound on fp32's
error of a rounding edge (~2.5 % of material cells), the cell goes to a list finished by mf_final in fp64 (the CPU's arithmetic).
ncu (32 x 722 x 1616 tile, card shared): G0 10.8 ms, G1 6.9, G2 17.6 before the fp32 final (fp64 pipe 62 % busy: divergent fallback
in 73 % of warps), 4x less after it. Host: three overlapped stages (reader thread for slab k + 1, the GPU for slab k, a writer thread
encoding slab k - 1's 128^3 shards a thread per shard: the old serial shard loop was 5 s per 384 rows), page-locked plane / mf
buffers (2.4 GB for 1667), the field planes decoded on the same GPU (UFSM_GPU_DECODE, --gpu-decode 1 default).

| 1667 q2 (4635 x 1568 x 1616, 3.97 G material cells) | wall | CPU s |
|---|---|---|
| CPU (pod, 13 threads, TH / 2) | 716 s | 6904 |
| CPU (desk, 16 lowprio threads, + --weighted) | 689 s | |
| GPU (desk card 1 shared with try9 + others at 57-100 % util, load 45) | **34 s** (kernels 15.6, GPU stage 21.7, waits on reads 9.3) | 175 |

The GPU's mf equals the CPU's byte for byte: 973 M cells (1667 rows 2048-2432), and test_mergeflag --gpu (raw, crop, zarr fields with
2 x 5 tiles). The whole-1667 flagged share 0.1398 = the CPU's.

**count-field --mf-w K.** fit_fields_load scales pc ps w by 1 - K mf / 255 as it reads (fit_fields_mf_weight; the mf plane of the
same fields, zarr), so the ref needs no weighted copy (the 3 planes the --weighted pass re-encoded at the source q: ~3x the mf write).
test_mergeflag: count-field --mf-w 1 on the fields gives byte-identical model files to count-field on merge-flag --apply's planes
(lossless test planes), and refuses fields without mf. On 1667 q2 (exact weights vs the re-encoded planes):
model coherence 0.3538 vs 0.3563, ref GT ids **0.8896 vs 0.8896** (|err| < 0.08 0.2610 vs 0.2611): the same ref.

## recto-sp: the source ring in y tiles, so big scrolls fit a 24 GB card (2026-11-18, branch rsptile-20261118, unrollperf)

The GPU path kept a z ring of the whole y / x source box (all field rows' y and x +- the profile reach). On PHerc Paris 4 that ring
was 28.2 GB: more than the pod's 24 GB RTX PRO 4000, so recto-sp fell back to the CPU path. That path then held two whole-box
source blocks plus the fields and was OOM-killed (rc 137) in the 31 GB pod cgroup. The P4 MFREF pair ran with RECTOSP=0 for that
reason.

Now the planner splits the cells' y blocks into nty tiles. A tile's blocks read only its rows +- the reach, padded to one height,
which is the ring's height. The blocks run shard row by shard row and, inside each shard row, tile by tile; rsp is still written one
shard row at a time. The ring restarts at each tile switch. Within a tile the next block's decode overlaps the kernel as before. At
a switch the decode runs after the kernel, because the new tile's slices take the running block's slots.

How nty is chosen: the fewest tiles whose ring, plus the cell arrays and 768 MB of slack, fits the device's free memory.
- `UFSM_RECTOSP_RING_GB` caps the ring size.
- `UFSM_RECTOSP_TILES` forces a tile count.

Every profile sample lies within its cell's reach, so it is inside both the old box and the tile box: the codes are the same.

Cost: each tile switch re-decodes the source chunk rows that neighbouring tiles share, about 2 x reach / tile height extra. At the
unroll's +-800 um, the reach is ~85 source voxels.

test_recto_gpu runs each of its three flag sets in 2, 3 and 4 tiles as well. sp and rsp match the CPU byte for byte in every case
(desk card 1). Still to do: the P4 run on the pod (ring size, tile count, wall time against the untiled run's 1521 s), after the
P4 pair and the final 1667 e2e.
## reader3 MX-fp4 (UFSM_XNET_MX): the intermittent illegal address fixed; MX parked opt-in (2026-11-18, branch convkmxoob-20261118, convk)

- The fault: plain MX5 runs of ink-ext died with rc 75 in about 1 of 5 processes on the pod (podrep: r3 of 5). The log said
  "mcuda: k_tshuffle8: the driver's linker does not start (error 700)", then "cudaMalloc ... out of memory".
  - Cause: conv_mx's B loader bounds the K chunk but not the output row. mx_pack1 padded the packed weight rows to 64, but the
    BN 128 tile (co > 64, M >= 4096) reads ceil(co / 128) * 128 rows. reader3's 320-output convs (encoder stages 4-5, decoder 0,
    tconvs 0-1) therefore read rows 320..383: ~92 KB of nibbles past the weights at K 2880, plus their scales. Those rows feed
    only discarded columns, so the maps were right; whether the read faulted depended on what the cache allocator had placed
    behind the block.
  - The 700 is sticky. mcudahw JIT-links each kernel at its first launch, and the first one after the fault was the decoder's
    k_tshuffle8. The next cudaMalloc then fails and reads as an OOM. k_tshuffle8 itself is in bounds.
  - Not affected: the fp16 path (conv_mx is MX only) and the halo kernel conv_mxh (BN 32).
  - Fix: rows padded to 128 (zero rows, valid outputs unchanged); xconv.mxrows; mx_launch exits if a tile grid passes the packed
    rows. test_xmx adds co 320 at M 4096 (the BN 128 tile) and a row-count check.
  - The fault was missed on the desk: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING, memcheck at small crops, synccheck and 3 cold-JIT runs were all clean.
    racecheck on conv_mx (pod) is clean too.
- Parked: MX stays opt-in for reader3. Numbers from the pod (RTX PRO 4000), w035, batch 16, nsys kernel totals:

  | variant | kernel total | wall |
  |---|---|---|
  | fp16 | 5823 ms (conv_igemm 2776) | 8.9 s |
  | pick unfused (MX5, MXQ 2, convs 2-4 skipped) | 5084 ms (conv_mx 1458, k_xq 278) | 10.5 s |
  | pick with the fused GroupNorm + quantise k_gnq (UFSM_XNET_GNQ, branch convkgnq-20261118, byte-equal to xgn + k_xq) | 5426 ms | 11.1 s |

  - k_gnq takes 916 ms, against 538 ms of k_gn_apply plus 172 ms of k_xq it replaces: one thread per 16-channel block coalesces poorly.
  - Wall time is worse than fp16 on one window: 2-3 GPU-idle gaps of ~0.9 s before the first conv_mx launches (cold JIT of each
    instantiation per binary).
  - Quality is fine: held-out ink AUC on the 1667 q2 stripes was +0.0010 for the pick and 0.8734 for the fused pick (fp16 0.874,
    gate -0.005).
  - The estimated ceiling of fused quantisation was ~16-20 % of reader3 kernel time, below the bar for more work.

## Train vs predict parity: the same function up to fp16 rounding, except the EMA default and the window context (2026-11-18, branch parity-20261118)

Audit (fix0332, lead + user): does predict run the function that training validates and trains? One fixed window per scroll (1667 GT
corner 20600,4676,3820 and Paris 4 38008,17540,21976, level 2, P 256) through train's validation (`--val-live 1 --noaug 1`, lr 0,
`UFSM_LAT_FUSE=0` so the normal / density channels are materialised) and through predict (`--fit-zarr`, the window as the box, grid
origin at its corner, halo 0), for try9's pab-A eval-10690 and u1 13000-w. Tools: `UFSM_PARITY_DUMP=DIR` (every forward appends its
numerics modes + an FNV hash of the active weights to DIR/modes.txt; train dumps the first validation window's full-resolution fp16
logits, predict its first window's), `UFSM_PARITY_GNW=FILE` (predict: each window's GroupNorm statistics), unroll.sh `FGRID` (window
grid offset). `test_parity` (gpu) is the same check on a fixture latent net (basis, lat-guide 3, fstem 16, gn_ema unwarmed).

| switch | train val | predict (default) | difference | impact | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| weights | EMA (`--val-live 0`) | EMA (`--ema 1`) | pab-A's EMA sits behind its own warm start | 1667 GT ids 0.798 vs 0.841 live, 46 / 54 boxes worse, body drift 1.64 vs 0.23 | **fixed: `auto`** |
| GroupNorm | live (auto, c93d5610) | live (auto, a8babaff) | equal since 11-18 | was GT ids 0.669 vs 0.729-0.841 | fixed before |
| head precision | fp16 cell logits (head_slab_pass) | fp32 chunk head (lh16_req 0, head_iz 1) | max abs d <= 0.008, 44-90 % bit-equal, corr 1.0000 | none | intended |
| activations / input | fp4 acts, input prec 4, scan-norm 62.9 / 37.59, film 0.999 | the same (modes.txt equal, weights hash equal) | none | none | equal |
| lat_step | 0.25 jittered (train aug: 0.224 seen) | 0.25 | aug only | none | intended |
| fstem-drop, axis jitter, augment | train only (`--noaug 1` in val) | off | none in val | none | intended |
| skip-empty | dense | `--skip-thr 20` | no change on a full window | none (wbench +0.004) | intended |
| window size | 768 training windows (216 bottleneck tokens) | 640 + halo 64 (or 512) | 256 vs 384-640: phase rms 0.43-0.55, corr 0.92; w4 rms 0.64-0.71; 512 vs 640 still 0.19 / 0.24, even in the inner 128^3 | the output depends on the window; not converged at 640 | open (pod arms) |
| basis-free `--lat 4` | cell-mean input | the same input (0.15 % ulp flips) | corr 0.85-0.97 | fixture only; no production net is basis-free | open |

**The EMA.** `unet_ema` steps once per optimizer update (train.c, decay 0.999), so at `--accum 10` its horizon is ~10 000 steps, about
the length of try9's whole lineage (pab-A: 8690 -> 10690 = 200 updates). The EMA is then an average over everything since the warm
start: pab-A 10690's EMA projects to -0.07 on the base -> live fine-tune direction (behind pab-base) and lies 3.1x the fine-tune's
displacement from the live weights. |ema - p| / |p|: pab-A 0.117, pab-base 0.134, u1 13000 0.049. Predicted with its EMA (arm E1,
everything else = AL), 1667 scored 0.798 / joined 0.822 / drift 1.64 / 32 real 5 dup 12 merged vs AL's 0.841 / 0.863 / 0.23; on the
out-of-sample C2-C24 boxes 0.735 vs 0.813. The default was EMA everywhere: predict `--ema 1`, unroll.sh `FEMA=1`, train validation
`--val-live 0`, so try9's val numbers scored weights the unroll did not run (the AL / pod unrolls set FEMA=0 by hand).

Fix: `--ema auto` (predict default, unroll.sh `FEMA` default) and `--val-live auto` (train default) use the EMA unless
|ema - p| / |p| > 0.08 (`EMA_REL_MAX`, src/gnmode.h: between u1's 0.049 and pab's 0.117 -- two points, so it is printed every time:
predict one line, validation one `val: step N: |ema - p| / |p| = ...` line per pass), then the live weights with a `DEFAULTED:` line.
predict reads the two arrays from the file (`checkpoint_ema_rel`, before the store attributes record `ema`), train from the device
(`unet_ema_rel`). Explicit `--ema 0|1` / `--val-live 0|1` win. `test_gnmode`: the rule and `checkpoint_ema_rel` on a synthetic file.
Not changed: the EMA's per-update cadence (a per-window decay, 0.999^(1/accum) per update, would shorten the horizon 10x; it is a
training change for the trainers to decide).

**Window context.** The bottleneck attention runs over the window's tokens (8 at 256, 27 at 384, 64 at 512, 216 at 768 in training)
and gfilm pools the window, so the field at a fixed voxel moves with the window around it, ~50x more than the fp16 head differences
above, and 512 -> 640 has not converged. Per-window occupancy (CT fraction above the skip threshold) on the
production 640 / 64 grid: 48 % of the CT windows hold < 0.25, while every GT box window holds >= 0.49. Window occupancy correlates with
GT ids per box: AL +0.34, u1 +0.38, def-pab +0.085, with AL - u1 at -0.08 (the low-occupancy third: AL 0.775, u1 0.759; high third
0.887 / 0.889). Position is confounded (low occupancy sits at the scroll's rim). The arms that separate the two (FGRID=256 grid shift,
LWIN 576 / LHALO 32, FBLEND=1) need a GPU: queued on the pod since card 1 failed (Xid 31, 11-18 10:56). Note: `--fit-zarr` needs a
stride that divides the 512 shard or is a multiple of it (640 / 64 and 576 / 32 are valid, 640 / 128 and 512 / 64 are not).

## Counting around merges: the ref on mf-weighted fields; 1667 joined GT ids 0.8606 -> 0.9129 (2026-11-18, branch mfref-20261118)

The merge-flag section below found that a local mask only removes ~20 % of the wrong voxels: a merge also misnumbers every sheet beyond
it. The integers of the joined model come from the ref (count-field; the slab fits snap to it, --ref-snap 1), so the lever is the ref's
least squares: count-field's per-cell weight is w / 255 times the orientation and sheetness ramps, and its phase-gradient targets need
confident phase. `ufsm merge-flag --apply FIELDS OUT` (and `--weighted OUT` in merge-flag's own pass) writes the fields with pc, ps
scaled toward 128 and w scaled by f = 1 - mf / 255 (w kept >= 1 on material), every other plane linked: the merged cells still exist
but carry little evidence, so the solve carries the count around them (along z and around the turn) instead of through them.

1667 q2 (u1 13790 fields, recto-blended sp; mf of the fixed rule; count-field with q2's flags on the desk CPU, 12 min; the base ref
reproduces the pod's to the printed digit: model coherence 0.2286, closing error 2.040 turns):

| ref fields | model coherence | closing error | ref GT ids | joined GT ids (desk card 1 slabs + join) | z drift body / whole / end (turns) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rsp (base) | 0.2286 | 2.040 | 0.8388 | 0.8606 (q2 pod: 0.8607) | 0.73 / 0.78 / +3.52 |
| f = 1 - mf / 255 | 0.3563 | 2.072 | 0.8896 | **0.9129** | 0.56 / 0.61 / +1.17 |
| f = 0 at mf >= 128 | 0.4254 | 2.133 | 0.8891 | | |

- Joined, weighted vs base: +0.052 [+0.027, +0.081] (box bootstrap), 41 boxes up / 11 down; every loser within -0.006 except C19
  (0.613 -> 0.507). Largest gains: C57 0.54 -> 0.91, C62 0.54 -> 0.92, C45 0.62 -> 0.95, C2 0.56 -> 0.84, C16 0.77 -> 0.97.
- Ref, weighted vs base: +0.051 [+0.027, +0.079], 42 up / 11 down.
- **Gate (all-voxel joined ids up on the 54 boxes, drift not up): PASS.** Paris 4: pending (needs a whole-scroll P4 field set + run).
- The slabs, join and check are unchanged (master settings: slab overlap 8, FITLANES 1 on card 1, < 4 GB); only the ref's input changed.

**Follow-ups (11-18 evening).** Weighted slab fields as well as the weighted ref (the slabs on merge-flag --apply's planes): joined
0.9138 vs 0.9129, +0.0008 [-0.0001, +0.0017], z drift body 0.62 vs 0.56, end +9.13 vs +1.17 turns: no gain, so the slabs stay on the
unweighted fields. The weight's strength (count-field --mf-w K, f = 1 - K mf / 255; ref GT ids): K 0 0.8388, 0.6 0.8686, 0.8 0.8812,
1 0.8896: monotone, K 1 stays. C19, the one box the weighting hurts (joined 0.613 -> 0.507): a core box (radius 3.5-8 mm in its log);
base is right inside 6 mm and -1 outside, weighted fixes the outside (-1 share 0.46 -> 0.22 at 6.5-7 mm) but turns the inside +1
(0.91 at 4.5-5 mm). 74-100 % of the material between it and the axis is flagged (the core turns): with that evidence gone the count
across the core is the solve's regulariser. A floor does not help (ref C19 0.562 base, 0.471 K 1, 0.429 K 0.8, 0.428 K 0.6). The core
is where the flag runs at ~0.9 of all wraps (wrapmf w000-w003): counting through it needs another reference (levelsolve's in-box fill).

**Unroll (MFREF=1, the default):** first as fields/mfw written by `merge-flag --weighted` (a019de5a); replaced the same day (above) by
count-field --mf-w 1: the weighting inside every field load, no weighted copy written. mflag runs in the foreground right after rectosp,
the ref's count-field gets --mf-w 1 once mflag is done, the slabs read $F; refstream (pass 1 behind the predict) is off under MFREF, a
pool cache only for unweighted runs. A failed mflag leaves the ref unweighted (DEFAULTED line). MFREF=0: the background mflag (no wall).

## merge-flag: where the net merges touching sheets, flagged from its own fields; the unroll exports those parts as uncertain (2026-11-18, branch mergeflag-20261118)

On packed sheets the net's phase runs one cycle across ~3 touching GT sheets ("Where the packed-sheet deficit lives" below). No
integer solve fixes that locally, so the export now says where it happens instead of passing it off as confident surface.

**Truth and evaluation in C: `ufsm merge-flag --eval LIST`** (src/mergeflag.c; LIST lines "name scroll fields-dir codes-root
codes-key"; box by box on threads, 3 min for all 114 pairs on 8 threads). GT radial intervals: along radial rays (16 z planes x 720
angles per box, one native voxel a step, from the fields' axis), consecutive GT sheet crossings one turn apart (codes, winding =
(code - 1) / 18 mod 14), the net's phase unwrapped across the interval: n; merged = n < 0.5 (the box's sign from the median). The
interval's features are its middle cell's. This is the label phase's count by construction (the GT codes are what the label phase is
rasterised from), without needing the phase raster, which is not on the desk for 1667. Boxes: the kept wbench fields of u1 13790
(u1-fd615-core / -ho) and try9 base (pab-base-core / -ho): clean Paris 4 (PH1-3, HOLD, 28 J boxes) and 25 clean 1667 boxes: 114
(net, box) pairs, 3.22 M intervals; merged share 0.02-0.06 on easy 1667 boxes, 0.60-0.70 on PH1 / PH2 / J12. (A numpy prototype gave
the same numbers within 0.003 AUC; it is not kept: the evaluation is the C mode, test_mergeflag runs it on synthetic GT.)

**Features** (net fields only; box filters with edge replication; per field cell):
- amp9: the phase confidence |(pc, ps)| averaged over material cells, 9-cell box;
- R5: the phase's turns per cell (per axis the angle of the 5-box mean of z(x + e_a) conj z(x), as a vector) times the density head's
  spacing in cells (5-box mean of the known sp / 8). Phase turns per density turn: ~1 where both count the same sheets, ~1/3 on a merge;
- sp9: the density spacing, 9-box (computed, weight 0 in the rule).
Prototype screening also tried, and dropped: other box sizes, the spacing over 0.5 mm, phase coherence, normal anisotropy (AUC
0.51-0.54), wind4 vs phase disagreement (0.63): ten features gained < 0.003 AUC over these.

**Rule: fixed, round constants:** p = 1 / (1 + exp(-6.5 (0.62 - R5 - 0.5 amp9))) (--coef 4.03,-3.25,-6.5,0), mf = round(255 p).
The fitted logistic (amp9, R5, sp9) is within 0.002 AUC of it on every split, so the fixed rule is the default:

| split (test boxes) | intervals | merged | fixed rule AUC | logistic AUC | R5 alone | amp9 alone | fixed: P / R at mf >= 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| held-out boxes (fit even, test odd) | 1.64 M | 0.250 | 0.934 | 0.933 | 0.927 | 0.898 | 0.764 / 0.769 |
| - of them Paris 4 | 1.33 M | 0.279 | 0.937 | 0.937 | 0.930 | | 0.764 / 0.802 |
| - of them 1667 | 0.31 M | 0.125 | 0.903 | 0.902 | 0.889 | | 0.756 / 0.459 |
| scroll-out: fit Paris 4, test 1667 | 0.64 M | 0.131 | 0.893 | 0.895 | 0.871 | 0.869 | 0.716 / 0.466 |
| scroll-out: fit 1667, test Paris 4 | 2.58 M | 0.329 | 0.941 | 0.942 | 0.936 | 0.895 | 0.787 / 0.840 |

- Within-box AUC (median over boxes with 5-95 % merged): fixed 0.917 held-out, 0.902 on 1667 scroll-out, 0.920 on Paris 4 scroll-out.
- R5 alone is 0.024 short on the 1667 scroll-out (0.871), so the rule keeps amp9; sp9's weight is not worth its own term.
- By GT gap (prototype, held-out): AUC 0.73 below 70 um (where the 19.2 um cells cannot resolve the sheets), 0.90-0.96 above.
- **Gate (AUC >= 0.8 on held-out boxes and across scrolls): PASS.** On 1667 the recall at mf >= 128 is ~0.46: its merges are fewer and subtler.

**ufsm merge-flag FIELDS [--out DIR] [--thr 179]** (src/mergeflag.c): z slabs of 128 rows (+4 each side) in memory, 128 x 128 tiles
on threads; writes plane mf (zarr, 128^3 shards, lossless; raw fields: mf.raw) with the coefficients and mf_thr in its attributes. The
1667 q2 fields (4635 x 1568 x 1616 cells) take 9.0 min on 12 threads (1.4 GB of rows per plane set); the fixed rule flags 17.4 % of the material at mf >= 128;
mf is 1.4 GB on disk. test_mergeflag: a numpy reference of the same definitions on synthetic fields (every cell within 1 byte,
0.001 % off by one), the merged half flagged / the clean half not, crops, wrap-mf's shares and grids, and --eval on synthetic GT codes
(AUC 1.000 on every split).

**Abstain in the unroll** (scripts/unroll/unroll.sh, MFLAG=1 default, MFTHR 179):
- mflag: a background stage started as soon as the final fields exist (after rectosp), beside ref / slabs / join on TH / 2 threads at
  nice 10, so it adds no wall to the critical path (it was first serial in check: +4-9 min, branch mfbg-20261118 moved it); only its
  consumers wait for state/mflag.done (mfready): the GT split, snap's wrapmf.tsv (before CLEAN deletes the planes it reads), perwrap's masks;
- check: with GTBOXES the joined model's confident part is scored too (fit --score-mf THR conf|unc: only the label voxels in cells
  mf < THR / >= THR; gtboxes.sh passes FITX; mkcrop.sh links mf) and logged beside the joined line as "ids right X, uncertain share of
  the GT voxels Y", so every GT-scored unroll reports both;
- snap: `ufsm wrap-mf` writes qa/wrapmf.tsv, the per-wrap uncertain share (vertices in flagged cells); CLEAN keeps the mf plane;
- perwrap: r/<w>/<w>_mf.tif, the mask on the render's pixel grid (wrap-mf --render 1: (w - 1) step + 1 pixels, as render --scale 1).

**GT check on 1667** (pod q2 joined model, u1 13790 fields, recto-blended sp as the unroll uses; 54 GT boxes, 2.31 G labelled voxels;
the fixed rule; deltas voxel-weighted, 95 % CI from a box bootstrap):

| confident = mf < | ids right | delta | CI | boxes up | coverage lost | wrong voxels removed | gain per point lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (all) | 0.8607 | | | | 0 | 0 | |
| 179 (p 0.7, default) | 0.8781 | +0.0174 | [+0.0130, +0.0221] | 50 / 54 | 5.4 % | 17.2 % | 0.0032 |
| 153 | 0.8799 | +0.0191 | [+0.0144, +0.0242] | 49 / 54 | 6.5 % | 19.4 % | 0.0016 |
| 128 (p 0.5) | 0.8815 | +0.0208 | [+0.0159, +0.0260] | 50 / 54 | 7.7 % | 21.5 % | 0.0014 |
| 102 | 0.8834 | +0.0226 | [+0.0175, +0.0280] | 50 / 54 | 9.2 % | 24.0 % | 0.0012 |
| 77 | 0.8854 | +0.0246 | [+0.0193, +0.0303] | 51 / 54 | 11.2 % | 26.9 % | 0.0010 |
| 51 (p 0.2) | 0.8881 | +0.0274 | [+0.0218, +0.0333] | 51 / 54 | 14.4 % | 31.2 % | 0.0008 |

(The fitted logistic at 128, before the fixed rule: 0.8800, +0.019 at 6.5 % lost: the same curve.) **Default threshold 179, the knee**:
the point farthest above the chord from (0, 0) to the 15 % end (0.0071 vs 0.0067 at 153, 0.0061 at 128); past it each point of coverage
buys half as much. At it: confident ids 0.8781 (+0.017), coverage lost 5.4 %; the uncertain part scores 0.556, wrong 3.6x as often.
**Gate (confident ids up measurably at <= 15 % coverage lost): PASS** (+0.017 at 5.4 %, +0.027 at 14.4 %).

Per-wrap uncertain share on the q2 wraps at 179 (qa/wrapmf.tsv): 0.14 of all vertices (the GT boxes sit in the middle turns, hence
their 5.4 %); the core wraps w000-w003 0.90 / 0.78 / 0.63 / 0.48, the middle w013-w027 0.04-0.07, rising to 0.58 at w043 (the outer
turns, where the papyrus thins). wrap-check's "merged" verdicts (w011-13, w018-22, w025-27; CT peaks between wraps) do not line up with
it (shares 0.04-0.11): consistent with CT peaks being no counting reference (section "rhocal" below).

**Limits.** A merge also shifts the numbering of every sheet beyond it; a local mask cannot remove that, so the confident part's gain
is bounded: at 12 % coverage 28 % of the wrong voxels go, the rest are confident cells numbered from across a merge. The mask is for
the export and for levelsolve's count-constrained fill (the agreed input: plane mf, mf_thr in its attributes), not a count correction.
The rule was fitted on the net's own sp; the 1667 unroll's fields carry the recto-blended sp (RECTOSP), on which the GT gain above was
measured.

## ink-ext: the next tile row rendered while this one runs on the GPU; to_ref_grid threaded (2026-11-18, branch stripe-20261118, unrollperf)

The stripes' reader3 (r3pre) is now the unroll's tail. In the pod A/B 1667 run it took 537 s for 39.3k tiles. At the GPU's
~150 tiles/s that is ~262 s of net, so about half the wall was waiting. In run_surface the main thread rendered a tile row's rows,
then handed its ~20 batches to the GPU worker one at a time, waiting on each. The next row's render therefore overlapped only the
last batch: ws000 took render 62 s + net 142 s = 204 of its 233 s. The surface's TIF canvas (to_ref_grid, surf_pn per pixel, one
thread over 59997 x 9793 px) added most of the remaining ~29 s.

- Tile row iy + 1's new rows are rendered on a second thread while row iy's tiles go to the GPU. The ring grows by the largest
  tile-row step: reader3 T 384, stride 192, ring 400 -> 600 rows x 17 layers x Wm, +200 MB on a 60k-px-wide stripe. The ahead
  render runs only when its slots no longer hold rows the current tile row reads. Rows render in the same order into the same
  slots, and the batch order is unchanged, so the output is the same bytes. UFSM_IE_AHEAD=0 restores the old order.
- to_ref_grid runs over rows on the run's --threads.
- Pod A/B, one ink-ext over stripes ws000 + ws002 + ws003 and wrap w040 (as r3pre does), batch 16, 8 threads. All 4 maps are
  byte-identical in every arm.

  | | ws000 | ws002 | total |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | master | 183.7 s | 99.0 s | 297 s |
  | ahead off, to_ref_grid threaded | 168.1 s | 91.8 s | 274 s |
  | branch | 118.0 s | 73.0 s | 205 s |

  ws000 is now net 98 s + ~20 s of normalisation, TIF and JPEG. Expected in the unroll: stripe reader3 537 -> ~380 s. The residual
  pass and every ink-ext call get the same overlap.

## try9 after the reboot: the card-1 layout sets the rate, not CPU contention; CPU weights for the trainer slice (2026-11-18, trainperf)

try9 resumed at 13250 in the rev-card1 layout (CT decode + ink on card 1, onfly phase + fibre on card 0) ran 0.18-0.19 samp/s
(82 Mvox/s), against 0.25 (113 Mvox/s) before the crash. That 0.25 was item C's (09:04-10:56: onfly phase + fibre on card 1). The
2.3 GB it frees on card 0 let the planner give the fp4 GroupNorm input copy 2.17 GB of spare instead of 0.33 GB (13.27 vs 10.98 GB
free at plan time). The rev-card1 layout ran 0.18-0.19 / 81-86 Mvox/s on 07:46-08:53 too. The desk was CPU-saturated at the same time
(load 58 / 32 CPUs; the main thread 25 % runnable-wait, nice 10 vs the dev jobs' 19 in one cpu group). `systemctl --user set-property
ufsm-train.slice CPUWeight=10000` (ufsm-dev.slice 100; enables the cpu controller under ufsm.slice, persistent) cut that to 7 %, but
the rate stayed 0.18: the step is GPU-bound (the main thread spin-waits in sched_yield). The weights are kept. Undo: set
ufsm-train.slice CPUWeight=100.
Item C restored at 12:54 on the same binary (lead): plan 10.07 of 13.27 GB, GN copy 2.17 GB; steps 14050 / 14100 fresh 0.25 / 0.24,
111 Mvox/s. try9 holds 3.3 GB on card 1, so card-1 jobs leave it 4.5 GB.

## Unroll ink path: residual geometry early, faster surf-resample, check side by side; pod setup (2026-11-18, branch r3geom-20261118, unrollperf)

In the pod q2 1667 timeline, perwrap (958 s) ended the run. Its critical path ran after the stripes' reader3 maps landed (14:42:36): the
r3once surf-resample (172 s), then the residual reader3 (117 s), then compose (22 s) and pw_fin (21 s), in series.

- surf-resample used 2-3 contended atomic adds per pixel and per vertex (npx / npxok / nseam, nv / nvok / hist) from 8 threads, and
  every 1667 pixel takes the cheap bilinear path (0 seam pixels). Per-thread counters, added once per thread: pod, q2 data, full mode,
  212 / 223 s -> 117 / 117 s wall, 1138 -> 400 CPU s. The pixel pass went 147 -> 55 s. Maps, src and residual surfaces byte-identical.
- surf-resample --geom-only 1 (SRC-MAPS "-") writes only the --residual surfaces, from the geometry. Every source counts as mapped and
  no map is read or written. On q2's 44 wraps it is byte-identical to the full run's residual. test_surf_resample checks band 0 / 6
  and fill-gap 0 / 4.
- unroll r3once (R3EARLY=1, the default): once distort.done exists (the final stripes) and the wraps are flattened, the residual is
  written from the geometry while reader3 still inks the stripes. When strip.ok lands, the residual reader3 (GPU) runs beside the
  resample (CPU). The resample writes its own residual to res.chk. If that differs from the early one (a stripe without a map), the
  run logs DEFAULTED: and re-inks from res.chk. R3EARLY=0 restores the old order.
- check: wrap-check, unroll-qa and cf-demod are independent, so they run side by side (2.8 + 24.2 + 13.2 s before). Verdicts are
  logged in the old order.
- Pod A/B: a copy of the q2 run (master 2b021688) with check, stripimg and perwrap redone by the branch, R3PWGATE=80 for q2's gated
  per-wrap maps.

  | | q2 | branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | check | 40 s | 25 s |
  | perwrap | 958 s | 705 s |
  | stripimg | 703 s | 699 s |

  The early residual was written at 18:10:04, 138 s before the stripe maps. Residual reader3 ran at 124 tiles/s beside the resample
  (147 alone). Byte comparison: all 44 per-wrap ink maps, all 4 stripe maps, and both mosaic overviews (img_fill, img_pap) identical.
  perwrap now ends 6 s after stripimg, so stripimg is the run's tail: about 545 s of stripe reader3, then 79 s of stretch renders and
  79 s of refill. The next win is the stripe renders overlapped with the stripe reader3.
- Trim (11 s) is unchanged. It makes 3 serial surf-stats calls, and a prefetch would measure the large outer wraps the walk never asks for.
- Pod setup.sh:
  - pip tifffile (test_img_gate passes on the pod now; inksdk's mkarms needs it).
  - LLVM / apt.llvm.org (55 s on the 11-18 pod) only without /usr/bin/cc, or with LLVM=1.
  - The scroll's CT is fetched in the background beside the JIT warm-up (61 + 52 s in series before).
  - CUBINS=FILE unpacks an earlier pod's mcudahw cache before the warm-up. The warm-up then packs the cache to
    POD/cubins-<gpu>-<driver>.tar.zst (262 MB -> 33 MB, 1.4 s) for the desk to pull. Kept at
    /vesuvius/ufsm/pod/cubins/cubins-NVIDIA_RTX_PRO_4000_Blackwell_595.112.07.tar.zst. A test setup on the pod with it: 64 kernels
    JIT'd in 6 s instead of 2220 in 52 s; the whole setup (warm ccache, level 5 only) took 57 s.
  - A desk-built binary cannot run on these pods (desk glibc 2.43, pod 2.39). Reuse a binary only between pods with the same
    native_id (NOBUILD / FOREIGN_BINARY).

## xnet: a failed device allocation stops the process (2026-11-18, branch xnetalloc-20261118, unrollperf)

Desk card 1, 10:55:58: Xid 31 (MMU fault at a null address) from the q2b reader3 ink-ext (--batch 16 beside try9 + fix0332), then
"xnet: forward: an illegal memory access", and try9's card-1 context died with it. r3ink.log: "1417 MB in use exceeds the 382 MB device
budget", then "cudaMalloc of 288 / 144 / 0 / 9 MB failed". xmalloc_dev returned nullptr after its retry, and no caller checked: the next
forward wrote through the null buffers. The same pattern hit the 08:28 card-0 run.

- xmalloc_dev never returns nullptr now. After the retry with the cache freed, it prints "xnet: cudaMalloc of N MB (B bytes) failed: out
  of memory (... MB in use, ... MB budget; lower --batch / --gpu-mem): stopping before any launch" and calls _exit(XNET_OOM_RC = 75).
  _exit, not exit, so no atexit handler or destructor touches the device after the failure, and the other threads (ink-ext's GPU worker)
  stop with it. Every xnet user (ink-ext, ink3d, dinovol, villawind, hercuvit, surfrecto, surfeval, dino's SSL path) gets this. The raw
  unchecked cudaMalloc calls in nn_dinovol / nn_villawind (cuBLASLt workspaces, bias16) go through xmalloc_dev too. deskq2.sh's
  "out of memory" grep still matches, so its R3BATCH 16 -> 8 retry is unchanged. A trainer that hits this in dino's SSL path now exits
  75 where it used to fault the context.
- UFSM_XNET_FAIL_ALLOC=N fails the Nth fresh (cache-missing) allocation without touching the device. test_xnet_oom (CPU, card list
  emptied) checks exit 75 and the message for 1 B / 4 KB / 9 MB / 288 MB.
- Pod (RTX PRO 4000), reader3 UFSM_IE_BENCH=16,3:
  - forced failures at allocations 1, 3, 8, 20, 40, 80, 160: rc 75, no illegal-access / fault line;
  - a real failure at batch 1024 (78 GB): rc 75, no fault;
  - baseline before / after: rc 0;
  - reader3 on wrap w040 of the q2 run: map byte-identical to the pod master build (142 vs 140 tiles/s).

## Slab-fit voxel unwrapping without records; the node fill from a frontier (2026-11-18, branch vunwrap-20261118, fp4teach)

After the stage-4 step A/B (above: the steps are not stage 4's cost) the voxel unwrapping was 1.7 of a slab's 2.8 s stage 4 on the pod
(1667 s030: setup 0.3, flood 0.6, nodes 0.8 s). perf on the desk: atan2 / hypot bound. For the unroll's fits (`--ref-snap 1 --uw-repair
0`) every voxel took theta = atan2 about the box's axis three times (uw_setup, uw_refsnap, uw_accum), the ref's radius / angle once
more, uw_q twice, and an 8 B record of fresh zero pages (0.5 GB a slab) was written and read twice. And the node fill (nodes without
voxels: the mean of their filled neighbours) always ran its 64 passes, each a sweep of all 440 K lattice nodes: 0.40 s.

- `fit_node_fill`: a pass fills exactly the unfilled neighbours of the previous pass's nodes, so the frontier version visits each filled
  node and its neighbours once; same nodes, same neighbour order, same doubles (0.40 -> 0.03 s). `UFSM_UW_FILL_OLD=1`: the sweep.
- uw_snapfused (ref_snap 1, no repair; `UFSM_UW_RECORDS=1`: the three passes over records): no records. The seed from q alone
  (uw_seedq, the same per-thread first maximum), the ref bias on its subsample and the seed's integer base from record values computed
  in place (uw_rec: uw_setup's expressions), and the snapped integer inside the node accumulation (uw_accum_snap): one atan2 and one
  hypot a voxel. The ref's radius / angle reuse the box's when the ref's axis at zr is bit-equal to the box's at pz and the y / x
  offsets are 0 (a z slab of the ref's box: every row of s030; checked per row, `UFSM_UW_SAME=0` off): equal arguments, equal results.
  mcc contracts no host FMA, so one theta reproduces all three of the old ones.

Byte-identical: the s030 model (desk, every run), test_fit_join's ref-snap slab against UFSM_UW_RECORDS=1 and UFSM_UW_SAME=0, test_uwfill
(frontier vs sweep on random lattices, cap hit and not), and the pod's joined 1667 model (md5 = the OV 8 arm's in all four arms).

Pod (RTX PRO 4000, 3 lanes x 9 threads, 1667 slabs .. join at OV 8, interleaved old / new x2, same binary, old = UFSM_UW_RECORDS=1
UFSM_UW_FILL_OLD=1):

| arm | slabs wall | slabs CPU | unwrap summed over 71 slabs (setup / flood / nodes) | stage 4 summed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| old 1 | 117 s | 1428 s | 138.1 s (28.5 / 44.6 / 65.0) | 159.0 s |
| new 1 | 99 s | 976 s | 70.2 s (6.7 / 3.1 / 60.4) | 91.0 s |
| old 2 | 117 s | 1437 s | 140.0 s (28.7 / 44.8 / 66.5) | 160.7 s |
| new 2 | 98 s | 976 s | 71.1 s (6.8 / 3.2 / 61.1) | 89.4 s |

The slab stage -16 % wall, -32 % CPU; join unchanged (22 s). Single-thread on the desk (s030): unwrap 12.6 -> 7.8 s. What is left is
the fused accumulation (~110 ns a voxel single-threaded: uw_q, one atan2 + hypot, two lattice evaluations); inlining ev_party_W did
not change it.

## Pod q2: full PHerc1667 at master on an RTX PRO 4000 (u1 13790, every speedup); the per-wrap ink gate bug (2026-11-18, unrollperf)

The podq2 queue (scripts/pod/podq2.sh, DESK=none + the desk pull scripts/pod/q2pull.sh) on a 24 GB RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell pod (cgroup
27.2 CPUs / 31 GB), master 2b021688, u1 13790 fields, INKMODE=r3 + R3ONCE, PERWRAP, KEEPINK: 23.5 min from the fields to the last wrap
(setup 4 min before it). Stage walls (s; max RSS GB): fields 62 (5.9), rectosp 31, ref 53 (16.2 at the auto CFMEM), slabs 137, join 26,
check 40, wraps 39, trim 11, snap 53, strip 26, stripflat 43, distort 12, stripimg 703 (14.7; the stripes' reader3 143.8 tiles/s), perwrap
958 beside the strip chain (r3once: 44 wraps, residual reader3 143.8 tiles/s, then compose); cgroup peak 25 GB, no OOM kill. 4 stripes,
179.2 cm, 1111 cm2, on papyrus 0.973. GT (desk, score1667.sh): gtboxes ids right joined 0.8607, ref-cf 0.8388 (54 boxes).

Held-out ink AUC at 40 um: the stripes' raw reader3 maps 0.8739; the wraps' maps ungated (surf-resample stripes -> wraps) 0.8721; the
wraps' maps as the unroll wrote them 0.6512. pw_fin ran r3ink.sh with its default gate (CT >= 80), meant for the strip renders' FILLED CT
(--fill-ct 80 recentres it onto papyrus); the per-wrap renders have no --fill, their inked pixels sit at CT ~44 (median, w001), so the gate
zeroed 46 % of the ink (95 % on w001). The CT render itself is unchanged by the render alias / --volume-out 0 (w001: byte-identical CT
tif with UFSM_RENDER_ALIAS=0 and the volume written). pw_fin now passes R3GATE=${R3PWGATE:-0} (no gate); test_podscripts checks it.

## Slab-fit kernels, step 1: fit_pool from tables, fit_loss2_list_k without its local arrays (2026-11-18, branch convkfit-20261118)

fp4teach profiled one slab fit: s026 of the desk 1667 u1 fields, 96 x 1568 x 1616 at h 2 cropped to the material, with unroll.sh's fit line.
With 3 lanes the slab stage is GPU-bound, so its kernels map about 1:1 to slab-stage time. Actual per-fit totals: fit_loss2_list_k 747 ms
(1000 launches), the phase gate 300 ms (k_pg_gate / rates / boxx), the selection 284 ms (fit_select_inv_k / fit_select_k), fit_pool_k 116 ms.
- fit_pool_k was fp64-bound: two __ddiv_rn and eight __dmul_rn a voxel, at the 5060 Ti's 1/64 fp64 rate, one thread per pooled cell
  walking ~8000 voxels. Every per-voxel term depends only on byte values: wi = w / 255, wi x (each t plane value), and
  8 wi / (h sp). So fit_pool_t_k looks them up in tables built per call with the same __d*_rn operations (fit_pool_tab_k: 256 +
  2 x 65536 doubles) and keeps only the __dadd_rn chains, in the original order. 115.8 -> 35.0 ms a fit; planes byte-identical
  (test_fit pool_tab_case: 3 pool factors x 2 cell sizes, holes in w and sp). UFSM_FIT_POOLT=0: the old kernel.
- fit_loss2_list_k: ncu showed 127 registers, 33 % occupancy, 0.58 IPC, and 45 % of the L1 sectors local memory. Two changes:
  - On the device, fit_vox2 adds its corner gradients to the fixed-point accumulator as each one is known (fit_gadd's conversion),
    instead of handing back the 32-entry ic / gv arrays the kernels indexed by a run-time count. The host pass (fit.c, the CPU
    backend) still fills ic / gv.
  - The per-thread fixed-point loss parts accumulate in the thread's own column of the shared reduction buffer, instead of 11
    long longs live across the grid-stride loop.
  127 -> 96 registers; ncu on the same launch (#300, interleaved): 314-333 -> 281-284 us. The remaining local traffic is the
  trilinear corner loop's arrays, which mcc keeps rolled. Unrolling it (a plain #pragma unroll; mcc drops _Pragma in a macro) removed
  every LDL / STL but took 168 registers and 16 % occupancy: 330 us. With __launch_bounds__ 2 (128 regs): 277-288 us, no better. Not kept.
All the sums are integers or the same double chains: the slab fit's delta.f32 / axis.f32 / model.json are byte-identical to master.

Step 2 (same branch): the phase gate's k_pg_rates and the minibatch selection.
- k_pg_rates: FP64-bound (86.6 % of the pipe), ~8 double divisions a cell. The divisions by byte constants (c0 = L / 127, t / 255) now
  come from tables of the same doubles (k_pg_rates2): 12.0 -> 9.8 ms per 16 M-cell block. UFSM_PG_OLD=1 gives the first kernels;
  test_fit_join checks planes and integer counts byte for byte against them (the sum of q is a double atomic, so its order varies run
  to run).
- Tried and dropped:
  - k_pg_gate and k_pg_boxx with their 2R + 1 box-sum terms loaded 8 ahead, then added in the same order: the gate stayed at 23 ms, and
    boxx went from 5.0 to 6.5 ms. The gate runs at IPC 0.16 with ~2400 SASS instructions a cell under mcc (NOP-padded DADD / F2F.F64
    chains).
  - A table for its blend: not byte-separable, since g (c8 - 128.0) / 127.0 rounds the product first.
- fit_select_inv_k / fit_select_k: the box / crop index helpers did 64-bit divisions per candidate. The list path has < 2^32 box cells,
  so fit_box_index32 / fit_crop_index32 compute the same integers in 32 bits. ncu on the same launches: select_inv 440 -> 333 us, select
  56 -> 45 us. UFSM_FIT_SEL64=1 gives the size_t helpers.
The slab fit's delta.f32 / axis.f32 / model.json are byte-identical to master again.
Measured end to end by fp4teach (12 slabs of the 1667 u1 fields, master 9c9c8977 against the previous binary, interleaved x2,
outputs byte-identical): 1 lane 68.2 / 72.4 -> 61.1 / 57.9 s (-15 %), 3 lanes 42.8 / 42.9 -> 40.7 / 39.9 s (-6 %). The desk was at load
~11, with a guest on card 1, so at 3 lanes the host side (5 threads a lane) capped it.

stage RSS from progress.log / stagetable.tsv, i.e. `time -v` of the stage's largest process):

| phase | consumer | memory | note |
