| desk host, other | /tmp tmpfs (the agents' shared scratchpad) | 29 GB (23 in one scratchpad) | the 18 GB of swap in use is tmpfs pages: no process had > 0.3 GB swapped |
| unroll, host | **ref** (count-field --model-only) | **28.2 GB** (11-17), 16.2 (q2) | 512-row chunks x 2.53 M cells x 10 B = 13 GB, x2 with --prefetch |
| | stripimg | 18.4 / 17.6 GB | one stripe render (ws000, 509 M px) at UFSM_RENDER_MEM 16 (halves itself to 50 % of available) |
| | rectosp, fields (predict), stripflat, join, snap, ink | 6.7, 5.8-6.2, 4.3-5.0, 4.5, 4.1-4.6, 3.5-4.1 GB | predict: the fit-field slab ring 4.4 GB (14.6 GB at 1152 windows) |
| predict, GPU | fields on a 5060 Ti | ~8.5 GB | ink-ext's auto --batch follows the free memory |

Most of the large figures are budgets that follow the available memory (the trainer's planner, count-field's --mem-gb and prefetch,
the render's UFSM_RENDER_MEM, zcache): they shrink on a small machine without changing results, except count-field, whose chunk rows
(a result-changing parameter) were capped by --mem-gb at 12 B per cell. The trainer's device memory buys no speed past the plan: at
P 768 the no-offload modes need ~11.5 GB for -0.2 % step (DESIGN "P 768 data parallel", 11-13). Freeing card 0 would take
`--onfly-gpu 1 --fibre-gpu 1` on try9 (-2.29 GB there, +2.3 GB on card 1, same kernels): headroom only, left to the swap process.

**count-field in shard pieces.** Pass 1 (the pooling) needs a chunk's 10 planes only one solve row and its two halo rows at a time,
and the GPU model pass only the solve rows themselves; whole 512-row chunks were held for the prior (the middle chunk) and because the
phase gradient stops at the chunk's first / last row. Now the GPU paths read 128 rows at a time (UFSM_CF_PIECE_ROWS, the fields' zarr
chunk; 0: whole chunks): `cf_gpu_pool_rows` takes the rows from host row blocks with the chunk bounds kept as the gradient's, each
piece's last solve row waits for the next piece with its P + 1 rows kept (a 228 MB carry at 1667's 2.53 M cells a row); the model
pass's pieces are whole 128-cell blocks of its kernel (else whole chunks) and sample the chunk's every 7th voxel from the chunk's first
row (`cf_gpu_gsum_piece`), so acc takes the same block partials in the same order. The prior reads the middle chunk again afterwards
with 4 of the 10 planes (pc ps sp w; it never reads the normals). The upload buffers are 512 MB (was 2 GB: 1 GB pinned instead of 4).
A requested --chunk-rows on this path is capped by the prior's 4.5 B per cell instead of 12 (a 16 GB scope keeps 512 rows; before,
its --mem-gb would have DEFAULTED the rows and changed the ref). CPU paths, --pool-split / --rho-* and the R > 0 output passes: as before.

| 1667 q2 ref (count-field --model-only, 512-row chunks, --threads 8, card 1) | max RSS | wall | model |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11-17 desk/pod run, prefetch (two chunks) | 28.2-29.5 GB | 55 s (27 threads) | |
| 11-18 q2 run, no prefetch (28 GB available) | 17.0 GB | 88 s | reference |
| pieces, in a 16 GB memcap scope (3 runs) | **8.1 GB** | 76-92 s | delta.f32 / axis.f32 / model.json byte-identical |
| pieces, UFSM_CF_STAGE_MB 2000 (the old 2 GB upload buffers) | 10.8 GB | 107 s | byte-identical |

(Walls on card 1 shared with try9's aux and the unroll chain, 83 % busy: noise of +-15 s; pass 1's pooling 31-39 s at either staging
size, so 512 MB stays.)

test_countfield `pieces_vs_chunks`: pieces of 8 / 12 / 16 rows against whole 24-row chunks, pooled sums and the model delta byte for
byte (16: the last piece short), the stride-2 model pass in pieces, and a failed piece (UFSM_CF_TEST_PFAIL) whose chunk is redone on
the CPU: the CPU run's bytes there, the GPU's elsewhere. REFSTREAM's `--pool-only --follow` beside the predicts uses the same path.

**The rest of the audit (11-18).** (1) try9's on-the-fly phase slots and fibre planes move to the aux card at the --val-gn-live resume
(`FIBGPU=1`, XFLAGS `--onfly-gpu 1`; lead-approved, trainperf verifies): card 0 -2.29 GB, card 1 +~2.3 GB; headroom, no speed expected.
(2) The agents' shared scratchpad and stale /tmp test / suite dirs held 22.5 GB of tmpfs (RAM, and most of the 18 GB of swap in use):
27 items not touched for 24 h deleted (16.6 GB; /tmp 29 -> 13 GB, swap 18 -> 10 GB, MemAvailable 93 -> 105 GB). test_latents.sh keeps
its dir only on a failure (by design: "kept $D"). (3) stripimg's 18-19 GB is the stretch stripe render's decoded-chunk cache
(UFSM_RENDER_MEM 16 in strip_refill.sh, halved to 50 % of available on smaller machines; the refill renders 1.7-3.8 GB): left as is, an
8 GB A/B (same images, maybe re-decodes) only if a pod runs short. (4) Predict fields (host 5.8-6.2 GB, the 4.4 GB slab ring; ~8.5 GB GPU)
and the trainer's host side (66-76 GB of a 140 GB slice) are not binding: no change.

## Where the packed-sheet deficit lives: the net merges contact sheets though they are labelled and loss-weighted x8; 4.8 um input and the Paris 4 spiral fit / segments both fail (2026-11-18, pseudolab)

This follows "Packed sheets are not resolved by finer CT" below, and the lever memo (/vesuvius/ufsm/pseudolab/lever-memo.md). The
scripts are in /vesuvius/ufsm/pseudolab/res48 (fieldcmp.py, fielddiag.py, w4diag.py, wb48.sh) and /vesuvius/ufsm/pseudolab/blight
(sheetcmp.py).

### (a) 4.8 um input, wbench DLV -1 (fd615b6f predict, cube windows; same fitter, codes, boxes)

Boxes: packed PH1-3 / C1 / C2 / C19, control HOLD / C6 / C8 / C10 / C12 / C15 / C57.
- **u1 13790:** packed Δids0 -0.063 [-0.136, +0.009]; control -0.195 [-0.377, -0.053] (C10 0.94 -> 0.30, C12 0.99 -> 0.56).
- **try9 base (--gn-live 1):** packed -0.063; control -0.252.
- **FAIL:** the gate was packed >= +0.05 with CI > 0. The packed boxes get worse too, so the "packed - control" difference only
  reflects the controls collapsing: 4.8 um input is off-distribution for nets trained mostly at 9.6, as early nets were (u1-3000,
  wind96, section 2026-11-12).

### B-light: the Paris 4 extras (dropped, no try9 time)

- **Spiral fit spiral-output-generation-19:** a 956 x 56913 tifxyz with per-vertex winding ids 10..135 (43.2 M vertices), x4 to the
  2026 scan's 2.4 um voxels, rastered at 9.6 (16 GB, 4 min). Against the q-9p6 GT on the wbench Paris 4 boxes:
  - sheets are placed well: 84 % of the packed GT sheets have a spiral sheet within 60 um, median 14-19 um;
  - the winding is not: adjacent-step consistency is 0.735 at < 100 um gaps and 0.89 above (PH1 0.70);
  - the best-gauge share per box is PH1 0.30 / PH2 0.45 / HOLD 0.67, against the try9 net's ids0 0.25 / 0.26 / 0.81, and the spiral's
    numbers are in-sample (it was fit from verified patches).
  It is net-quality, not GT-quality, where it matters.
- **The 12 unused published segments,** wind-assigned into June's gauge with the July recipe:
  - 5 duplicate June surfaces;
  - 3 conflict (dropped);
  - 4 are new: about 210 cm2, ~2 % of June's area, all in one neighbourhood.
  Too little to clear the ~0.02 arm noise.

### Diagnostics on the kept wbench fields (CPU; try9 base and u1 agree within ±0.08)

- **The net merges contact sheets.** Between consecutive GT sheets one turn apart, the share where the net's unwrapped phase advances
  < 0.5 turn, by gap (0-70 / 70-100 / 100-130 / 130-180 / > 180 um):
  - HOLD 0.65 / 0.39 / 0.16 / 0.08 / 0.07;
  - 1667 C2 0.62 / 0.20 / 0.09 / 0.04 / 0.02;
  - C1 0.90 / 0.55 / 0.34 / 0.34 / 0.29.
  There are almost no extra turns. The fields are h 2 (19.2 um cells), so the 0-70 bin is near the unwrap limit, but the 70-100
  bin is clean and already shows the merge; no h 1 re-check is needed.
- **PH1-3 are low-contrast regions.** The net merges there even at wide gaps (> 180 um: PH1 0.41, PH2 0.56, PH3 0.79). Compared with
  HOLD / C2 / C10 / C15:
  - the net's phase confidence (|pc, ps|) is 0.11-0.17 vs 0.51-0.72;
  - the CT contrast (CV along the ray between GT sheets) is 0.15-0.26 vs 0.38-0.53 (PH3 at < 130 um gaps: 0.02-0.03, nearly flat CT).
  The net is correctly unsure where the CT shows almost no sheet structure.
- **The winding-mod-4 plane (dx over 32 voxels) does not rescue the count:** within 0.5 turn of GT at < 100 um gaps PH1 0.31 /
  PH2 0.29 (0.25 = chance), HOLD 0.55, C2 0.65; at > 150 um 0.71-0.92. The density head's spacing tracks a typical spacing:
  sp / GT gap is 1.4-1.75 at < 70 um and 0.4-0.8 above 180 um.
- **The labels are reliable there.** The independent June and July tracings agree on the winding at 0.963 of the < 100 um sheet
  crossings (adjacent-step consistency 0.94), against 0.99+ at wider gaps. The merges are the net's, not label noise.
- **The fitter is not the limit.** On the label phase at the same 19.2 um cells it scores 0.81-0.99 on PH1-3 (the ceiling).

### Where the deficit lives, and the recommended lever

The deficit is in the net's local perception of sheets in contact. The labels there are good (~96 %), and the fitter counts them
when given their phase. Finer CT does not show the sheets apart, and fed 4.8 um input breaks the net. Paris 4's extra data is either
net-quality (the spiral) or tiny (the segments). The heads that should carry the count across contacts (wind4, density) are near
chance or biased toward a typical spacing exactly there.

**Correction (same day): the contact-sheet loss weighting already exists and is on.** try9 and u1 both train with
`--packed-weight 8` (`--packed-um` 120 default; section "Packed-sheet label targets" 2026-11-14 and the 10-13 density section). It
weighs the phase and normal / density losses x1 at sheet spacing >= 120 um, rising to x8 at 60 um. So the labelled contact sheets
already get up to 8x the loss, and both nets still merge them. A x3 weight raster (the first draft of this lever) would only lower
that; it was not built.

**Remaining lever: non-local counting across contacts.** Carry the turn count from where the same sheets separate:
- fitter side: constraints along the sheet, e.g. fibre / relative-winding links. The fitter reaches 0.81-0.99 on PH1-3 given the
  label phase.
- net side: more context per prediction (halo 64 vs a theoretical receptive field of 439 cells; window borders cut it).
Cheapest first check, with no training: fixed-fields wbench (FIELDS = the kept pab-base fields) on PH1-3 / HOLD / C1 / C19, with the
fitter's long-range terms raised. If the counts recover, the lever is in the fitter; if not, it is the net's context.

## try9's 1667 unroll was on GroupNorm statistics it never trained on; live GN + the cooled checkpoint beat u1 (2026-11-18, branch gnlive-20261118)

Question (lead): why is try9's full-scroll 1667 unroll (pod B def-pab: ref GT ids 0.669, body drift 1.35) so far behind u1's (0.831, 0.71)
when the wbench box gap between the nets is 0.004-0.011? Cause: try9 trains with `--gn-ema 1 --gn-ema-warm 1000000000`, i.e. always on
each window's own GroupNorm statistics; the running statistics are only accumulated (header ge_n 8690 < ge_warm 1e9). predict's default
normalised with those running statistics (its own log said so: "GroupNorm on the running statistics (8690 updates), which the net never
trained on"), the wbench scoring ran `--gn-live 1` (scripts/integ/e2e.sh gnflag). u1 has no gn_ema: its windows use their own statistics.

Arms on desk card 1 at def-pab's exact settings (640/64 fields, `--ema 0`, dir -1, FSKIP 20, occupancy 5, the whole box; fields ~5 min on
the 5060 Ti), up to check; GT ids on the 54 non-noise 1667 wbench boxes (gtboxes, CPU), /vesuvius/ufsm/fix0332/gn1667:

| arm | checkpoint | GN at predict | ref ids | joined ids | ref ids C2-C24 (16) | wrap-check real/dup/merged | body drift |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| u1 (pod def-u1) | u1 13000 | own (no gn_ema) | 0.831 | 0.853 | 0.806 | 33 / 6 / 12 | 0.71 |
| def-pab (pod) | pab-base 8690 (lr 3e-4) | running | 0.669 | 0.699 | 0.644 | 35 / 4 / 10 | 1.35 |
| A | pab-A eval-10690 (lr 0 cooldown) | running | 0.729 | 0.754 | 0.707 | 26 / 4 / 17 | 0.50 |
| B | pab-base 8690 | live (`--gn-live 1`) | 0.742 | 0.766 | 0.724 | 31 / 5 / 11 | 0.69 |
| AL | pab-A eval-10690 | live | **0.841** | **0.863** | 0.813 | 32 / 5 / 10 | **0.23** |

- Live GN: +0.07 ref ids on 8690 (0.669 -> 0.742), +0.11 on 10690 (0.729 -> 0.841); body drift 1.35 -> 0.69 / 0.50 -> 0.23.
- Cooling (8690 -> 10690): +0.06 on the running statistics, +0.10 with live GN; the two compound. Neither alone reaches u1, both together
  pass it (+0.010 ref, +0.010 joined, body drift a third of u1's).
- In-sample caveat: 1667's C25-C70 boxes are in-sample for both nets (paired, so the comparison holds, but the level is optimistic). On the
  16 boxes outside that range (C2-C24, 6.7e8 labelled voxels) the ranking is unchanged: AL 0.813 / 0.839 (ref / joined) vs u1 0.806 /
  0.833, def-pab 0.644; per box AL vs u1 is a tie (ref 6 better / 7 worse by > 0.005, joined 7 / 7). So: AL >= u1, not clearly above it.
- wrap-check verdicts did not track GT here either (A: 17 merged at ids 0.729; see "rhocal" above).

Fix (predict, src/gnmode.c): a gn_ema checkpoint whose --gn-ema-warm was never reached defaults to `--gn-live 1`, with a `DEFAULTED:`
line; `--gn-live 0` forces the running statistics; warmed checkpoints, `--gn-frozen` and non-gn_ema nets unchanged. test_gnmode. Train's
validation the same way (branch valgn-20261118): `--val-gn-live` unset = each window's own statistics while the net's ge_n < ge_warm (the
function it trains with at that step; one DEFAULTED line), the running ones after; `--val-gn-live 0 | 1` forces either. Before, the
default 0 validated try9 (and chose its best.ckpt) on the running statistics; try9 gets an explicit --val-gn-live 1 at its next launch. Also on the branch: unroll.sh FPX (extra fields-predict flags), and SGPU now applies under a caller's
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (an index into it, as --gpu): with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 SGPU=1 the ref count-field had run on card 0, try9's card.

## Ink the papyrus once: the wraps' reader3 maps resampled from the stripes' (r3once; per-wrap AUC +0.004, 7.6k instead of 37.5k tiles; 2026-11-18, branch inkonce-20261118)

Under INKMODE=r3 the unroll inked the same papyrus twice with reader3: once per wrap (the per-wrap images, perwrap's r3pre) and once per
strip stripe (the mosaic, stripimg's r3pre). On 1667 that is 37.5k vs 38.0k tiles (1187 vs 1189 M px), desk 826 s and 952 s on a shared
5060 Ti (--batch 4); at the pod's 85 tiles/s ~440 s of GPU each, which made the strip chain the critical path (unrollperf 11-17).

`ufsm surf-resample SRC-SURFS SRC-MAPS DST-SURFS OUT` moves a map rendered on one tifxyz surface set onto another by 3-D position, so it
needs no lineage between the sets (the wraps' and the strip's flattenings are unrelated parametrisations): source vertices in a spatial
hash (8-voxel cells), each destination vertex projected onto the nearest source surfaces' bilinear patches (Gauss-Newton, walking across
cells; the closer of the two best surfaces, <= --max-dist 4 voxels), destination pixels on render's canvas interpolated from their
corners (at a switch between sources: the pixel's own point projected), the source map sampled bilinearly. 97.6 % of the stripe vertices
project within 0.25 voxels. CPU only: 4 stripes 62 s, 44 wraps ~95 s on 8 threads. test_surf_resample: a synthetic cylinder sheet, two
overlapping sources (one with a hole) and a destination of its own parametrisation: mean |d| vs the analytic map 0.32 / 255.

Which direction: 1667 held-out ink AUC (scripts/inkgt/inkscore.sh = wrapscore.py, 1.84 M held-out samples; desk reader3 maps on the
try9-6250 pod surfaces, podun/PHerc1667/inksdk):

| map | 20 um | 40 um | 80 um |
|---|---|---|---|
| A reader3 on the stripes | 0.8666 | 0.8624 | 0.8505 |
| D reader3 on the wraps (the per-wrap images until now) | 0.8633 | 0.8580 | 0.8445 |
| C wraps -> stripes resampled (A where no source) | 0.8635 | 0.8583 | 0.8450 |
| E stripes -> wraps resampled (0 where no source) | 0.8662 | 0.8619 | 0.8496 |
| F stripes -> wraps, composed (r3once, below) | 0.8664 | 0.8622 | 0.8500 |

The resampling itself is free (C = D, E = A within 0.0005); the per-wrap images were the weaker inking (D 0.004 below A: reader3 reads
the strip's chunked flattening better than the per-wrap SLIM one; not investigated further). Wraps -> stripes also cannot cover the
stripes: the per-wrap flatten keeps part of each wrap only (w060: a 2177 x 2318 lattice, a 562 x 747 flat), 3.6 % of the stripe pixels
have no per-wrap source (ws002 17 %, ws003 81 %). So the stripes are inked and the wraps resampled from them.

r3once (unroll.sh, INKMODE=r3, R3ONCE=1 the default; perwrap after its renders waits for the stripes' raw maps, state/strip_chain.failed
or UPTO: the old per-wrap r3pre): surf-resample stripes -> wraps with three additions, then one ink-ext over the residual, then --compose:
- --fill-gap 16: unsampled surface slivers within 16 px of a sampled pixel take its value (35 % of the unsampled pixels are within 4 px,
  44 % within 16: the stripes' and the wraps' borders differ by a few px);
- --edge-band 32: 6 of the 44 wraps cross a stripe boundary, where the stripe maps carry reader3's tile-edge effect (stripes -> wraps
  alone: |E - D| within 16 px of the switch 11.4 vs 7.1 elsewhere, p95 46 vs 28); a 32-px band there is left unsampled;
- --residual DIR: per wrap a tifxyz copy holding only the vertices whose pixels are still unsampled, + 8 vertices of context (+ 32 for
  the band: with 8 the band kept |d| 12.8), the rest invalid; reader3 on it skips the empty tiles; --compose puts its map into the
  unsampled pixels. (Seeding the residual by the pixel under each vertex must use render's pixel rule, all 4 cell corners valid, or every
  vertex next to a hole seeds it: 6.8 M residual vertices before, 1.6 M after.)

Result F: held-out AUC 0.8622 at 40 um (+0.0042 over D, A's level); the seam band |F - D| 4.3 (it is inked on the wrap) vs 7.1 elsewhere;
the residual pass 1.6 M vertices, 7,559 tiles (20 % of the per-wrap pass), desk 88 s vs 826 s; + 98 s resample and 12 s compose on
8 CPU threads. Expected on the pod: perwrap's ~440 s GPU pass -> ~90 s GPU + ~110 s CPU.

End to end on the desk (full 1667, post-snap, ur/PHerc1667-post1, card 1 shared with try9 + fix0332's predict, capped to <= ~5 GB of
mine: R3BATCH 4, SPAR 1, SJOBS 1, RJOBS 1, UFSM_RENDER_GPU_MEM 2; card-1 peak 11.1 GB total):

| step (perwrap + stripimg run side by side) | old (per-wrap r3pre) | r3once |
|---|---|---|
| stripes' r3pre (stripimg; its maps kept for r3once, R3PRECP) | 38.0k tiles, 952 s (r3all 11-17) | 38.0k tiles, 577 s (render 84 + net 493: the same work, a less crowded card) |
| per-wrap reader3 (perwrap) | 37.5k tiles, 826 s | residual 7,559 tiles in 44 surfaces, 71 s (105.8 tiles/s) |
| surf-resample stripes -> wraps / --compose (CPU, 8 threads) | - | 138 s / 16 s (1,183 M px resampled, 4.05 M from the residual) |
| GPU reader3 tiles over both | 75.5k | 45.6k (-40 %) |

perwrap 858 s wall here includes waiting for the stripes' maps (it starts r3once once ink/r3/strip.ok exists) under SPAR 1; the
stripimg chain failed on its first try on a bug of the r3 wiring (strip_refill.sh called r3() before defining it: `r3: command not
found` on the first reused stripe; fixed on this branch) and took 38 s after the fix on the kept renders and maps. Stage walls on the
shared desk card are not the pod's; podq2.sh's stagetable.tsv will give the pod's.

## strip-flatten: a full-size chunk without a mesh fails only above 0.1 % of the strip's vertices (2026-11-18, branch inkonce-20261118)

Audit 11-14 #7 made any full-size chunk (2 S + 1 columns) with surface but no mesh fail the stage (before, it was skipped with exit 0).
The 1667 z band 3072+1024 (the r3 re-time) then failed on one chunk of 204 scattered vertices. Now the dropped vertices are summed over
such chunks and the stage fails only when they exceed --nomesh-max (0.001) of the valid vertices of every chunk read (both counted with
the chunks' 2x overlap); below it prints `DEFAULTED: strip-flatten: N full-size chunks without a mesh, D of V valid vertices (..)` and
their columns come from the neighbouring chunks' tails, as a narrow edge chunk's do. test_strip: a 400-column gap with 8 isolated
vertices (2 full-size chunks without a mesh, 16 of 401,552 vertices): continues with the DEFAULTED line at the default, fails at 1e-6.

The unroll's distort gate counted every "no mesh" line of stripflat.log (also narrow edge chunks, and the appended log's earlier runs)
and stopped the strip at any. It now reads the latest strip-flatten invocation only: full-size chunks that strip-flatten DEFAULTED and
narrow edge chunks are logged (`distort: DEFAULTED: ...`, `... narrow edge chunk(s) ... (not gated)`), full-size ones without a
DEFAULTED share still gate. The 1667 band (z 3072+1024, ur/PHerc1667-r3) then ran through: stripflat 12 s (14 full-size chunks without
a mesh, 2,774 of 19.3 M vertices, 0.0144 %; 3 narrow), distort 0 s (p95 0.207, folded 0.00288), stripimg 101 s (3 stripes, the stripes'
r3pre 38.1 tiles/s on the shared card; strip 143.7 cm, 119.2 cm2, on papyrus 0.945).

## Packed sheets are not resolved by finer CT: CT peaks per GT turn at 9.6 / 4.8 / 2.4 um (2026-11-18, pseudolab)

The next-lever memo (/vesuvius/ufsm/pseudolab/lever-memo.md) rested on the premise that finer CT resolves the sheets the 9.6 um net
misses. On the holdouts, corr(packed share, ids0) is -0.55, and boxes with >= 30 % of their GT turns under 100 um score 0.47 vs 0.81.
Before any 4.8 um teacher run, the premise was tested directly on the CT.

- **Method:** fix0332's ctgt.py (section "The curve on three scrolls"; copy in /vesuvius/ufsm/pseudolab/res48 with SIG / L / P
  tunable), on the same scan, the same GT codes (Paris 4 q-9p6 at 9.6, 1667 codes at 4.798) and the same rays. Only the CT level
  changes: key 2 (9.6), key 1 (4.8), and for Paris 4 key 0 (2.4 um, NAS L0). Two detectors:
  - (b) equal physical scale: sigma / mean-sd / prominence windows scaled with the voxel, 1.2 / 12 / 24 at 9.6 -> 2.4 / 24 / 48 at 4.8
    -> 4.8 / 48 / 96 at 2.4;
  - (a) native voxels, unscaled.
  The 9.6 rerun reproduces fix0332's Paris 4 curve: 48901 vs 48897 intervals, 1.045 vs 1.044.
- **CT peaks per GT turn, detector (b):**

| | 0-70 um | 70-85 | 85-100 | 100-115 | all |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paris 4 9.6 | 0.52 | 0.74 | 0.88 | 0.97 | 1.05 |
| Paris 4 4.8 | 0.58 | 0.80 | 0.93 | 1.03 | 1.11 |
| Paris 4 2.4 | 0.60 | 0.84 | 0.94 | 1.05 | 1.12 |
| 1667 9.6 | 0.45 | 0.67 | 0.78 | 0.87 | 1.54 |
| 1667 4.8 | 0.48 | 0.71 | 0.83 | 0.92 | 1.60 |
| 1667 2.4 (NAS L0, --nz 4) | 0.50 | 0.74 | 0.84 | 0.93 | 1.64 |

- **Per box** (gap < 100 um | >= 100 um, 9.6 -> 4.8):
  - PH1 0.60|1.10 -> 0.64|1.18 (2.4: 0.66|1.21);
  - PH3 0.75|1.57 -> 0.83|1.71;
  - HOLD 0.70|1.11 -> 0.73|1.17;
  - 1667 C1 / C2 / C19: +0.02 to +0.04 at gaps < 100 um, the same or more at wide gaps.
  The rise is uniform, not selective for packed sheets. The share of 0-70 um turns whose count is off by >= 0.5 barely moves
  (0.54 -> 0.51 -> 0.51).
- **Detector (a):** raises every bin 1.6-2.6x (Paris 4 overall 1.69 at 4.8, 2.65 at 2.4). That is texture and noise peaks, not
  sheets.
- **Reading:** below ~100 um, adjacent sheets do not appear as separate CT maxima, even at 2.4 um. They behave as compressed into
  contact, not as under-sampled. This corrects latbeat's "mostly resolution" (2026-11-11): the latent net's deficit at 60-150 um
  spacing is real, but finer input CT does not visibly separate those sheets. The resolution lever (multi-res teachers for winding)
  loses its premise. Still to test (cheap; the net is not a peak detector): u1 13790 fed 4.8 um (wbench DLV -1) on PH1-3 / C1 / C2 /
  C19 against control boxes. Gate: packed Δids0 >= +0.05 with CI > 0, and >= +0.05 beyond the control Δ.

The question: do fit-derived pseudo labels (section "Fit-derived pseudo labels", 2026-11-17) or the unlabelled DINO/ssl trunk term
(section "Self-supervision for the latent net") help try9? A control-paired test, run while try9 was held (s2ctl hold 11-17 16:24 ->
11-18 04:02, ~11.6 h; scripts/pseudo/ab_chain.sh + ab_arm.sh).

- Base: try9's last.ckpt at the stop, step 8690 (pab-base.ckpt). Each arm resumes it for 2000 steps (--steps 10690) on card 0 with try9's
  argv and binary pinned from scratch2.resume.log (ufsm.scratch2.fd615b6f, CPU CT decode), try9's full sampler (12 slots / 10 workers /
  3 onfly slots), --det 1, --echo-max 0 (echo reuse depends on sampler timing), env MALLOC_ARENA_MAX 4, UFSM_HEAD_SLAB_Z 16,
  UFSM_HOSTMEM 1, UFSM_SAMPLER_THP 0. --det check first: 2 x 20 steps, step lines byte-identical up to " qk ".
- A (control): sources-scratch1-ph80-ho.json. B: A's weights x0.85 + PHerc1667-pseudo 0.15 (the dm1 refit, dir -1: tile gate 0.703
  material-weighted, 29 of 79 wraps, 6878 mm3 of labels, gt-gate keeps 0.076, outward 0.9998; wbench C1-C70 +64 at weight 0 and the
  11-14 holdouts + C25-C70 (holdouts-20261118) masked, guard 32; 0332 excluded). C: A + the 35 unlabelled ct_only scans
  (ssl-sources.sh, HOLD=holdouts-20261118), --ssl 16 --ssl-share 0.25, trunk term only. MEM_DRY at P 768: A 11.25 GB, C 11.40 GB.
- Schedule note: the WSD cooldown is 0.2 of the whole run, so with --steps 10690 it starts at 8552 and every arm decays ~2.8e-4 -> 0
  over its 2000 steps. Arm - base differences therefore include the cooldown; only B-A and C-A are treatment effects.
- Scoring: wbench, fd615b6f predict, cube windows (WZARGS=), --gn-live 1 (try9 never trains on its running GN stats); step 2000
  (primary) and 1560 (ring 10250; 1500 is no snapshot step). Paired box bootstrap, 95 % CI. Clean sets: HOLD and the 11-14 holdouts
  (45 boxes); core reported with 1667 split out (in-sample for try9 and u1). Results: wbench/res/pab-{base,A,B,C}-*.tsv, the stats
  /vesuvius/ufsm/pseudolab/pseudo/abstats.py.

ids0, treatment - control:

| | HOLD (A -> X) | holdouts 45 | of them 1667 (24) | core Paris4 + 4j (32) | core 1667 (12) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## rhocal (label-free count calibration from CT peaks): rejected by 1667 GT; the CT peak count is no counting reference (2026-11-18, branch rhocal-20261117)

Idea (lead / user 11-17: a per-scroll auto-calibration for the corpus, 0332 the test bed): wrap-check counts CT papyrus peaks per fitted
turn by radius band; scale count-field's density term per band (--rho-r, K(r) <- K(r) x CT(r)^1.3, median-3, cap [0.8, 1.6], gated bands)
until CT/turn ~ 1, keep it only if wrap-check dup + merged and the body z drift do not get worse. unroll.sh stage `rhocal` (RHOCAL=1,
RHOCALMODE radial | global, RHOCALMIN / MAX / G / TOL / IT) with tests/test_rhocal.sh: kept on branch rhocal-20261117 only, not merged.
1667 A/B on pod B (u1 13000 and pab-base 8690 fields, 640/64, dir -1), GT ids right on the 54 non-noise 1667 wbench boxes (gtboxes,
ref models; CPU on the desk; the GT codes never leave the desk):
| fields | default ref | radial pass 1 / 2 / 3 | radial, K >= 0.95 | global pass 1 / 2 | rhocal's own verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| u1 13000 | 0.831 (joined 0.853) | 0.581 / 0.526 / 0.517 | 0.581 / 0.526 | 0.592 / 0.501 | accepted (dup+merged 21 -> 8-11) |
| pab-base 8690 | 0.669 (joined 0.699) | 0.523 / 0.375 / 0.376 | same | 0.491 / 0.305 | DEFAULTED (body drift +0.23..+0.51) |
Why: wrap-check --gt-int --ct --codes on the default u1 ref (55386 intervals between consecutive GT sheets): per GT turn the fit counts
1.024, the density term 1.22, the network phase 0.93, the CT peak detector 1.54 (off by >= 0.5 on 54 % of the intervals). The CT peaks per
GT turn follow the sheet spacing: by GT gap 0.56 (< 70 um), 0.84 (85-100), 1.04 (115-130), 1.20 (150-180), 1.34 (180-230), 2.21 (> 230); by
radius 1.96 (0-4 mm) .. 0.93 (12-14 mm). "CT peaks per fitted turn = 1" is right only near ~120 um gaps (Paris 4's 1.05 calibration was
that regime). So the CT peak count can not calibrate a count, and wrap-check's verdicts reward the wrong direction too: the recovered u1
rhocal fits checked 52 real / 12 dup / 0 merged against the default's 33 / 6 / 12 while losing 0.25-0.33 GT ids. unroll-qa's pw48 / w4
fell with the "corrections" (0332 and 1667) and agreed with GT: the 11-17 claim that they penalise correct counting is withdrawn.
Kept (master, branch rhocalkeep-20261118): wrap-check --bands / --intervals, cf-demod's body vs end drift + body z range, ZR=auto
(opt-in), the DRIFTWARN ALARM on the body excursion, count-field --rho-r (a tool). The rhocal stage, its install fix and test_rhocal stay on
branch rhocal-20261117 (pushed, not merged).
Corrections to the 11-17 PHerc0332 section below: "try9 undercounts 20 %" and "u1 counts right" rest on the same uncalibrated CT
objective. Read through 1667's gap curve, try9's 0332 fit (gaps ~160 um, CT/turn 1.18) maps to ~1.0 turns per GT turn and u1's (~132 um,
1.04) to ~0.95; the fits disagree (62 vs 72 wraps, pair accuracy 0.27 at 2 mm) but which is right is not decidable label-free with CT
peaks. The 0332 AGREE pseudo-label boxes (CT/turn 0.95-1.05) are withdrawn. The broken top end (zr 512,7680) and body drift stand.
**The curve on three scrolls (11-18, CPU; /vesuvius/ufsm/fix0332/curve).** CT peaks per GT turn by GT normal gap (um), wrap-check --gt-int
(model + fields) for 1667 (def-u1 ref) and Paris 4 (u1 ref-cf, q9p6 codes, z 6400-12800); 0139 has no fields on the desk, so ctgt.py does the
same detector and interval rule fields-free (material = CT > 0, normal from the GT label structure tensor, wbench boxes; it reproduces
1667's overall 1.545 vs wrap-check's 1.54 and reads its bins ~0.05-0.1 lower):

| gap um | <70 | 70-85 | 85-100 | 100-115 | 115-130 | 130-150 | 150-180 | 180-230 | >230 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1667 wrap-check | 0.56 | 0.73 | 0.84 | 0.95 | 1.04 | 1.10 | 1.20 | 1.34 | 2.21 |
| P4 wrap-check | 0.55 | 0.73 | 0.86 | 0.97 | 1.09 | 1.20 | 1.35 | 1.54 | 1.98 |
| 1667 ctgt (boxes) | 0.46 | 0.68 | 0.78 | 0.88 | 0.96 | 1.05 | 1.15 | 1.30 | 2.14 |
| P4 ctgt (boxes) | 0.51 | 0.76 | 0.87 | 0.96 | 1.06 | 1.16 | 1.26 | 1.43 | 1.88 |
| 0139 ctgt (boxes) | 0.40 | 0.66 | 0.79 | 0.89 | 0.97 | 1.06 | 1.14 | 1.26 | 1.97 |

Same shape on all three (0139 ~ 1667, P4 +0.05..0.2 above 130 um); the share off by >= 0.5 turn is 0.35-0.7 per interval everywhere. The
lookup test: wrap-check --intervals now writes the fitted normal gap and the GT turns (gap_um, gtq; all rows), and CT / lookup = sum npk
/ sum f(fitted gap) per model:

| model | GT turns per fitted turn | raw CT/turn | CT / f_1667 | CT / f_P4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1667 def-u1 ref (GT ids 0.83) | 0.985 | 1.473 | 0.944 | 0.958 |

| P4 u1 ref-cf | 1.033 | 0.925 | 0.976 | 0.942 |

Within a scroll the lookup ranks right where raw CT/turn ranked wrong (rhocal's dups read 0.905 vs 0.944), ~0.04 for 0.03 GT turns,
most of it from the < 70 um bin. Across scrolls the level is not portable: P4's ref over-counts GT (1.033) yet reads 0.94-0.98, below
or level with 1667's under-counting def. So no lookup target or gate: a calibration error of ~0.05 equals the counting errors that
matter. At most CT / lookup as a same-scroll A/B diagnostic; counting stays a model problem (labels on more scrolls).

## Pod B rounds: 0332 count-rescale arms and the 1667 rhocal A/B, rhocal REJECTED by GT (2026-11-17/18, podunroll + fix0332, branch podun-20261118)

**Verdict first:** rhocal made 1667 worse on ground truth (GT ids 0.831 -> 0.50-0.59 with u1 fields, 0.669 -> 0.31-0.52 with pab), and the
CT peak count it calibrates against reads 0.56-2.21 peaks per GT sheet depending on the spacing (see the next section and "GT scoring"
below). Every "improvement" in the tables here (merges -> 0, CT peaks per turn -> 1) is in the wrong direction on 1667; read them as the
record of a refuted method, not as gains.

ph25k12 and rr1h; the dense-qa reruns of those two were dropped (lead: the 48-tile qa is enough). test_unet~narrow at master f69cebd9
passed 2/2 on this card (the RTX PRO fault fixed in ab60f6ba).

## Latent-ink smoke on pod B: cancelled before a scored step. Cold https CT was the wall; the restart recipe (2026-11-18, scripts/inksmoke)

The plan (user-approved: smoke test only, ~10.5 h) is the retrain from the inkpod diagnosis (section "Production ink = reader3").
- Two arms of 3000 steps from the u1 trunk (`/vesuvius/ufsm/podun/u1-13000-w.ckpt`, sha1 0d056422; `--lat-basis klt1.lcb` required).
  - A: human ink labels only.
  - B: human labels + ink-teach soft labels from reader3 + ink9um. On 1667 held-out the reader3 + ink9um logit blend scores 0.8623 vs
    reader3 + argus2 0.8601, both within noise of reader3's 0.8583.
- Both arms: holdouts-20261118; `--replay 1 --fstem-drop 0 --ink-radial-drop 0.15 --ink-mil-r-um 50 --um-rungs 4.8,9.6:3
  --trunk-lr-mult 0.2`; per-scroll weights P4 0.50, 0139 0.20, 1667 0.15, the rest 0.05 each.
- Scoring on the desk (scripts in /vesuvius/ufsm/inksmoke). `score.sh TAG CKPT` = latink over the whole 1667 box at level 2 (9 min on desk
  card 1), the 17 labelled up/ wraps rendered (ink, c12, c13) and gated with img-gate (3.6 min), then pairwrap held-out vs reader3.
  Validated: inkpod-15000 re-scored this way gives the pod table's 0.5824 exactly, on the same 1,296,287 samples.

**What happened on pod B** (RTX PRO 4000 24 GB, 10.2 CPUs, 31 GB cgroup):
- Setup (master clone, build, mcc from ~/.local/mcc) and test_unet~narrow (PASS) took 5 min.
- The GT fetch took about 1 min: 291 files, md5-checked, from open-data S3 + the HF bucket (`gtmanifest.py` / `gtfetch.sh`; no labels desk -> pod).
- Arm A then ran 30 steps in 4 h: 0.003 samples/s, 3.2 Mvox/s, and 809-1732 s per 10 steps in the derived cache (19-37 k ink-target
  cells computed per 10 steps).
- Cause: the CT came over https, cold, through one sampler worker (1 worker / 2 slots for the 31 GB cgroup: the desk sampler-only check
  of arm A held 23-24 GB RSS at 2 / 2; the pod trainer's anon was 17.4 GB at 1 worker, with memory.events "max" counting, no OOM). The
  worker reads serially, ~1 MB/s: 13 GB of CT in 4 h. The ink targets themselves are computed on the GPU and disk-cached; they only waited
  on the CT.
- `ufsm prefetch arms/sources-A.json --levels 1,2 --threads 48 --P 1024` fixed the input side: 481,871 chunks (~132 KB each), 47 GB local,
  30 MB/s, 42 min (08:00-08:42).
- Arm A was relaunched on the warm cache at 08:42:43. The user stopped the pod at 08:43:38, before its index finished, so the warm-cache
  step rate is unmeasured. Reference: inkpod at P 1024 with local CT ran 0.8 samples/s, i.e. ~1 h for a 3000-step arm.

**Fixes found on the way (merged):**
- The ink onfly path took at most 64 held-out boxes per scan, and 1667 has 74 (all on labelled meshes). Now INKFLY_MAXEXCL = 256 (the boxes
  are in device memory).
- `--lat-basis` was missing (u1 needs it: without it the net had 4 inputs and --init-from failed).
- install_mcc into a non-default prefix failed on the pod (stddef.h not found): podq uses ~/.local/mcc at the pin.

**Restart recipe (a future pod, >= 24 GB GPU; the kit is /vesuvius/ufsm/inksmoke/kit, 316 KB + klt1.lcb):**
1. `rsync -a kit/ POD:/root/ink/kit/`, `kit/inkgt/ -> /root/ink/inkgt/`, `kit/arms/ -> /root/ink/arms/`. The jsons point at /root/ink;
   rebuild them with mksources_u2ink.py ROOT=... for another root.
2. `COMMIT=<master> setsid nohup bash /root/ink/kit/podq.sh > /root/ink/podq.out 2>&1 &`. podq.sh now prefetches each arm's CT before
   training (state/prefetchA.done; ~47 GB for A, more for B's teacher windows; disk >= 120 GB free) and stops an arm whose mean
   samples/s at step 50 is below MINSPS (0.1).
3. Report the step-10 line as soon as it prints (stepwatch.sh A 10: every 10-step line, STALL after 25 min without one) and the gate at
   step 50. Below the gate, the fallback is `--um-rungs 9.6` only (production's rung; ~1/8 of the input chunks per window) with Paris 4
   dropped (41 % of the chunks), before giving up.
4. When the queue is done (state/ALLDONE: both arms, snapshots 1000 / 2000 / 3000), report the pod idle at once. Pull the six snapshots and
   score them on the desk (score.sh, pairwrap with --maps reader3=...,A=...,B=..., --ref reader3, --split heldout).
**GT scoring (fix0332, desk).** _to be filled in: gtboxes on the itN models vs def-u1's ref; wrap-check --gt-int --ct --codes on def-u1's
fields: CT peaks per GT turn by radius band._

## rectosp's m7 source fetched beside the fields: ufsm z3-fetch, 17.9k chunks cold in 22 s (2026-11-17, branch rdup-20261117)

fp4teach found the pod's rectosp stage (103 s) waiting 77 s on its helper, mostly the cold network fetch of the m7 prob source (desk:
cold 137 s wall / 104 s wait, warm cache 35.6 / 11.7 s). The source box is known at run start (box.txt), so unroll.sh now runs
`ufsm z3-fetch SRC KEY --cache fields/rsp.cache --box BOX --scale LUM/um` in the background from the fields' start (m7fetch; M7FETCH=0
off; rectosp stops it by PID before removing the cache). z3-fetch fetches every present inner chunk the box (+- 128 voxels) touches into
z3_open's chunk cache, no decode, z first; per shard the box's uncached chunks are read in file order with neighbours merged into one
range request exactly as z3_read coalesces (gap <= UFSM_Z3_GAP 64 KiB, span <= UFSM_Z3_SPAN 2 MiB; z3_prefetch_shard). Cache files are
the ones z3_read writes (cache_put, tmp + rename): a reader beside it is safe.

1667 m7 source (L2 prob, 9.596 um, 1024^3 shards of 128^3), the whole scroll box, desk, cold cache, 8 threads:

| fetch | wall | chunks fetched |
|---|---|---|
| one request per inner chunk (z3_prefetch_chunk) | 323 s | 17,893 |
| per shard, coalesced (z3_prefetch_shard, 160 shards) | 22.3 s | 17,893 |

17,893 = the pod rectosp's 6,536 GPU- + 11,304 host-decoded chunks plus the margin's. 22 s is well inside the fields' 99 s, so rectosp
should start warm (fp4teach's warm 35.6 s vs cold 137 s on the desk; the pod's 103 s -> ~30 s expected, not yet measured end to end).
Test: test_z3_fetch (a 256^3-sharded array over a local range-serving HTTP root: 6 chunks in the box, 4 present, fetched in 1 request;
a second fetch fetches nothing; the box then reads through the cache with no chunk requests and equals the local array).

## render --volume-out 0: the r3 renders write no volume image (2026-11-17, branch rdup-20261117)

Under INKMODE=r3 render's volume image (<wrap>.tif / <stripe>.tif) is always replaced by r3ink.sh (mv over it) before anything reads
it, so writing it was wasted (the pod's ws000: writes 9.7 s, three images on their own threads). render --volume-out 0 (needs --ct)
writes only <wrap>_ct.tif and the fill flags; the volume itself stays, aliased to the CT (decoded once, section below), because --fill's
search needs a volume beside the CT. unroll.sh passes it on the per-wrap and the 3 stretch renders when INKMODE=r3 and the render has
no --gate; strip_refill.sh when R3INK is set and it is ungated. test_render_gate: no volume image, CT and fill flags equal.

## render decodes one array once when it is several volumes: the r3 renders' CT x2 -> x1 (same bytes; 2026-11-17, branch rdup-20261117)

Under INKMODE=r3 the unroll's renders pass the CT as both --volume and --ct (the volume's render is replaced by r3ink.sh), so every stripe
and per-wrap render decoded and uploaded each CT chunk twice (the pod's 1667 stripe ws000: 37.6k chunks, 63.5 GB uploaded, half of it
the second copy). render's chunk-ordered path now aliases a volume to an earlier one when they are the same array (same z3 handle, or same
root + key + chunk + shape + element size): the alias takes no decode-list entries and its chunk table is the earlier volume's (CPU), its
device pointer keys the same slots (GPU). Block chunk ranges are already the same for all volumes (the reach is the max depth + fill
reach), so lifetimes and frees are unchanged. UFSM_RENDER_ALIAS=0 restores per-volume decoding.

PHerc1667 w035 (the whole try9-6250 wrap, 33.3k blocks, the unroll's r3 flags: --depth 1 --scale 1 FILLX, local CT level 2, card 1
shared, pool 2.5 GB, 4 threads), arms interleaved, decode mode pinned:

| decode | arm | wall | user | chunks | uploads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU (UFSM_GPU_DECODE=1) | per volume | 2.09, 2.07 s | 6.9 s | 7048 | 0 |
| GPU | alias | 2.09, 1.48 s | 5.7 s | 3524 | 0 |
| host (=0) | per volume | 9.18, 11.35 s | 38-46 s | 7048 | 9.72 GB |
| host | alias | 5.37, 5.66 s | 23 s | 3524 | 4.86 GB |

w035.tif / _ct.tif / _fill.tif byte-identical over all 12 runs (alias on/off, GPU/host decode). The first, unpinned pair mixed the modes:
render enables GPU decode by itself only above ~3 GB of free device memory (render.c), which card 1 crossed between runs, so an unpinned
A/B on a shared card measures the switch, not the change. Test: test_render_gate (CPU and GPU) renders the CT as volume, CT and a gate
with alias on and off: equal bytes, and on the GPU a third of the chunks.
## The fused fine stem: fields predict's fstem_fwd_k 46.7 -> 24.2 ms a window, same bytes (2026-11-17, branch convkfs-20261117)

After the fused up + stem became the fields default (6a5933f1), fstem_fwd_k<true> took 47 of 122 ms of kernels a window (PHerc0332, 640
windows, u1 13000), against a ~10 ms floor. The floor counts 6 fp16 outputs written once plus the CT read: fzA launches ~14.5 B a voxel, fzB
(the w4 pair) ~6.5 B, ~198 GB over the profile, 442 ms at 448 GB/s, against 2072 measured. ncu on bench_fstem (P 512 slab of 32 planes, 6
outputs) showed 92 registers, 41 % occupancy, DRAM 38 %, and two causes:
- fs_stage. Each thread staged its 16 CT rows one after another (load, convert, store, next row), so it waited out 16 DRAM latencies in
  turn: the top stall. mcc also emitted fs_stage out of line in the UP instance, on generic pointers, with every __half2 as two LD.E.U16
  and every sr write a generic ST.E.U16. Now all 16 rows' loads go out before any store, and the helpers are __forceinline__.
  bench 0.784 -> 0.630 ms fused, plain 0.583 -> 0.571.
- The per-block setup. The W1 A fragments wait behind fs_w1_exp's scans and a barrier, 10.6 % of the samples, repeated by every
  1024-voxel tile's block. The fused kernel is now persistent: 2 x the resident blocks (occupancy API), each looping over tiles, setup
  once. bench 0.630 -> 0.561 ms; 1 x resident 0.574. The plain kernel, the trainer's head-slab instance, is slower persistent
  (0.574 -> 0.59), so it keeps a block per tile.

Every tile's arithmetic is unchanged. In situ: fstem_fwd_k 46.7 -> 24.2 ms a window, all kernels 121.8 -> 99.2. The fit-zarr fields
(sp w dz dy dx pc) are byte-identical, 0 of 537 M voxels differ. bench_fstem's three output hashes are unchanged. test_fstem
checks the persistent forward byte for byte against a block per tile (plain, fused fp16 / fp32 cells, 96 tiles over 3 blocks) and runs
the fused-vs-chain checks with 3 blocks. UFSM_FSTEM_PERS: 0 a block per tile; N both kernels persistent at N x resident.
Still ~14 ms above the floor: 92 registers and 5 blocks an SM; the per-output qs rows and the side-pair loads are the next items.

## ink-ext's CT prefetcher: reader3's unroll ink from 258 to 86 s over 5 wraps (same maps; 2026-11-17, branch r3fetch-20261117)

The unroll's ink is now reader3 per surface (INKMODE=r3, da14d47f). Its end-to-end split on PHerc1667 (try9-6250 wraps, CT level 2 over
https, 8 threads, card 1 shared): w035 from a cold cache 50.2 s wall = render 46.3 s (3575 chunks, 1.1 GB: each band's chunks fetched one
z3_read at a time, ~90 chunks/s, the band's rows waiting for them) + net 11.4 s (89 tiles/s) partly beside it; warm 12.3 s (render 6.0,
net 11.2: net-bound); w036 after w035 needed 639 new chunks of 3848 (neighbouring wraps share ~83 %).

- `--fetch-threads N` (16; with --cache and a remote CT): I/O threads fetch the encoded chunks of each surface into the --cache
  (z3_prefetch_chunk, no decode) in its 64-row bands' order, and the next --surface's while this one's net runs; render_rows' decodes
  then find them on disk. A hint only: a chunk not fetched yet the renderer reads itself, the same bytes. render_keys / render_init are
  render_rows' / run_surface's own chunk and level choice, shared with it.
- The unroll (inksdk's r3pre) runs one ink-ext per surface set with a shared `--cache $O/ink/ct.cache`, wraps in wrap order (decoded
  chunks stay resident across surfaces, --ct-mem 3 GB), so the prefetcher is on there by default.

| 5 consecutive wraps w035-w039, cold CT | wall |
|---|---|
| A: one process per wrap, no --cache (podink.sh) | 258.2 s |
| B: one process, --cache, --fetch-threads 0 | 140.1 s |
| C: one process, --cache, prefetcher (7982 chunks fetched ahead) | **86.3 s** (render 6.4-7.8 s a wrap, net 12.6-13.6 s: net-bound) |

Maps: A == B byte for byte; C differed by 1 on 0.7 % of the pixels, because the free device memory on the shared card made ink-ext's
automatic --batch 14 instead of 17 (the net's sums depend on the batch); C rerun with --batch 17 (and again after the rebase onto
da14d47f): byte-identical to A on all 5 (2) wraps. A fixed --batch in the unroll's R3X keeps the maps reproducible (told inksdk).

## The MX head conv at 3 blocks an SM: fields predict's conv1_mx_t_k -20 % (2026-11-17, branch convkc1v-20261117)

conv1_mx_t_k (the 1x1 head conv on MX-fp4 level-0 activations, GN+SiLU on load; u1 fields: 96 inputs, nine passes of 16 outputs) was
21.6 ms of a 0332 640 window's ~140 ms of kernels. ncu: ~5000 issued instructions a voxel for its 1536 FMAs (FFMA 37 %, LDS 10 %, MUFU
6 %, the rest per-channel bounds checks, branches and addressing), 89 registers -> 2 blocks of 256 an SM, 58 % issue slots, 1.1
eligible warps a scheduler.

- **conv1_mx_tv_k** (UFSM_C1_V=2, default; 1 the old kernel): full 32-channel blocks without the per-channel checks, and
  __launch_bounds__(256, 3) (85 registers, 24 warps an SM). Fields 0332 640 (nsys, 2 interleaved pairs): 21.6 -> 17.3 ms a window,
  kernel min-sum 142.9 -> 138.5 ms; fit-zarr outputs byte-identical (0 data files differ). 4 blocks an SM: 20.2 ms.
- V = 2 voxels a thread sharing each channel's weight loads (UFSM_C1_V=3): 204 registers, 8 warps an SM, 29.6 ms. Kept only as an option.
- The same chains (bias, ci in order, act_ab on the same decoded value): test_headz now compares the kernels bit for bit. It also gained
  96- and 48-channel level-0 cases (three full MX blocks; one full block and a tail). The trainer's head forward uses the same launcher,
  so it is byte-identical there too.
- **lat_ct_x8_k** (UFSM_LAT_CTX8=0 the old kernel; branch convkct-20261117): the guided head's z-scored CT planes at 8 voxels a thread
  (8-byte loads, 16-byte stores), the same expression. ncu had lat_ct_x_k at ~270 GB/s with one byte a thread. Fields 0332 640: 6.2 ->
  4.75 ms a window, 0 data files differ; test_lathead checks it against the host expression.
- **lat_pred_in_bas2_k** (UFSM_LAT_PIB2=0 the old kernel; branch convkpib-20261117): the --lat-basis input (29 projections of each
  cell's 64 z-scored CT values) with the basis in shared memory (float4 reads), the cell's CT as 16 4-byte rows and dyo / dxo once a
  plane. ncu: the old kernel issued ~12500 instructions a cell, 2077 global loads among them. Fields 0332 640: 8.5 -> 2.57 ms a window,
  0 data files differ. The first version differed on ~130 of 135 M values of the radial channel: the compiler contracted
  dy dy + dx dx the other way round (the old SASS: FMUL dx dx, FFMA dy dy +). The new kernel pins fma(dy, dy, dx dx) with
  __fmaf_rn / __fmul_rn. test_lat compares old and new bit for bit, but its 73 k-voxel case is too small to show a 1e-6 flip.
- **gn_prenorm_f4z_k at 6 blocks an SM** (GPZ_MINB; branch convkgpz-20261117): the slabbed GN+SiLU MX-fp4 copy of
  conv_fwd_f4v_k's input. ncu: 101 registers -> 2 blocks of 256, 29 % occupancy, 40 % issue slots, 25 % DRAM, so latency-bound.
  Fields 0332 640: 5.6 ms a window -> 4.06 / 3.37 / 3.16 / 3.03 at 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 blocks, 0 data files differ (register allocation
  only). The trainer's preslab path uses the same kernel.
- **up_fine_f4v_k at 4 blocks an SM** (UPF_MINB; branch convkupf-20261117): 99 registers -> 2 blocks, 31 % occupancy before.
  3.42 -> 2.69 ms a window (3 blocks 2.79, 6 blocks 3.12), 0 data files differ.
- Tried for the head conv, byte-identical but not kept: passes of 48 outputs instead of 16 in lp_conv1_fwd_mx_r. The 96 inputs are
  then decoded and GN+SiLU'd 3 times instead of 9, with the weights a float4 at a time. 17.6 -> 17.0 ms at 3 blocks of 128, 18.8 at 4,
  20.1 with all 48 weights in registers. The kernel is FMA / LDS issue-bound, not decode-bound. fma.rn.f32x2 (FFMA2) runs on sm_120 under
  mcc and is bit-identical to fmaf, but the microbenchmark peak is the same 11.3 TFMA/s: it saves issue slots only (~10 % ceiling here).

## reader3 ink-ext: the depth-fusion conv streamed over depth, conv_igemm at 2 blocks an SM (2026-11-17, branch convkx-20261117)

Profile (nsys, unrollperf's warm-cache PHerc1667 w035, 1012 tiles, card 1 shared): 9.6-15 s of kernels a wrap, the 128 x 128
conv_igemm ~1/3 (136 registers -> one 256-thread block an SM, 16 % warps active), k_dfc16 (the Reader's 16 -> 16 3x3x3 depth-fusion
conv with GN on load) ~1/5, k_gnpart + k_gn_apply ~1/7, k_dfc1 ~1/14, k_dattn ~1/20.

- **k_dfc16s** (UFSM_XNET_DF16=10, the new default; 1 the old halo kernel): a block owns a TY x TX column over the whole depth with
  a ring of three (TY + 2)(TX + 2) planes; plane z + 2 is fetched into registers before plane z's 27 taps and stored (GN-applied) over
  plane z - 1's slot after them. Reads and GN applies 2.66x -> 1.33x the outputs, smem 57 -> 46 KB (2 blocks an SM). Same tap order,
  MMAs and expressions: byte-identical (test_xmx dfs: 42 cases, plain and GN-in, ragged). XMX_DFBENCH 4 x 17 x 384^2 (best of 10,
  shared card): plain 6.35 -> 2.96 ms, GN-in 8.07 -> 3.45 ms (2.3x). Tilings 11-16 (4/8/16 rows, 2/4/8 warps) were slower.
- **conv_igemm minB 2** (XN_MINB, 8-warp tiles only): 128 registers, two blocks an SM. Byte-identical (register allocation only).
- In situ, ink-ext w035 with --batch 8 pinned, interleaved 3x against master's kernels (the card was shared, so per-kernel times are
  normalised by k_gnpart's in the same run): k_dfc16 2.55-2.61 -> 1.21-1.26 (2.1x), 128 x 128 conv_igemm 4.03-4.16 -> 3.11-3.28
  (-23 %); wraps byte-identical to master in every pair.
- ink-ext is not run-to-run byte-stable unpinned: the auto --batch follows free device memory (8 / 10 / 16 on the shared card) and
  two master runs at different batches differed on 270 k of 39 M pixels by 1 LSB; at a fixed batch every run is identical. A/Bs pin it.
- **k_dfc1x<2>** (UFSM_XNET_DF1=2, default; 1 the old k_dfc1): two x voxels a thread, each channel's 27 weights read as 7 float4
  into registers and fed to both FMA chains, the 16 outputs packed into half2 words. Same chains: byte-identical (test_xmx c1).
  XMX_DFBENCH 2.83 -> 1.75 ms (<4> 2.38); in situ (w035, batch 8, quiet card, 2 pairs) 0.81 -> 0.50 s a wrap, kernels 8.99 -> 8.6-8.7 s,
  0 px differ. The first x-blocked try (below) indexed its output array by a rolled channel loop and ran 2-3x slower.
- Tried and dropped (bench, byte-identical but not faster): the first k_dfc1 x-blocking (2.8 -> 6.7-8.3 ms, see above),
  k_gnpart with 4 rows' loads in flight + an 8-channel k_gn_apply (2.55 -> 2.52 ms). The GN kernels' reader3 time is ~8000 small
  launches on the 2-D levels (~0.12 ms each): fusing the apply into the next conv's loads (as gnin) is the remaining lever.
- **ink-ext batch independence** (branch convkgs-20261117; UFSM_XNET_GNOLD=1 the old path): xgn_stats split each sample into
  512 / n chunks, so each sample's partial sums, its GroupNorm statistics and its output followed the batch size. ink-ext's auto --batch
  follows free device memory, and two master runs at batch 8 / 16 differed on 267 k of 39.4 M px of the 1667 w035 wrap (max 1). Now 64
  chunks a sample whatever the batch, with the same kernels and speed (k_gnpart / k_gn_apply 1.13-1.24 in both). w035: two batch-8 runs
  and batch 16 are byte-identical (0 px). Against master at batch 8: 658 of 39.4 M px differ, by 1 code, so any pair AUC can move by
  at most ~2 x 658 / 39.4 M = 3e-5. test_xmx gnx checks that each sample's gm / rs are bit-equal alone and inside a batch (4 shapes).
  An exact-integer statistics version (fp16 values as integers in 64-bit limbs: any partition, any order) was also batch-independent,
  but k_gnpart took 2.5x as long (64-bit integer ops). It is not kept, but it is the form a fused igemm-epilogue version would need.
- Parked (branch convkgf-20261117): the GN statistics from the conv_igemm epilogue (xconv_fwd_gs). Per-128-row-block partials are
  reduced in a fixed order; it needs S % 128 == 0, so every block lies inside one sample at a fixed place, and it is used for reader3's
  bbd / rstem / dconv. Deterministic and batch-independent (w035 batch 8 x2 and 16: 0 px); 227 k of 39.4 M px differ by 1 from master.
  XMX_GSBENCH (conv + stats, N 8): 384^2 -19 %, 192^2 -12 %, 96^2 -8 %, 48^2 0 with float in-warp partials; double partials gave no
  gain. In situ (4 interleaved pairs on a shared, busy card) the GN+igemm share showed no gain beyond the noise, and float partials
  without a shift are less robust when mean >> std. Not worth a 0.6 % pixel change.
- Parked (branch convkwave-20261117): wave-aware tiles for > 64 outputs (128x128 / 128x64 / 64x64 / 64x32 picked by waves x
  occupancy x per-tile cost). ncu showed the 24^2 x 320 layer at 108 blocks on 72 slots (1.5 waves, tensor pipe 77 % active) and 12^2
  at 27 blocks; XMX_IGBENCH: 24^2 -11 %, 12^2 -29 %, 12^2 x 1280 -25 %, byte-identical, but those layers are ~10 % of conv_igemm and
  the in-situ A/B (3 pairs, normalised by k_gnpart) showed no gain beyond the +-3 % noise of the shared card.
- GN kernels are at the memory roofline (ncu in situ: k_gn_apply 80-92 % of memory throughput, the large k_gnpart ~69 %). Parked
  (branch convkgn-20261117): the first GN of each Reader residual block applied inside c2's conv_igemm A staging (in place in smem after
  cp.async, k_gn_apply's expression): byte-identical (test_xmx gna, w035 0 px), k_gn_apply -30 %, but conv_igemm +23 %: a 3x3 conv
  stages every input 9 times (K = 9 Ci), so the apply runs 9x. A register-path (ld.global + transform + st.shared) form was the same.
  Left: the stats as deterministic per-block partials in the producer's epilogue (a different summation order: near-identical).
## Production ink = reader3 (INKMODE=r3, the default); inkpod parked: memorisation, not labels (2026-11-17, branch inkr3-20261117)

User decision 11-17: the latent ink head (inkpod) is not used in production until it is retrained. On the 1667 held-out regions it
scores 0.58 against reader3's 0.858 (previous section). The unroll's ink is now reader3, applied to our own renders:
- `scripts/unroll/r3ink.sh SURFDIR OUT.tif CT.tif` replaces a render's ink image with ink-ext on the same surface. ink-ext's canvas
  is the render's grid, (w-1)/scale+1. The result is then gated by the filled CT: `img-gate --min T` binarises the gate image at
  T = R3GATE, default FILLCT 80, so the output is 0 where CT < T. R3W picks the checkpoint (a,b = ensemble; argus2 runs as
  `--model reader3`), R3MODEL the port.
- One ink-ext call per surface set (`r3pre`): all stripes before the strip mosaic, and every per-wrap surface in wrap order between
  perwrap's render pass and its finisher pass, with one shared `--cache $O/ink/ct.cache` (unrollperf's fetch threads switch on by
  themselves with --cache and a remote CT). r3ink.sh picks up the precomputed `R3PRE/<name>_<model>.tif`, and a missed surface
  falls back to its own call.
  1667 w035 + w042 e2e (desk card 1, local CT levels 2-5): perwrap 75 -> 40 s; the net 39 -> 85 tiles/s with the warm shared
  cache; the same mean (0.305 on w042).
- The `ink` / `inkcal` stages are no-ops under r3, so the latent ink predict and its calibration no longer run. The `INKMODE=lat`
  (latink / inkpod) and `ift3` modes are kept behind the flag. The pod's unroll.sh defaults to r3, and setup.sh fetches reader-v3
  at its pinned HF revision (sha256 checked).
- ink-ext skips CT levels that are missing (the unroll's local CT holds levels 2-5 only). It reads the coarsest present level
  <= 1.05 x the model's spacing, else the finest present one.

**Why inkpod does not transfer (diagnosis for the retrain).** 1667 scored on our wraps, 2-D surface AUC, 40 um tolerance:
| map | training regions | held-out |
|---|---|---|
| reader3 | 0.839 | 0.858 |
| inkpod | 0.84 | 0.582 |
- The held-out regions are not harder (reader3 scores higher there), so 1667 is not a data floor at 9.6 um.
- The 3-D targets are correctly registered. The splat (inkgt/gt PHerc1667.zarr 9.596, `render --known --depth 3`) rendered on the
  17 labelled wraps has, inside the held-out regions, 95.4 % of its positives on human 2-D ink and a recall of 0.25 (open-face band
  only); as a ranking map it scores AUC 0.62, because it is sparse.
- The holdouts were honest (holdouts-ink.json boxes + the validation rasters of 35 of the 39 1667 segments).
- The gap is memorisation. Positive ink supervision came only from human labels on 144 segments (37 % of the windows), with
  replay 3 over 15k+ steps of P 1024 windows. Also fstem-drop 0.25 on ink windows (predict always runs the stem), training mostly
  at the 4.8 um rung while production reads 9.6, and no held-out validation in the trainer.
- Retrain plan, sent to the lead before any launch:
  - ink-teach soft targets from reader3 + ink9um on all segments and on our unroll wraps;
  - holdouts-20261118;
  - fstem-drop 0, ink-radial-drop 0.15, ink-mil-r-um 50, replay 1, rungs weighted to 9.6, a per-scroll human weight cap;
  - held-out 2-D AUC every 1000 steps, early stop;
  - a 2-arm 3k-step smoke (human vs human + teacher) on the RTX PRO 4000 pod.

## lat_heads_tc_k: predict's heads with a tensor-core stem, 2.4x (2026-11-17, branch convklh-20261117)

lat_heads_k (nn_lat_heads_place, predict --heads) was 31 % of the ink recipe's kernel time: 37.5 ms of 121.9 per window on the 0332 set.
ncu on one window: 41.0 ms at 255 registers, 8 % of warps active, issue active 17.5 %. Without the stem (timing only) it ran 26.0 ms, so
the stem was 15.0 ms and the rest was latency.

lat_heads_tc_k (UFSM_LATHEADS_TC, default 1; 0 = lat_heads_k):
- A block of 128 threads takes a row of 32 cells. It stages the CT taps of the row's 4 x 64 stem blocks once in shared memory (36 rows,
  fp16, z-scored as nn_lat_ct_x).
- pre = W1 taps runs per 8-block n-tile with mma m16n8k16, with fstem_fwd_k's scaled fp16 W1 fragments, k-steps and B pairs. pre and
  h = silu(pre / scale + b1) are therefore the bits nn_fstem_fwd produces in the slab composition.
- h goes into shared memory over the dead tap rows: 18 KB, 5 blocks an SM.
- Thread (lane = cell, warp = z quarter) then does its 16 voxels per head with lat_heads_k's arithmetic (the W2 . h projection c
  ascending as fstem's, the fp16 adds, the rv fusion, the byte).
- __launch_bounds__(128, 5): 96 registers.

| registers (ncu, 0332 window) | ms |
|---|---|
| 150 (smem-limited to 3 blocks) | 20.1 |
| 128 | 17.0 |
| 96 (some spills) | 16.9 |
| 80 | 18.5 |

Bytes:
- test_lathead: byte-identical to the slab composition (lat_up + shuffle + nn_fstem_fwd + place). Against lat_heads_k, whose fp32 stem
  sums run in another order: 14 of 12.3 M bytes differ, all by 1.
- PHerc1667 1024^3 level-2 box (inkpod 15000), against lat_heads_k:

  | head | voxels that differ (of 1.07 G) |
  |---|---|
  | ink | 434 |
  | c12 | 1353 |
  | c13 | 1151 |

  All differ by 1; the means are unchanged.

Ink recipe (0332, 32 windows, interleaved twice, the same binary at TC 0 / 1): 112.8 / 112.8 -> 91.4 / 90.6 ms per window (-19 %),
lat_heads 37.5 -> 15.4-16.2 ms. Fields does not run this kernel.

## recto-sp: the profile kernel in short launches, the helper's streams first (PHerc Paris 4's 1532 s; same codes; 2026-11-17, branch rectosp-20261117)

Paris 4 on the pod (RTX PRO 6000, try9-6250 unroll): recto-sp 1521 s, 25.5k CPU s, against 0332 83 s and 1667 103 s. Its box is 8x 1667's
(629 M cells against 62 M; 149 blocks of 4.2 M cells). From its log: 813 s on the blocks (kernel 799) + 698 s waiting for the helper = the
wall; the helper's source 1508 s for 166k non-fill chunks (7066 on the GPU decoder, 158871 on the host). Host decode and https are not it:
on the desk 10 ms CPU a chunk (ufsm read, 1 thread), 1024 cold chunks in 4 s (8 threads). The cause: k_rsp's grid is sized to the
resident blocks, so a launch holds every SM until the block's last cell (5.4 s on P4); every chunk the helper puts into the ring (host
or GPU decoded) is a gather kernel (nn_ctw_put) on another stream and waited for it, the 43 workers spinning in their syncs (the CPU s).
The helper and the kernel ran one after the other instead of side by side.

- rsg_run launches the cells in slices of UFSM_RECTOSP_SLICE (32) cells per resident warp (~100 ms on the pod's P4 blocks; 0: one
  launch); the ring upload / memset stream and the chunk workers' streams (nn_ctw_new_prio) at the device's greatest priority, k_rsp's
  at the least, so between launches the helper's work goes first. The cells are independent: the same codes (test_recto_gpu, also with
  UFSM_RECTOSP_SLICE=1; the A/B's sp / rsp shard files md5-equal).
- Desk A/B (card 1 shared, desk load 50-70, 1667-u1 fields 4635 x 1568 x 1616, warm m7 cache, 8 threads; interleaved 0 / 32 / 0 / 32):
  wall 99.0 / 83.0 / 106.1 / 105.4 s; waiting for the helper 29.3 / 25.9 / 37.0 / 32.3 s; kernel 18.7 / 20.4 / 16.8 / 19.6 s; chunks
  on the GPU decoder 1465 / 11876 / 1161 / 13136 (of ~17.8k non-fill): the decoder's gathers no longer wait for the kernel. On the desk
  the 1667 kernel is short (0.25 s a block) so the wall moves within the noise; the P4 case (5.4 s blocks) is the one it is for:
  expected ~1521 -> ~850 s (the kernel's 813), not measured (needs a big-card pod: the 28 GB ring does not fit a 5060 Ti).
- Open: the kernel's cost per cell, 1.27 us on P4 against 0.10 us on 1667 (pod), with similar source density (m7 nonzero 55-75 % vs
  37-67 %), the same n (335 samples) and flags. Suspect the 28 GB ring against 5.5 GB (TLB / L2 reach of the trilinear gathers); a
  ring-size experiment waits for a big-card pod.

## The stride-2 fp8 down conv: one block for every output channel plus a prenorm pass, 2.1x (2026-11-17, branch convks2-20261117)

conv_fwd_s2_f8_k (the 96 / 128 / 160-wide nets' down convs: predict, and the training forward) was staging-bound.
- A block of 64 outputs (2 z x 4 y x 8 x) took one 32- or 64-row output tile: Cop 96 -> MT 2, three tiles.
- So each tile re-staged its 765 input positions x 32 channels: decode, GN + SiLU, the block amax, e4m3. That is about 1,150 instructions
  a thread per chunk against about 200 for the 27 x MT MMAs.
- ncu, the fields window's 96 -> 96 160^3 -> 80^3 conv: 15.9 ms, 8 % tensor pipe.

Two changes:
- UFSM_S2_WIDE (default 1): MT 6 / 8 / 10 for 96 / 192, multiples of 128 and 160 outputs, so every output channel sits in one block and the
  input is staged once. Three taps a weight round keep two blocks an SM.
- UFSM_S2_PRE (default 1, with the wide tiles, not under a trainer's sealed memory plan, at most a quarter of the free memory):
  s2_prenorm_k writes the GN input once as an MX-fp8 tensor with the bytes and scales the staging would form. The kernel then copies it
  (TY: the output type stays MX-fp4).

Per output the MMAs and their order are unchanged, so the bytes are identical: test_s2wide covers 96 / 128 / 160 / 192 / 256 outputs with
and without GN and partial tiles, and the fields and ink predict outputs are byte-identical.

| ncu, fields window | old | wide | wide + prenorm |
|---|---|---|---|
| 96 -> 96 160^3 | 15.9 | 8.4 | 1.6 + 5.4 |
| 128 | 2.16 | 1.57 | 0.26 + 1.11 |
| 160 | 0.88 | 0.47 | 0.04 + 0.35 |

Predict, 0332, 32 windows, interleaved, full-key ksum:
- fields: down convs 17.5 -> 8.2 ms per window; kernel time 151.0 / 151.0 -> 142.3 / 140.9 (-6.2 %).
- ink: 11.8 -> 5.4 ms; 113.3 -> 106.9 (-5.6 %).

Also tried: predict's cell head (144 outputs from 96 channels, conv1_mx_t_k in 9 passes of 16) on constant-bank weights, 48 outputs a
pass (conv1_mx_cn_k, branch convkc1-20261117). It is bit-identical but slower: 21.7 -> 25.6 ms per window, since the 18 KB of weights
overflow the constant cache, and 16 outputs a pass is no faster (ncu). Parked.
## test_unet~narrow's pod fault: a stale lean-2 plan flag in the fp32 rebuild (2026-11-17, branch narrow-nob-20261117)

test_unet~narrow (P 32, MX-fp8 activations and gradients, lean 2, chunked up part) failed 3/3 on the RTX PRO 6000 and 2/2 on the PRO
4000 pods (illegal address, then "gn_dsums: cudaMalloc") and passed on the desk. Not the pod's JIT: with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
MCUDA_TRACE=1 the first faulting launch is conv_fwd_k<3, 1, 4> (the fp32 backward-data conv), whose SASS on the pod is identical
to the desk's. A probe of each buffer's driver allocation (cuMemGetAddressRange) against the bytes the kernel touches found it on
the desk too: in the nn_set_tf32(0) whole-network gradient pass, four decoder convs wrote their concat gradient (96 / 160 / 160 / 96
channels) into 32 / 64 / 96 / 64-channel buffers (12.6 MB into 4.2 MB at level 0). build_acts' tensor-core gradient plan sets u->nob
(lean 2: no B buffer, block_bwd writes the input gradient in place over gy) and free_acts never reset it, so the fp32 rebuild, which
gives every level its own full-width gA / gB, still ran block_bwd's in-place branch. On the desk the overrun landed in mapped
memory (silently: the fp32 reference gradient itself was off; rel L2 vs tensor cores 0.276 -> 0.264 once fixed), on the pods past
the mapping. memcheck had not seen it (the overrun stays inside pooled allocations). Fix: free_acts resets nob (and gA_bytes) with
the other plan flags. Pod PRO 4000: 2/2 pass. Only a rebuild that leaves the tensor-core plan for the fp32 one is affected (tests;
training never switches nn_set_tf32).
## Predict fields: the fused fstem_up (default after trainperf's fix, -3.5 % of its kernels); 1152 windows no GPU gain; writer pool; DF16 v7 (2026-11-17, branch fsup-20261117)

**Fused head slab.** trainperf's nn_fstem_up_fwd_t (fp32 cells) does up-slab + sub-cell shuffle + fine stem in one kernel. It is wired into
predict's plane path (fzA and the winding pair fzB) and gives byte-identical fit stores at 640/64 and 1152/64. nsys kernel minima (u1 13000,
0332 box, 640/64, ms per window; ksum.py, card shared with a wbench job, so minima only):

| arm | fstem_fwd_k | lat_up4_k | lat_shuf_k | sum | all kernels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| three kernels (default) | 33.2 | 17.6 | 9.0 | 59.8 | 141.5 |
| all 11 planes fused (zero W2 rows for 2-8) | 71.8 | - | - | 71.8 | 154.8 |
| stem planes fused, planes 2-8 plain up-slab | 54.4 | 8.7 | - | 63.1 | 146.1 |

The fused instance runs at 95 registers + 6.3 KB dynamic shared memory against the plain one's 62 (`__launch_bounds__(FS_BT, 1)` for UP),
6.43 against 3.57 ms for the same 63360-block launch, which outweighs the up-slab and shuffle passes it saves. So it stays opt-in
(UFSM_PRED_FSUP=1, the hybrid split) until the kernel's occupancy is fixed. It was not occupancy: trainperf's bc55ce95 (fsu_row picked its
upsampling weights by bx & 1, a divergent branch in every warp; now by index, cell type templated, 32-bit offsets; 95 -> 78 registers)
gives, on the same recipe: the three kernels 33.1 + 17.5 + 9.0 = 59.6, the hybrid 49.2 + 8.3 = 57.5 (-3.5 %), all kernels 125.9 -> 124.2
ms per window, byte-identical. The hybrid is the default now (UFSM_PRED_FSUP=0: the three kernels); lat_shuf_k is gone from the fields path.

**1152 against 640 fields windows, quiet card** (master 442668dd, same box, x2): 640/64 32 tiles, gpu(fwd+d2h) 9.09 / 9.17 s, main wall
9.6 / 9.5 s, RSS 4 GB; 1152/64 4 tiles, gpu 9.34 / 9.20 s, main wall 13.7 / 11.1 s (the fit writer drains the last slabs after only 4
windows), RSS 14 GB. With --skip-empty, 640 drops air in finer pieces, which eats the halo saving (1.95x -> 1.42x on paper): no GPU gain on
this box. The "-15 %" in the predfwd section was a contended number. 1152 needs nearly the whole 16 GB, so any other process on the card OOMs it.

**Head writer pool (unrollperf's a923e259), 0332 ink, 544/16, q 0, 3 heads, x2:** byte-identical; writer-wait 3.42 / 2.59 -> 0.31 / 0.09 s,
main wall 11.6 / 11.8 -> 10.7 / 11.0 s (-7 %). gpu(fwd+d2h) rises 1.5 s while the pool compresses beside the forward.

## mcc 5744025: thread-block clusters (__cluster_dims__); live-range splitting at calls (2026-11-17, branch mcc-rasplit-20261117)

**Clusters** (for convk's fp4 wgrad: the 8 co-tile CTAs of one ci tile stage x once instead of 8 times; x staging is 85 % of
conv_bwd_w_f4ws_k's instructions). `__cluster_dims__(x, y, z)` on a kernel (template instances included) is PTX
`.reqnctapercluster x, y, z` on its .entry for sm_90 on, and nothing on ARCH=86. A plain `<<<>>>` (mcudahw's cuLaunchKernel)
takes the shape from the kernel. The cluster operations are inline asm (mapa, st / ld.shared::cluster, barrier.cluster,
fence.acq_rel.cluster, %cluster_ctarank / %cluster_nctarank; st.async ... mbarrier::complete_tx, mbarrier init / expect_tx /
remote arrive / try_wait in a braced label loop), which mcc passes through. src/nn_cluster.cu + tests/test_cluster.c (gpu, smoke)
on the desk's sm_120 card: clusters of 1 x 1 x N, N = 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 (convk: the card's 3 GPCs of 12 SMs hold 36 one-CTA-per-SM blocks in
clusters of those, 8 only 24), 512 B and 90 KB of dynamic shared memory; each block writes into its neighbour's shared memory
(st.shared::cluster, and st.async completing on the receiver's mbarrier, then every block arrives on each member's barrier
remotely) and reads back what its predecessor wrote: 0 wrong words in all 16 cases. The ARCH=86 compile leaves out the cluster
code and the directive (test SKIP there). All 169 other units' PTX is unchanged.

**Live-range splitting at calls.** Every xmm register is caller-saved on x86-64, so ra.c (linear scan, no splitting) kept each
float that lives across a call in a stack slot all its life, every read a load. Long float functions that call libm (fit_vox2:
sincosf / logf / atan2f, 540 of 1574 instructions on the stack) paid that on each use. After the first allocation (beside the
loop splits), a spilled register read at least twice in a call-free run of a block and not written there gets one copy before
the run's first read; the run's reads use it. MCC_NOSPLITCALL=1: off; MCC_SPLITCALLMAX=N: the first N copies (bisecting).

| paired A/B, 120 single-thread CPU suite lines, same ufsm source | cycles | geomean | instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16cd2b7 then call splits | -1.01 % | 0.988 | -0.13 % |
| call splits then 16cd2b7 (the old one second) | +2.15 % for the old | 1.012 | +0.05 % |

Instructions hardly move (stack loads become register reads, copies are added); the gain is in cycles. (Measured before the
slot-alias guard below, which only adds a move where a split copy's original shared its slot.)

The first version miscompiled ufsm (the fast tier caught it: test_replay_lean SIGSEGV in nn_w4.cu's cpu_runs, `runs + a` NULL).
A split copy that gets no register is given the original's stack slot (the loop splits' rule: the same value through the run).
But once the original's range ends at the copy, move coalescing may put a register written in the run on that place: here the
loop counter's next value (a + 1, moved back into a's phi), so the copy read a + 1. Bisected with MCC_SPLITCALLMAX to copy 94 of
109 in that unit. Now the slot alias needs the original to be the slot's only register (the same guard covers the loop splits'
copies). Two more lessons: a first A/B showed -5 % cycles because its baseline was built from an older ufsm tree (volcomp's faster
lossless encoder came in between): rebuild both sides of an A/B from one source. And cpu_pair.sh does not check exit codes:
the fast tier is the gate, not the timing run.
