## Predict forward: where the GPU time goes; the fit-field head per z chunk (1152 / 64 fields windows on a 16 GB card) (2026-11-17, branch predfwd-20261117)

Profile on a quiet card 1 (0332 level 2, CT from a local cache, 32 windows; `UFSM_PRED_PROF`, `UFSM_PTICK`, nsys per-(kernel, grid, block)
minima x count, /vesuvius/ufsm/predfwd/win.sh):

| recipe | wall | GPU (fwd + d2h) | other | kernel min-sum / window | top kernels / window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ink (inkpod 15000, 544 / 16, heads ink c12 c13, q 0) | 8.55 s | 4.99 s | writer-wait 3.17 s | 128 ms | conv_fwd_f4_k 52.5, lat_heads_k 37.7, conv1_mx_t_k 14.6, conv_fwd_s2_f8_k 11.8 |
| fields (u1 13000, 640 / 64, --fit-zarr, fit-h 2) | 9.3 s | 9.02 s | | 175 ms | fstem_fwd_k 55.8, conv_fwd_f4_k 28.3, conv1_mx_t_k 23.4, lat_up4_k 17.7, conv_fwd_s2_f8_k 17.4 |

- Ink on a quiet card is bound by its writers, not the GPU: three single-thread q 0 head writers, 20.5 thread-seconds for 96 shards
  (~6.8 s each against 5 s of GPU). The earlier "GPU-bound, 11 of 12.7 s" was a shared card. More writer threads per head: ~-38 % wall
  (unrollperf's codec / writer area).
- Fields per window (ptick, 284 ms): trunk 134, the fit path 127 (winding mod 4 46, fine stem 26, upsample + shuffle 23, before the chunk 23).
  fstem_fwd_k is trainperf's kernel (also the training head); predict reuses its fix.
- Halo overhead: fields 640 / 64 compute (640 / 512)^3 = 1.95 voxels per kept voxel, 1152 / 64 1.42; ink 544 / 16 1.20, and its two grids
  double that (the latink A/B decides the second grid).

**1152 fields windows did not fit a 16 GB card** (`cudaMalloc of 13.76 GB`, unet.c build_acts): the whole window's fp32 cell logits,
288^3 cells x 144 outputs x 4 B, which the fit path reads per z chunk anyway; the activations at 1152 are ~3.3 GB. Change: with --fit-zarr's
plane path (fzs, not the fused fit-h 8 kernel) the build holds no logits (`unet_set_head_infer_z`) and the 1^3 head runs per chunk
(`unet_head_fwd_z32`) on the cell planes the chunk reads (its planes, the winding pair's +-d, +-1 cell of upsampling taps) into a held-plane
buffer that the `_c` upsample / shuffle kernels read (q0 / qd). Two buffers: the overlap with the previous chunk is one pitched copy, the new
planes are written in place (`conv1_mx_t_k` plane stride Ly), so each cell plane's head runs once. The head is the same kernel instantiation
with a voxel range: bit-identical (test_headz: couts 32 / 11 / 144, ranges incl. into a wider plane stride; 0332 640 / 64 fields zarr
byte-identical, diff -r). Cost at 640 (nsys minima per full launch configuration: kernel, grid x y z, block, dynamic smem, registers):
kernels 182.2 + copies 35.1 ms per window vs 188.0 + 31.3 with the whole-window head (the first version's 144 per-channel copies per chunk
cost +31 ms a window). (ksum.py grouped by grid product + block before convk's note 11-17: same-grid launches of one kernel with different
specialisations shared a minimum, undercounting the slower ones; the figures here are rescored.) 1152 / 64 now runs on the 16 GB card, 7.2 GB free after the
first window; GPU 9.23 s for the 1024 x 2048^2 box (4 windows) vs 10.81 s at 640 (32 windows), one other app on the card: about -15 %
(the trunk's 27 % fewer computed voxels, the fit path unchanged). Host RSS 14.6 GB at 1152 (16 pinned shard buffers). UFSM_PRED_HEADZ=0:
the whole-window logits.

Also measured: convk's conv_fwd_f4v_k (UFSM_F4V) on both predict recipes, byte-identical outputs throughout. 71ef14b2 lost (its GN convs
ran in-kernel GN staging: predict's level-0 convs are z-range slabs, which the prenorm copy excluded); 32ba38cb (z-range prenorm) and
ce3b6778 (the prenorm masked under --skip-empty) win, full-key minima per window F4V 0 -> 1: fields 189.3 -> 182.4 ms (-3.6 %), ink
149.9 -> 139.5 (-6.9 %); the fp4 convs + prenorm alone fields 38.7 -> 34.3, ink 73.3 -> 63.1 (run-to-run noise on the shared card ~+-2 %).
Ink teachers on the same quiet window: see the 2026-11-16 section (ink9um 1667 segment fp16 old 163.7 s, fused 127.9, MX5 100.9, pick 116.0).

## conv_fwd_f4v_k: the MX-fp4 3^3 conv at ~70 % of the MMA peak, bit-identical (2026-11-17, branch convk-20261117)

**Diagnosis** (ncu works on the desk under mcudahw: bench_sp24, card 1). conv_fwd_f4_k<4, 2> at L0 (32 x 256^2 x 256, fwd after the
prenorm): tensor pipe 46 % of peak, issue slots 23 % busy (IPC 0.92), 4 warps a scheduler with 0.38 eligible. Latency-bound, not
issue-bound as read on 11-14. LP_MINB(2) caps it at 128 registers, so it spills (116 M LDL + 116 M STL a call: 55 % of the L1
sectors, 56 % of the L2 traffic), and long_scoreboard is the top stall. The weight stage gathers 16 B per 32 B sector, with 279 M
ldgsts bank conflicts. The input staging sits behind barriers with nothing in flight.

**Kernel** (src/lp_f4v.cu). The MMA core and the per-accumulator order are unchanged: f4r_mma_grp's 4-row path with the
mma_f4_sel scale selectors.
- One block an SM: 233-255 registers, no spills, 67 KB smem.
- A 16 x 8 x 4 output tile: 64 rows x 4 rows of 16 voxels a warp. A staged byte feeds 2x the MMAs, and the halo is 1080 positions
  for 512 voxels (was 720 for 256).
- The input tile is double-buffered by cp.async: 16 B rows, zero-filled when outside or masked. Its scale bytes go through
  registers.
- The weights are re-laid out once a call (prep_w4v_k into lp_buf u8 slots 0 / 1: [co block][chunk][pair][64][32 B], with the sw16
  swizzle and the scale pairs pre-built). Each 7-pair stage is then one contiguous 15 KB copy, double-buffered.
- The statistics epilogue (f4v_epi_st) keeps each 2-plane half's sums apart and adds them in conv_fwd_f4_k's warp order, so the GN
  statistics come out bit-identical too.
- GN+SiLU staging (template G): the rows land by cp.async, then each thread transforms its own positions one stage later. Bit-exact,
  but not overlapped with the MMAs: L0 50 ms vs 29 ms copy-staged.

**Coverage, via slabs** (UFSM_F4V_DEBUG=N prints each call's kernel and reason). try9 also had two other cases on the old kernel.
Its L0 GN trunk convs used the in-kernel GN, because the plan's GroupNorm copy budget is 0.15 GB and the layer needs 963 MB. All
four decoder conv1s are split inputs with the fused upsample and per-segment GNs. Both now run by z slabs that fit the budget:
- lp_f4v_preslab: gn_prenorm_f4z_k per slab, then the copy-staged conv on the output z-window, with the slab as a z-range input.
- lp_f4v_preup: per slab, the coarse rows once (up_coarse_f4v_k = f4ru_coarse), the up part at full resolution (up_fine_f4v_k =
  f4ru_blend plus the e2m1 requantisation), the skip part prenormed, then the split conv.
Every staged byte is the old staging's, so outputs and statistics are the same bits.
Still on conv_fwd_f4_k: Cip <= 64 (the ring kernels take those before the hook), statistics with a 2-plane conv_fwd_f4_k tile and
W % 16 != 0, slab-local GN, staging SR, ARCH=86.

**MT 2, the default.** The first kernel had MT 4 (64 rows) and so needed Cop % 64 == 0. That left the 96 / 160-wide predict nets
(u1, inkpod) on the old kernel, and fp4teach's predict A/B showed no gain.
- MT 2 is 32 rows a block with 4 weight stages a chunk (pairs [0, 4) [4, 7) [7, 11) [11, 14): the same pairs in the same order).
  That makes 46 KB and 128 registers, so two blocks fit an SM and one block's prologue / epilogue overlaps the other's MMAs.
- It beats MT 4 at every width, so it is the default (UFSM_F4V_MT=4 keeps MT 4).
- At short K (96 inputs: 3 chunks) MT 4 sat at 53 % tensor. ncu put ~20 % of its stall samples in the epilogue, with no other
  block to cover it.
- Statistics: each block reproduces the conv_fwd_f4_k block of its voxels. The per-channel sums depend on the block's voxels and
  warp order, not its channel count. conv_fwd_f4_k runs MT 4 at TZ 2 (Cop % 64 == 0), else MT 2 at TZ 4 (depth >= 16) or TZ 2.
  So f4v_epi_st (2-plane halves) is used when that tile is 2 planes deep, else the plain epilogue.
- 11 more test_f4v cases (96 / 160 / 288 outputs), all byte-equal with UFSM_F4V_MT=0 and 4.
- A tried variant: storing the scale bytes at issue removes MT 2's remaining spills (42 M LDL a call at L0) but stalls on the load:
  29.1 vs 28.0 ms (F4V_SDIRECT, off).
- Mixed MT 4 + an MT 2 tail for 96 / 160 was slower than all-MT 2: 1.90 / 0.85 ms vs 1.72 / 0.55.

| case (ncu, GN + stats unless noted) | conv_fwd_f4_k ms | MT 4 ms | MT 2 ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| 96 -> 96 32 x 160^2 (u1 / inkpod level 0) | 2.16 | 1.90 (with a 32-row tail) | 1.72 |
| 160 -> 160 40^3 | 0.72 | 0.85 (with a tail) | 0.55 |
| 128 -> 128 64 x 80^2 | 2.00 | 1.51 | 1.46 |
| L0 256 -> 256 32 x 256^2, bdata | 42.2 | 30.7 | 28.0 (69.5 % tensor) |
| L1 320 -> 320 32 x 128^2, bdata | 16.5 | 11.6 | 10.5 |

**Predict.** fp4teach's A/B (0332, fields u1 640/64 with --skip-empty, ink inkpod 544/16, 32 windows, nsys kernel minima) first showed
+5.5 / +12.5 % with F4V on. Four findings:
- Predict's level-0 convs run as unet's in-place z-slabs (nn_set_zrange: sp.zi0 / sp.Di), which the prenorm copy excludes. Their
  GroupNorm inputs ran f4v's in-kernel GN staging, which loses to conv_fwd_f4_k's (ncu 96 -> 96 64 x 160^2 7.86 vs 6.89 ms).
  lp_f4v_preslab now takes z-range / z-window inputs: it prenorms only the planes each slab reads, then copy-stages the conv
  (6.90 -> 4.26 ms prenorm included). The G staging runs only at UFSM_F4V=2 (tests).
- The remaining "+2.9 / +4.4 %" was a measurement artefact. ksum.py took per-(kernel, grid product, block) minima, and the fast GN
  convs and slow fused-upsample conv1s of conv_fwd_f4_k share grids. In the F4V=0 run the up calls were charged at the GN calls'
  minimum; with F4V=1 they stood alone. The key now includes the grid dimensions, dynamic smem and registers.
- Under --skip-empty the prenorm ran dense. gn_prenorm_f4z_k now skips every voxel the conv does not stage: outside the 3^3 halo of
  an active output tile, or masked out of the input. test_skip_empty with forced slabs gives the F4V=0 logits.
- Result, ce3b6778, full key, outputs byte-identical:

| recipe | F4V=0 ms/window | F4V=1 ms/window | change | fp4 convs + prenorm | GPU busy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fields | 189.3 | 182.4 | -3.6 % | 38.7 -> 34.3 | 271.6 -> 258.1 |
| ink | 149.9 | 139.5 | -6.9 % | 73.3 -> 63.1 | 323.4 -> 205.2 |

(Run-to-run noise on the shared card is about +-2 %.) The fused-upsample conv1s still run conv_fwd_f4_k in predict: they get the
z-range too, and lp_f4v_preup refuses it.

**sparse24 on top.** bench_sp24 (wall clock, shared card 1), dense vs 2:4-sparse conv:
- against conv_fwd_f4_k the sparse kernels win 1.24-3.35x;
- against conv_fwd_f4v_k they win 1.06-1.08x at L0, 1.03-1.04x at L1, 1.02-1.03x at L2, 1.03-1.10x at L3, before their masking
  costs.
So --sparse24 mode 3, which changes results, no longer pays.

**Weight gradient** (conv_bwd_w_f4ws_k, bench_wgl0 128^3 256 -> 256, ncu):
- 21.5-22.4 ms, tensor 29 %, issue 57 %, no spills. 85 % of the instructions are the producers' x staging (decode, GN + SiLU with
  3 MUFU, two requantisations), repeated for each co tile (8x at Co 256).
- Dropping the bf16 round trip from the LY 1 decode is exact for MX inputs: 22.4 -> 21.9 ms.
- UFSM_F4W_MT4=1 (64 co x 8 ci tiles): 21.5 -> 20.3 ms. The LY 1 lanes then sit on 6 of the 11 producer warps.
- Ceiling with the staging stubbed out: 12.4 ms (52 % tensor).
- An x pre-pass into LY 1 records would move ~9.5 GB per call (~450 B per plane, channel and tile, read once per co tile): ~21 ms
  of DRAM time, so no gain.
- Predict's decoder conv1s (2026-11-17, branch convkup-20261117): lp_f4v_preup now takes the z-range / z-window inputs of unet's in-place
  decoder slabs, which before fell back to the old kernel (90 calls a window in fields). The slabs walk the output window [zw0, zw1). The
  fine input planes are a = max(z0 + zi0 - 1, 0) .. min(z1 + zi0 + 1, Di), the coarse ones are in the Di / 2 numbering, and the skip
  prenorm's mask offset is a - zi0. test_f4v has 3 new run_up cases (z-range, z-range + z-window, z-window); they are byte-equal,
  statistics included.
  - fp4teach, 0332, 32 windows, both UFSM_F4V=1, interleaved twice, full-key ksum, outputs byte-identical (ms per window):

    | recipe | master | convkup | change |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | fields | 177.0 / 175.6 | 170.1 / 168.8 | -3.9 % |
    | ink | 138.5 / 138.8 | 121.9 | -12 % |

  - Busy time: fields 243 -> 218 ms, ink 142 -> 129.
  - Fields choice log: conv_fwd_f4v_k calls 72 -> 95.
- Statistics at W % 16 (2026-11-17, branch convkw16-20261117). The shape gate refused statistics at widths that are not multiples of 16.
  Predict ink's windows (544: level widths 136 / 68) therefore ran their GN z-range, fused-upsample and plain convs on the old kernel.
  - At such widths conv_fwd_f4_k writes its output per lane (fwd_epilogue's last path), and its sums run per lane: the 2 rows, the x pairs,
    v0 then v1, then the xor-1 and xor-2 shuffles, then old warp by old warp.
  - The new kernel now calls fwd_epilogue<NOST>: the output and the stored_stats rewrite of acc, but not its statistics. f4v_st_pl then forms
    each old warp's per-lane sums from its half of this warp's 4 rows, and f4v_epi_st's ordered tail adds them.
  - Tests: 6 new test_f4v cases (W 36 / 40 / 37 / 68, stored stats, GN z-range, fused upsample), byte- and stats-equal.
  - Ink predict (0332, 32 windows, interleaved twice, convk's runs on card 1): 121.5 / 121.6 -> 112.2 / 112.5 ms per window (-7.6 %), busy
    128.8 -> 121.3. The old kernel's 18.6 ms is gone. Data shards byte-identical.
  - Fields: 172.2 -> 167.9 ms (one run each, a foreign process on the card), byte-identical.
- Clusters, tried and parked (branch convkw-20261117, conv_bwd_w_f4wc_k, nvcc build, bit-equal to the plain kernel in test_f4wc):
  the CL co tiles of a (1, 1, CL) cluster share one x staging.
  - Each block stages every CL-th LY 1 group and bulk-copies its 432 B slot to the others (cp.async.bulk shared::cluster with
    complete_tx on their FULL mbarrier; scale pairs by u32 st.async). EMPTY counts all blocks' consumers.
  - CL 4 splits each row over two lanes.
  - A first version used per-row st.shared::cluster + fence.acq_rel.cluster: the fence compiled to MEMBAR + CCTL.IVALL per lane per
    z-step (CL 2 54 ms, CL 4 98).
  - The cluster-scope try_wait / arrive forms add CCTL.IVALL / ERRBAR; the CTA-scope forms are enough for shared-memory data.
  - Card 1: 3 GPCs x 12 SMs, so clusters of 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 keep all 36 SMs busy and 8 idles a third of them.

| ncu 128^3 256 -> 256 | ms |
|---|---|
| CL 1 (conv_bwd_w_f4ws_k, nvcc) | 24.7 |
| CL 2 | 31.0 |
| CL 4 | 41.4 |
| CL 4 without the bulk copies (timing only) | 24.6 |
| CL 4 without the remote scale stores | 37.1 |
| CL 4 without any remote traffic | 21.5 |
| CL 1 with the LY 1 staging removed (the consumer ceiling) | 12.4 |

  Even free of remote traffic, staging a quarter of the groups with half rows gains only 13 %. The producers are bound by each
  pass's latency (the chain decode -> GN / SiLU -> amax shuffles -> requantisation, then the per-pass barrier), not by their
  instruction count. Next: more passes in flight per block.



**Tests.** tests/test_f4v.c (fast tier) has 21 cases comparing old and new kernel. Each must show equal output bytes, equal GN
statistics, and the new kernel actually having run. The cases cover:
- GN + stats, partial tiles, stored stats, plain input;
- bdata with output SR, odd width;
- split input, z-window, z-range;
- in-kernel GN: a masked partial chunk, a split input with one GN and with two;
- the slabbed prenorm against the in-kernel GN;
- the fused upsample with 8- and 4-plane slabs and with one slab, odd sizes;
- the L0 shape.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| L1 32 x 128^2 x 320 | 16.5 | 10.6-11.1 | 1.49-1.55 | 69-72 |

## Unroll perf 7: the heads' shards encoded by one pool for all heads (predict --heads at q 0; same bytes; 2026-11-17, branch inkwriters-20261117)

fp4teach's quiet-card profile of the unroll's ink predict (0332, 32 windows 544 / 16, heads ink,c12,c13, q 0): wall 8.55 s, gpu(fwd+d2h)
4.99 s, writer-wait 3.17 s; the 3 head writers 20.5 s over 96 shards, ~6.8 s each. Each head's writer did compress a shard with all
--threads (z3w_write_shard), but shard by shard: its threads wait for the shard's slowest chunk (lossless chunk cost varies ~10x with the
content) and its file write before the next shard, and the main thread (ring of 2) waits for the slowest head every window.

- z3w_pool (src/z3w.c): one set of threads encodes the inner chunks of every queued shard of any array, oldest shard first; the thread that
  encodes a shard's last chunk writes its file (z3w_write_shard's bytes: the same chunk gather + encode function and write_file) and calls
  done. predict --heads: the CPU-encoded heads (q 0, or UFSM_PRED_GPU_ENC=0) share one pool of heads x --threads (as many threads as the
  head writers had together) within ufsm_ncpu; a head writer hands its shard to the pool and takes the next one; the --resume log, the
  GPU pyramid's pieces (pyacc_post, under its mutex) and the buffer's release run in done. Each head's ring has 3 buffers (was 2) so the
  main thread does not wait for the slowest head's shard. UFSM_PRED_HPOOL=0: the previous writers; =N: N pool threads.
- Bench (CPU only; 16 shards 512^3 x 3 heads decoded from PHerc1299's inkpod-9000 q 8 heads, re-encoded at q 0; desk at load 33-68, nice
  19, so ranges): all shards queued, 3 writers x 8 threads 12.0 / 12.3 s wall, one pool of 24 6.6 s (1.8x); 3 x 3 threads 16.5 s, pool of
  9 12.0 s. Emulated predict (one window per 0.15 s hands one shard per head, writer_submit's ring wait): 3 x 8 threads ring 2: 15-26 s;
  pool 24, ring 2: 13-20 s; pool 24, ring 3: 9.8-11.2 s (1.5-2.6x); 9 threads: 3 x 3 20-33 s, pool ring 3 14-17 s. Serial cost: 1.4 s
  (ink) to 2 s (c12, c13) a 512^3 shard per thread at nice 19.
- Same bytes: tests/test_z3w_pool.c (3 arrays: q 0, q 8, uint16; fill chunks, an all-fill shard over a stale object, a failing shard
  reported with its error, the others written); test_predict_heads (1b): every file of the q 0 heads' stores (shards 128 and 256, levels
  3, GPU pyramid) equal with UFSM_PRED_HPOOL=0 (diff -r); the bench's pooled stores md5-equal to the per-head writers'.
- On the GPU (fp4teach, master 442668dd, 0332 ink recipe 544 / 16, 32 tiles, q 0, 3 heads, --threads 20, interleaved x2, card 1
  nearly quiet): the stores byte-identical; writer-wait 3.42 / 2.59 -> 0.31 / 0.09 s, but the main wall only 11.62 / 11.80 -> 10.66 /
  11.01 s (-7 %): gpu(fwd+d2h) rose 7.73 / 8.62 -> 9.60 / 9.81 s, the pool's threads now overlapping the forward and competing with it
  (CPU / PCIe). The reader is the next floor (read 6.7-7.5 s, slot-wait 2.3-2.9 s).

## Fit-derived pseudo labels: gated winding labels from our unrolls, the build on the pod (2026-11-17, branch pseudolab-20261117)

User (11-17): "at some point we need to feed our refined unwraps back in as training data — pseudolabeling and such"; (11-10) "judge the
good parts from the bad parts". The fitter adds global spiral topology the net does not see, so a gated fit is a better target than the
net's own predictions (the --ssl-heads path); errors are masked (weight 0), never negative labels. Desk CPU only so far.

**Inventory (latent nets).** try9-6250 pod unrolls (dir -1; on the desk only wraps_snap 57 MB, qa, wrapcheck, strip; fields / joined stay
on the pod): PHerc0332 wrap-check 54 / 7 / 4, unroll-qa tiles over conf_lo / pw48 / w4 25 / 36 / 10 of 48 -> 0.12 pass all three (0.14
material-weighted), z drift 0.84 (ALARM), join 0.955, distort trusted 0.618; PHerc1667 39 / 6 / 6, 14 / 22 / 4 -> 0.44, drift 1.21, join
0.960, trusted 0.623. u1-13000 PHerc0332 (unroll2, dir -1): 0.29 (0.33); its +1 twin 0.25. The 11-12 u1 batch (19 scrolls, default
+1, before unroll-qa) kept only logs except 1667-u1 (wrong hand), P4-u1 and 1299-u1; fibfit/1667/dm1 (dir -1 refit, 0.762 same-sheet vs
the published unwrap). Dense unroll-qa (all 2126 material tiles of 128^3 cells, 13 min at 4 threads) of dm1 on the u1 fields: 0.673 pass
(0.703 material-weighted), over conf_lo 244, pw48 525, w4 187.

**Does the tile gate track truth.** geo-gate's per-GT-box ids (qa_rows.json, per-box gauge): 1667 joined boxes passing conf_lo <= 0.4,
pw48 <= 0.1 and w4 >= 0.8: 41, mean ids 0.892, 88 % >= 0.8, none < 0.5; failing 13, mean 0.654. Paris 4 ref-cf: passing 6, mean 0.62 (2
< 0.5); failing 31, mean 0.198. Inside a good run the tile gate selects good labels; a P4-like run must be refused whole (run gate).

**Precedent.** -good (scripts/rv/good.sh: surf-labels -> gt-gate against the m7 prob, a stored gated phase, scope local) and -b3
(scripts/univ/b3_1299.sh: phase on the fly from codes.zarr, rmax 20, one weight.zarr from phase-coh --coh 0 --box-scale --papyrus 64).
sources.h's scope "w4" is the matching scope: the winding mod 4 trains per tile (the sampler unwraps the label phase inside the window),
no long-range count loss.

**Build (scripts/pseudo/build.sh RUN OUT), where the unroll ran.** Codes (1.6-2 GB) and weight (~1.4 GB) are label data: built on the pod
from its own unroll, never copied desk -> pod. Steps: (1) unroll-qa --tiles 100000 --gate-boxes (new: every tile as a phase-coh box, s 0
over a gate, 1 passing) and the run gate (material-weighted pass share >= RUNMIN 0.5, else REFUSED, exit 3); (2) surf-labels on
wraps_snap (wrapcheck dup / merged, strip.args trim, --min-onpap 0.2, holdout boxes + 0.5 mm, dir from the manifest); (3) gt-gate against
the m7 prob (good.sh's 25 deg / MINKEEP 0.3); (4) phase-check --cells -> the aligned reversed chunks (b3 rule (b), dirmask.py); (5)
optional AGREE: surf-labels --gt OTHER --gt-cells (new: the GT comparison per cell) -> cells where two fits disagree (pair accuracy or
phase agreement < 0.8, agreemask.py); (6) phase-coh --coh 0 --box-scale (agree, dir, tile) --box-default 0 --papyrus 64 -> weight.zarr;
(7) source.json (scope w4, heads phase / normal / density / wind4 / rv, holdout_file + mask). scripts/pseudo/mksources.sh BASE OUT W DIRs
adds them at total weight W in proportion to the gated volume. Cost on PHerc0332 u1 (desk, 4 threads): surf-labels 32 min, 3.4 GB RSS,
66 / 73 wraps kept, phase known 21.1 cm3, kept 19.4 cm3 (0.917), codes 1.6 GB, the full phase raster 13 GB (deleted after the weight).

**Qualifying now.** PHerc0332 fails the run gate (try9 0.12, u1 0.29). PHerc1667 passes (try9 0.44 on 48 tiles, dm1 0.70 dense),
outside its GT and the C boxes. Paris 4 fails and has its own GT. The rated-good 1218 / 1299 and the -good scrolls 0139 / 0009B / 0175A
need try9 pod unrolls with UQTILES=100000 (hands from count-field's model-coherence estimator first; 1299 / 0009B / 0175A are "?").

**ssl-sources.sh MIRROR=1** (the pod A/B's unlabelled pool): the volumes of a list (VOLS, from the desk's v2/ct, a tiny file) read from
the volcomp mirror, each checked by its zarr.json; HOLD=holdouts-20261114.json rejects every per-scroll holdout and wbench box on the CT;
the axis is matched by scan basename. On the scratch1 -ho json: 37 unlabelled volumes on the mirror (35 locally), 11 with an axis.

**The wbench 1667 boxes C25-C70 were never held out (found 11-17).** holdouts-20261114 has only C1-C24 for PHerc1667 (from
wbench/holdouts.json, which predates the 10-25 C25-C70 additions), and every u1 sources file (sources-u1 / u1b / u1c / u1d) used
wbench/holdouts.json too: u1 and try9 both trained on C25-C70 through 1667-gt / A48 / B48, i.e. on 9 of core's 12 1667 boxes (C26 ...
C60). Core's 1667 rows are in-sample for both; the clean numbers are HOLD and the 11-14 holdout boxes. Lead 11-17:
`/vesuvius/ufsm/univ/scratch1/holdouts-20261118.json` = holdouts-20261114 + the 46 boxes as `wb-C25` ... (score 0: masked from
training, never validation boxes) for future runs; try9 keeps its holdouts at the resume (it has trained on them). Report core with the
1667 rows split out. The 1667 pseudo source masks all 70 wbench C boxes: weight 0 on each box + 64 level-2 voxels (the first box list
of its phase-coh weight) and holdout_file pseudo/holdouts-pseudo1667.json (= holdouts-20261118) with the run's --holdout-guard 32.

**Tests.** test_unroll_qa: --gate-boxes on the right model's 8 tiles (all s 1, 64^3 boxes) and the wrong model's box (s 0, --gate-scale 2
doubles it). test_surflabels: --gt-cells against itself, every cell's kept voxels and pairs right.

## fstem fused forward: a divergent branch per lane, the cell type as a template (byte-identical; 2026-11-17, branch fsupreg-20261117)

- **Why look:** fp4teach wired nn_fstem_up_fwd_t into predict's fields path. It was slower there: 54.4 ms + an 8.7 ms 7-channel
  lat_up4 against 59.8 ms for stem + up + shuffle. fp4teach suspected registers (95 a thread, ~5 blocks an SM).
- **Launch bounds were not it.** ncu durations are stable to 0.01 ms even with card 1 shared; P 640 slab 64, 4 outputs / P 768
  slab 16, 11 outputs:

| launch bound | registers | ms |
|---|---|---|
| (128, 1) | 95 | 3.06 / 1.70 |
| (128, 6) | 80 | 3.68 / 1.72 |
| (128, 8) | 64 | 3.90 / 1.83 |

  Achieved occupancy stayed at 33-47 %.
- **Two other ideas made it slower.** Prefetching the side pair's 16 sub-cell loads went to 123 registers and 3.44 ms. Batching 3
  qs items a thread went to 3.52 ms.
- **What ncu showed instead:** the fused kernel executed 491 M instructions against the plain kernel's 307 M.
- **Two byte-identical fixes:**
  1. fsu_row chose fsu_x<2> or fsu_x<0> by bx & 1. Odd and even lanes of a warp then ran both paths one after the other. Now the
     weights row is picked by index (FLW[2 (bx & 1) + dx]), with the same expression.
  2. The cell type is a template parameter (LT = f16 / float) instead of a runtime branch per load, and the cell-row offsets are
     32-bit, computed once a block. nn_fstem_up_fwd_t refuses qd h w >= 2^31.
- **Result:** 491 -> 433 M instructions, 95 -> 78 registers, ncu 3.06 -> 2.46 ms at P 640 / 4 outputs and 1.70 -> 1.40 ms at
  P 768 / 11 outputs, the training head-slab shape.
- **Checks:**
  - bench hashes equal at P 384, P 640 and P 768.
  - test_fstem gained cases where most cells are +-0, covering signed-zero sums. All 24 fused cases (fp16 / fp32 cells x
    random / zeros x 3 slabs x stem on / off) match the up-slab + shuffle + stem chain in all 59136 logits.
- **Expected for predict's fields path:** 54.4 x 0.8 + 8.7 ≈ 52 ms against 59.8 ms.

## fstem forward for predict's shapes: occupancy, not bandwidth (byte-identical; 2026-11-17, branch fstempred-20261117)

- **Why look:** the fields predict spends ~30 % of its kernel time in fstem_fwd_k: convk's profile, u1 13000, window 640, about
  50 ms a window. It calls the plain kernel with 6 outputs, 4 of them held (channels 0, 1, 9, 10), adding into the planes that
  lat_up_slab_c and lat_shuffle_c wrote.
- **Diagnosis:** at P 640 / 4 outputs the plain kernel moved 185 GB/s, 41 % of DRAM. ncu (bench_fstem, card 1) put achieved
  occupancy at 40 %. Shared memory capped it at 5 blocks an SM (19.2 KB a block), registers at 6, and warps sat waiting on
  L1TEX. So the kernel was latency-bound. The fused variant (nn_fstem_up_fwd, the trainer's path) held 36 KB a block, i.e. 2
  blocks an SM.
- **Changes, all byte-identical:**
  1. fs_stage goes row by row with aligned 4-byte pairs instead of a division and a bounds test per element.
  2. The MMA results stay in registers until every warp has finished reading the staged rows. h then reuses their shared memory,
     since sr and hs are a union: 10.7 KB a block.
  3. The fused variant's qs is dynamic shared memory, sized nout x 4 x 66 floats instead of 16 x ....
  4. Launch bounds: (128, 8) for the plain variant. The fused one stays at the default, because a 64-register cap made it spill
     (2.8 -> 6-8 ms).
- **Results**, bench_fstem, card 1 shared, min of 8 calls; old = master 105a9db9 (which already has the 454632bf unrolls):

| shape | old ms | new ms |
|---|---|---|
| P 640 slab 64, 4 out, plain | 2.49 | 1.72 (1.45x) |
| P 640 slab 16, 4 out, plain | 0.64 | 0.45 |
| P 640 slab 64, 4 out, fused | 5.94 | 2.77 (2.1x) |
| P 768 slab 16, 11 out, plain | 1.22-1.41 | 1.17 |
| P 768 slab 16, 11 out, fused (training) | 2.86 | 1.54 (1.85x) |

- **Checks:** at P 384 the forward, backward and fused-forward hashes equal master's. test_fstem passes, and so do its racecheck
  and synccheck variants (0 hazards), test_predict_heads, test_heads and test_lat_fuse.
- **Expected effect:**
  - Predict fields: fstem ~50 -> ~35 ms a window.
  - Training: 96 fused calls a window x ~1.3 ms, ~-125 ms (~2.5 %).
- **Left for predict's call pattern (fp4teach):** the fields path still runs up-slab + shuffle + plain stem. That is two extra
  read-modify-write passes over the stem's planes that the fused kernel writes once. The fused kernel now runs at P 640 / 4
  outputs in 2.77 ms against the plain stem's 1.72 ms alone.

## Training perf 3: try9 is sampler-bound after the GPU gains; the host profile, word-wise byte scans in draw_ (2026-11-17, branch samplecpu-20261117)

- **The swap's live rate stayed flat.** fd615b6f went into try9 at step 6942. The replay ran identical windows with --det and no
  echo: windows 2-10 at 79.6 Mvox/s on the old binary and 88.1 on the new one (+10.7 %). Live, the first 360 windows ran 0.156
  samp/s against 0.15 before. Echo went from 0-8 % to 10-24 % and fresh windows dropped to 0.11-0.14/s. The GPU is now waiting for
  the sampler, so its gain shows up as more echo windows. Gate: wind4 acc 0.594 vs 0.604 and gn_step 0.88x, no rollback.
- **Host profile** (perf, read-only, try9 live; desk at 28.4 of 32 cores niced work, 0 idle). The 10 workers ran on ~2.7 cores
  together and spent ~75 % of their time asleep, ~19 core-s per fresh window. Where the CPU time goes:
  - CT decode on the CPU (vfx_decode_subs_sink, dct16_inv, zcache_read): ~37 %. try9 has no --ct-gpu-decode.
  - On-the-fly ink labels (inkfly_rays, tri_box_z, pool_derive, chunk): ~28 %. All of it runs on the CPU because the inkfly GPU
    budget never fits beside the trainer: card 0 has 0.2 GB free against a 1536 MiB reserve, logged as "7000 chunk(s) over the GPU
    budget".
  - draw_'s whole-window byte loops: ~12 %.
  - Faults, memset and memmove: ~8 %.
  - CUDA calls inside the workers: ~5 %.
  - The main thread spins ~0.6 core in cudaStreamSynchronize.
  The context switches: 52 % timer preemptions (CPU contention), 13 % libcuda's launch rwlock, 12 % the w4 ctx_run nanosleep poll,
  7 % page-cache reads.
- **The byte loops** (src/bytescan.h, new): the aux planes' unknown fill, the ink-bit pack (plus the 0 / 1 mask rewrite) and the
  --min-phase known counts over side / ink / aux. mcc leaves them as one movzbl per voxel. The new versions work on 64-bit words:
  per-byte 0x80 flags with no carry across bytes, a popcount, and a multiply to gather the bits. Min of 5 runs on 118 M bytes
  (desk loaded): count 0.061 -> 0.010 s, fill 0.130 -> 0.047 s. test_bytescan checks them against the byte loops: lengths 0-70 and
  1 M, values biased to 0 / 1 / 127 / 128 / 251-255, byte-exact.
- **Proposed, not yet done:** `--ct-gpu-decode 1 --ink-gpu 1` in launch.env. Both GPU paths are byte-identical (test_gpudec,
  test_ink_splat). Together they move ~65 % of the sampler's CPU time onto card 1. The lead decides that, because card 1 is shared.

## Training perf 2: mcc's local arrays in the head kernels (fstem 1.75x, the guided fuse pass ~2x; byte-identical; 2026-11-17, branch trainperf-20261117)

- **Audit.** `cuobjdump -res-usage` over the mcudahw cache (`~/.cache/mcudahw/*.cubin`, one file per call) lists the kernels with a
  stack frame. Under mcc a small array indexed in a loop that is not unrolled lives in local memory, even when the loop has a constant
  bound (nvcc would unroll it). The hot ones in try9's step: `lat_fuse_k` 2544 B (the guided side pair's v / ga [7][27], p / gp [7][9],
  q / gq [7][3]; ~all of try9's lat_fuse calls are guided: lat_fuse_fin grid 6048 = 7 channels), `loss_stats_k` 1248 B and
  `loss_grad_k` 624 B (the offset-tolerant path's helpers; not in try9's hot loop), `input_latc_k` 432, `fstem_fwd_k` / `fstem_bwd_k`
  160 (h [16] in the 1x1 projection's `c < C` loop, go [16] in the backward, the W1 A fragments af [4][4]), `conv_fwd_f4_k` 80-216
  (its accumulators; ptxas spills, not a loop-index array: left alone).
- **Fix: `#pragma unroll` to the array's static bound, with the runtime bound as a guard** (`for c < FS_MAXC: if (c < C) v += ...`):
  the same additions in the same order, so the bits are unchanged. fstem: stack 160 -> 96 B. bench_fstem (now also the fused
  `nn_fstem_up_fwd`, the trainer's head-slab path, and hashes of all three outputs) at P 768, slab 16, 11 outputs, card 1 shared
  with an unroll (min of 8): fused up fwd 5.04 -> 2.86 ms, plain fwd 1.96 -> 1.24-1.41, bwd 2.64-3.50 -> 1.82-1.93; the three hashes
  identical to fd615b6f's at P 384. In try9 fstem_fwd_k is 96 calls x 4.37 ms a window: ~-170 ms (~3 %) expected, bwd ~-40 ms.
- lat_fuse_k guided path: the channel loops of the per-row / per-voxel work unrolled (v and ga stay indexed per rz). test_lat_fuse
  TLF_HASH=1 (new: FNV hash of each case's fused gradient) equal to the old build in all 8 cases; TLF_BENCH=768 guided grad min 12.3
  -> 6.2 ms (shared card: only the min means anything). In try9 75 ms a window (48 calls x 1.56 ms): ~-35 ms expected.
- Not done: loss_stats_k / loss_grad_k (frames from the tol path, not touched per voxel), conv_fwd_f4_k's spills (a register budget
  question inside the MMA tile; the kernel is issue-bound on staging, see the headroom note in the section below).

## Training perf: try9's step profiled; the head adjoint's gather 7x faster, the w4 runs pinned (2026-11-17, branch trainperf-20261117)

**Profile.** try9's exact argv and env (binary c2646d35, snap/5000.ckpt, `UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB 10.98` reproduces its plan "MX gradients,
chunked, lean 2, shared encoder a1, 10.07 GB"), --det 1, lr 0, card 1 held exclusively, nsys over steps 5006-5013 (8 windows, one
update), /vesuvius/ufsm/trainperf (rp.sh, nsum.py). The windows come from the wind fixture (make_wind_fixture fx 1024 2 1,
sources-ink.json): the replay on try9's sources needs ~30-35 GB of host memory and was OOM-killed twice in the 40 GB dev slice.
6.01 s a window (try9 on card 0: ~6.7 with real windows and the sampler's GPU work beside it). Per window:

| stage | ms | share |
|---|---|---|
| 3^3 conv forward incl. the lean recompute and backward-data (conv_fwd_f4_k 1828, conv_fwd_s2_f8_k 138) | 1974 | 33 % |
| weight gradients (conv_bwd_w_f4ws_k 1215, conv_bwd_w_s2_f8_k 142, the head's conv_bwd_w1_tc_k 187) | 1570 | 27 % |
| head slabs / losses (lat_adj_xy_t_k 458, loss_grad + loss_stats 143, w4 events / runs / stats / grad 214, lat_fuse 92, slab_tg 61) | 1080 | 18 % |
| fine stem (fstem_fwd_k 417: upsample + stem + logit write fused; fstem_bwd_k 106) | 526 | 9 % |
| input build, scanner aug, label warps | 184 | 3 % |
| head 1^3 forward / backward-data, GroupNorm, optimizer (NorMuon + AdamW at accum 10), MX converts | 136 / 120 / 72 / 18 | 6 % |
| attention (4 blocks at the deepest level) | < 1 | 0 |
| GPU idle: ~5 gaps > 10 ms a window, all in the label-warp stage at the window start | 210 | 3.5 % |
| launch gaps < 1 ms (what CUDA graphs could remove) | 8 | 0.1 % |

**The head adjoint's y / x gather** (nn_lat_up_adj_c: the slab's fp16 logit gradient onto the coarse cell grid, 2 calls a slab, 48 slabs)
ran at ~30 GB/s: lat_adj_xy_t_k (the 11-13 "tiled" kernel) indexes lat_adj_w's 10-entry weight arrays with loop variables, so they
live in local memory, and every voxel was staged 2.5 times. bench_latadj at try9's slab (192^2 cells, 16 planes, 14 channels), card 1:

| kernel (UFSM_LAT_ADJ_TILE) | ms | GB/s of fp16 gradient read |
|---|---|---|
| 2: lat_adj_xy_t_k (the default until now) | 8.6-10.0 | 26-31 |
| 0: lat_adj_xy_k (per cell) | 2.6-3.3 | 80-102 |
| 1: lat_adj_xy_r_k (new default) | 1.0-1.2 | 220-260 |

lat_adj_xy_r_k: a thread owns a coarse column of 8 coarse rows and walks the 38 fine rows they read once (1.19 reads per voxel), each
row's 4 + 3 + 3 taps as three 8-byte loads (the neighbours' from L1), the weights in registers (lat_adj_w1, no tables), each row's x sum
added into the coarse rows it reaches in ascending tap order: lat_adj_xy_k's sums term for term. test_lat compares all three modes
byte for byte (3 grid shapes incl. a partial strip and a 1 x 1 grid, 3 slabs each). A first strip version with a local `const float
A[10]` took 4.8 ms and one with per-row local tables 72 ms: under mcc any indexed small array costs local memory traffic.

Fixture A/B (try9 binary / new / try9 binary, 14 windows, --det 1, lr 0): every step's losses identical across the three arms;
5.921 / 5.551 / 5.951 s a window over steps 5003-5014: **-6.4 %**.

**The w4 runs upload.** The window-start nsys timeline showed the trainer thread inside one cudaMemcpyHtoDAsync for ~150-200 ms with
the GPU idle: nn_w4runs_apply_z copied the slot's runs (off / ro / cb, ~14 MB, malloc'd in the sampler slot) with cudaMemcpyAsync from
pageable memory, which waits for the copy stream (the CT aug, the phase warp and its 453 MB round trips) to drain before it returns, so
the forward was launched only after the label stage. They now go through a per-device pinned staging buffer (reused after the previous
call's event; UFSM_W4_PINNED=0 the old path). Same bytes (test_w4dev, test_slot_planes; the fixture A/B's step lines identical). Small:
the window-start idle gaps > 10 ms went 210 -> 188 ms a window (nsys, the same capture), the wall clock within noise (5.527 against
5.506 / 5.557 s for the lat_adj binary before and after it). lat_adj_xy in that capture: 458 -> 41 ms a window.

**The copy stream at the highest priority.** With the trainer thread unblocked, every label-stage operation was issued at the window
start, yet the label planes were done only ~180 ms after the forward (nsys, the issue times of the copy stream's work): the w4 rebuild's
~60 small kernels (w4_runs_k / w4_out_k, ~1 ms each) and the warps got SMs only between the forward's conv kernels, one per gap, and the
head's first slab waits for them (ev_lab). copy_stream() is now created at cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange's greatest priority
(UFSM_COPY_PRIO=0: the default priority): idle gaps > 10 ms 186 -> 41 ms a window, kernels busy 96.4 -> 99.0 % of the capture, step
lines identical, 5.464 -> 5.322 s a window (two arms 5.321 / 5.322): **-2.6 %**.

**The head's weight gradient, 4 output tiles a block.** conv_bwd_w1_tc_k (256 MX-fp4 channels -> 160 outputs on the cell grid) ran one
block per (8-output tile, 32-channel input block): every x tile was dequantised, GroupNorm-ed and SiLU-ed 20 times. NT 4 keeps 4 column
tiles on one staged act(x) tile (the reduction buffer overlays the operand tiles after the loop); per (ci, co) the voxel order, the
warps' order and the blocks are those of NT 1, so the sums are the same (test_hgscale: byte equal, 256 -> 160 and 32 -> 16; UFSM_W1_NT=1
the old path). 189 -> 146 ms a window; 5.497 -> 5.453 s (**-0.8 %**).

Together on the fixture: **5.921 -> 5.321 s a window (-10.1 %)** against try9's binary, every step line identical.

**What is left** (result-neutral): fstem_fwd_k at ~70 GB/s of logit writes (417 ms; ~35 KB of shared memory a 128-thread block, so 2-3
blocks an SM; ncu could not profile it inside the trainer under mcudahw), and the convs (60 %, tuned: no fusion left, sparse24-20261113). Result-changing: --sparse24 mode 3 (~5 % of this
step), skip-empty above thr 0. Not worth it: the optimizer (1.2 %), attention (0), CUDA graphs (launch gaps 0.1 %).

| CPU fp64 (41 wraps, ~8 min each) | 2241 | - | 0.1389 | 0.5819 | 0.00109 | the noise floor (two valid solvers) |

fp32 against the noise floor (lead: CPU fp64 vs GPU fp64 = two valid solvers of the same problem; GPU fp64 run to run is
bit-identical). 0332, the 41 wraps with a CPU fp64 run (w035 / w069 included): every per-wrap maximum within 1.5x the CPU-vs-GPU
maximum (aniso>1.2 w069 12.9 % vs CPU 14.7 % on w068; cm2 w035 2.33 % both); 6 of 17 mean metrics above the CPU spread (energy 1.05e-3
vs 0.96e-3, aniso p50 / p95 / p99, ink mean, frac50; each <= 1e-3 relative), judged noise against -27 % per wrap. w035 / w069 renders
(ink + CT) fp32 vs fp64 side by side: no visible difference (/vesuvius/ufsm/unrollperf/gate/eyeball, deleted with the gate data).

1667 (47 wraps, base run up to the strip with the ink head only; GPU fp64 vs fp32, one binary):

| | strip s | per-wrap s | distort p95 | trusted | folded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU fp64 | 59 | 452 | 0.1409 | 0.6406 | 0.00143 |
| fp32 | 67 | 356 | 0.1401 | 0.6402 | 0.00143 |

aniso>1.2 per wrap: worst degradation +3.1 % relative (w041) against the 0332 CPU-vs-GPU worst +5.6 % (w049); fp32 better on 10
wraps, worse on 13. The largest change (16 %, w003, 1.16 cm2, a strongly distorted wrap) is an improvement (aniso>1.2 14.5 -> 12.1 %,
energy 4.30 -> 4.26). Trusted share -0.0004 (0332 CPU-vs-GPU -0.0002): accepted (lead, 0.06 % relative, changes both ways).
Default since then: flatten / strip-flatten run the CG's matvec in fp32 (dot products, r / z / x / p and the step in fp64); the fp64
solve is `--cg-fp32 0` or `UFSM_FLAT_CG_FP32=0`. test_flatten_gpu checks both paths against the CPU solver (fp32 max |duv| 3.2e-5 on the

- The unroll's ink is now the critical path: with recto-sp on the GPU (192 -> ~45 s) the chain from the ink's start to snap is ~520 s
  on 0332 against the ink's 682 s (full4). The ink predicts are GPU-bound (UFSM_PRED_PROF, latink recipe, 32 windows: gpu(fwd+d2h)
  11.1 of 12.7 s wall; --threads 12 / 20 / 28 the same; UFSM_PRED_DEVREAD=1 the same wall at +50 % CPU, same bytes), but their
  --q 0 head writers and the three concurrent ink-blends are CPU: perf on the predict, vll_encode_block 29 % + vll_encode 27 % +
  the CT decode 13 %; on a blend the lossless decode (vllx_decode_sub_sink) 40 %, ib_rows 22 %, the encode 18 %. Ink runs beside
  rectosp / ref / the slab fits, which want the same cores.
- third_party/volcomp.h, the lossless encoder (the bytes unchanged): the bit writer stores whole 32-bit words (it wrote byte by byte;
  shared with the lossy encoder, whose bytes are unchanged too); the block's DENSE / SPARSE cost estimate by one table lookup per voxel
  (three 21-bit sums in a word) instead of per-voxel branches; DENSE tokens by table, the context by table, the counts in two
  interleaved histograms; the tANS lanes in registers. One core, 32 ink / CT chunks of 128^3: 9.3 -> 3.7 / 9.1 -> 4.5 G cycles
  (91 -> 229 / 92 -> 186 MB/s). Byte-identical to the old encoder over 76 chunks (ink, CT, 12 synthetic kinds covering CONST / RAW
  chunks and CONST / SPARSE / DENSE / RAW blocks) at q 0, 2, 8, 32 (gcc A/B); tests/test_volcomp_vll.c holds the old encoder's sizes
  and hashes for the synthetic chunks (lossless, integer-only so build-independent; mcc matches them).
- src/volcomp_fast.h vllx_decode_sub_sink, the DENSE loop: both tANS lanes in registers, a voxel pair per step, the context model by
  table: ~25 % fewer cycles per lossless chunk (decode only, 3.9 -> 3.0 G cycles over the 32 ink chunks); test_volcomp_vll decodes
  every synthetic chunk through the sink, whole and in a box cutting blocks.
- ink-blend's voxel loop for two inputs (the unroll's grids): the row's wz wy product hoisted (the same (wz wy) wx order, volatile), the
  masks per row: a further 13-17 % of a blend's cycles (0332 mini box, ink / c12 / c13: 135 -> 118, 149 -> 125, 150 -> 124 G cycles),
  outputs identical (md5 of every file).
- Predict, latink recipe, 32 windows: user CPU 240 -> 182 s, wall 12-14 s either way (GPU-bound); outputs identical. ink-blend of one
  head (0332 mini box, g0 + g256): 765 / 774 -> 639 / 650 G cycles (-17 %), outputs identical (all three heads compared).
## 2-D ink teachers in MX-fp4: quantiser options, deterministic GroupNorm, accuracy floor (2026-11-16, branch fp4teach-20261116)

Goal: reader3 / ink9um (ink-ext, Reader V3 architecture on xnet) in MX-fp4 at fp16 accuracy. Gate as set: on the 24 held-out eval crops
(16 Paris 4, 4 PHerc0139, 4 PHerc1667; mean per-crop AUC vs the human labels, paired vs fp16), within 0.001 overall and no scroll worse
than 0.003. Tools in /vesuvius/ufsm/inkteach/fp4t: v.sh (tvar.sh on a binary, CROPS= for /vesuvius/ufsm/inkgt/evcrops-ho: 10 more
crops on PHerc0500P2 / 0841), pair.sh (paired per scroll), pairci.py (paired, bootstrap 95 % CI), lerr.py (logit rms and 1 - corr vs
the reference over all maps), bench.sh / benchpair.sh (one full PHerc1667 segment).

**MX runs were not reproducible.** Two identical MX5 runs of ink9um differed by 0.004 on 1667 and 0.001 overall (logit 1 - corr 0.006
between them). The cause was xgn: its GroupNorm statistics summed through float atomics (shared, then global), so the per-channel sums
depended on the schedule. That is harmless in fp16 (rms logit 0.003 run to run), but every changed fp16 bit near an e2m1 rounding
boundary moves a whole quantisation step. Fix: `k_gnpart` / `k_gnfin`, a one-pass sum and sum of squares of x - sh_c per (chunk,
sample), with sh_c the sample's first voxel so there is no cancellation. Each thread has a fixed channel pair and row stride, rows
combine in a fixed order, the chunks go to a buffer and are summed in order in double. MX runs now repeat byte for byte, and fp16 maps
move rms 0.003 (AUC unchanged). The stats also got faster: 18.6 -> 3.7 ms per reader3 batch (old: 2 x 64 launches of a few blocks each,
float smem atomics). Test: test_xmx gn (host double reference, mean >> std, 320 / 640 channels, run-to-run equality).

**Quantiser options** (all off by default, so gambiarra / dino3d are unchanged; env at net load, setters for tests):
- `UFSM_XNET_MXQ=1|2`: weight block scales of least squared error. Per 16-K block, the e4m3 codes -4 .. +2 around amax / 6 (MX6: 2^e
  or 2^(e - 1)). 2 also searches the per-row scale gs = amax_row / 2688 x 2^(j / 8), j 0..7, which aligns the blocks' e4m3 grid.
  Rel weight error 0.095 -> 0.0856 (reader3, every conv alike). Rows are packed on 16 threads (MXQ 2 load 25.8 -> 3.5 s).
- `UFSM_XNET_MXA=1`: the same least-squares search for the activation block scales in k_xq (7 candidates x 16 values per block,
  hidden in the memory-bound pass).
- `UFSM_XNET_MXROT=1`: each 16-block of the weights (at pack) and of the inputs (in k_xq) rotated by H16 / 4. This is exact in real
  arithmetic: the block dot products are invariant under the orthonormal transform. It applies to convs fed by k_xq only (the fused
  gambiarra producers quantise unrotated: a rotated conv refuses a q-only input).
- `UFSM_XNET_MX_SKIP=2-4,...`: convs (initialisation index within a net, `xnet_wseq_reset` per ie_load) kept fp16.
- FQ probes: `UFSM_XNET_FQ` activation code 7 (least-squares scale) and code 9 (H16) for both operands.
test_xmx covers MXQ 1 / 2, rot, lsa (sf 5 and 6, generic and halo kernels) against host references written from the definitions.
Fast-math detail: the host reference and the pack must agree on every choice, so gs and amax / 6 / gs are computed in double, 2^(j / 8)
comes from a table, and a later candidate replaces an earlier one only when it is 1e-9 better (weights) or 1e-5 better (activations,
float on the device).

**Where the error comes from** (ink9um, logit 1 - corr vs fp16 on PHerc1667, the most sensitive scroll):

| fp4 acts only (FQ 5,0) | 0.0178 | -0.0019 / -0.0009 / -0.0103 / +0.0000 |
| fp4 acts only, LS scale (FQ 7,0) | 0.0114 | -0.0015 / -0.0030 / -0.0037 / -0.0005 |

### Speed: where an ink9um tile goes, and the depth-fusion fusions

Card 1 was at 100 % from 2-4 other jobs throughout, so wall times swung +-40 % and only per-kernel minima from nsys (the same launch
shape over 22 forwards, `nbp.sh`, `UFSM_IE_BENCH=32,10` = the new synthetic bench: B tiles x N forwards per checkpoint) are quoted.
ink9um, 128x128x17 tiles, batch 32, ms of kernel time per tile per checkpoint:

| path | total | depth fusion (f1 stem, f2 conv, GN, head, attention) | 2-D U-Net | GN stats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp16, before (igemm f1 / f2, xgn + xhead + attn_max) | 0.88-0.93 | ~0.55 | ~0.25 | 0.17 |
| MX5, before | 0.955 | ~0.55 | ~0.20 | 0.17 |
| MX5, fused (this branch) | 0.650 | ~0.37 | ~0.20 | 0.08 |

The 2-D U-Net that MX speeds up is only ~a quarter of the tile; the depth fusion on 17 full-resolution layers is the rest. Fused:
`k_dfc1` (the 1 -> 16 stem straight from the one-channel input instead of xunfold + a K 72 implicit GEMM), the f1 GroupNorm +
LReLU applied in `k_dfc16`'s halo load (`xconv_fwd_gnin`; f1 never rewritten), and `xdepth_collapse16` (f2's GroupNorm + LReLU,
the attention logit, softmax over depth, weighted sum and max in one kernel reading f2 twice, never writing it). Output: test_xmx
references (gnin max |d| 0, dattn 2.4e-4 vs the separate kernels, c1 vs a double reference); the AUC of both teachers on the 24
crops is unchanged to the fourth digit. `--weights s42,s43` now runs one render pass forwarding both checkpoints per batch
(`UFSM_IE_ENS1=0` for the old pass per checkpoint; byte-equal maps): the render / blend CPU work is halved. Host robust-norm
params cost 0.07 ms per tile (ink9um). A/B switches: `UFSM_IE_DATTN=0`, `UFSM_XNET_DF1=0`, `UFSM_XNET_DF16=0`.
Segment wall times on a quiet card: pending (`fp4t/quiet.sh`, `quiet2.sh`).

## Training perf: the validation regen pass was 95 % THP compaction (2026-11-17, branch trainperf-20261117)

try9's validation passes (--val-store regen, every 500 steps) idled card 0 for ~25 min each, and the step-5500 pass for >75 min. The 3
validation workers were not sampling: after ~65 min each had 31-141 s user against 1500-3250 s system time; perf (15 s, the three
threads): 99 % of the samples under `__alloc_pages_direct_compact <- do_huge_pmd_anonymous_page <- draw_` (the memmove into window
scratch), 34 % in `native_queued_spin_lock_slowpath` from the HMM mmu notifiers of each migrated page, the rest TLB shootdowns;
/proc/vmstat ~13 compaction stalls a second, all failing (Shmem 57 GB of pinned buffers and 20 GB of swap: no order-9 blocks to make).

Cause: `sampler_start` requests huge pages for the worker scratch (`wbig_alloc`, MADV_HUGEPAGE) when `gpu_aug != 2`. The training
sampler runs gpu_aug 2 (`--gpu-aug 3`), so it was off there (training workers 6100-6600 s user / 330-370 s system over 13 h), but the
validation sampler is a copy with `vc.gpu_aug = 0`, and regen starts a fresh sampler at every pass, so each pass faulted its whole
scratch again through compaction. The 2026-11-09 note had measured the same stall (493 s system vs 125 s user for 24 P 512 windows).

Fix: `sample_cfg.thp_off`, set on the validation sampler (it warps nothing, so huge pages buy it nothing in any mode). The windows'
bytes do not depend on the page backing. Live runs: `UFSM_SAMPLER_THP=0` (try9's launch.env since 08:45) does the same for every
sampler. Expected pass time: the user time above, ~1-3 min of sampling plus the 32 forwards, against 25-75 min; at --val-every 2000
that is ~10 % of the wall clock back (~30 % at 500).

## Unroll perf 4: the strip's papyrus gate inside the render, the gated stretch in C (2026-11-17, branch unrollperf4-20261117)

- strip_refill.sh rendered every stripe three times when the ink is gated (the ink, then each of c12 / c13 with the same CT, fill and
  inpaint) and multiplied them with img-gate (perf 2). `ufsm render --gate ROOT KEY` (at most 2, needs --ct and --fill) decodes the gate
  volumes in the same chunk-ordered pass (render.c now takes up to 4 volumes, CPU and GPU paths; the gates are sampled at the ink's
  points, after the --fill search on the CT, with the ink's depth), runs them through the same push-pull, and writes the ink x max(gates)
  / 255 with img-gate's table. Byte for byte the three renders + img-gate: tests/test_render_gate.c (CPU and GPU, a fixture with a CT
  void, normal fill, inpainted and grid-hole pixels) and on real data, 0332 wraps w091 / w092 (the inkpod zarr standing in for both
  gates): ink, CT and fill-flag images equal. Time per gated wrap 21-28 s -> 11.5-15 s (3 runs each, card 1 shared). On the 0332
  stripimg run (5 stripes, 9:00 wall) the two gate renders per stripe were 2 x 20-50 s of the stripe's render work.
- strip_refill.sh re-rendering a stripe the mosaic had consumed kept its old `.gated` marker and skipped the gate (latent since perf 2);
  the render now clears the marker first.
- The gated stretch (numpy's linear percentiles over every 7th masked pixel of the 3 middle stripes, ~2 min in python with the
  full-size float temporaries) is `ufsm img-stretch CTL CT1 INK1 ...` (imggate.c, numpy's virtual-index / lerp arithmetic in doubles;
  tests/test_img_gate.py: 12 random distributions equal to numpy). Three 0332 wrap renders (90 M CT pixels): 2.6 s vs numpy 182 s
  (desk busy), the same 39,197,15,195.

## recto-sp on the GPU: byte-identical fp64 profiles, the source decoded once into a device ring (2026-11-17, branch rectogpu-20261117)

recto-sp (unroll stage rectosp: the fit fields' sp blended with the m7 recto-hit spacing, --half-um 400 --half2-um 800 --blend 0.3) was the
second-largest unroll stage, all on the CPU, competing with the ink predict that runs beside it. `--gpu N` (default 0; -1 the CPU; the CPU
path stays for --cls, no device, or too little device memory for the ring) now runs the per-cell part on the GPU (src/nn_rectosp.cu).
Its sp and rsp chunk files are **identical** to master's on both scrolls (diff -r). test_recto_gpu (gpu) compares them byte for byte on a
noisy lossy synthetic: 3 flag sets, 5 row blocks, ring wrap, stride 3 with --rows, the host-decode path, and zero runs.

- **Exact fp64.** The kernel mirrors rs_axis / rs_tri / rr_peaks / rs_rows operation by operation in double. nn_rectosp is in
  UFSM_EXACT_CU (-fmad=false in every build; a contracted FMA moves a peak position by an ulp and flips a median pick). rr_peaks' taps
  come from rr_taps (rectoruler.c), so they are the same doubles. The tap sum for a full window is added on the device in rr_peaks'
  order (host fast math may reassociate). The comparisons are moved to fp32 only where they are provably the same: minima of floats,
  `float < double` against the nearest float bound (f_up / f_dn).
- **fp64 is the floor.** A consumer card runs fp64 at 1/64 rate (ncu: fp64 pipe 84 % busy). The pipe charges a warp instruction the same
  whatever its active lanes. So the kernel is one warp per cell with compacted work lists (ballot) in full warps:
  - the samples to interpolate; eight zero corners give +0 at once
  - the smoothed samples whose window is not all zero
  - rr_peaks' candidates, which are independent: every sample its plateau skip passes over equals tmp[i] and is never a candidate. They
    search their prominence in fp32 and are compacted in order.

  Lane 0 merges the hits and picks the median. The cell axes run in their own kernel, one thread each (computed 32x per warp they were
  40 % of the fp64 instructions). The grid is sized to the resident blocks (a grid-stride grid of 2.4 waves had a partial last wave).
  One 1M-cell block went 394 -> 244 ms. Each sample still costs ~70 fp64 ops: the 0332 kernel total is ~30 s on a 5060 Ti.
- **The source decoded once.** The CPU path decodes each 64-row block's source box with an 85-voxel halo each side: ~2.3x the volume.
  The GPU path keeps the source as a device z ring of the run's fixed y / x box: 0332 512 x 2959 x 3183 = 4.8 GB, 1667 5.5 GB; RZ is a
  multiple of 128 and one block step deeper than a block needs. Each block adds only its new slices, read up to the source's chunk-row
  end, as whole 128^3 chunks gathered on the device (predict's nn_ctw_put / gpudec). It zeroes the slices first, so fill chunks
  (57 % on 0332) cost nothing. While our kernel holds the GPU, the GPU decoder hands most chunks to the CPU (~16k host, ~500 device on
  0332); the bytes are identical either way. The host-decode-and-upload variant (UFSM_RECTOSP_DEVDEC=0) uploaded 74 GB of raw slices
  for 0332: 38 s of pageable copies.
- **Pipeline.**
  - A helper thread prepares block k+1 while block k's kernel runs. Its source part and its field part run on two threads. The field
    part loads rows chunk-aligned and keeps them for the next block, loading t0..t5 and w only (fit_fields_skip_planes bit 4: no pc / ps).
  - The shard row's net sp read, the blend (threaded) and the sp / rsp shard writes (two arrays at once) run in a writer thread behind
    the next row's blocks. This also speeds the CPU path (0332 192 -> 129 s, same bytes).
  - A pass-0 shard that the box covers entirely no longer re-reads the input sp.

| warm m7 cache, 16 threads, card 1 shared | master (CPU) | this branch --gpu -1 | this branch GPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| PHerc0332 (3943 x 1392 x 1504 fields) | 192 s, 1864 CPU s, 9.6 GB | 129 s, 1595 CPU s | **38.7-45.0 s**, 500 CPU s, 6.3-6.7 GB |
| PHerc1667 (4635 x 1568 x 1616) | 169 s, 1630 CPU s, 11.2 GB | 151 s, 1754 CPU s | **54.6-60.6 s**, 610-655 CPU s, 7.3-7.9 GB |

The GPU run's time splits as:
- blocks (kernel) 31-35 s
- waiting for the helper: 6 s on 0332, 12-16 s on 1667 (its field loads take 35 s there)
- the writer's shard writes: 19-23 s on 0332, 35-40 s on 1667, overlapped except for the last row

Left: the 1667 field decode (t0..t5 + w of 11.7 G cells; only 1/64 of them are sampled, but the codec decodes whole chunks), the
lossless shard encodes, and the fp64 kernel. A lazy profile (±half first, the ±half2 tail only where the inner window has fewer than
--min-int intervals, exact when hit clusters separated by >= sep bound the window) would cut ~1/3 of the kernel: not done.

## Unroll perf 3: no context on unlisted cards; the ref's chunk rows fixed (2026-11-17, branch unrollperf3-20261117)

- SGPU (perf 2) pinned the stages without a --gpu, but a predict on --gpu 1 still opened a 128 MiB context on card 0 (the training card;
  lead). Without a caller's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES the run now exports CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES = the cards it was given (FIELDGPUS, FITGPUS,
  INKGPU, SGPU, RGPU; GVIS) and every --gpu passes the card's index in it (lg); per-job CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<card> stay physical ids.
  DRY=1 prints each stage's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (desk, FITGPUS=FIELDGPUS=INKGPU=1: every stage 1, every --gpu 0).
- The ref's chunk rows came from the free host memory (count-field --mem-gb lowered to 60 % of what was available) and change the ref:
  0332 full3 / full4 picked 512 / 640 rows and their joined models differed. unroll.sh passes --chunk-rows ${REFCZ:-512} to every
  count-field (solves, DIRCOH, the streamed pass 1); count-field takes fewer rows only when --mem-gb cannot hold the asked ones, and
  then prints `DEFAULTED: count-field chunk rows = N (...)`; the ref stage logs the rows used to progress.log.

## Unroll perf 2: stages pinned off card 0, 3 slab lanes, the ink beside the critical path, flatten's relax pass, the strip gate in C (2026-11-17, branch unrollperf2-20261117)

0332 end to end WITHOUT UPTO on the desk (card 1 only: FIELDGPUS=FITGPUS=INKGPU=1, PERWRAP=1, local CT cache, master's FBLEND 0 /
FSKIP 20). Stage walls in s; the ink runs beside the chain, stripimg and perwrap wait for it and run side by side:

| stage | before (02:37) | + pinning, lanes, flatten, img-gate (full3) | + ink from the fields, blends at once (full4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| fields | 157 | 112 | 116 |
| rectosp | 126 | 128 | 221 (beside the ink predicts) |
| ref | 280 (CPU fallback) | 54 | 92 |
| slabs | 320 (1 lane) | 155 (3 lanes) | 190 |
| join .. snap | 173 | 174 | 190 |
| strip + stripflat + distort | 226 | 83 | 139 |
| ink (beside) | 771 from the slabs | 770 from the slabs | 682 from the fields, done before the snap |
| stripimg | 764 | 433 | 457 |
| perwrap | 784 | 608 | 612 |
| **total** | **2441** | **1832** | **1422** |

PHerc1667 end to end on the same setup (master c2216919, local CT, 44 per-wrap renders): 1248 s = fields 125, rectosp 293 and ref 111
(the ink's predicts beside them), slabs 219 (73 slabs, 3 lanes), join .. snap 114, strip + stripflat + distort 82, then stripimg 281
beside perwrap 385; the ink (651 s from the fields) was done at the end of the slabs.

The joined models of full3 and full4 differ: the ref picked 512 vs 640 chunk rows from the free host memory (the ink's predicts beside
it in full4), the nondeterminism of "Unroll perf 1"; with the same ref every slab fit is byte-identical whatever the lanes (below).

- Card 0: unroll.sh ran every stage without a --gpu of its own (ref / refstream count-field, strip-flatten, the strip renders) on CUDA
  device 0 whatever FITGPUS said. On the desk that is the training card: 0.7 GB free sent the ref's CG and the renders to the CPU, and
  strip-flatten's SLIM ran there beside try8 (204 s; 30 s on the pod). SGPU (default: the first of FITGPUS) now pins them:
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$SGPU for every stage except fields / slabs / ink / perwrap (those place themselves) and for the streamed ref;
  an explicit CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (also an empty one) is kept. The ref on card 1: 280 -> 54 s (CG + model pass on the GPU).
- Slab lanes: a 0332 slab fit is 96 x 1392 x 1504 fields cells, ~1.9 GB of device memory, ~4.4 s of fit after ~1 s of setup; one lane
  left the card idle between fits. Refitting all 62 slabs on card 1: 1 lane 232 s, 2 lanes 171 s, 3 lanes 132 s, 4 lanes 134 s (95 %
  GPU busy), every delta.f32 byte-identical to the 1-lane run (so the joined model is too). fitlanes' auto rule was (device GB - 8) / 16
  (1 lane on 16 GB cards, written for Paris-size slabs of 10-16 GB); now the device's free GB - 1 over 12 B per slab cell + 0.5 GB,
  clamped to 1..3: 0332 3 lanes on a 16 GB card, a Paris 4 slab (~1.3 G cells) still 1. Without the fields' shape (DRY) the old rule.
- flatten (per-wrap unroll renders, strip chunks): prolongate's flip relaxation swept the whole fine mesh 200 times per level (every
  0332 level ran all 200 rounds; 6.3 M triangles at D1), 42 % of a flatten. It now visits only the triangles with a relaxed vertex, in
  index order, so the sums, flip counts and marks are the full sweep's bit for bit (a triangle outside that set keeps its unflipped
  start). The three quantile sorts of each stats line run on 3 threads. w107 (3.2 M vertices): 31.4 -> 18.1 s, outputs identical
  (diff -r); all 69 wraps' flattens 2554 -> 1827 job-s in the pipeline. What is left is the GPU SLIM itself: fp64 CG, 200 steps per
  iteration, every iteration at the cap (res 0.02-0.2), memory / fp64 bound on the 5060 Ti (1/64-rate fp64): all 69 wraps serially
  671 s with 396 s inside the solves, 469 s with 4 or 8 jobs (the card saturated). Keeping the CG's scalars on the device (no host
  round trip per step) changed nothing measurable (33.4 vs 32.4 s, 135 vs 133 s on the 25 smallest wraps; same bytes), so not kept.
  Faster from here changes the results: fewer CG steps, fp32 CG, decimation by vertex count (the recipe picks --decim from the .sfc's
  bytes, so 3 M-vertex wraps run at decim 1).
- stripimg: strip_refill.sh's papyrus gate (ink render x max(c12, c13) / 255) was a numpy one-liner with 2 GB float32 temporaries per
  0.5 G-pixel stripe: 28 s alone, 50-180 s beside the per-wrap renders, ~6 of stripimg's 11 minutes. `ufsm img-gate IMG G1 G2` does it
  through a 256 x 256 table built with float32 rounding forced by casts (numpy's bytes; tests/test_img_gate.py checks all 65536 pairs
  and both file layouts): ~5 s per stripe (the deflate reads). Its renders now run on card 1 (GPU path) too.
- The ink was then the critical path: 770 s from the end of the slabs (INKAT=slabs) = ~5 min of predicts (two grids) and three
  ink-blends one after the other (~125 s + 35 s of pyramid each, CPU, the card idle), while stripimg and perwrap waited for it (8.5 min
  idle after distort in full3). latink.sh runs the three blends at once (independent outputs, same bytes). INKWAIT=0 with INKAT=fields
  lets the slab lanes share the ink's card instead of waiting for all of it (INKAT=fields alone made the INKGPU lane wait: on a one-GPU
  run the whole slab stage). One-GPU runs (FITGPUS = INKGPU) now default to INKAT=fields INKWAIT=0: full4, 1832 -> 1422 s; the ink
  (10487 CPU s) slows rectosp / ref / slabs, but it is done before the snap. Runs with 2+ fit GPUs keep INKAT=slabs (not measured).
- Left on 0332 (full4): perwrap 612 s and stripimg 457 s side by side after the snap (perwrap = the GPU SLIM above; stripimg = 3
  renders per stripe, the ink and its two gates, ~10-30 s each, plus the mosaic), and the fields -> slabs chain (~620 s with the ink
  beside it). The ink's predicts (~0.6 s per window, ~1000 windows over its two grids) are item (4), fp4teach's / inksdk's kernels.

## NorMuon with --init-lr-mult (warm starts); try8 vs try6 was the warm start (2026-11-16, branch nmwarm-20261116)

**Why try8 lagged.** try8 (scratch2, from scratch, one card) sat at phase bce 0.681 (ln 2 = 0.693) for 4300 steps; HOLD p05x 0.474 / 0.489
at steps 2000 / 3000. try6 reached HOLD p05x 0.882 (ids0 0.810) at step 2357, u1-13790 0.887 / 0.813: HOLD is held out of every run
(boxes.tsv), so those are fair. try6 was not from scratch: it resumed try5, the scratch2 net warm-started from widened u1-13750
(--init-from --init-widen 1 --init-lr-mult 0.3 --init-lr-steps 2000; header init_inh, down_norm 1 from the donor). try4, from scratch,
had stalled the same way ("phase stuck at ln2 for 2600 windows"). Everything else of try8 matched try6 (lr, accum windows, P, um rungs).
The user (17:00): no more from-scratch runs; warm starts (try9).

**NorMuon + --init-lr-mult.** The trainer refused --init-lr-mult with --normuon / --muon-ns polar. The ext path (muon_ext) already takes
per-matrix lr multipliers (mx_lrm, --trunk-lr-mult); the inherited matrices (inh_has, the plain path's partition rule) now get init_lr
there, recomputed each step (the --init-lr-steps ramp). A bug on the way: muon_table returned early on its later calls with the host
descriptor list in collection order, while the device table had been partitioned inherited-first; the ext path indexes the multipliers
and NorMuon's row offsets by that host list, so from the second step they paired with the wrong matrices. The early return now applies
the same partition. test_init_lr: a NorMuon arm, two steps on one net; with the partition fix reverted its second step moves 6912
inherited parameters at multiplier 0 (FAIL), with it 0. Still refused with --init-lr-mult: --trunk-lr-mult, anvil, Muon-C, hyperball,
--muon-vr, the adaptive / cautious / Frobenius / AdEMAMix / attention-lr variants. Fast tier (card 0): 331 PASS, 1 SKIP, 2 NEED2.

## Unroll perf 1: the FBLEND half-stride grid ran each window up to 8 times; a per-run CT cache; field-blend tables (2026-11-16, branch unrollperf-20261116)

Profile of the 0332 unroll (desk, card 1 shared, CT over https, u1 13000, FBLEND on): fields 2767 s = grid-0 predict 368 s (505
windows) + **half-stride predict 2055 s (3138 windows)** + field-blend 342 s (4714 CPU s); rectosp 289; ref 291 (card 1 full: the CG
level 0 and the model / output passes fell back to the CPU; 36-79 s on a free card); slabs 377; snap 159 (CT decode over https 125 s).
- **Half-stride grid.** predict.c's shards start at the box. On a box off the window grid (`--grid-origin 256` with a 512-aligned box),
  every window whose interior covers k shards runs k times (once per shard, its cells clipped to the shard; up to 8x), so 3138 runs
  instead of ~650 windows. unroll.sh (fpred1) now starts that predict's box back on its own grid (box - origin multiple of the stride,
  up to 256 voxels earlier per axis; the end unchanged). field-blend crops an input that covers in[0]'s cells on the same grid to
  them (offset / origin / shape, as `--box` does for in[0]). Each window computes the same cells either way, so the blend is
  byte-identical. 512^3-cell box: 64 -> 27 runs, every chunk file equal. Whole fields stage on a 1024 x 2048^2 box of 0332 (master
  unroll.sh vs this one, same binary): 249 -> 88 s, half-stride predict 253 runs / 199 s -> 73 / 38 s, blended fields byte-identical
  (fields.json differs only in the input paths).
- **CT cache (UFSM_HTTP_CACHE, CTCACHE).** z3_open uses `$UFSM_HTTP_CACHE` as the chunk cache of any HTTP array opened without one,
  and predict defaults `--cache` (and with it the prefetcher) to it. unroll.sh exports `$O/ctcache` for an https CT (CTCACHE=0 off,
  CTCACHE=DIR elsewhere; the default dir is deleted at the end unless KEEPCT=1), so the second grid, wrap-check, unroll-qa,
  surf-stats, wrap-snap, render and faces read the CT locally after its first fetch. Grid-0 predict on a 32-window box: no cache
  34.4 s (reader 27.3 s of z3_read), cold cache 23.0 s (reader 15.3 s, prefetch 16 threads), warm 19.7 s (reader 4.9 s, GPU-bound
  at 0.52 s a window). Outputs byte-identical. A local CT root reads at the warm-cache rate
  (`ufsm mirror` of 0332 level 2, 5.8 GB in 51 s; predict reader 4.3 s for the 32 windows), so pods with CTROOT need no cache. (An
  earlier "local is as slow as https" reading was a test script that still pointed at https.)
- **field-blend.** sin / cos of the winding-mod-4 codes come from 256-entry tables (the same doubles), and the tile weight of each
  cell is stepped through x / y / z instead of a div / mod per cell. 512^3 cells: 73.4 -> 49.5 CPU s (7.2 -> 5.3 s at 16 threads),
  byte-identical to the 11-11 master binary. What is left: combine 29 %, atan2 / hypot ~9 %, the volcomp encode of the output 22 %.
- **recto-sp.** rr_peaks takes its 2R + 1 gaussian taps from a table built per call instead of an exp per tap per sample (exp
  was a third of the CPU). 1024 x 2048^2 0332 box: 294.8 -> 175.7 CPU s (25.6 -> 18.6 s), byte-identical; test_recto compares the
  smoothed floats with the per-sample exp at 5 sigmas (one past the 256-tap stack table).
- **Re-baseline with FBLEND off (master 5497da44 default: one grid; 0332 has m7, so rectosp runs and the ref is not streamed)**, 0332
  to snap, card 1 shared, old = 5dce8d46 script + binary with FBLEND=0, new = master: fields 264 -> 163 s (the CT cache's prefetch),
  rectosp 299 -> 148, ref 285 -> 382 (both on the CPU fallback, card full: old 128 rows per chunk at 6.9 GB available host memory,
  new 640 at 28.8 GB), slabs 285 -> 268, check 55 -> 28, trim 21 -> 5, snap 102 -> 47; total 1346 -> 1078 s, without the ref
  1061 -> 696 s (1.5x). wrap-check verdicts equal (65 / 8 / 3), slab fits s000-s022 byte-identical; from s023 on they and the snap
  (70 vs 71 wraps) follow the ref, which differs because of its chunk rows.
- **The ref depends on its chunk rows, which count-field picks from the free host memory.** Same 0332 fields (1536 x 2784 x 3008 at
  z 2048), `--chunk-rows 128` vs `384`: delta.f32 differs on 99.99 % of cells, p99 0.017 turn, max 1.03 turns, model coherence
  0.0589 vs 0.0605; the same chunk rows twice: byte-identical. So a ref (and everything after it) varies with how loaded the machine
  is. Passing a fixed `--chunk-rows` (unroll.sh's refcz, from CFMEM and the field shape only) would make it reproducible; left to the
  unroll owners (memory policy).
- **--skip-empty on u1's fields predict (speed side; the accuracy A/B is the lead's wbench skipthr.sh)**, grid 0, local CT, card 1
  shared, margin 1: 0332 whole box dense 243.2 s / thr 20 212.2 / 40 212.4 / 60 210.6 (mean level-0 active tile share .553 / .553 /
  .536); 1667 whole box dense 271.7 / thr 40 235.3 (share .529); Paris 4 z 8192..10240 full section dense 216.0 / thr 40 203.6
  (share .768). So -13 % per predict on 0332 / 1667, -6 % on packed Paris 4: ~60-75 s of a 683 / 872 s fields stage. The threshold
  hardly matters on these masked scans (air is 0). Whole windows are already dropped before the GPU (--occupancy: no CT > 0 in the
  interior on level 5; windows over absent chunks): 505 -> 473 run on 0332, 578 -> 524 on 1667; of the run windows 0 (thr 20) / 3
  (thr 60) have no active level-0 tile (`UFSM_SKIP_REPORT=1` now counts them). Not made default (u1 trained dense).
- **1667 (box at 0, local CT), fields + recto-sp** (desk, card 1 shared): fields 872 s (grid 0 373 s / 578 windows, half grid 272 s /
  567 windows, blend 225 s). The old half grid planned 3524 windows (+752 air) on the same box: ~2290 s at the old 0.65 s a window,
  so the old fields stage was ~2990 s (3.4x). recto-sp on its fields, warm m7 cache: 280 -> 157 s (2433 -> 1750 CPU s), byte-identical;
  max RSS 8.1 -> 11.3 GB (two source blocks in flight).
- **Boxes at 0** (1667, Paris 4 and every box starting at a volume face): the half-stride grid's box would start 256 voxels before
  the volume, which predict refused, so unroll.sh kept the old box there and the 6x window runs. predict now accepts a box up to
  a shard before the volume with --grid-origin (that CT reads as fill, as every window crossing a face already did), and unroll.sh
  always starts the box on the grid. 1667 box 0,1024,1024 + 1024^3: half grid 46 runs (+18 air) / 28.7 s -> 18 / 12.2 s, the
  blended planes identical. test_predict_fitgrid: a box at -64 equals the on-grid box on their common rows.
- **recto-sp, part 2** (0332 full box, warm m7 cache, same fields): phases were source decode 52 s, profiles 56, field load 23,
  blend 43, shard writes 18 of 207 s. The blend (net^(1-a) rsp^a per material cell, single-threaded exp / log) is a 256 x 256 table
  of the same codes (43 -> 4 s), and each 64-row block's source box is decoded by a helper thread while the previous block's
  profiles run. 225 -> 144 s, output byte-identical (sp and rsp chunk files). Larger row blocks (less halo re-decode) gave 173 -> 157 s
  at 256 rows for +8 GB RSS: not taken; a decoded-chunk cache (zcache) needs ~4 GB of shm for the reuse distance: not in the dev slice.
- **0332 end to end, UPTO=snap** (desk, card 1 shared with a 7 GB job at 100 % in both runs; master 7f2c69b8 + recto-sp):

  | stage | 15:02 run (5dce8d46, ufsm-inkspeed 926b3bb4) | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | fields | 2767 s (12560 CPU s) | **683 s** (5180): grid 0 254 s / 505 windows, half grid 248 s / 502 windows, blend 180 s |
  | rectosp | 289 | 223 (1468 CPU s) |
  | ref | 291 (CPU fallbacks: card 1 full) | 60 (GPU) |
  | slabs | 377 | 385 |
  | join / check / wraps / trim | 10 / 65 / 25 / 24 | 10 / 35 / 24 / 4 |
  | snap | 159 (CT decode over https 125 s) | **41** (cached CT) |
  | **total to snap** | **4007 s** (+ 575 s of DIRCOH refs) | **1465 s (2.7x)** |

  The ref and so everything after it differ from the 15:02 run: that run's ref ran its CG level 0 and model pass on the CPU (card 1
  full) and used another binary. The equality check is the fields stage: old (5dce8d46) vs new unroll.sh, same binary, on a full
  0332 cross-section (512 x 2784 x 3008 at z 4096, the box edges included): half grid 209 runs / 126 s -> 65 / 32 s, stage 166 -> 69 s,
  every chunk file identical.
- Tests: test_fblend blends with a larger second input (B's whole zarr arrays, one / two cells more per side) against the per-cell
  rules byte for byte, and refuses a smaller second input. test_http_reader checks that UFSM_HTTP_CACHE fills the same cache as --cache.
