## ink-ext: the CT chunk hash saw no z (ink9um 1.21x, half the CPU) (2026-11-16, branch inkspeed-20261116)

perf on ink9um over one PHerc1667 segment (194.6 Mpx, card 1, local CT): ct_find 45 % of the CPU samples, ct_tri 13 %, render_worker 8 %.
chash took bits 20-29 of key x 0x9E37..: those depend only on key bits 0-29 (the chunk's x and the low bits of y), never on z (bits 42+),
so all chunks of a band that differ in z alone probed one chain. A full 64-bit mix: wall 236 -> 196 s, user 1052 -> 560 s, render
36 -> 16 s, network 87 -> 85 s. Output: ink-ext is not bit-reproducible run to run (the old binary twice: 3.45 M of 206.8 M px differ by
1); old vs fixed differ by the same (3.42 M px, max 2). test_ink_ext_tiling runs again (its weights linked under ~/ufsm-data/inkext;
the PyTorch parity tests need upstream villa / hecate sources, not run here). Fast tier: 330 PASS, 1 SKIP, 2 NEED2 (card 0 in training).

## mcc 16cd2b7: sin + cos fused into sincos; straight-line loops of 4+ trips unroll to 1800 instructions (2026-11-16, branch mcc-host2-20261116)

Host-speed round 2. Per-function excess over clang (the 16 suite lines with the largest absolute excess, perf cycles:u): the
largest were fit_vox2 + fit_grad_terms (fit's CPU loss; 47 G, clang 17.6 G for all of cpu_loss_run), write_spatial_tm (20 G), and
cos / sin (31 G) where clang called sincos. Paired A/B (cpu_pair: both builds of a line back to back, min of 3; A/A noise +0.5 %).

| change (microc) | cycles | instructions | lines that move (instructions) |
|---|---|---|---|
| aba120a: sin (x), cos (x) of one x, one dominating the other: one sincos call (glibc's sincosf64 / sincosf32 alias) | -1.54 % | -0.51 % | patchid -7.7 % cycles, score_par -7.1 %, surflabels -2.1 % instructions |
| 16cd2b7: a straight-line body (no if / continue / break / return) of >= 4 trips unrolls up to 1800 IR instructions (was 1200; token pre-test 2400 -> 4800) | -1.08 % | -1.40 % | repair -11.5 % (cycles -5.3 %), fit_emb -8.2 %, fibertrace_dyad -5.4 %; none above +0.5 % |

The first unroll try (1200 -> 2400 for any body) regressed test_raster +26 % instructions: chamfer_reference's 13-neighbour loop
with an `if (out of box) continue` per neighbour, unrolled, computed all tests up front and spilled; branchy bodies keep 1200.
Results are bit-identical (glibc's sincos is sin's and cos's code); all 167 PTX sidecars identical.

Also measured and dropped: speculating an arm's load when the join reads the same address (makes write_spatial_tm's row clamp
loop vectorisable: +0.02 % instructions overall), turning off "a test of a just-loaded value stays a branch" (+3.7 % cycles),
splitting whole-record `= {0}` for slot_carve (13 refusals in all of ufsm's host code: no lever).

Gap to clang, same commit, paired, 118 single-thread CPU lines: instructions 1.429x (pin 367942e) -> 1.397x; cycles 1.34-1.36x
(the two runs in different load windows). What is left is broad: spilled scalars in long float functions (fit_vox2 still 2x),
the vectoriser's 64-bit index loops (write_spatial_tm's B0 row), CT decoders (volcomp vfx_decode_sub).

## mcc 367942e: spill-slot sharing could give two live values one stack slot (fixed; try8 not affected) (2026-11-16, branch mcc-rafix-20261116)

microc d2117c0 (11-15) shares a spill slot between the two sides of a copy when their live ranges never meet; the merged range list
is built by ra.c ranges_union, which held a pointer into the range pool (rg_next) across the pool's realloc. When the pool grew in
the middle of a union, the link went into the freed block and the merged list lost its tail, so a later merge could put a value on a
slot still live with another one. Found when an experimental loop split segfaulted in it (villawind.c -g); fixed by keeping the tail
by index (microc 367942e).

Scope, from an instrumented compiler that reproduces the old truncation (it gives the old frames byte for byte) and tests every merge
against the true ranges: try8's binary (ufsm a3d7b7eb, mcc a420db2, release): 448 host units, 0 bad merges. Pin 7add328 (master
0f8c0f18, verify): 3 bad merges in sample.c draw_. The fix changes 14 host objects (slot numbers and frame size only), PTX identical.
The loop split that found it, extended to registers a loop writes (copy in, copies back at each exit), measured neutral (paired A/B
+0.19 % cycles, geomean 0.998) and was dropped.

## mcc 7add328: host code, where the 1.3-1.4x against clang comes from; the slot-argument inline bonus (2026-11-16, branch mcc-host-20261116)

Priority 2 of the mcc round (host speed). Method: every fast-tier CPU line of tests/suite.txt without a gpu / slow / flaky tag and not
python (118 lines), one CPU each (UFSM_NCPU=1), perf stat cycles:u + instructions:u, 8 lines at a time. The desk is shared (load 15-25
from the other agents), so whole-run cycle totals drift by up to 10 % between runs; instruction counts do not. A/B now runs both builds
of a line back to back on one worker, min of 3 (A/A: total +0.49 %, geomean 1.005).

| 118 CPU lines, same commit, same window | G cycles | G instructions |
|---|---|---|
| clang + nvcc (llvm-verify, -march=native: AVX-512) | 925 | 2654 |
| clang, -mno-avx512f | 955 | 2768 |
| mcc 9aea0ba | 1245 | 3809 |

So mcc runs 1.38x clang's instructions at about the same IPC, and AVX-512 is worth ~3 % to clang: the gap is code quality (registers,
memory traffic, vectoriser coverage), not the vector width. GPU tests carry the same host gap (fast tier user CPU 1.52x).

What was tried:
- **Inline limit** (-finline-limit 12 default; 24 / 48 / 100): 100 is -2.3 % instructions, cycles within noise. More inlining alone is
  not the lever.
- **Spill choice** (ra.c spills the active interval with the least weight per length; weight alone, or per sqrt length): +2 % / +0 %
  instructions, +3 % cycles. Dropped.
- **Calls that pass a local's address** (microc 7add328, -finline-slotarg=160): one such call left in a function (volcomp's
  vf_rdec_init(&rd, ...) before the token loop) keeps the whole record in memory, so slot_carve / opt_split cannot put its fields in
  registers and every field access in the loop is a load or a store. Host call sites with an OP_SLOT argument now inline up to 160
  instructions (clang's SROA bonus); device code unchanged (all 169 units' PTX byte-identical). Paired A/B: cycles -1.02 %, geomean
  -1.9 %, instructions -0.35 %; test_flatten -26 %, test_idle_release -13 %, test_sampbias -12 %, test_crush -10 %; vf_decode_sub
  -10 %. Release .text 10.16 -> 11.04 MB, build time unchanged. Fast tier (card 1): 330 PASS, 1 SKIP, 2 NEED2. microc gate green.

Next (measured, not done): the register allocator spills whole intervals; its loop split (x64.c split_loops) only covers values a loop
reads and does not write, so loop-carried scalars (counters, accumulators, bit-reader state) cost a load, the op and a store per
iteration (vf_decode_sub's nnz_ac / hmask). Splitting written values at loops is the next step.

## mcc 9aea0ba: PTX packed as MPY (~10x), verify builds keep it in sidecar files; GPU tests are not slower (2026-11-16, branch mcc-sass-20261116)

Priority 1 of the mcc round (GPU test time, binary / build size). All numbers desk, same commit (master 9a9d46a4 + this branch),
mcc against clang + nvcc (llvm-verify / llvm-release).

**GPU test time: not a JIT problem once the cache is warm.** With ~/.cache/mcudahw warm (jit_warm.sh: 0 kernels to compile, 5 s
scan), the smoke tier on card 1: 32 GPU tests 73.7 s wall under mcc vs 78.8 s under clang + nvcc (0.93x), 34 CPU tests 13.4 vs
15.2 s. mcudahw's own work per process (unpacking, its text passes, hashing for the cache key) is ~3 % of test_unet's cycles; the
rest is libcuda and the test. The "1.6x" was most likely cold-cache runs (every changed kernel is JIT-compiled once per text,
GPU model and driver). The fast tier's CPU half: user time 500 s under mcc vs 385 s under clang (1.30x; wall 1.04x), which is the
host-code gap (next priority), not the GPU path. The full fast tier on card 1 (sidecar build vs llvm-verify, same commit): 207 GPU tests 1399 s wall vs 1239 s (1.13x), their user CPU 1341 vs 881 s (1.52x); 124 CPU tests 393 vs 337 s wall, user 463 vs 335 s (1.38x); suite wall 264 vs 236 s. The GPU tests' extra time is the host code they run (references, data setup), not the JIT.

**MPY packing (microc 413bb68, `--cuda-ptx-pack=2`, the default).** MPZ (11-15) was LZ77 with a varint distance per copy. PTX
instantiations of one template differ in a few constants and register numbers, so copies break off and resume at the same
distance; MPY codes three repeat offsets in 1-3 bits and entropy-codes literals, counts, lengths and offsets (canonical prefix
codes of at most 11 bits, prices from a greedy parse of a 2 MB sample). `--cuda-ptx-pack=3` parses optimally (forward DP over 1024
positions), 1 is MPZ, 0 plain. The unpacked text is byte for byte the same, so mcudahw's JIT cache keys do not change.

| ufsm's 124 release units (337.6 MB of PTX) | packed | lp_f4fwd_i0p (18.6 MB): cycles |
|---|---|---|
| MPZ (a420db2) | 87.9 MB | ~1.8 G |
| MPY pack 2 (greedy) | 43.5 MB | ~1.9 G |
| MPY pack 3 (optimal) | 34.2 MB | ~10 G |
| zstd -9 / -19 --long (reference) | 37.3 / 28.9 MB | 0.6 / 22 G |

**Sidecar files (microc 9aea0ba, `--cuda-ptx-file`; ufsm `UFSM_PTX_FILE`, on in verify builds).** Every suite binary links every
kernel unit, so each carried the same packed PTX. Now mcc writes a unit's record to OBJ.ptxz and the object keeps the plain
prologue (what mcudahw's first-launch scan reads), two FNV-1a hashes and the file's absolute path; the bodies are read when first
wanted, and a missing or stale file is refused with its name (`MCUDA_PTXDIR=DIR`: a moved build directory). Release binaries stay
self-contained.

| build (-j 8, desk) | wall | user / sys | size |
|---|---|---|---|
| release, mcc a420db2 (MPZ) | 15.9 s | 92.6 / - s | build/ufsm 108 MB |
| release, MPY pack 2 | 14.4 s | 79.3 / 10.3 s | build/ufsm 63.1 MB |
| release, MPY pack 3 (UFSM_PTX_PACK=3) | 23.7 s | 145.3 / 10.3 s | build/ufsm 53.7 MB |
| release, clang + nvcc | - | - | build/ufsm 57.9 MB (31.4 MB fatbin) |
| verify suite-bins, mcc a420db2 | 33.3 s | 170.9 / 47.0 s | 19 GB (test binaries ~140 MB) |
| verify, MPY pack 2 | 31.1 s | 150.6 / 35.7 s | 9.6 GB |
| verify, MPY pack 2 + sidecars | 23.6 s | 148.2 / 24.9 s | 1.8 GB (60 MB of .ptxz; test_ink_splat 23 MB) |
| verify, clang + nvcc (cold ccache) | 9 m 13 s | 53 m user | 7.4 GB |

Pack 2 stays the default everywhere (pack 3 costs +9 s on a full release build for 9 MB). Checks: the unpacked PTX of every unit is

## The ink builder's GPU buffers under one budget (2026-11-16, try7's step-450 death)

try7 (one card) logged "inkfly gpu: out of memory (nn_inkfly.cu:169)" at sampler start-up, switched the on-the-fly ink to the CPU
for good, and died at step 450 with "CUDA error unknown error at a low-precision kernel (lp_check's latch)" before best.ckpt. The
cause: every sampler worker kept its own stream and growing buffers on the training card (static __thread ictx), unbounded and
never freed, beside the trainer; the file's header claimed one context behind a mutex, which the code never had. Now all threads'
buffers are under one budget (UFSM_INKFLY_GPU_MB, default 1024) and above a free-memory reserve for the trainer
(UFSM_INKFLY_RESERVE_MB, default 1536, cudaMemGetInfo); a chunk that does not fit, or a stream that cannot be made, goes to the
CPU for that chunk only (return 1) and the GPU path stays on; over-budget chunks are counted (inkfly_gpu_over) and logged at
1 and every 1000. Buffers are kept between chunks (cudaFree synchronises the device and would stall the trainer).
test_ink_splat: 8 chunks on the GPU, 0 of 11.4 M voxels differ; test_ink_splat~over (UFSM_INKFLY_GPU_MB=1): 0 GPU chunks,
8 over the budget, 0 voxels differ.

## The fused fit kernel's winding pass from planes (UFSM_PRED_FIT_W4P), and the fused kernel under mcc (2026-11-15, branch univinf-port-20261115)

Ported from wip-snap-univinf-20261115 (efe2e22f, 11-12, written on the h 8 kernel; the WIP drain, /vesuvius/ufsm/wipdrain/ledger.md).
`predict --fit-zarr` with the fused kernel (nn_fit_accum_lat) and a winding pair (--task unwrap2's channels 9-10): every 8^3 block
recomputed the upsampling and the fine stem on 3 partner regions (the block shifted by +d along z, y, x) only to read the pair's logits
there. `nn_fit_accum_lat_w4p` instead writes the pair's fp16 logits once, in pass A (the block pass, its blocks extended by d along each
axis so the partners are covered; no sums there), into `wl` [2][planes][W][W]. Pass B (`fit_w4_plane_k`) sums the winding terms from
`wl` in the region path's order: h 8, one thread per accumulator over the block's 512 voxels; h 1 / 2 / 4, one thread per field cell
(as the 11-14 small-h path). The values are fp16-exact either way (upsampled fp16, then + the stem's fp16-rounded term), so the
accumulators are the same bytes. A sub-cell pair (sbase >= 0 and ch_w4 < 2) keeps the regions.
- predict: on by default (`UFSM_PRED_FIT_W4P=0`: the regions); the planes are 4 B per voxel of the chunk's planes + d (fzW, logged
  once), < 1/5 of the plane path's head planes, which the fused path does not allocate.
- Tests: test_fit_lat (h 8 / 4 / 2, stem and sub-cell on / off, windows on and off the 4-voxel grid): 0 of the 12 + 9 accumulator
  planes differ for w4p, and the winding planes are non-empty (512 of 512 cells with pairs at h 8). test_predict_heads (part 0):
  fused w4p == fused regions == plane path for every field at --fit-h 8, and now at --fit-h 2 with `UFSM_PRED_FIT_FUSED_SMALLH=1`
  (w4p and regions) == the plane path, whole volume and the off-grid box (the end-to-end check unrollperf-20261112 had, ported).
- Kernel bench (test_fit_lat UFSM_TEST_BENCH=1, 256^3 window, stem + sub-cell on, d 16, card 1 under the exclusive suite lock):

| build | h | plane path | fused, regions | fused, w4p | fused without the winding pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mcc (verify) | 8 | 5.3 ms | 13.2 | **11.2** | 8.6 |
| mcc (verify) | 2 | 4.9 | 12.8 | **10.8** | 8.2 |
| llvm-verify (nvcc) | 8 | 6.3 | 5.4 | 5.4 | 3.7 |
| llvm-verify (nvcc) | 2 | 4.6 | 5.0 | 5.0 | 3.4 |

  w4p is 15 % faster than the regions under mcc and the same under nvcc, so it is the default. (unrollperf-20261112 measured nvcc
  cells 2: plane 6.0 vs fused 5.6 ms, cells 8: 7.8 vs 5.5, on 11-12.)
- **Open (not changed here): under mcc the fused kernel is 2.1-2.6x slower than the plane path** (11.2 vs 5.3 ms at h 8). nvcc's
  fused kernel takes 5.4 ms, so it is mcc's PTX for fit_accum_lat_k (the mma16816 stem and the shared-memory union), not the design.
  predict's default at --fit-h 8 is the fused kernel (`UFSM_PRED_FIT_FUSED=0`: the planes); production unrolls run --fit-h 2, which
  takes the plane path unless `UFSM_PRED_FIT_FUSED_SMALLH=1`, so they are unaffected. Either the default at h 8 follows the compiler
  or mcc's code for this kernel gets fixed (reported to mcc-gpu); the fit part is a small share of a fields predict either way.

## conv_fwd_f4_k: double-buffered weight stages, opt-in (UFSM_F4_WDB=1) (2026-11-15, branch convfuse-port-20261115, off wip-convfuse-20261114)

conv_fwd_f4_k (the MX-fp4 3^3 forward for Cip >= 96, i.e. every trunk conv above level 0) loads each 32-channel chunk's weights in two
stages of 7 tap pairs, each behind a barrier: load, sync, MMA, sync. The parked convfuse WIP gives it two stage buffers: stage s + 1 is
issued by cp.async (16-byte rows; the scale pairs by plain stores) before stage s's MMA, so the load overlaps the tensor cores, when
two blocks per SM still fit (2 x (smem + 1 KB) <= the SM's shared memory; the fused-upsample instances keep one buffer). The port fixed
one race: stage 0's copies were not committed as their own cp.async group, so the first `wait_group 1` could pass with them in flight.
Same MMAs in the same order: outputs bit-identical (bench hashes equal; test_mx4_wide's exact references pass with it on and off).

Measured (mcc build-verify, card 1 shared with merge3's suites at 100 % utilisation, so +-2 % noise; min of 10, two runs):
256->256 @96^3 40.7 / 37.0 ms one buffer vs 37.3 / 37.2 two; 256->320 @96^3 46.4 / 45.7 vs 46.7 / 46.4 (0.98-0.99x, slower both
runs); 448->288, 288->288 @48^3 and the GN+SiLU 256->256 / 448->448 within 1 %. No measured gain (the weight stage is a small part
beside the input staging and MMAs at these widths), so it stays off by default: UFSM_F4_WDB=1 / lp_f4_wdb(1) turns it on. Kept tested
by test_mx4_wide~F4_WDB=1 (fast tier); tests/bench_f4wide.c is the A/B (re-measure on an idle card before changing the default).

## Label compression: the labcomp codec for winding-code rasters (2026-11-15, branch labcomp-port-20261115, off wip-labcomp)

Goal (user 11-15): the rendered training labels small enough to upload once and let pods download them instead of computing them.
This lands the first codec and its plumbing; the upload itself is not part of it (no credentials, desk uplink 3 MB/s).

- `src/labcomp.{c,h}`: one 128^3 uint8 chunk per stream ("LBC" + kind + version), a zarr v3 inner codec `labcomp` (inside
  sharding_indexed, before crc32c), so a packed store is an ordinary sharded array. Kind 1 `codes` (winding-code rasters, exact): the
  support (code != 0) as volcomp's lossless mask (mode 5), then every support voxel in raster order against its 13 causal
  26-neighbours: "equals their majority code" (adaptive binary, context agreement x neighbour count), else "equals the second most
  frequent", else the byte through an adaptive bit tree; LZMA-style integer range coder, 15-bit probabilities, deterministic. A sheet
  carries one code over its patch, so the stream is essentially the sheet geometry.
- Readers: zarr3.c parses the codec (`z3_meta.lbc`, uint8 128^3 only, the only coding codec of its chain) and decodes in
  decode_into; band_onfly's tile_gpu (the on-the-fly pair-rule phase) decodes labcomp chunks on the host into its pack and uploads them
  as raw chunks (no device decoder yet). Both reach lbc_decode through weak references (zarr3.c refuses a labcomp array in a binary
  built without labcomp.c), so the test targets listing zarr3 / band_onfly link unchanged.
- `ufsm labcomp-pack IN_ARRAY OUT_ARRAY [--threads N] [--verify 1]`: re-encodes a uint8 label array (stored chunks only, the chunk
  map), every chunk decoded again and compared (--verify 0: off); OUT never overwritten; attributes kept plus a `labcomp` record.

Numbers. Probe (labcomp agent, /vesuvius/ufsm/labcomp/probe/r2_codes.txt: 256^3 boxes of real 1667 / 175B / A48 codes rasters):
6.5-24x smaller than volcomp lossless (380-1330x vs raw), one box 2.2x (A48_2: 1.4 % conflict voxels, eq-neighbour 0.83). Phase
labels (r2_ph*.txt) would gain 1.3-1.7x lossless, ~1.6-3x lightly lossy: not implemented (kind 1 only). test_labcomp (mcc
build-verify, CPU): synthetic sheets 0.23 bit per support voxel (157x vs raw), +0.5 % foreign codes 0.33 bit; random bytes 8.1 bit
(0.99x); a 300 x 260 x 520 store packed 42x smaller than volcomp lossless, read back equal. Speed, one desk thread: encode 73-98,
decode 85-93 Mvox/s per sheets chunk; z3_read of the whole store 55-57 Mvox/s vs 383-391 for volcomp lossless, so labcomp is a
transport / archive format: a store a trainer reads hot should stay volcomp (or be unpacked after download). test_phase_onfly: the wind
fixture's codes repacked give the same phase as phase-raster on the CPU and the GPU path.

## count-field: the density count rescaled at the solve (--pool-split, --rho-solve, --rho-map) (2026-11-15, branch geocount-port-20261115, off wip-snap-geocount)

The geo-count audit (11-14) found the density head counting 1.2-1.3x the GT sheets on Paris 4 and 1667. `--rho-scale K` already
scales the density term, but at pooling time, so every K costs a new pass 1 (~1 h on a whole scroll). Opt-in, off by default (outputs
unchanged without the flags): `--pool-split 1` keeps the density term's level-0 pooled sums apart (Sd, Gd; S / G still hold density +
phase), CPU pooling (the GPU pool path does not split; with the flag the chunk pools on the CPU); with `--pool-cache FILE` they go to /
come from `FILE.dens` (4 float32 planes over the level-0 solve grid). `--rho-solve K` (global) and / or `--rho-map FILE` (float32 per
level-0 solve cell, z-major; non-finite or <= 0: 1) then add (K - 1) Gd to G before the coarser levels are summed, the phase-gradient
targets (--phase-w) untouched; either implies --pool-split, and a cached pool without its .dens is refused. The log line gives the
Sd-weighted mean K. The quality A/B (K from the GT sheet counts per region on Paris 4 / 1667) is the open next step; geo-count's
prototype had no real-data numbers.

Test (test_countfield, mcc build-verify): with no --phase-w, G is the density term alone, so K x the split sums equals --rho-scale K's
pooling up to float rounding. A --pool-split run into a cache, then --rho-solve 0.75 and --rho-map (0.75 everywhere) from that cache:
wc vs the plain run 3.8e-6 turn, vs --rho-scale 0.75 8.6e-6 turn (both), over 52608 cells; the rest of test_countfield passes.

## The volcomp decoders stay IEEE under fast math (UFSM_EXACT_HOST / UFSM_EXACT_CU) (2026-11-15, branch fastmath-port-20261115, off wip-snap-fastmath)

The fast-math round (fmfix, below) found that the GPU decoder's IDCT (nn_gpudec, `-use_fast_math`) and the host's (zarr3.c:
volcomp.h + volcomp_fast.h, `-ffast-math`) round apart by +-1 on rare voxels, and that the nets amplify one such voxel: per-window
GroupNorm statistics and MX-fp4 block scales spread it over the window (test_predict_heads (1d): 16 % of the rv bytes, max 123). It
answered with tolerances. This takes the other way: the two decoders are compiled IEEE in every build, so a CT window is the same bytes
whichever decoder made it, and the same bytes as the reference decoder the stores were checked with. CMakeLists.txt: `UFSM_EXACT_HOST`
(zarr3) gets `-fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno` after the common flags (the fast-math host signed zeros were the
host-side half: -fsigned-zeros on zarr3.c alone restored it, fm round); `UFSM_EXACT_CU` (nn_gpudec) gets the strict CUDA flags
(`-fmad=false` under mcc) whether or not UFSM_STRICT_MATH is on. test_gpudec / test_volcomp_fast build their reference decoder with the
same IEEE flags and compare byte for byte again (fm_cmp_u8 tolerance 0 / 0); test_ct_gpu_decode compares GPU vs CPU decode, the
batch hashes and the device inputs byte for byte in every build (before: only under strict); test_predict_heads (1d) the CT windows and
the rv / ink outputs of the device-read runs byte for byte.

Numbers (mcc build-verify, desk, 2026-11-15; PHerc0139 9.362 um level 0, a 512 x 1024 x 1024 box at 8000, 2500, 2500, 3 runs each,
master d7910396 = the fast-math decoders vs this branch):
- GPU decode (`ufsm read`, UFSM_GPU_DECODE=1, card 1 while merge3's suites shared it): master's output differs from the host decode on
  3306 of 537 M voxels; this branch's equals it byte for byte. Speed within the noise of the shared card: 665 / 713 / 787 vs
  814 / 696 / 670 Mvox/s, GPU round trips 0.36 s in both (8328 substreams).
- Host decode (UFSM_GPU_DECODE=0): 518 / 539 / 582 vs 548 / 551 / 593 Mvox/s, the same bytes in this box (the +-1 voxels are rare; the
  decode is mostly the serial tANS chain, the IDCT a small part).
- Tests (mcc verify, card 1): test_gpudec, test_volcomp_fast, test_volcomp, test_z3_sink, test_ct_gpu_decode, test_predict_heads parts
  0-2 pass, all decode comparisons exact.

## Eval tags carry their checkpoint's identity (scripts/wbench/ckid.sh) (2026-11-15, branch evalfix-port-20261115, off wt-evalfix)

Eval audit 11-14 #21: wbench / wgate / ueval rows carried no checkpoint hash, and a rerun of a tag with another checkpoint overwrote
`$O/ckpt` while the old fields, predictions and result rows stayed and were reused (every stage skips work whose output exists). Now
`ckid_check DIR CKPT` (sourced) writes `DIR/ckid` = sha256 prefix (16 hex) + the header's `"step":N`, and refuses (exit 2) a tag dir
that already holds another checkpoint's id; `FORCE_TAG=1` accepts it and says the outputs mix. wbench.sh (`runs/TAG`, plus
`res/TAG.ckid` beside the result tsv), wgate.sh (`gate/TAG`) and ueval.sh (`E/TAG`, the id in its first log line) call it. Cost: one
sha256 of the checkpoint per run, 1.7 s for the 2.08 GB admuon start.ckpt (page-cached). Test: tests/test_ckid.sh (fast tier, CPU, 0.05 s): accept,
rerun, refuse (the old id kept), FORCE_TAG, missing file.

## Muon update scaling (--muon-scale rms) and cautious weight decay (--muon-cwd 1) (2026-11-15, branches muonscale-20261115, cwd-20261115)

Two opt-in Muon options, both off by default. They are implemented and tested; the quality A/B is deferred by the 11-15 drain order (plan
below). They come from main's "improve adaptive Muon further" queue (items 3 and 4 of batch 1).

**Shape-matched update scale, `--muon-scale rms --muon-rms r` (Moonlight, Liu et al. 2025, arXiv 2502.16982).** An orthogonalised
Co x K direction has element RMS 1 / sqrt(max(Co, K)). Under the default kj scale sqrt(max(1, Co / K)) a 3^3 conv (K = 27 Ci >= Co) moves
lr / sqrt(27 Ci) per element:

| Ci | K = 27 Ci | kj element RMS / lr | rms element RMS / lr (r 0.2) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 864 | 0.034 (1/29) | 0.2 |
| 256 | 6912 | 0.012 (1/83) | 0.2 |
| 448 | 12096 | 0.0091 (1/110) | 0.2 |
| 1x1 attention linear, C 288 | 288 | 0.059 (1/17) | 0.2 |

The rms mode multiplies by r sqrt(max(Co, K)), so every matrix, conv or linear, gets element RMS r x lr and Muon takes AdamW-sized lrs.
Muon-C and `--muon-fro` (O rescaled to a nominal RMS) target r under it. The per-matrix reference path `nn_muon` now follows the scale
mode; before, it ignored `--muon-scale spectral` as well. lars (`--muon-lars`) uses the same scale function. To match the base
update's total norm, lr_rms = lr_kj sqrt(sum Co / sum Co K) / r. For the scratch2 widths (256 .. 448, four 3^3 convs per level)
that is 0.003 x 0.0104 / 0.2 = **1.5e-4**. Moonlight's recipe (Muon lr = AdamW lr = 3e-4) is ~2x that norm. The net effect: narrow and
1x1 matrices move less than under kj, wide ones relatively more.

Test (test_admuon, card 1): from the same state, the rms step equals the kj step times r sqrt(max(Co, K)) / sqrt(max(1, Co / K)) per
matrix. The worst relative error is 2.1e-5 (plain), 2.1e-5 (ext), 3.7e-5 (ext + NorMuon), 2.9e-5 (ext + fro). The element RMS / (lr r)
lands in [0.830, 0.914]: the quintic NS leaves singular values below 1. Under fro it is exactly 1.0000. mcc 9f63cdd (verify preset) and clang + nvcc
give the same numbers.

**Cautious weight decay, `--muon-cwd 1` (Chen, Liang et al. 2025, arXiv 2510.12402).** On the Muon matrices an element decays only where
the step u = lr s O (subtracted) has the weight's sign (u w >= 0, so step and decay both shrink |w|). Elsewhere the decay would fight the
optimizer's direction and is skipped. AdamW parameters are unchanged. Off, the update is the plain expression in the plain rounding order.
Test (test_muoncwd, card 1): plain batch, ext and ext + NorMuon match the host reference to 3.0e-7 relative to |w| under mcc 9f63cdd
(1.3e-6 under clang + nvcc). The mask decays 50.1 %
of the elements. cwd on at wd 0 is bit for bit the plain step. Default `--wd 0.01` x Muon lr 0.003 is 3e-5 per update, which
shrinks the weights only ~1 % over 300 updates. Cautious decay matters only with a real decay (`--muon-wd-mult 10`, wd 0.1).

**Deferred A/B (WIP plan, script `scripts/opt/mab_arm.sh`).** One from-scratch arm per run on one card, P 256, 1500 windows, NorMuon,
WSD warmup 150 cooldown 0.2, --accum 5, --det 1, seeds 7 and 8, held-out validation at the end. The run directory is deleted afterwards and
the log kept. Arms:
- `base` at 0.003 / 3e-4 (try7);
- `base` at LR=0.0015 (the pending LR pair);
- `rms` at MLR=1.5e-4 (the norm-matched lr; it isolates the per-layer redistribution);
- `wd10` vs `cwd10` (Muon decay x10, plain vs cautious).
Report paired per-10-window differences with block-bootstrap CIs (scripts/opt/pair_ab.py), per head (phase, wind4 separately), gn, and the held-out val.
The noise floor is ~0.01. Batch 2 after that: tuned NS coefficients with fewer iterations (`--muon-ns polar` exists: measure
orthogonality error, step time and fewer iterations), the conv reshape (out x in·27 vs per-tap vs in-major; Muon-C exists as the per-
frequency variant), and a GNS-driven schedule.
## Ink teachers: MX-fp4 gambiarra / dino3d, fast prep, 2-D teacher labels (ink-teach) (2026-11-15, branch inkteach-20261115)

**Part A: the 3-D teachers fast.** gambiarra (24.5 M params, 59.1 GMAC per 64^3 output crop = 225 kMAC / output voxel) ran 11.9 ms /
crop in the fp16 xnet (convs 71 %, InstanceNorm 22 %): ~1 Mvox/s end to end at stride 32. New in xnet (`UFSM_XNET_MX=6` MX-fp4 ue8m0
scales per 16-K block, `=5` NVFP4-style ue4m3 block scales + an fp32 per-row weight scale):
- `conv_mxh`: halo-tiled 3x3x3 MX-fp4 conv (`mma.sync m16n8k64 kind::mxf4nvf4`), 256-voxel output tiles staged with ldmatrix and
  per-lane tap offsets, tile configs (2,4,32) / (4,4,16) / (4,8,8): 1.09 ms for the 64^3 32->32 conv at B 16 (~107 TMAC/s, ncu).
  `conv_mx`: generic MX-fp4 implicit GEMM (stride 2, 1x1 skips, the transposed conv) with the tconv shuffle + bias + quantise in the
  epilogue, straight into the decoder's concat buffer.
- InstanceNorm sums out of the conv epilogues (double atomics); one fused apply (`k_inq`) = norm + residual + LReLU + the next conv's
  MX copy; the head fused into the last apply; the 1-channel first block: the stem recomputed from constant-memory weights, its 1x1
  skip IN analytic; pooled skips as a 2^3 stride-2 conv with w / 8.
- `UFSM_XNET_FQ=A,W` (+ `_MASK`): fake quantisation for accuracy probes. Logit 1-corr vs fp16 (gambiarra): act/weights 8/8 0.002,
  5/5 0.029, 6/6 0.040, 4/4 0.040: the weights dominate. dino3d MX6 0.008, MX5 0.003.
- `test_xmx`: the MX conv against a host reference (formats 6 and 5, the halo and generic shapes).
Network time 11.9 -> 1.36 ms / crop (ncu, base clocks: ~190 Mvox/s at 4.8 um without overlap); dino3d 1080 -> 164 ms per 256^3 crop.

`ink3d-ext --fast 1`: the crop grid aligned to 16 output voxels, the p1 / p99 of each crop's parent (crop + 32 per side) as a sum of
16^3-block histograms computed once per slab (exact, the published np.percentile), LUT, gather and the 2^3 pooling on the GPU, rolling
slab reads; `--tile T` (64, 128) with parent T + 64.

## mcc round: microc main 441a1a1 is ufsm's compiler; the encoder u8 tolerance 4 (2026-11-15, branch mccround-20261115)

The user made mcc the only supported compiler. The clang + nvcc presets (llvm-release / llvm-verify) keep building for comparison.
The fast tier at microc main 441a1a1 (475ac78 + mainvfma 626fa40: vsearch / vector FMA / ptx setp.ftz + strip 688b3c6), desk card 1,
release build/ beside build-verify, jit_warm first: 319 PASS, 2 NEED2 (one card), 2 SKIP (data), 1 FAIL. All 32 failures of the
first mcc round (fc8e90e) pass. The one FAIL was test_predict_heads part 1: GPU vs CPU fit-field encoder, rv 9.6 plane, 1828 of
16.7 M bytes differ, max 4. clang + nvcc stays within 2, so this is mcc's host float code (the u8 encoder), and an mcc strict build
is byte for byte. Decision (lead, 11-15): the tolerance becomes FM_ENC_MAXD = 4 (tests/fm_tol.sh) for the rv / ink planes in
fast-math builds; strict math stays exact. The host-math delta is a low-priority microc item (mcc-host: most likely the lossy

Disk: an mcc build-verify is ~65 GB (every binary embeds ~330 MB of uncompressed PTX vs nvcc's ~68 MB compressed SASS fatbins);

## Skip-empty: masked convs bypass the ring kernels; test_skip_empty racecheck QUICK (2026-11-15, branch skipmask-20261115)

test_skip_empty~racecheck FAILed on the pod after 3289 s: section (5), at its racecheck width 64, reported masked forward 0, backward-data 0,
wgrad 0 and gx bytes differing. This was neither a launch failure nor an OOM (the cgroup oom_kill counter stayed at 4). Only `launch_f4`
(lp_f4fwd.cuh) applies the mask (`lp_skip_get`), and `fwd_f4_t` sends Cip 32 / 64 convs to the ring kernels (`launch_f4r`, and `f4ru` for
dec0.c1) before it reaches `launch_f4`. So any 32 / 64-wide conv on a level grid ran dense silently in the forward and was never marked.
For backward-data, a masked conv whose gy is 32 / 64 wide would land on the ring kernel and abort in `nn_skip_bwd_check`; that path was
loud, not divergent.

Fix: `nn_skip_masks(xs, sp)` (nn_skip.cu) gives `launch_f4`'s decision without `lp_skip_get`'s side effects: forward means the output grid
is a level and there is no SR; backward-data means the conv was seen masked. When it is set, `fwd_f4_t` skips `launch_f4r` / `f4ru`.
`p16_f4` (input <= 16 channels) and `f4u` (the fused upsample) still run dense. Their forward is consistent (the conv is not marked, so its
backward runs dense too), and a masked conv whose backward-data reaches them aborts in `nn_skip_bwd_check` as before.

test_skip_empty (5) now runs at widths 256 and 64. At 64 the masked bwd-data matches the dense one on the zeroed gy byte for byte, and the
wgrad / bias rel is 0 (desk and pod). Under racecheck the test runs a QUICK size: P 32, material z < 6 (level 0: 2 of 4 tile planes active),
no margin profile, and width 64 only in (5). At P 64 racecheck took ~110 s per forward on the pod's RTX PRO 4000 (setup + (1) 443 s,
each margin forward 105-126 s). QUICK under racecheck: 505 s on the pod, 0 hazards, oom_kill unchanged (suite EST 760 s);
synccheck (full size) 3 s, 0 errors. test_memws and test_split_ab (the skip-empty CLI paths) pass.

Cost of the bypass at the try7 config: with try7's argv (widths 256-448, `--lat-c 29`, P 768, `UFSM_SKIP_DEBUG=1`), exactly one conv takes
the bypass, the level-0 input conv 32 -> 256 at 192^3. Bench `/vesuvius/integ19/skbench/mb/bench_skipring.c` (desk 5060 Ti, MX-fp4,
SR on, mean of 10). It times the masked `launch_f4` against `UFSM_SKIP_RING=1`, the old path (ring forward, dense and unmarked, so
backward-data and wgrad run dense too):

| active tile planes | masked fwd / bwd-data / wgrad, ms | ring (dense), ms | masked total vs ring |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 of 24 | 7.78 / 4.67 / 20.88 | 15.27 / 14.55 / 35.11 | 33.3 vs 64.9 |
| 12 of 24 | 10.97 / 8.06 / 25.41 | 15.29 / 14.56 / 35.13 | 44.4 vs 65.0 |
| 18 of 24 | 14.32 / 11.57 / 32.59 | 15.29 / 14.56 / 35.13 | 58.5 vs 65.0 |
| 24 of 24 | 17.69 / 14.70 / 36.28 | 15.30 / 14.58 / 35.18 | 68.7 vs 65.1 |

The bypass costs at most +3.6 ms a window, at 100 % active. At the try6 step rate (0.28 windows/s over 2 GPUs, ~7 s a window a GPU)
that is <0.1 %, under the 2 % threshold, so there is no follow-up to put the mask into the ring kernels. With air in the window the
masked path is faster (-6 to -32 ms). `UFSM_SKIP_RING=1` stays as the A/B knob. `p16_f4` and `f4u` are not bypassed (see above).

Runs affected: scratch2 try4 through try6 (11-14 08:22 onward, `--skip-empty 1 --skip-thr 0 --skip-margin 1`, `--lat-c 29`) ran that input
conv dense in all three directions. Forward and backward were consistent: the conv was never marked, so its backward ran dense, and the
masked-bwd-data-on-a-ring-kernel case aborts in `nn_skip_bwd_check` and never fired. Their losses and gradients are those of the net as
run, so no correctness caveat applies; they only skipped less than `--skip-empty` reported. try7 (not launched) gets the masked conv.

## Fast-math round: the last four fast-tier failures (2026-11-15, branch fmfix-20261115, off fastmath-20261114)

The fm integration (mega-audit 087325a0 + fastmath 9561823b, desk) left four fast-tier failures. Each checked against the master
fcfbb0b7 build and a `-DUFSM_STRICT_MATH=ON` build of the same tree:

- **test_predict_heads (1d), device-read CT**: 16 % of the rv bytes differ (max 123), always the same two of the eight 160^3
  windows. Not a race or an indexing bug: master 5 of 5 and strict 2 of 2 byte-identical, fm deterministic (3 runs equal), and
  `UFSM_PRED_DEVREAD_GPU=0` (every chunk decoded on the CPU, then uploaded and gathered into the same device windows)
  byte-identical to the host reader. The cause is the fast-math GPU decoder: its IDCT rounds apart from the host's by +-1 on 92 of
  16.7 M voxels (`ufsm read` with UFSM_GPU_DECODE=1 against 0; 140 of 32.8 M in the dumped windows). In the 3-step fixture net,
  per-window GroupNorm and fp4 activations spread one changed input voxel over its whole window (up to 52 codes), and which windows
  are affected depends on the window's z-score: with `--norm 42,52` three other windows differ. A 2e-5 change of the z-score alone
  changes nothing (`--norm 42,52.001`: 0 bytes), because the 8-bit input quantiser absorbs it. So the outputs of the GPU-decoded runs
  cannot be compared under fast math. (1d) now compares the CT windows the net saw (`UFSM_PRED_CTDUMP=FILE`, every window in order:
  within 1 on 1e-4 of the voxels) and the outputs of a `UFSM_PRED_DEVREAD_GPU=0` run byte for byte. Under strict, everything is
  still compared byte for byte.
- **test_heads part 0**: no NaN, no layout bug, and not fast math. `tests/heads_ref.txt` dated from 11-11. The strict build (which
  repeats itself run to run) and the master build also log 0 of 4 layouts equal. fibn's 5768 against 5488 supervised voxels is the
  same in the strict and fm builds (b93713bc's fibre-normal halo stopped dropping seam voxels), and gn at step 1 moved with
  870900d2's head-gradient scale. The 7 reference lines were rewritten by the strict build: strict matches exactly
  (4 + 2 + 1 layouts), and fm is within the per-step tolerances.
- **test_spatial_augment parts 0 / 1**: real rounding, plus a test bug. The CT channel's fast-math error is absolute. Both writers
  pull the source coordinate through the same float terms in a different order, so a coordinate can move by a couple of fp32 ulps
  of P, and trilinear interpolation multiplies that by the steepest corner difference (up to the span of the CT value table). The
  measured result is 2 fp16 ulps at |x| 0.06-0.12, |d| <= 1.2e-4 at P 128. The bound is now `warp_tol` =
  6 x gain x span x P 2^-23 + 1e-5 (2 ulps of P per axis, 3 axes): 7.7e-4 to 8.3e-4 at P 128 (depending on the plan's span),
  1.5e-3 to 1.6e-3 at P 256, 3.3e-3 at P 512. No element exceeds it in the full tier, and a wrong corner or LUT entry moves a value
  by about 0.8. Part 1's failures were all bf16 (fmt 2) configurations: ws_cmp decoded
  bf16 bits as fp16, so its absolute check was meaningless there. It now decodes each format as itself.

## Stride-2 fp4 forward (conv_fwd_s2_f4p_k): tap rows as kz x ky (2026-11-15, branch s2f4p-20261115)

The tap-row loop ran "#pragma unroll 3" over tr = 0..8 with kz = tr / 3, ky = tr % 3 and the input slot ((2 oz0 + 2 wz + kz) % NP).
In each of the three unrolled copies mcc computed tr / 3 and the % 5 again (it does not know tr is a multiple of 3 there), 31 SASS
of lp_s2.cu:582 in the MMA loop where nvcc has 1. Now kz is a rolled loop (unroll 1) around a fully unrolled ky, and the slot is
kz = 0's (one % NP before the loop) plus kz with one wrap, as conv_fwd_f4p_k's sl[] does. Same MMAs in the same order, so the same
sums. MMA loop SASS (smallest loop holding the MMAs), MT 2 mx8 / mx4, MT 1 mx8 / mx4: mcc 122 / 122 / 104 / 104 -> 81 / 81 / 63 / 63,
nvcc 83 / 87 / 65 / 65 -> 72 / 76 / 49 / 49. lp_s2 totals: nvcc 469784 -> 469736, mcc 598728 -> 598560. Tests: test_mx4 (s2 fwd
gn+silu, fp4 kernel against the reference, deterministic), test_l0_slab "fp4 down (s2_f4p)".

## f8 weight gradient: slab-GroupNorm coefficients out of the channel loop (2026-11-14, branch wgradgn-20261114)

conv_bwd_w_f8_k's x staging (lp_f8wgrad.cuh: the cooperative MX path and the xdecode lambda) computed each channel's GN+SiLU affine
with chan_ab, which repeats the split / segment tests, gn_row's slab clamp and the integer division Cg / G in every unrolled channel
copy (48 copies in <1,6,...>), and the uni path also tested `gp.ns || sp.gp2.ns` per channel. Now the test sits outside the loop and
chan_ab_pl (lp_common.cuh) computes the per-plane part (both segments' statistics rows, channels per group) once; chan_ab_q does the
per-channel rest with the same arithmetic, so (a, b) are unchanged bit for bit.

Static SASS of all 54 lp_f8wgrad kernels (14 units), nvcc 13 sm_120a: 409984 -> 348176 instructions (-15 %), BRA 14330 -> 13254,
MUFU 5342 -> 4334 (one integer-division reciprocal per channel fewer), spill bytes 11540 -> 10112, registers 4900 -> 4898; no kernel
grows. conv_bwd_w_f8_k<1,6,mx4,mx8>: 17640 -> 14328. mcc (lp_f8wgrad_i0 + i4): 289720 -> 251840; the same kernel 29008 -> 24104.
Covered by test_l0_slab (wgrad fp8 cases with 8-plane slabs, SR, the network-input tile), test_mx4 (f8 wgrad cooperative ==
per-element with GN, bit for bit: the non-slab branch) and test_grad_mx4~L0_NORM=4,L0_SLAB=8,L0_SLAB_KERN=1.

## Fast math everywhere, native builds, LTO / PGO; UFSM_STRICT_MATH=ON for the bit-exact build (2026-11-14, branch fastmath-20261114)

The user: "enable fast math everything". Before: host C `-ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno` (IEEE), the CUDA units nvcc
`-use_fast_math` except the 11 `UFSM_STRICT_UNITS` (nn_gpudec nn_cf nn_ftrace nn_latvol nn_band nn_fibre nn_inkfly nn_gpuenc
nn_mcodes nn_faces nn_render: `-fmad=false`, IEEE), so those matched their CPU versions byte for byte. Now:

- Host C: `-ffast-math -fno-finite-math-only`. Reassociation (float reductions vectorise), contraction (fast, across statements),
  reciprocal division, no signed zeros, `-fapprox-func`, no errno. `-fno-finite-math-only` is a correctness requirement, not a
  trade-off: ~226 isnan / isfinite / NaN-fill uses (the loss's NaN guards, fwd_nan, zarr fill values, volcomp's typed-chunk checks)
  are folded to false under finite-math-only, i.e. the guards silently deleted. Checked: no code relies on signed zeros (the
  copysignf sites take the sign of nonzero data) or on libm errno (the errno reads follow strtod and I/O). No compensated sums or
  magic-constant rounding tricks in src / third_party (grep: Kahan, TwoSum, 0x1.8p23 ...), which reassociation would break.
  (FTZ / DAZ: see the widening below.)
- Every CUDA unit gets `UFSM_CU_FAST` (nvcc `-use_fast_math`), the former strict units included.
- `-DUFSM_STRICT_MATH=ON` restores the old flags exactly (host and the strict units) and defines `UFSM_STRICT_MATH` for the tests;
  CMake writes `$BUILD/strict_math` (0 / 1) for the shell tests.

Widened the same day (user: "all possible optimizations everywhere", "fast fp contract etc unsafe optimizations", "native
optimization"):
- Host: `-ffp-contract=fast` explicit, `-mtune=native`, `-fno-plt -fno-semantic-interposition -fomit-frame-pointer` (-g kept), and
  FTZ / DAZ in MXCSR set by a constructor (`src/fpenv.c`, linked into every executable by `ufsm_exe`; crtfastmath.o is not used
  because clang links it only from a gcc installation, not with compiler-rt). New threads inherit MXCSR from their creator
  (POSIX), and the constructor runs before main. Under UFSM_STRICT_MATH the file is empty.
- LTO: `UFSM_LTO=full` (default in release dirs; `off` under UFSM_VERIFY because the suite links ~250 executables against CORE and
  each would be a whole-program LTO link; `thin` with `UFSM_LTO_JOBS`). Consequence: the suite tests the non-LTO host code, and
  the shipped binary differs from it by cross-unit inlining (with fast math this can move roundings by an ulp).
- PGO: `UFSM_PGO=gen|use`, `UFSM_PGO_DIR` (default <repo>/pgo). `scripts/toolchain/pgo_collect.sh WORKLOAD` builds an
  instrumented `build-pgo/`, runs the workload lines with `$U`, and merges the profiles into `pgo/ufsm.profdata`. The workload
  (`scripts/toolchain/pgo_workload.txt`) runs on the 384^3 wind fixture: a 200-step train with --gpu-input (try7's argv to replace
  the flags), sampler-only (UFSM_SAMPLER_ONLY), predict with all heads + fit-zarr at q 4 and a read-back (volcomp encode /
  decode), and the instrumented test drivers of count-field, slab fit, render and volcomp (their profiles key the same CORE
  functions). Queued as a sweep post-pass, with a full GPU suite against an LTO build dir (the shipped configuration, once per
  toolchain change). Host only: device code has no PGO.
- Device: clang -x cuda contraction `fast` (`on` under strict; test_half allows 1 ulp outside strict), `-Xcuda-ptxas -O3`; nvcc
  `-Xptxas -O3`, `--extra-device-vectorization`, host side `-march=native -mtune=native`. No device LTO (`-dlto`): it needs
  `-rdc` plus an nvcc device-link step, and the units are whole-program objects linked by clang / lld, so device LTO has nothing
  to work on without restructuring the link.
- Native device code: `UFSM_ARCH=auto` (release preset) and `UFSM_GPU_SM=auto` read the compute capability from nvidia-smi at
  configure time. They produce SASS only for that GPU (`sm_120a` on the desk, nn_* included), with no PTX. `portable` (or no
  visible GPU) gives the old sm_120 + PTX / sm_86 + PTX targets. `$BUILD/native_id` (cmake/native_id.sh: CPU model, flags hash,
  GPU compute capabilities) is written at configure time; `scripts/pod/setup.sh NOBUILD=1` rebuilds when it does not match the
  pod, and `FOREIGN_BINARY=1` is the explicit override for desk-compiled binaries or objects.

Not taken, though fast math allows it: `-ffinite-math-only` (the guards, above). No measurement shows a speed reason to go
further: the hot paths are on the GPU, and the host float loops that vectorise already do so under `-fno-finite-math-only`.

Data written under the old flags:
- volcomp lossy (mode 0) stores: decode is open-loop (no state carried from reconstructed voxels into the entropy decode), so a
  fast-math decode is the old decode within +-1 LSB on rare voxels whose IDCT output sits at a .5 rounding boundary. The codec
  already allows exactly that between its own AVX2+FMA and C kernels ("Cross-build agreement", third_party/volcomp.h). The stores
  carry no hashes of decoded voxels.
- volcomp surface chunks (mode 6): their refinement contexts are read from the base's own reconstruction, so encoder and decoder
  must agree to the bit. That reconstruction runs under `#pragma clang fp contract(off) reassociate(off)` (VF_STRICT_BEGIN) with
  only + and * (no division, so -freciprocal-math has nothing to change; -fno-signed-zeros only changes the sign of zero results),
  hence bit-exact under fast math: old surface stores decode identically. The GPU decoder (nn_gpudec) handles mode 0 only.
- volcomp typed chunks: mode 7 is integer; mode 8 decodes k * q as one binary64 multiply then binary32 rounding (no expression
  for fast math to change), and its encoder verifies the bound per element. Unchanged.
- surfcomp (.sfc), embz int8 stores: decode is integer dequantisation times a scale; new encodes may differ in a few levels from
  old ones (test_tfx's golden hash, kept under strict only), old files decode the same.
- Runtime GPU / CPU mixing: paths that fall back per piece (faces when the device pool fills, gpudec's CPU retry of a failing
  substream, render's host tier, count-field's GPU vs host) now agree within rounding (+-1 on u8 at boundaries) instead of to the
  bit; outputs that mix pieces from both paths can show such +-1 seams.

Tests: the checks that were exact only because both sides were IEEE now go through `tests/fm_tol.h` (C) / `tests/fm_tol.sh`
(shell); every bound collapses to exact under UFSM_STRICT_MATH=ON, so the strict build still runs the old byte-identity checks. The
bounds were set from the arithmetic (no GPU was available to measure, the 11-14 sweep had them): a u8 that is round(float)
moves by at most 1 and only near .5 boundaries (+-1 on <= 1e-4 of voxels for volcomp decode); classes cut at a float threshold
flip whole (count bounds, 1e-4 .. 5e-3 by test); floats rel 1e-6 (fp32 one-pass), 1e-5 (recursive filters, iterative fits 1e-4);
fp16 +-1 ulp; golden hashes / coded bytes / det_cmp batch hashes are compared only under strict, otherwise decoded and compared
within bounds (losses within 2 % for det runs). Tests touched: test_gpudec, test_volcomp_fast, test_ct_gpu_decode.sh,
test_zarr.sh, test_vcgpu, test_predict_heads.sh, test_fit, test_tfx, test_render_stream, test_render_fill, test_band_pair,
test_phase_onfly.sh, test_codes_onfly.sh, test_mesh_phase, test_fiberraster, test_fibre_onfly.sh, test_ink_splat, test_ftrace_gpu,
test_faces, test_countfield, test_lldec, test_fuse, test_sample_ops, test_spatial_augment, test_wind_sampler, test_scan_augment,
test_gpu_aug, test_gpu_input, test_heads, test_pyports, test_imgops, test_coreline, test_qkclip, test_half (clang -x cuda path). The `ufsm --ref` compares
(phase-onfly, codes-onfly, fibre-onfly) have no tolerance option: the wrappers accept their failure exit under fast math when the
logged per-window differing-voxel counts sum within the bound. Measured bounds and speed: TODO after the first fast-math sweep.
## Eval: no silent drop-outs in wgate, unreached voxels, saturated ink (2026-11-14, branch evalfix3-20261114, audit eval#11-13)

Source only (no builds, user 11-14); the final sweep builds and tests.
- wgate-table.sh (eval#11, #12): every rule needs numeric values and the full box set. The expected n per set is the baseline's own n
  (`wbench-stats REF`, the same clean set since both sides use REF's ceilings); a candidate box that failed (na) or is missing now
  lists the boxes and ends in `VERDICT TAG: INCOMPLETE` (exit 3) instead of dropping out of the paired stats. Before, "na" + 0 = 0 passed
  R3 and failing the hard boxes made a candidate look better.
- fit score (eval#12): "winding ids right" stays right / nd so stored baselines stay comparable; the line gains
  `ids right of all labelled` = right / (nd + unreached) and the `unreached` share (labelled voxels without U), appended at the end so
  the existing greps keep working.
- ink-vscore (eval#13): a prediction's 255 was skipped as unknown, but the ink heads write round(255 sigmoid), where 255 = p >= 0.998.
  `--pred-unknown auto` (default) skips 255 only for prob254 arrays (fill_value 255, as ink-splat writes); otherwise 255 is scored in
  the top bin and the count is logged. Numbers of sharp models rise relative to earlier vscores (their most confident voxels now count).

## Split, thread and RNG audit fixes (2026-11-14, branch thrfix-20261114; source only, not yet built or run)

Fixes for audit-20261114 targeted/split.md, mini/threads.md and mini/rng.md. They are source-only by the user's order; the final sweep
builds and tests them.

- **gfilm under --split (split #1).** Nothing installed `unet_set_gfilm_reduce`, so the gfilm A / B gradients of the whole (split-top)
  decoder levels counted twice in the allreduce. Scratch2 has two such levels of five (dec 3, 4).
  - Now `gfilm_bwd` zeroes side 1's copy by itself.
  - The token path's dg (UFSM_GFILM_TOKGRAD=1) is summed through a split reduce that train installs. Without the reduce, that path
    aborts under split.
  - Check: `test_split_lat~gfilm` compares the A / B block on its own.
- **Loss-path A/B in the suite (split #2).** `test_split_ab` (gpu2, slow) runs split_lat_ab.sh's first-step loss / gradient dump on the
  wind fixture with the live feature set in small:
  - 6 levels, --split-top 3, 4 attention blocks, --attn-pe scroll, --gfilm, --film 2, --fstem 16, --gn-ema, --skip-empty 1
  - --lat 4 --lat-guide 3, --rv 2, ink head with MIL, fibre head
  - Pass condition: split vs one GPU within 2x the one-GPU rerun plus a floor (loss 1e-7, gradients 1e-6), on the loss, the whole
    gradient and the gfilm block.
- **Smaller split items.**
  - #4: the distillation and deep-supervision guards test split_h0 rather than sp_on, which is off on the whole levels.
  - #5: --skip-empty --split refuses a seam off the 8-cell tile grid.
  - #6: replica check. Every card's master weights are hashed at the checkpoint steps, and a mismatch stops the run.
    UFSM_REPLICA_CHECK=N sets the interval; 0 turns it off.
  - #3 (predict --split for latent / attention nets) is deferred: it is a feature, not a fix.
- **Threads.**
  - vws_next returns -1 after a persistent fill failure.
  - zcache: an O(1) LRU list, and keys by z3_id rather than the array's address.
  - sources: acquire / release on the lazily opened arrays.
  - The echo gate's busy callback runs outside sp->mu.
  - Per sampler: THP and bank_own. The env is read once.
  - Atomic lazy env ints.
  - dc_free waits for its readers.
  - dcache_default_dir is built once.
- **RNG.**
  - --finetune reseeds the sample / SSL / SR streams from the loaded checkpoint's step.
  - A resume reseeds the SSL teacher stream.
  - --phase-dense draws its keep mask per draw.
  - --det retries a failed read from the same RNG state.
  - SR seeds keep all 32 bits (was h | 1).
  - Deferred: 64-bit SR seeds (the kernels take uint32), and libc rand in inkseam / srpairs (replacing it would reshuffle existing
    sr-pairs holdout splits).

## PHerc1667: the spiral had the wrong hand; same-sheet (fibre) pairs in count-field (2026-11-14, branch fibfit-20261114)

Task: fibre-continuity constraints in the winding fit, measured against the published PHerc1667 unwrap (section "The 1667 unroll
against the published full unwrap" below: our wrap id matched the published sheet 48 % of the time, +1 / +2 in a sector "about
-180..-50 deg"). Measuring first showed a different cause, the spiral's direction; the fibre term is in, opt-in, with an oracle bound.

**The hand.** Per published vertex, the offset our id - published sheet is not a sector of voids. It ramps with the axis angle: 0 at
+60..+180 deg (same 0.80-0.87), +1 at -60..-140, +2 at -180 (0.67), then it resets at our theta cut. That is 2 sheets of drift per
revolution: the wraps are a spiral of the OPPOSITE hand. They follow the right sheets where the phase is confident and hop where it is
weak, i.e. in the voids, hence the void crossings. The published surface's turn grows as atan2(y - cy, x - cx) DEcreases
(|mean e^{2 pi i T} e^{+i theta}| = 1.00), i.e. W = U - dir theta / 2 pi needs dir -1. The 11-12 run had dir +1, and following our
field across the seam, wrap k's end continues into wrap k-1's start (radii at z 18000). The cause: count-field takes dir from
fit_init_prior on its middle chunk, and the ring vote demodulates by a fixed pitch, so with sheets this far from circles (one turn's
radius 3.7..5.4 mm) no ring was coherent ("median winding per ring 0.000 over 0 rings") and dir fell back to +1, silently; the slabs
take --dir from the ref. Every unroll on disk has dir +1 (P4, 1299, 1667); P4 is +1 by measurement (fit.h).

Sheet identity of a W field against the published surface (`wpub.py`: W at every 20th published vertex, minus T - u, the published
turn and the angle fraction from theta = pi; the share of the modal integer; 1.95 M vertices). The ref decides it: the 11-12 ref
gives 0.461, surfcmp on the final wraps 0.482.

| ref (count-field, the run's flags) | same | +1 | -1 | r 3 / 5 / 7 / 9 / 11 mm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dir +1 (11-12 run) | 0.461 | 0.314 | 0.034 | - |
| dir -1 | 0.731 | 0.088 | 0.103 | 0.42 / 0.77 / 0.83 / 0.76 / 0.53 |
| dir -1 + oracle short pairs (0.2-0.4 mm, 2 % of vertices, 3.7 M, --cf-fib 1, 3 IRLS) | 0.768 | 0.086 | 0.094 | 0.49 / 0.80 / 0.86 / 0.79 / 0.58 |
| dir -1 + oracle long pairs (0.8-3 mm, 1 %, 2.7 M, --cf-fib 4, 1 IRLS) | 0.844 | 0.017 | 0.096 | 0.98 / 0.98 / 0.97 / 0.78 / 0.48 |

With dir -1 the per-angle share is flat (0.65-0.86 in every 30 deg sector; with +1 it was 0.01 at -180 and 0.85 at +90).

The whole chain with dir -1 (ref-dm1 -> 73 slab fits with the run's flags, on CPUs: desk `fit --cpu` + 23 slabs on the perf pod's CPU,
~50 s / slab uncontended -> fit-join -> wraps -> wrap-snap mix -> wrap-dump every 4th vertex), surfcmp.py on every 4th published
vertex and every 4th of ours (`--sub 4 --rev-every 4`; the full run OOMs in the shared 40 GB dev slice), both runs measured the same way:

| PHerc1667 wraps_snap | same sheet | +1 | -1 | +2 | pub cov 100 / 200 um | pub d med | ours cov 50 / 100 um | ours d med |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11-12 run (dir +1) | 0.487 | 0.309 | 0.030 | 0.115 | 0.792 / 0.883 | 70 um | 0.498 / 0.726 | 51 um |
| dir -1 | **0.762** | 0.089 | 0.089 | 0.015 | 0.794 / 0.883 | 70 um | 0.503 / 0.730 | 49 um |

(The distances are larger than the pub1667 section's 19 / 17 um because only every 4th vertex of ours is the nearest-vertex set.) Same
geometry, a different sheet assignment: 0.762 against the 0.482 there. fit-join's overlap agreement is 0.9507.

**Direction code.** `fit_init_prior` now walks the network phase around circles about the axis when the ring vote is empty
(`loop_winding`: 16 rows, a loop per 3 cells of radius, 2/3-cell steps, confident cells only; the unwrapped total of a loop is -dir,
no pitch assumed) and prints a WARNING with that vote. `--dir-loops 1` (fit, count-field) takes it; default off, because it is noisy
on Paris 4: per z row the +-1 loops split 4:0 .. 16:71, and the middle row votes -1 (79 + / 6 - of all signs) against P4's measured +1.
1667 middle rows: 44:28 .. 80:8 for -1. unroll.sh passes the ref `--dir` from SPIRALDIR or `scripts/unroll/spiral_dir.tsv`
(PHerc1667 -1, with its evidence) and copies an empty-vote warning to progress.log. test_fit_dir (CPU): a non-circular spiral (radius x
(1 + 0.35 cos 2 theta)) gives no ring vote for either hand (+1 by default); the loops get both hands right; circular: the rings do.

**One direction rule, and a refusal (audit-unroll #1).** There were four no-evidence fallbacks: count-field +1 (silent), fit_init_prior
+1, the slab prior -1 (`vote > 0 ? 1 : -1`), and fit_load +1 when model.json has no "dir". Now all of them follow one rule (fit.h FIT_DIR_*):
--dir given > ring vote (>= 3 rings, non-zero median) > phase loops (only with --dir-loops 1) > DEFAULT +1. fit_model.dir_src records the
source. count-field logs `dir %+d (given | ring vote | phase loops | DEFAULT (no evidence))` and REFUSES DEFAULT (exit 2) unless
`--dir-default-ok 1`. The exceptions are --pool-only, whose cache header now carries the source (an old cache counts as DEFAULT), and the
UFSM_CF_READ_ONLY bench. The slab prior with no vote warns and takes +1; fit_load warns on a missing key. unroll.sh's ref passes `--dir`
from SPIRALDIR or spiral_dir.tsv (columns scroll, dir, source GT | published | estimator | unknown, evidence) and logs the decision and
any refusal to progress.log. Not done: the 2x2 closing error is no direction gate, since it is 2.061 at -1 vs 2.060 at +1 on 1667. The
label-free gate for phase coherence against W at +-1, which needs a second LS solve (since added, see below). Added later, source-only and unmeasured: the w4 gate (`fit_dir_w4`). The winding-mod-4 planes' tangential grad W is summed around the loop_winding circles (dq >= 64, divided by the covered share), which gives -dir per loop with no mod-1 slips. Its vote (>= 8 loops, 2:1) is preferred over the phase loops when decided, and a disagreement is warned. count-field runs the gates on 32 middle rows loaded with every plane whenever pass 1 found no evidence (--model-only skips the w4 planes there). They decide only with --dir-loops 1; otherwise they print beside the refusal. unroll.sh records spiral_dir / spiral_dir_src (env | tsv | gate: SOURCE) in the run manifest when mset exists. The +-1 coherence gate (source-only, unmeasured, off by default): count-field prints `model coherence C` = |sum z| / sum |z| over the solve cells' phase-vs-model phasors (gr, gi before the smoothing). The right hand leaves one gauge phasor; the wrong one turns twice per revolution, so C should fall to ~0. With unroll.sh DIRCOH=1 and no env / tsv hand, ref() runs two solves from the same (dir-free) pooled sums, --dir +1 and -1. The higher C wins by >= DIRCOH_MARGIN (0.05); otherwise it refuses. The manifest gets `gate:coherence +1 Cp -1 Cm`. scripts/fibfit/dir_gates_measure.sh measures the w4 / loops / coherence votes on 1667, P4 and 1299 against spiral_dir.tsv (post-sweep, CPU). Every
caller without --dir on a scroll with no ring vote now stops: scripts/cfit, corpus, pod/unroll.sh, cal/gate.sh.

**Every unroll's hand from published segments (scripts/fibfit/seghand.py, segfetch.py).** Take a published segment that covers >= 0.8 turn
per grid row. Over that turn its radius changes by one pitch, and the sign against the unwrapped angle is the hand. No axis model is
needed (theta is taken about the row's ring centroid), and the non-circular shape cancels over the turn. Checked against the published
1667 unwrap (-1, rows 253:1) and P4's documented +1. Results in scripts/unroll/spiral_dir.tsv:

| scroll | dir | evidence | u1 unroll ran |
|---|---|---|---|
| PHerc1667 | -1 | full unwrap + 18 of 20 local wrap segments | +1: wrong, redo |
| PHercParis4 | +1 | 3 segments on 20260411134726, rows 291-293 : 0-2 | +1: right |
| PHerc0814 | -1 | 2 segments on 20250804134230, rows 24 / 27 : 1 / 2 | default +1 (no log kept): wrong, redo |
| PHerc1451 / PHercMAN5 | +1? | one raw / flattened-product segment each, scan frame not checked | +1 |
| 1299, 0009B, 0257, 0332, 0358, 0483B, 0490B, 0813, 0846B, 1203, 1545, MANB | ? | no segment covering a turn on our scan | default +1, unverified |

Only exact +1 / -1 entries drive unroll.sh. The "?" ones refuse at the ref when count-field finds no ring vote.

**Fibre (same-sheet) pairs in count-field.** The slabs snap their integers to the ref (`--ref-snap 1`), so a fibre term in the slab fit
(`fit --w-fib`, 10-26) cannot move a turn step; the integer reference is count-field's LS solve. `count-field --fibers F.fib`
(fiber-export frame) or `--pairs F.f32` (za ya xa zb yb xb dW) with `--cf-fib W`: rows c . U = t, c = trilinear(b) - trilinear(a)
on the solve grid, t = dW + dir dtheta / 2 pi (U = W + dir theta / 2 pi; a fibre: dW = 0, pairs every 4th native-voxel sample at
spans 16 / 32 / 64 / 128, `--cf-fib-spans`), on every level; Huber `--cf-fib-huber 0.25` over `--cf-fib-irls 3` reweighted level-0
solves. The CG gathers the pairs per cell (cell -> pair-entry index), so the z-row threads stay race-free; with pairs the CG runs on
the CPU (1667 level 0 with 3.7 M pairs: 291 s vs 54 s without). test_countfield: a band that counts 0.75 of its 3 sheets in one
sector leaves W off by > 0.5 turn on 1.000 of the sector beyond it; arcs along the true sheets (`--cf-fib 4`) bring it to 0.000.

**What fibres can do here (oracle).** Pairs sampled from the published surface itself are leaky (the score is against that surface):
upper bounds. Correction (audit-ugeom, geo-outer): the "outer radial miscount" below is not one. Against pub our radial count matches at r 5-12 mm. The one-sheet difference is in the core (r 3.5-5.5 mm). The long oracle pairs fix the core and drag the masked (zero-CT) outer turns along, so the outer -1 tracks the CT mask (geo-outer: k < 0 share 0.65 within 0.8 mm of masked CT, 0.05 beyond 50 mm). Short pairs, at about the length of our fibhv traces (0.6 mm median, 11-11), add +0.04. Long pairs, at the length
of the AFV tracings (2 mm median), fix the inner turns (r 3-7 mm 0.42-0.83 -> 0.97-0.98) but not the outer ones. r >= 9 mm stays at
-1 (0.16-0.29). That is a radial miscount around the whole circumference, one sheet missing beyond ~8 mm. It has no curl, so no
along-sheet constraint can see it; it needs a count fix (CT peaks, wrap-check). 1667 has no AFV and no published fibre
prediction (open data: lasagna only). wgraph's fibhv-d predicts for one 1667 slab (pod) failed at the time of writing. So no real-fibre
run yet: the term waits for mm-long fibres (AFV-like tracings or a longer-tracing fibre model).

Files: /vesuvius/ufsm/fibfit/1667 (ref-dm1 = the dir -1 ref, pool.bin its pass-1 sums, ref-orc02 / ref-orclong the oracles,
dm1/ the dir -1 chain: slabs, joined, wraps, wraps_snap; cmps-* the surfcmp outputs). Scripts: scripts/fibfit/ (offang.py, wpub.py,
oracle.py, loops2.py; surfcmp.py is on pub1667-20261114, run here with a `--sub 4` vertex stride) and /vesuvius/ufsm/fibfit/deskpipe.sh.
Next: re-run the 1667 unroll with SPIRALDIR -1 (or the tsv) on master; the outer-turn miscount; mm-long fibres for 1667.

## I/O error paths: atomic zarr writes, HTTP retry by time, chunk CRC, checked writers (2026-11-14, branch iofix-20261114)

Fixes for the mini audit items store 1-10, zarr 1-8, errpaths 1-8 and volcomp 1-7 (/vesuvius/ufsm/audit-20261114/mini/). Source only,
not built or run here (the user stopped compile testing 11-14 15:00); the final sweep builds and tests. Correctness fixes are on by
default; the format change (crc32c) is opt-in.

- z3w: every zarr.json and shard is written to `<path>.<pid>.<tid>.tmp`, then fflush + fsync (UFSM_Z3W_FSYNC=0 skips the fsync) +
  fclose, all checked, then renamed; on any failure the tmp is unlinked and an error returned. Before, two writers of one shard shared
  `<shard>.tmp`, a failed fclose published a short shard, and metadata writers reported success on a full disk. A shard that becomes
  all-fill now unlinks the old object instead of leaving stale data. pthread_create failures are counted and only created threads joined.
- crc32c inner codec: the reader accepts and verifies it (last codec, per chunk, sub and whole reads, also z3_chunk_raw); z3w writes it
  only with UFSM_Z3W_CRC=1 (a format change: older readers refuse arrays with it). Volcomp itself has no checksum, so a bit flip in a
  tANS / bypass payload decodes to wrong voxels with status OK; with the codec on it is a read error. A substream (z3_read_sub) read does
  not check the chunk's stream tail; the codec covers that too.
- zarr3 reader: shard size 0 refused (SIGFPE before); a 404 shard is no longer cached as "missing" for good (logged once, read as fill,
  asked again on the next open); the cached shard index stores the payload size, so the entry range check also runs on cached indices,
  and a failed size probe is an error rather than a disabled check. The chunk cache still assumes immutable published shards (documented
  in zarr3.h).
- store (HTTP): retries are bounded by time (UFSM_HTTP_RETRY_S, 600 s) and transport failures by count (12), not 12 attempts of any kind
  (an outage over ~1-2 min failed the job); requests get a size-scaled timeout (60 s + len / 256 KB/s, whole objects
  UFSM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_S 1800) and a low-speed abort at 16 KB/s, so a stalled stream frees its slot; non-429 4xx fail at once; whole
  reads refuse text/html bodies (error pages served as 200); HEAD without Content-Length falls back to a 1-byte ranged GET; a suffix
  range the server ignores falls back to a plain tail read; response buffers are capped (UFSM_HTTP_MAX_MB, 1024); the cache-dir claim is
  a temp file linked into place (an empty claim is reclaimed); UFSM_HTTP_RPS also applies to HuggingFace roots.
- Writers that reported success on failure now check fwrite / fprintf / fclose (and fsync where a file is renamed over a live one) and
  unlink partial output: annot st_save / st_log (the HTTP handlers answer 500), repack zarr.json, wrap-anchor and patch-id anchors,
  write_pgm, the PNG writer, villawind dumps (no .shape after a failed .f32), reg-render samples.bin, sheet-pbr diagnostics. Ignored
  `mkdir -p` results in train and surf-eval are errors (train also fails when run-defaults.txt cannot be written, since a resume reads
  it); dino logs a failed last.ckpt symlink.
- CUDA copies that fed results unchecked now fail loudly: nn_skip_set / nn_skip_share, the Muon descriptor table (ns5_lt), nn_pred_stats
  (CK, sticky error), the lp_mxsw self-test.
- GPU volcomp decoder: a device failure (G.broken) prints a warning at exit as well as when it happens; UFSM_GPU_DECODE_ITEMS large
  enough to overflow the 32-bit substream offsets (~87000) disables the GPU decoder instead of corrupting offsets. gbr_finished stays
  stricter than the CPU check (documented: the CPU redo is the reference). Partial-read zero fill and the sink fall-through are
  documented at the API.

## Kernel workspaces inside the memory plan (2026-11-14, branch memws-20261114, audit net#4)

At P 768 data parallel GPU 0 ran 15.75 of 16.3 GB while the planner's fixed 550 MB term stood in for every grow-on-demand kernel
workspace, allocated at first use after the plan, grown with cudaFree + cudaMalloc mid-step (a device-wide synchronisation), and either
aborting (lp_buf, fstem, tc_wbuf, s2b copy) or silently falling back (prenorm, gy records) on a full card. netfix already allocates the
optimizer / attention cuBLASLt workspaces, the Muon pool and the 96 MB input-conv chunk before the measure. This branch does the rest:

- **One per-device registry** (nn_core.cu `nn_ws`): the 24 lp_buf slots (4 element types x 6), the fp4 GroupNorm input copy
  (f4_prenorm_buf), the fine stem's partial sums, the 16-bit tensor-core weight copy / scales, the s2b gy overlap copy. `nn_ws_reserve`
  grows an id now; after `nn_ws_seal` a growth prints `nn_ws: ... grew after the memory plan` (a planner miss), and an id with a soft
  limit (`nn_ws_limit`) returns nullptr instead (its caller's fallback).
- **unet_ws_plan** (unet.c): for every 3^3 conv at its level of the dry build, each site's own sizing formula: weight prep 28 Cop Cip,
  the fp4 gy pre-pass slabs (per_zt x min(nzt, 96 MiB / per_zt)), GroupNorm backward partials, the stride-2 backward-data's MX-fp8
  chunks (gx / gy / dilated gy / accumulate temp, or the whole layer with 8-bit gradients), the flipped weights, the bf16 tc weights,
  the s2b gy copy, the head's fp16 weights; plus the fp4 prepared-weight memo (3 passes x both orientations of nq + ns per conv: one
  cudaMalloc per conv and pass at its first call, now checked), charged but not pre-allocated (keyed per call site).
- **Planner** (train.c): need += unet_ws_plan per mode, replacing the "3 x 96 MB" wide-s2 term; the fixed term is now 400 MB of CUDA
  context growth + margin (UFSM_WS_RESIDUAL_MB) instead of 550 MB with the workspaces inside. After the pick, every id is allocated at
  its bound on every GPU and sealed. The fine stem's partials (5.3 MB) are reserved before the measure.
- **The fp4 GroupNorm input copy** (a whole layer, 17 B per 32 channels and voxel: ~0.96 GB at level 0 of the 256-wide P 768 net)
  ran wherever the card's free memory allowed at first call: on try6 it could fit GPU 1 (2.5 GB free) but not GPU 0 (0.55 GB), so the
  replicas could run different kernels. Now it gets the largest layer within 3/4 of the plan's spare above 256 MB, the same on every
  GPU, and the label planes' device spare shrinks by it. Expected at try6 (P 768 DP): GPU 0's spare is ~1.34 GB, so the budget is
  (1.34 - 0.256) x 0.75 = ~0.81 GB < 0.96 GB: level 0 takes the non-prenorm path on both GPUs. GPU 0 already ran that path (it had no
  room); GPU 1 loses the prenorm it had, so a slower step on the pass's comparison is this rule, not a regression (audit-net review).
- **The whole-layer gy records** (lp_gn_silu_bwd_apply_rec) are capped at the planned record bytes (lp_gyrec_set_cap); larger layers
  take the plain apply and the weight gradient's own pre-pass (fail-soft path that existed).
- gscr (the apply's bias scratch) is allocated at >= 1024 channels once; abk / cfb / skip masks / attn8 scratch are < 1 MB (skip:
  one byte per 8x8x16-cell tile; attn8: tokens of the bottom level) and stay lazy.

Check: tests/test_memws.sh (gpu, slow): try6's flags at P 256 on the wind fixture with UFSM_MEM_REPORT=4; FAIL on any "grew after the
memory plan" line or any >= 1 MB device allocation after the first step line. Not run yet (mega pass: CPU only); no measured numbers.

## Label-free sheet-identity gates: `ufsm unroll-qa` (2026-11-14, branch geogate-20261114)

The unroll's gates measure self-consistency with the count-field reference: fit-join agreement 0.96-0.97, wrap-check 0.976 and slab
coherence (Spearman 0.07 with identity) all pass Paris 4, whose GT sheet identity is 0.12-0.21 on PH1-3. `ufsm unroll-qa`
(`src/unrollqa.c`) measures the fitted W against evidence the reference never integrated, per box (`--box`) or over 48 material tiles of
128³ field cells (default, ~1 min CPU). Full audit: `/vesuvius/ufsm/audit-20261114/geo-gate.md`.

**Validation.** 92 clean GT boxes, with ids from `fit --model --codes` per box: 54 1667 C boxes, held out, on ref-cf and on joined;
Paris 4 PH1-3, HOLD and 34 July J boxes on ref-cf. Spearman with ids per box, within each scroll:

| metric | 1667 ref | 1667 joined | Paris 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| pw48: net phase unwrapped along an axis over 48 cells vs the model's ΔW, share > 0.5 turn apart | -0.66 | -0.79 | -0.56 |
| conf_lo: material share with phase confidence < 0.3 | -0.63 | -0.46 | -0.79 |
| w4: W vs the winding-mod-4 head (dz dy dx over 32 voxels), share within 0.5 turn | 0.53 | 0.72 | 0.74 |
| fib_pers_h: fibre traces (H) through W, persistent sheet changes per m (12 / 12 / 32 boxes with fibres) | -0.62 | -0.77 | -0.70 |
| lcoh_lo (16³ blocks with phase-vs-W coherence < 0.5) / tang_tpm (\|∇W\| along the sheet): reported | -0.69 / -0.63 | -0.80 / -0.62 | -0.57 / -0.78 |
| tilt of ∇W vs the net normal; \|∇W\| × net spacing; mod-4 loop closure; zero-CT share in material | ~0 | ~0 | ~0 / -0.55 (ct0) |

The fit stays parallel to the sheets at the right spacing even where its integer is wrong. The slips show up in sheet counting and in
the evidence, not in local geometry. Inside 1667 C1 (ids 0.60), the wrong-integer cells sit where the phase confidence is low (AUC 0.73).

**Gates** (warn-only; `--strict` exits 3; tiles: warn when more than 0.35 of them are over):
- conf_lo > 0.40, pw48 > 0.10, w4 < 0.80, and fib_pers_h > 130 /m with `--fibres`.
- Each flags PH1-3. Together the first three flag 30 / 33 Paris 4 boxes with ids < 0.5 and 8 / 9 1667 joined boxes with ids < 0.7,
  against 1 / 79 good 1667 box fits (ids ≥ 0.8).
- Whole runs, share of 48 tiles over conf_lo / pw48 / w4: 1667-u1 joined 0.10 / 0.29 / 0.21, all ok; Paris4-u1 0.75 / 0.46 / 0.65,
  WARN on all three.
- fiber-judge on the same fibres: Spearman -0.85 over 44 boxes, AUC 0.96. It needs fibre traces, and our fibhv traces put 3 / 5 good P4
  boxes over 130 /m.

**Pipeline.** unroll.sh check stage, after wrap-check: `unroll-qa` on `joined`, with ok / WARN lines in progress.log. `UQSTRICT=1` makes
it fatal and `FIBRES=` adds the fibre gate.

**Test.** `test_unroll_qa`, CPU: a synthetic spiral with its true model passes every gate. A model with 1.5 turns per 128 voxels along
y fires the fibre and pw48 gates, exits 0 by default and 3 under --strict.

**Not caught.** The ±1 slips of a mostly good fit, such as 1667's handedness ramp, need an along-the-wrap angular check. The masked-CT
coverage loss is invisible here, because the material ends with the CT; that is audit-ugeom's wrap-snap share gate.

## Kernel numerics fixes, audit kernels.md #4-#7 (2026-11-14, branch kfix46-20261114)

Source-only fixes, not built or tested (the audit's one final build-and-test sweep runs them). Each keeps the old bits wherever the old
arithmetic stayed in range.
- **#4: the fused-upsample half2 blend** (stage_up_smem_h2, f4ru_blend, stage_up_smem16_h2).
  - Before: the fp16 tap weights carried the coarse block's scale, so the corner tap (1/64) went subnormal once a block's amax fell below
    ~1.8, and large scales could overflow the half accumulator.
  - Now: the weights are relative to the largest of the 8 blocks' scales (2^(e - e_max) <= 1), and 2^e_max is applied to the fp32 result.
- **#5: the core-1 attention backward** (nn_attn_tc.cu).
  - Before: dO went to fp16 with one per-tensor scale.
  - Now: one scale per head (k_fa_amax_h: max |dO| and max |v| of head h into a per-device scratch, fa_amh), used by k_fa_bprep / k_fa_dkv
    / k_fa_dq. Heads are independent, so each scale divides out within its head.
  - lp_attn8 (core 2) keeps the tensor scale (at_fa_bprep without head scales).
- **#6: SiLU / dSiLU through tanh.approx** (14 sites in lp_*).
  - Before: 1 + tanh(h) cancelled for h < -1, so tanh.approx's ~2^-11 absolute error was most of silu(u) at u < -6.
  - Now: tanh_silu takes h < -1 from exp (2^-24 absolute) and keeps tanh.approx elsewhere, so the bits are unchanged for u >= -2.
- **#7: GN statistics of MX tensors** (gn_sums_mx2_k).
  - Before: raw per-thread fp32 sums of x and x^2, then E[x^2] - m^2.
  - Now: each thread accumulates x - c and (x - c)^2 with c its first row's value, recombined in double, and the reductions are in double
    into the fixed-point slots.
  - Variance error for mean / std 10 drops from ~1e-4 to ~1e-7.
  - The block partition is unchanged, so slab-vs-whole and split statistics stay consistent with each other. Split-vs-one-GPU byte
    tests may move by one ulp: the slots now receive doubles, where they received float partials before.

## Masked CT: no coupling through data-free cells, a majority data test in wraps, one no-data gate (2026-11-14, branch geoouter-20261114)

**Problem (geo-outer audit, /vesuvius/ufsm/audit-20261114/geo-outer.md).** PHerc1667's fields ran on the `-masked` CT, whose SAM mask clips
the outer turns (16 % of the published area lies on zero CT). Two effects:
- **Count field.** fibfit's oracle count-field (dir -1, the published surface's own same-sheet pairs) loses one sheet beyond r ~8 mm:
  - against the published surface, identity is 0.97 at turns <= 17, then 0.90 / 0.58 / 0.41 / 0.08 at turns 18 / 23 / 24 / 29;
  - the masked parts of the outer turns are off by 3 turns or more (W radially flat: a no-data edge carries only the theta term);
  - on UNMASKED published vertices, the k < 0 share falls with the along-sheet distance to the nearest masked vertex: 0.65 (< 0.8 mm),
    0.53, 0.36, 0.12 (12-50 mm), 0.05 (> 50 mm), the same within each turn band;
  - the same fields without the pairs (ref-dm1) show no such drift, so the pairs into the data-free cells carry the deficit;
  - 22.9 % of the 2.73 M pairs have an endpoint in a no-data solve cell.
- **Wraps.** The u1 wraps put whole duplicate outer wraps on the zeroed CT. At z 20000, w043-w049 lie entirely on it, 100-400 um deep,
  at 24-44 um pitch. The cause is `wraps --fields`' data test: the max-pooled material w > 0 (any cell). The network's weak response
  (w 4-40) within ~100 um of the mask edge, pooled 4x, kept them.
- **The 2023 7.91 um scan.** Range reads of 6 slices from dl.ash2txt, mapped with r2-transform. At the divergence the published sheets
  sit on CT layers. Published gaps show no skipped-sheet signature. Under the masked zone, faint low-density layers lie beneath the
  published turns 24-30.

**Changes.**
- **count-field: no-data pairs dropped** (default; `--cf-fib-nodata keep` keeps them). A pair or fibre sample pair is dropped when
  either endpoint's level-0 solve cell has pooled weight S < `--cf-fib-smin` (0.1) x the median S of the data cells. It prints
  `count-field: no-data: N of M pairs (share) ...` and a WARNING above 0.02.
- **wraps: majority data test.** `fit_field_array_frac` pools 255 x the share of a pooled cell's field cells with material
  >= `--data-thr` (128). A vertex is kept where that share is >= `--data-min` (128, a majority). `--data-thr 1 --data-min 1` restores
  the earlier any-cell test. The radius bounds and the id pruning keep using "any strong cell", which is still a superset.
  - 1667-u1 joined, z 19900-20100 (`--zr 4975,5025`), against the old test:

    | | wraps | vertices | on zero CT (level 4) |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | old (any cell) | 65 | 663 k | 11.4 % |
    | new (majority) | 42 | 547 k | 0.32 % |

  - w044-w066 are gone. Near z 20000 the dropped vertices are 96.1 % on zero CT at level 1, with median depth 115 um. The other 338
    are all within 100 um of the mask. The 2-D simulation at pool 4 kept 99.5 % of the on-CT vertices and 4 % of the masked ones.
