- The nmlars gain opens after the lars EMAs settle (beta 0.99, ~200 updates). Throughput is unchanged (0.668 vs 0.662 samp/s).
- Seed 8 (other windows) confirms the direction at a smaller size. Cooldown loss: -0.016 (seed 7), -0.003 (seed 8). wind4: -0.007 in both
  seeds. acc: +0.016 and +0.014. Every loss and wind4 CI after window 500 excludes 0 in both seeds.
- Ablation (seed 7): NorMuon alone carries the whole gain, and lars adds nothing consistent on top. What helps is NorMuon's per-row
  (per output channel) second-moment normalisation, not the per-layer equalisation of the update / weight ratio.
- Seed-8 NorMuon (2026-11-15, stopped at window 740 for a merge gate, not rerun: two seeds were judged enough): same sign as seed 7,
  smaller this early. Windows 501-740: loss -0.004 [-0.008, -0.001], wind4 -0.007 [-0.009, -0.004], phase flat, gn 4.9 vs 5.6. NorMuon
  is positive on wind4 in both seeds. It also lowers gn (seed 7 -1.9 to -2.1, seed 8 -0.7), so its steps are steadier.
- A 0.0015 control (seed 7, stopped at window 830) beats 0.003 by -0.017 loss, -0.007 phase, -0.013 wind4: about 4x NorMuon's effect.
  The lr ranking is monotone (0.0015 > 0.003 > 0.006 > 0.012). That is what the start-checkpoint bias predicts: every arm resumes a
  net converged at 0.003, and a smaller step disturbs it less. So this does not justify a lower peak lr. The from-scratch
  check was not run: training was paused until the bug-fix round ends. It would be a pair of `admuon_desk_scratch2.sh` arms
  (normuon, 0.003 vs 0.006, then 0.0015 vs 0.003; the original admuon_desk_scratch.sh's rm guard refused scratch_* outputs).
- Recommended for try7: `--normuon 1` at Muon 0.003 / AdamW 3e-4. Run the from-scratch pair before choosing the peak lr. lars and DoG
  stay off (both are opt-in flags, checkpoint-compatible).

## Sampler GPU work vs the training stream; the pair rule on both cards (2026-11-14, branch w4stream-20261114)

**The w4 context stream was blocking.** Training kernels launch on the legacy default stream (no stream argument, no per-thread
default stream). nn_w4.cu's sampler contexts (--gpu-aug 3: the winding mod 4 runs on the device) created their stream with a plain
cudaStreamCreate, which synchronises with the legacy stream both ways. So each w4 op of a worker waited for the queued training work
on that card (try5: a worker spun 0.7 core inside cudaMemcpy2DAsync in ctx_run), and the next training kernel waited for the w4 op.
Now cudaStreamNonBlocking; the context's buffers are its own. Perf pod, scratch2's net on one card, P 512, --det 1, 8 workers / 6
slots, 30 steps after 10: 0.864 -> 0.908 samp/s (+5.1 %), sampler wait 11.2 -> 5.7 %; UFSM_BATCH_HASH identical (5 batches); the step
losses differ at the level two runs of master differ. Audit of the other sampler-side GPU paths (nn_band pair rule / codes, nn_fibre,
nn_inkfly, nn_mcodes, nn_gpudec, nn_ctdev): all on non-blocking streams; the legacy-stream calls left are one-time (constant tables,
gpudec's position table) or buffer growth (cudaFree / cudaMalloc, a device sync but only when a box exceeds the reserve).

**Host side of the step otherwise clean.** nsys on the same setup at P 768, gaps before the trainer thread's ops attributed to its
previous API call: 26 ms of host-caused idle per 11.7 s busy (0.2 %), plus ~120 ms of cuBLASLt lazy loading in the first steps.

**--onfly-gpu A,B.** try6 (P 768 data parallel, the pair rule's 3 slots on GPU 0, fibre and ink on GPU 1): GPU 0 100 % / 15.7 GB,
GPU 1 74 % / 13.7 GB, the gradient all-reduce waiting for GPU 0. band_pair_gpu_devices puts --onfly-slots contexts on each listed
device, taken round robin (bg_ctx.dev, cudaSetDevice per call); the planner's budget is the minimum free memory over the cards, so
2 + 2 slots (1.54 GB each) instead of 3 on GPU 0 (2.3 GB) also raises it. test_phase_onfly: --onfly-gpu 0,0 --onfly-slots 2 gives
the stored-phase batches.

## Gradient noise scale in the trainer (2026-11-14, branch gns-20261114)

`--gns 1` logs the gradient noise scale B_noise (McCandlish et al. 2018, "An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training", app. A.1), the
batch size in windows above which a larger batch stops buying proportionally fewer updates. E|G_b|^2 = |G|^2 + S / b for a b-window
mean gradient (S = tr Sigma, the per-window gradient variance), so two squared norms at batch sizes b < B give unbiased |G|^2 =
(B |G_B|^2 - b |G_b|^2) / (B - b) and S = (|G_b|^2 - |G_B|^2) / (1/b - 1/B); B_noise = EMA(S) / EMA(|G|^2) (`src/gns.h`, header-only,
bias-corrected EMAs, `--gns-beta` 0.99 per update).

Which pair. The brief was b = one GPU's accumulated gradient before the cross-GPU sum, B = after it. The trainer does not have that
gradient: the all-reduce runs every step (window), and `--accum` accumulates the already averaged gradient. So the pairs are:
- `--accum K` (try6: K 5 x 2 GPUs): b = one step's all-reduced gradient (nl B = 2 windows; |G_b|^2 the mean over the update's K steps),
  B = the update's mean (2K = 10 windows). Both norms are computed anyway (the per-step non-finite check, the update's clip norm): zero
  extra work, no extra sync. B / b = 5 conditions the estimate better than 2.
- data parallel without `--accum` (no `--split`): b = each replica's own window (mean of |g|^2 over the replicas, one more fp32 sumsq per
  GPU per step), B = the all-reduced mean.
- one GPU without `--accum`, or `--split` without `--accum`: one batch size only, no estimate (a notice with `--gns 1`; trains as before).
Default on whenever a pair exists. Norms are of the raw unscaled fp32 gradients (after the loss-scale division, before clipping, Muon,
weight decay), reduced by `nn_sumsq`. A non-finite window is left out of both norms, as it is out of the update.

Log: ` gns N W (|G|^2 a, S b)` on the log line; log.csv gains `gns,gns_g2,gns_s` (empty before the first pair; the header of a resumed
run's older log.csv is extended in place at start, `csv_extend_header`). scripts/u0/watch.sh reads log.csv by position and now ignores the
trailing columns.

Test (tests/test_gns.c, CPU): synthetic per-window gradients with |G|^2 = 1 and uneven diagonal noise (true B_noise 20.05) replayed
through both pairings, 20000 updates each: per-update means of |G|^2 and S within 0.5 %, EMA (beta 0.999) B_noise 20.18 (accum 5 x 2),
19.88 (accum 4 x 1), 21.01 (b 1 vs B 2), 19.89 (b 1 vs B 8). With noise 108 windows (B_noise >> B) the same run's EMA ratio was off by
up to 15 % at beta 0.9995: the |G|^2 estimate's spread is ~S / B per update, so a run far below its noise scale needs a long EMA before
the ratio settles; read B_noise over hundreds of updates. test_accum.sh checks the line, the csv columns and the one-GPU notice.

Caveats. `--echo-max` replays windows; an echo inside one update correlates its windows and pulls S down (B_noise reads low). Loss terms
normalised per window (dice, MIL) make "per-window gradient" the unit, which is what B counts. Per-parameter-group B_noise (trunk /
attention / heads) is not done: it needs per-tensor sumsq over the grad buffer's offsets; the whole-net number first.

### --accum auto: the batch follows the noise scale (same branch, follow-up)

`--accum auto --accum-min A --accum-max M --gns-k K` (A: the checkpoint's accumulation, else 1; M 64; K 1): the target batch is K x EMA
B_noise windows, accum = round(target / windows per step) (windows per step = nl B, the GPU count on try6). Controller (`accum_ctl` in
gns.h), once per update: nothing during the first `--accum-warm` 1000 updates of each (re)start (only the EMAs run); then a change only
after the target stayed above `--accum-margin` 1.25 x the current batch for `--accum-hold` 200 consecutive updates (a NaN or <= 0 estimate
restarts the count), at most one change per `--accum-gap` 500 updates, x2 at most, capped at M, never down. The lr is not touched: the WSD
schedule counts windows, so a larger batch at the same lr is the "grow the batch instead of decaying the lr" regime. Each change is logged
(`step N: --accum auto: accum a -> b (... B_noise, K; update u)`).

Mechanics: the update condition is (step - anchor) % accum == 0 and the optimizer's step count upd_base + (step - anchor) / accum (anchor 0,
upd_base 0 for a fixed --accum: the old steps % K and step / K exactly). A change at an update sets anchor = that step, upd_base = its update
number. The gradient sum buffers are allocated at start when M > 1 (no allocation after the first steps). The checkpoint's extra gains
`"gns":{"g2","s","w","n"}` (the EMAs, with --gns) and `"accum","anchor","upd"` (auto only), appended last; a resume restores the EMAs and,
under auto, the accumulation (anchor = the resume step: a partial sum at the checkpoint is dropped, as before).

Tests: test_gns's controller traces (2 windows per step, start accum 5): B_noise 11 never moves it (11 < 12.5); 40 -> accum 10 at update
1200 (warm 1000 + hold 200, x2 cap), 20 at 1700 (gap), then held (40 < 1.25 x 40); 150-update excursions above the threshold never change
it; 1e4 -> 10, 20, 40, 64 at 1200 / 1700 / 2200 / 2700; 60 then 2 -> up, never down; a NaN every 150 updates holds it. test_accum.sh (5):
the trainer with K 1000, warm 2, hold 1, gap 1 goes accum 2 -> 4 at step 6, 4 -> 8 at step 10, the checkpoint holds accum 8 / anchor 10
/ upd 4, and a resume continues at accum 8 with the EMAs (step 20 = update 5).

## Recompute and host offloads in scratch2: what the memory modes cost (2026-11-14, branch recomp-20261114)

Goal: free device memory on the desk's 16 GB cards and spend it on less recompute / fewer host offloads (estimated 5-10 %).

**P 1024 --split z (try5), the per-card plan** (UFSM_MEM_DRY=1 UFSM_MEM_REPORT=2 on the perf pod, `--gpus 0,0` = one card twice,
UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB 13.66 = the desk card's free memory at the planner; the plan line matches try5's log: 11.59 of 13.16 GB):

| part | GB |
|---|---|
| network (dry build, 136 x 256^2 cells): encoder a1 / a2 / GN + down outputs 2.65, decoder 1.44, gout / gskip 1.21, rest 0.08 | 5.38 |
| task: head slabs 0.67, gpu-aug staging 1.16 (uint8 CT / labels), full-resolution input 1.14, latent head slab 0.29, label stream slab sets, split halo planes 0.27, +1/14 margin | 5.26 |
| workspace (tb / 14) + fixed (550 MB) | 0.96 |
| mode 4 (lean 2, chunked, shared a1 offloaded; 3.21 GB host offloads each way) | **11.59** |
| the same without host offloads (encoder a1 re-run instead) | 13.89 |
| mode 0 (no lean, no chunking, no offloads) | 23.39 |

Weights, optimizer state, the on-the-fly phase / fibre / ink buffers took 2.76 GB before the planner; the cards ran at ~15.4 of 16.3 GB,
so ~0.9 GB of real headroom: no offload-free mode fits at P 1024.

**P 512 data parallel (try6, from 08:32)**: the per-card plan is 4.27 of 12.90 GB (cards 8.6 / 8.1 GB), so the fastest mode fits.
Perf pod, one RTX PRO 4000, try6's flags on the wind fixture, UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB 12.9, UFSM_BENCH_SAME=1 (GPU time, the same batch),
--det 1, 24 steps, s/step over the second half:

| setting | s/step | peak device |
|---|---|---|
| --mem auto (lean 2, chunked, shared a1, 0.75 GB offloads each way) | 1.019, 1.012 | 7.15 GB |
| --mem fast (picks "MX gradients, no host offloads") | 1.002, 1.000 | 8.41 GB |
| --mem fast + UFSM_HEAD_SLAB_Z 32 | 1.004 | 8.90 GB |
| --mem fast + UFSM_HEAD_SLAB_Z 64 | 1.011 | 9.88 GB |

--mem fast: **-1.4 %** step for +1.26 GB per card; losses within the run-to-run spread (auto vs auto 2e-3 at step 5, the same for fast).
The recompute left in every mode is recompute 1: GN + SiLU applied in the conv's operand staging (fused) and the decoder's upsampled
part rebuilt, both cheap; UFSM_RECOMPUTE=0 is not supported with MX storage (aborts "MX storage needs MX inputs and outputs of one
format"). The step is 75-85 % convolutions (UFSM_PROF), so the memory modes cannot give 5-10 % here. Larger head slabs: no gain.

**P 768 data parallel (try6 from 09:01: accum 5, --onfly-slots 3 x 768 MB on GPU 0)**: GPU 0 has 11.04 GB free at the planner
(15.75 of 16.3 GB used live). Plan at that free memory (UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB 11.04): auto / fast both pick lean 2 + chunked + offloads,
9.70 GB (2.54 GB offloads each way); the smallest mode without offloads needs 11.51 GB (lean 2 + shared a1 re-run), mode 0 19.06.
So --mem fast changes nothing at P 768 (it falls back, no refusal). Upper bound if it fit (pod uncapped, UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB 14, same
batch, 20 steps): auto 3.421 s/step, peak 12.35 GB; fast (lean 1, no offloads) 3.414 s/step, peak 15.76 GB: **-0.2 %**.
split3's bench_s2 sweep at the P 1024 split card share (128 x 256^2 cells, network only) agrees: each of the six offload / share
switches and lean 1 within +-0.5 % (3.41-3.45 s); the offloads overlap the kernels.

Use: MEMMODE=fast only where the window leaves ~1.3 GB spare (P 512: -1.4 %); at P 768 / 1024 keep --mem auto. No memory mode
gains more than 2 % on this net: the remaining host-side cost is PCIe contention in the trainer (perf2's ~180 ms exposed), not the
activation offloads or recompute.
tests/bench_s2: one desk card's share of the P 1024 split trunk on one GPU (synthetic input; the unet env switches, BS2_CAP_GB ballast).
## The head's backward-data on the tensor cores by default (2026-11-14, branch headtc-20261114)

conv1_to_mx_tc_k (perf2 11-13: the latent cell head's 160 fp16 logit gradients -> 256 MX-fp4 channels with m16n8k16 MMAs) was off by
default since test_lat_head failed with it on. On the pod (RTX PRO 4000), old kernel vs perf2's row-scale patch (c1b_wh_k: each
weight row times 2^e so that its largest |w| sits in [2^14, 2^15) before the fp16 conversion, 2^-e back on the fp32 sums: exact):

| check (UFSM_HEAD_BTC=1) | old | row scales |
|---|---|---|
| test_head_tc bwd-data, |w| ~0.1 (6 shapes): rel L2 vs FFMA | 7.5e-3 .. 8.1e-3 | the same |
| test_head_tc bwd-data, |w| ~3e-7 (new case: fp16 subnormal weights) | 0.257 FAIL | 8.1e-3 |
| test_lat_head "a second equal net" | passes (4e-9) | passes |
| test_lat_head 144 head vs the 8-output net, trunk grads | rel 0.28-0.32 FAIL | rel 0.28-0.32 FAIL |

The last row is not a kernel fault: the 8-output net takes the FFMA kernel (K <= 16), so its gx differs from the tensor-core one by
the ~8e-3 of fp16 weights and another sum order, and each MX-fp4 SR flip behind it spreads through the small test trunk. Measured
against the SR noise floor of the same net (the FFMA kernel, the backward's SR seed moved): tensor cores vs FFMA rel 0.33-0.39, the
other seed 0.65-0.73. The check now runs its exact comparison with the FFMA kernel (1.4e-9) and requires the tensor-core gradient
within 1.5x that floor + 0.15 (TLH_FP8, MX-fp8 gradients without SR: floor ~1e-7, tensor cores vs FFMA rel 0.063-0.074,
the fp16 weights' rounding through e4m3 steps). Default on (UFSM_HEAD_BTC=0: the FFMA kernel); test_head_tc keeps the tiny-weight case. Time (nsys, scratch2 net + heads, P 768 one card,
the wind fixture): conv1_to_mx_t_k 111.1 ms a step -> conv1_to_mx_tc_k 20.4 + c1b_wh_k 0.1 ms, -91 ms (~2.5 % of the kernel time).

## Two fast-tier failures on master: test_lldec pool 3, test_wbench_stats without bc (2026-11-14, branch fixtests-20261114)

- test_lldec: the pooled codes views 8x deep (pool 3) returned rc -2 from phase_onfly_decode_gpu since 2dd6744 (band gpu, 11-13),
  which changed tile_gpu's size guard into `k > 2` (no device path at 8x) while the walk above it and bg_codes_run take k <= 3 and
  the test checks pool 3. Now `k > 3`: an 8x tile goes to the device again, and a box that does not fit the reserved slab buffer
  still returns -1 (the CPU path) without allocating, as at 2x / 4x.
- test_wbench_stats: the script built its B table with `bc -l`, which the pods do not have (the paired difference came out empty);
  awk instead.

## Kernel fusion for scratch2: what is left to fuse, the head slabs (2026-11-14, branch fuse-20261114)

Goal: fuse GroupNorm-apply + SiLU + MX-fp4 quantisation into the 3^3 convs (forward and backward) for the scratch2 step.

**Profile** (perf pod, RTX PRO 4000; scratch2's 92 M net and heads on one card, the wind fixture, P 768, `UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB=15.5` so the
planner picks a 16 GB card's mode: MX gradients, chunked, lean 2, shared encoder a1; /vesuvius/ufsm/fuse/prof.sh). UFSM_PROF per step:
conv fwd 737 ms (27 %), bwd_data 543 (20 %), wgrad 1075 (40 %), loss 275 (10 %), gn 30 (1.1 %), optimizer 38-57. Level 0 is ~75 % of
the conv time (dec0.c1 fwd / bdata / wgrad 302 / 207 / 379 ms; enc0.c2 and dec0.c2 ~95 / 92 / 185 each). nsys kernel shares:
conv_fwd_f4_k (fwd + bdata) 31 %, conv_bwd_w_f4ws_k 25.5 %, lat_up4_k 3.3, fstem_fwd_k 3.3, lat_adj_xy_k 3.0, conv1_to_mx_t_k 3.0,
conv_bwd_w_s2_f8_k 2.5, conv_fwd_s2_f8_k 2.4, conv_bwd_w1_tc_k 2.4, loss_grad_k 2.2, w4_events_k 2.1.

**The planned fusion is already there.** conv_fwd_f4_k applies GN + SiLU while it stages its input (gnp_t; or gn_prenorm_f4_k once per
layer when the input is re-read by several output blocks) and writes MX-fp4 plus the next GroupNorm's sums in its epilogue; the
backward's GN-SiLU apply is deferred into the weight gradient's gy pre-pass (lp_gnpend). Everything GroupNorm-shaped left is ~2.7 % of
the kernel time (gn_silu_bwd_apply_rec_k 1.3, the stats 0.5, gy_pre4_k 0.4, gn_prenorm 0.2), so the 15-25 % is not available there.

**Conv pipelining: no gain.** The earlier convfuse agent's ablation of conv_fwd_f4_k<4,2> (L0 32 x 256^2 x 256 slab, 25.8 ms): no MMA
13.6 ms, no input staging 19.7, no weight staging 19.0 (the "no epilogue" arm lets the compiler drop the MMAs). Double-buffered weight
stages by cp.async (the next stage in flight during the MMAs, two blocks per SM still fit): L0 fwd 26.79 -> 26.79 ms, bdata 30.6 ->
30.4, L1 unchanged (bench_sp24, min of 7, twice). So staging is not exposed latency; it costs issue slots and shared-memory bandwidth
next to the MMA loop's ldmatrix traffic (per tap pair and warp 2 KB of A + 1 KB of B for 16 MMAs). Not kept. A wider output tile per
staged input is the remaining conv lever (sparse24's note too); ncu is not available on the pod (ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM).

**Head slabs: the pad outputs skipped.** With --fib-head the head is padded from 23 to 32 outputs (g_pad_ch, no loss); the slabs still
upsampled them (lat_up4_k, both passes), zeroed their gradient and adjoined it (lat_adj_xy_k / lat_adj_z_k): 9 of 32 channels of
work for zero gradients. LUPN (train.c) leaves them out of the upsample, the zeroing and the adjoint (the coarse rows stay at the
zero they start at). UFSM_LAT_PAD_UP=1: the old path. The first gradient pass's coarse gradient planes (UFSM_LATG_DUMP, 2.26 GB):
byte-identical; loss category 279 -> 255 ms a step.

**Head slabs: the fused gradient pass with --ink-head.** nn_lat_fuse_grad (upsample + BCE gradient + transposed upsample per coarse
cell, no fp16 slab) was off for every --ink-head run by a blanket !g_ink2 in its condition; the ink channel (11) lies outside the
fused normal / density group (2-8) and has its own targets and sums. Now on: the same dump byte-identical to the chain as well (the fp32
re-association of the fused sums does not reach the fp16 planes on this window), step-1 loss equal, loss category 255 -> 219.5 ms.
Together 279 -> 219.5 ms of ~2.72 s GPU time a step: -2.2 % at P 768 one card. UFSM_LAT_FUSE=0 turns the fused pass off as before.
At P 512 (try6's per-card shape, the same config): loss 85.0 -> 68.4 ms of ~870 ms (UFSM_PROF sums), -1.9 %. What is left of the head /
loss path at P 512 (nsys, share of kernel time): fstem_fwd_k 3.2 (both passes), conv1_to_mx_t_k 2.4 (perf2: the TC version), lat_fuse_k
2.0, fstem_bwd_k 1.6, lat_adj_xy_k 1.5, w4_events_k + w4_runs_k 2.7, lat_up4_k 1.4, loss_grad_k + loss_stats_k 2.1, conv1_mx_tc_k 1.2,
lab_unpack_k 1.0, ink_sym_k 0.9, the target builders (packed_mask, ink_tg, unwrap_tg, w4_stats / w4_grad) ~2.5.

**The ink-MIL plane-bound overflow (try6, P 512 DP, step ~400).** "a slab's pairs exceeded its plane bound by 19064" was not the
histogram (k_plane_hist and k_pairs run the same samp arithmetic, the same FFMA chain in the SASS) but the rays: in lean memory modes
d->milr[1] aliased milr[0], and upload_async's mil_take copied the next window's rays on the copy stream before any of its stream
waits, so they landed under the current step's backward slabs; the pairs came from other rays than fin's counts. With
UFSM_MIL_ASYNC=0 (the readback) the run went on, with those steps' MIL gradient computed from the next window's rays. try5 (--split z, P 1024)
was exposed the same way: its plan was lean 2 too (one ray buffer), and upload_async's split branches (upsplit / hsplit) also called
mil_take before their waits; its logs hold no overflow line (try5-20261114/), so either no overlap reached the bound or the excess
stayed within it: its MIL gradients were not checked. Now two ray
buffers in every mode (+2.6 MB at 65536 rays), the copy waits for ev_done[i] (the step that last read buffer i), and an overflow
reported by a later step switches every thread to the per-slab readback with a warning instead of exit(1). test_ink_mil: rays A for
the passes and fin, rays B (6 planes away in z) copied over them before the backward slabs, then a step on B: the old code returned
-1, now rc 0, one overflow counted, and the second step's gradient byte-equal to the readback's.

## Split peer copies off the copy engines (2026-11-14, branch peerk-20261114)

**What was exposed.** The desk nsys of the scratch2 split step (11-13, ny2) shows both cards kernel-idle for ~175 ms per step at
three points, each ending in `zs_add_k`, the split's GN-statistics all-reduce:

| when | idle (ms) | big copy running |
|---|---|---|
| forward start | 81-88 | a 606 MB D2H, then a 1212 MB D2H (level-0 a1 out) |
| backward | 50 | a 1212 MB H2D (a1 back) |
| backward | 36 | a 1212 MB H2D (a1 back) |

The all-reduce's peer copies are a few bytes to 0.84 MB. Without P2P on the 5060 Tis, `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` is staged through the
host on the copy engines. In the trace each tiny peer copy starts within 0.01 ms of the big copy's end: the copy engine runs its
queue in order across streams. Every all-reduce issued during an a1 transfer therefore stalls both cards until the transfer ends.

So the activation offloads themselves are overlapped as designed. What is exposed is the collective queued behind them on the copy
engine.

**Bench (RTX PRO 4000, kcopy.cu / cechunk.cu).**
- A small D2H on another stream waited 39.4 ms behind a 1212 MB D2H. Splitting the big copy into chunks of 8-256 MB changed
  nothing, because all chunks are queued ahead of it.
- The same copy done by kernels through mapped pinned host memory (SM loads and stores over PCIe, no copy engine) took
  0.04 ms (4 KB), 0.35 ms (1 MB) and 1.3 ms (4 MB), whether the copy engine was idle or busy.

**Change.** `peer_copy` in nn_loss.cu replaces the five `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` calls of the split: halo begin, halo k, gather, xchg
and the GN all-reduce.
- Copies up to `UFSM_PEER_KCOPY_KB` (default 4096; 0 off) between 16-byte aligned addresses take the kernel path.
- Ordering: the source device's helper stream waits for the caller's stream. A kernel there writes the bytes to a per-direction
  mapped staging buffer (with `__threadfence_system`). The caller's stream waits for that write, and a kernel copies the bytes in.
- The staging buffer's next write waits for this read.
- Larger or unaligned copies, and a one-GPU split, keep `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync`. `UFSM_PEER_KCOPY_SAME=1` forces the kernel path
  on one GPU so the tests can cover it.

**Tests.**
- test_split_lat and test_split_gnbwd pass with and without `UFSM_PEER_KCOPY_SAME=1`. In test_split_lat that runs 5092 `kc16_k`
  copies.
- test_split (all its cases) passes with `UFSM_PEER_KCOPY_SAME=1`. The perf-pod fast tier passes apart from the pre-existing
  test_wbench_stats, test_univ2 and test_lldec.

**Desk A/B** (try4's stop 3, 11-14 06:22; `/vesuvius/ufsm/perf2/peerk_swap.sh`, the try4 recipe with `--echo-max 4`, 10 steps each).

| arm | Mvox/s, steps 2-9 |
|---|---|
| `UFSM_PEER_KCOPY_KB=0` | 80.0 (74.9-83.7) |
| kernel copies | 82.1 (78.4-86.1), +2.6 % |

The nsys of the kernel-copy arm has no gap before the all-reduce behind an a1 transfer any more. What is left before a `kc16_k` is
2-13 ms with no copy running: the two cards waiting on each other. The largest remaining idle is the step-boundary label warp:
65 + 66 + 181 + 64 ms with 570 MB copies, which lsplit-20261114 moves under the forward.

## The early label warp under --split z (2026-11-14, branch lsplit-20261114)

**Problem.** lab_early (2026-11-13, "The next batch's label warp under the forward", below) never engaged under `--split z`.
- It hangs off `hsplit`, which requires `!split`, and it allocates a second scratch plane.
- try3 and try4 have no "label warp:" line, so the warp still ran at the step boundary into the input buffer, and the next forward waited
  for it.
- The 11-13 desk nsys shows ~350 ms per card per step there: `lw_phase` / `lw_ink` kernels with 570 MB D2H and 636 MB H2D copies,
  both cards kernel-idle.
- A second plane per card cannot be had: a split side's plane is ~570 MB, and the cards run with 63-553 MB free.

**Change.**
- Under `--split z`, `upload_async` uploads the input first and records `ev_up`. The label warp follows on the copy stream and records
  `ev_lab`.
- The forward starts on `ev_up`. Head pass 0 and the aux stream wait for `ev_lab` (already so since lwarp).
- The host batch is released, and validation's buffer switch happens, only after `ev_lab`.
- The scratch is hs_lg alone: idle from the gradient pass to the next statistics pass, 629 MB on the desk. `nn_lw_sink` (nn_aug.cu)
  makes every `_z` label builder write its output in chunks of up to 64 planes through two chunk buffers in hs_lg. These are the
  phase / ink warps, the symmetry, the w4 runs, the ink bits and the identity copies.
- After each chunk's kernel, a callback on the same stream moves the chunk on: a D2H into the pinned host planes, or `nn_lab_pack`
  into the device-kept packed planes.
- The kernels already index their output relative to `k0`, and the source stays staged, so a chunk costs one kernel launch. Nothing
  is restaged.
- `UFSM_LAB_EARLY=0` turns it off.

**Two fixes the test needed.**
- The sink is per thread: each split side uploads on its own thread, and both sides share one device in the emulation.
- In the one-GPU emulation, the label builders now take the side's staging slot, `nn_aug_set_slot`, as the CT already did
  (`nn_zcomm.slot`). With the warp after the CT, side 1's labels had restaged the buffer side 0's CT was reading.
  compute-sanitizer showed `aug_write_k` reading 12 KB past a 1 MB stage. Two real GPUs never shared a slot.

**Test.** `tests/test_lab_early_split.sh` (gpu): `--gpus 0,0 --split z`, P 128, the wind fixture with ink and fibre targets, `--rv 2`,
`--gpu-aug 3` (w4 runs), `--det 1`. Each side's plane is 96 planes, so it goes through 2 chunks.
- With `UFSM_LAT_STREAM=check` every slab's streamed planes equal the device-built ones (0 of 47 M slab bytes differ).
- The losses equal those of `UFSM_LAB_EARLY=0`, line for line.
- The same holds with the planes in pinned host memory (`UFSM_LAT_LDEV=0`, the desk's case).

**Desk A/B** (try4's stop, 11-14 07:13, `lsplit_swap.sh`, P 1024, 10 steps each).

| arm | Mvox/s, steps 2-10 |
|---|---|
| `UFSM_LAB_EARLY=0` (warp at the step boundary) | 80.2 |
| default (warp under the forward) | 83.2 (+3.7 %, noisy) |

Both arms' losses are finite.

The two-GPU `UFSM_LAT_STREAM=check` run did not fit at P 1024: check mode keeps the device-built planes too, so the smallest mode
needs 19.91 GB. `lsplit_check.sh` repeats it at P 768. The one-GPU emulation's check passes byte-equal.

## Widening warm start: u1 -> scratch2's architecture with the donor's function (2026-11-14, branch widen-20261114)

From scratch, scratch2's architecture does not learn phase or wind4: try4 was at chance after 1866 steps, and every latent net that
works was warm-started. But `--init-from` copies only exact-shape tensors, so u1 (10 M; widths 96,128,160,192; 4 levels) gave
scratch2 (6 levels, 4 attention blocks, gfilm) nothing.

`train --init-from u1.ckpt --init-widen 1` (`unet_init_widen`) builds the wider, deeper net so that it computes u1's function.

**How.**
- **Replicated channels.** Every channel space of the donor's levels 0..3 is replicated GroupNorm group by group. Both nets have
  8 groups. Target channel j of group g is a copy of donor channel g·cpg_d + (j mod cpg_t) mod cpg_d. Each conv's input weights
  are divided by the copy count, so every conv computes the donor's sums. The convs covered are the encoders, the down convs (with
  down_norm), the decoders and the head.
- **When this is exact.** A group's mean and variance stay the donor's only if every source channel has the same number of copies,
  i.e. the target's channels per group are a whole multiple of the donor's.
- **The extra levels.** They sit between the donor's bottom (enc3) and its first decoder (dec2). The path runs through dec[3]
  (conv, GN, SiLU, conv, GN, SiLU, with no residual), which cannot be an identity. Instead it passes the raw bottom tensor `a` with
  silu(z) − silu(−z) = z:
  - enc3.c2 writes +a and −a in pairs. Each group is symmetric, so its mean is exactly 0 and its normalisation is a per-group scale r.
  - dec3.c1 takes the pair difference (centre taps) into new pairs, and dec3.n1 scales again.
  - dec3.c2 takes the difference: r·r'·a.
  - GroupNorm is scale-invariant, so dec3.n2 (the donor's enc3.n2 parameters and FiLM) reproduces the donor's output exactly.
- **New parts.** Levels 4-5 feed dec3.c1 through zero weights. gfilm (A/B zero) and the attention stage (zero out-projections) start
  as identities, so the new parts are a no-op at step 0 but receive gradients.
- **Head and stem.**
  - Head rows are mapped by name: rows 0-10 kept, rv 12-13 from 11-12, and the sub-cell rows 32-159 from 16-143. The usual
    lat-guide-3 sub-cell zeroing is skipped.
  - Ink and fibre rows start fresh with their bias priors.
  - The fine stem keeps W1 and b1; its W2 rows are mapped by channel, and its 10 new outputs start at 0.
  - FiLM pairs are copied per channel; the new norms get none.
- **Other state.** EMA weights get the same mapping. Optimiser state starts at 0, and the inherited ranges are recorded for
  `--init-lr-mult`. gn_ema's running statistics start empty, so the warm-up forwards use the window's statistics, as u1 does.
- **Requirements, otherwise it refuses:** the same group count and input count; down_norm as the donor (u1 has it, so try4 needs
  `--down-norm 1`); the bottom width at least twice the donor's (for the pairs); no residual blocks or custom decoder widths.

**test_widen**, on the perf pod RTX PRO 4000. Each figure is mean |d| / mean |logit| on the same random window, inference.
- 3 → 4 levels with attention and gfilm, whole copies (32,64,96 → 64,128,192,96): 3.0e-4 at 16-bit.
- u1-like uneven copies (96,128,160 → 256,320,384,96): 1.6e-2.
- The real u1 → scratch2 config, rows 0-10:

| target widths | per group | 16-bit | MX-fp4 (u1's own fp4 vs 16-bit gap 0.24) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 192,256,320,384 +288,288 (2x) | whole copies | 3.0e-4 | 0.23 |
| 288,384,480,576 +288,288 (3x) | whole copies | 4.4e-4 | 0.25 |
| 256,320,384,448 +288,288 (scratch2) | 12->32, 16->40, 20->48, 24->56 | 0.124 (max 1.0) | 0.30 |

**Through the trainer** on the wind fixture: P 512, lr 0, `--det 1`, the same windows. Reference is u1 itself (an identity widen, so
its sub-cell rows are kept). Widened is 2x widths, 6 levels, attention, gfilm, gn-ema.
- Per step, phase bce reference / widened: 0.7088/0.7097, 0.5681/0.5577, 0.4483/0.4452, 0.5604/0.5524.
- wind4 acc: 0.360/0.363, 0.539/0.537, 0.701/0.677, 0.543/0.550.
- rv bce: 0.362/0.356, 0.191/0.181.
- These agree within the fp4 noise.
At scratch2's own widths (uneven copies), the same windows give:

- wind4 acc 0.376, 0.552, 0.686, 0.540.

On the fixture's labelled windows these widths stay as close as the exact 2x: the 12% logit deviation on random inputs does not show up as a loss gap there.

## Echo in try4: slot-bound new windows, and a GPU-idle meter (2026-11-14, branch echofix-20261114)

try4 (P 1024 `--split z`, accum 4, `--echo-max 4`, 4 slots, 10 workers) logged echo 48-78 % and "wait" 11-21 % at windows
1900-2550, at 73-80 Mvox/s. The run with `--replay 2` before it ran at 69-77 Mvox/s.

**Why so few new windows.**
- The startup line says "at most 3 windows are built at once": 4 slots minus the trainer's one.
- Echo held 2 more slots as candidates, and builders took one back only while a new window was ready, so one window was built at a
  time.
- A redraw costs 0.40-0.44 s there against a ~7 s step, so one candidate is enough.
- `sampler_start` now holds 2 candidates per window only when slots - w >= workers + 2w (w: the windows a step takes), otherwise 1.
  try4 and try5 (13 slots / 12 workers) get 1. `UFSM_ECHO_KEEP` overrides.

**What "wait" counts.**
- Under echo, the trainer is inside `sampler_next_gate` from the end of its launches until a card's `ev_done`, while the GPUs still
  run the queued backward. The wait meter counts that time.
- The step line now adds " (GPU idle for data N%)": from the first probe that finds a card done to the batch handover. The gate
  polls every 0.5 ms whenever a probe is given, also with nothing to echo yet.

**Test.** test_echo gains a `--split z` case: one GPU, a starved worker. It logs echo 100 % with GPU idle for data 0 %.

## Adaptive data echoing: `--echo-max M` (2026-11-14, branch echo-20261114)

scratch2 waits on the sampler for 20-35 % of a long run (the 30-step bench showed 0 %), and the user accepts data echoing in
exchange for zero data wait. `--replay K` (2026-11-12) already trains every window K times with a new device-side augmentation,
but it echoes at a fixed rate whether the data path is behind or not. `train --echo-max M` echoes only when a step would otherwise
wait.

**Rule.**
- When the trainer asks for its next batch and a new window is ready, it gets the new window. New windows always come first.
- When no new window is ready, it gets the most recently released window again. The replay thread has already redrawn that window
  with a new device-side augmentation: a new cube symmetry and warp record, a new scanner plan, new intensity jitter. This is the
  same `replay_window` as `--replay`, so the labels stay exact.
- Each window is echoed at most M times.

**The gate.** An echo is handed out only once the step really would wait, not merely when the host asks early.
- The host takes the next batch right after launching a step. The step's gradient exchange and update are launched after that.
- So the trainer passes `sampler_next_gate` an `echo_busy` probe: a non-blocking query of each GPU's `ev_done`, the event recorded at
  the end of the backward.
- While every GPU is still computing, a new window that becomes ready is still taken (0.5 ms timed waits).
- Once one GPU has finished, it is waiting on the host, so the newest echo candidate goes out at once.
- `--split z` uses both cards' events, and one-window-per-GPU runs use the events of the GPUs fetching.

**Candidates.**
- The trainer keeps `echo_keep` released windows as candidates: two per window a step takes, so one is ready while the replay
  thread redraws the other. That is 2 under `--split z` (one shared window a step) and 2 x the GPU count otherwise (each GPU takes
  its own window). `UFSM_ECHO_KEEP` overrides it.
- On release, candidates beyond that go back to the builders.
- A builder that finds no free slot reclaims the oldest candidate only while a new window is ready, which the trainer takes next.
  Otherwise the candidates stay: letting builders take them down to one left the trainer a single candidate, often still being
  redrawn (numbers below).
- The replay state is now allocated before the workers start. Before this, a worker that finished its first window early left it
  unreplayed under `--replay`, and echo's reclaim read a null `rq` (a segfault in the first sampler-only test).
- `UFSM_ECHO_THREADS` sets the number of replay threads (default 2 in echo mode). Measured 1 / 2 / 3: no difference, since a redraw
  takes 0.1-0.2 s at P 512.
- B > 1 echoes the whole batch of B windows, each redrawn.

**Losses.** An echo is a complete batch with its own label planes, built by the same transform as its input. The per-label means
(phase, side, winding, ink, papyrus masks and their known-voxel counts) are computed per batch exactly as for a new window, and
nothing is double-counted. The only change is that a window can be seen up to M + 1 times, so the data distribution over steps
shifts toward the windows that were in the queue when the data path fell behind.

**Reproducibility.**
- Echo decisions depend on timing: whether a builder finished before a GPU did.
- Under `--det 1` the sampler therefore switches echo off and says so, and a `--det` run stays bit-reproducible.
- A non-det run with echo is not reproducible step for step. It was not reproducible without echo either, because the worker order
  already depends on timing.
- Mutually exclusive with `--replay K > 1`. Needs the `--replay` configurations (`sampler_replay_ok`: `--gpu-aug 2` cube batches).

**Logging.**
- The step line gains ` echo N%`, the share of the batches since the last line that were echoes.
- `UFSM_SAMPLER_ONLY=N` takes `--echo-max` too. `UFSM_SAMPLER_STEP_MS=T` simulates a T ms GPU step per batch, so the echo share at
  a given pace can be measured without a GPU.

**Numbers.**

CPU only: `UFSM_SAMPLER_ONLY=60`, the scratch2 recipe at P 512 with `--split z`, the GPU on-the-fly paths on the CPU, `UFSM_SAMPLER_COV=0`.
`UFSM_SAMPLER_STEP_MS=300` simulates a GPU step faster than the 4 slots / 6 workers deliver; "waited" is the time spent in
`sampler_next` after the first batch.

| run | wall (s) | waited (s) | new windows | echoes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--echo-max 0` | 39.4 | 20.7 (53 %) | 60 | 0 |
| echo, keep 1 | 21.7 | 3.3 | 24 | 36 |
| echo, keep 2, reclaim down to 1 | 23.6 | 5.1 | 26 | 34 |
| echo, keep 2, reclaim only above keep (default) | 19.0-20.0 | 0.5-1.5 (3-8 %) | 21-22 | 38-39 |
| same, no `--split` (2 GPUs: keep 4) | 20.2 | 1.8 | 20 | 40 |

New windows arrive at the same rate in every arm, about 1.1 per second: echo fills the wait and does not take time away from the
builders. A redraw costs 97-193 ms on a replay thread.

At a 1.5 s step (the sampler keeps up at P 512): 10 % echo over 30 batches, the remaining batches new.

GPU check, `tests/test_echo.sh` (fast tier, perf pod RTX PRO 4000): the wind fixture, P 64, one worker. Over 40 steps it echoes
62 % on average. The cap of 3 echoes a window bounds that share at 75 %, so the step still waits 20-40 % (the det run without echo
waits 18-55 %). Losses are finite. Under `--det 1` echo is off and the losses equal those of the run without the flag, line for line.
`--split z` with echo is covered only by the sampler-only runs above: the pod has one GPU. The first two-card run is scratch2's swap.

**Use.** Replace `--replay 2` with `--echo-max 4`: under `--replay 2` every window is trained twice whether data is short or not,
while echo spends only the steps that would otherwise wait.

## Test-suite speed: shards, the runner's defaults, a smoke tier, changed-file selection (2026-11-14, branch testspeed-20261113)

The fast tier (the merge gate) was slow mostly because the runner was too conservative, not because the tests are big.
- **Runner defaults.** It ran `-j CPUs/3` with 2 GPU slots per card. The tier averages ~1.1 CPUs per test and most GPU tests wait on
  the card.
- **Long tests.** A handful of single long tests set the tail: test_attn 204 s, test_fit 122 s, test_infer_mem 91 s quick (on the pod).
- **Estimates.** The hand-written EST column was off by up to 10x (test_http_reader 166 s estimated, 30 s measured), so longest-first
  packed badly.

Measured on the rented pod (RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell, a cgroup quota of 10.2 CPUs although nproc says 48), master 15e66f0's tests:

| run | -j | GPU slots | wall | CPU (user + sys) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| master runner and tests (base1) | 3 | 2 | 546 s | 1781 s |
| new -j / -G defaults only (r2) | 10 | 6 | 361 s | 1905 s |
| this branch (r3) | 10 | 8 (free memory) | 196 s | 1850 s |

- **Runner** (`tests/run_suite.sh`):
  - `-j` defaults to the cgroup CPUs (2..16) and `-T` to 2 CPUs/j.
  - GPU slots per card = the least free memory / 2.5 GB, 2..8. The largest fast-tier test peaks at ~2 GB (`-P`), and a card a
    training run holds keeps 2 slots.
  - Tests without the `gpu` tag get `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=` (empty). `-P` showed six tests using a GPU untagged, i.e. without a lock,
    on cards that training runs held: test_attn, test_attn_ray, test_attn_dfm, test_spiralfit, test_countfield, test_mesh_phase. They
    are tagged now.
  - `-t smoke` is a 61-test cross-section of the fast tier for the edit loop.
  - `-c REF` runs only the tests a change since REF can affect: the sources in the DWARF line tables of the binaries a test runs,
    cached per binary, plus every CUDA source for binaries that link the GPU ops. A changed manifest line selects its test; a build or
    runner file selects all. Example: a src/unet.c change selects 87 of 259 tests in 0.7 s.
  - `tests/suite_est.py results.tsv` rewrites the EST column from measured wall times.
- **Shards** (`UFSM_TEST_PART=K/N`, `tests/test_part.h` / `tests/test_part.sh`; lines `NAME~partKofN`). These are the same sections
  and checks, run side by side, and each section sets the state it runs with:
  - test_fit: 9 shards;
  - test_infer_mem (quick): 6 shards, 10-30 s;
  - test_spatial_augment (quick): 3 shards, 17 s whole -> ~6 s each;
  - test_heads: 3 shards; lat_plain stays with the ssl section, which reads its log;
  - test_predict_heads: 3 shards; each retrains its 3-step net, < 1 s.

  The `~full` slow-tier lines are unchanged.
- **test_attn** (204 -> 20 s on the pod). The central differences (180 of the 204 s) now run in UFSM_NCPU threads on private copies of
  P and x, so each value is bit for bit the serial one. Core 1 replays core 0's random draws and reuses its reference values. The worst
  core-1 block error is 1.6e-3 (it was 1.8e-3 on its own draws; the tolerance is 2e-3).
- **test_http_reader** (30 -> 14 s on the desk). The 24 cache combinations, the 88 failure-mode reads and the four 429 back-off reads
  run concurrently, each under its own URL tag, so the warm-cache request check sees only its own requests. The back-offs are real
  sleeps: 15 s of the old 30.

What did not get faster, and why:
- **CUDA process start.** Every CUDA process costs ~0.42 s wall and ~0.2 s of system time for its context (pod, persistence on).
  CUDA_MODULE_LOADING / CUDA_MODULE_DATA_LOADING and a keeper process change nothing; a live context elsewhere gives 0.34 s. The
  shell tests start 40-200 ufsm processes each: test_predict_heads 206 calls, 48 s of its 55 s.
- **Spin-waiting.** `cudaDeviceScheduleBlockingSync` (tried behind an env switch, reverted) left the CPU time unchanged: the tests'
  CPU is real host work (references, the CPU fit backend: test_fit's CPU-backend shard alone takes 84 CPU-s).
- **Fixture cache.** make_wind_fixture 256 takes 1.2 s and 3.7 MB. Twenty tests make one, so caching it would save ~25 CPU-s and was
  left out.
- **test_latvol.sh** (46 s uncontended). Its sections share the HTTP server and the nets of the first section, so it was left whole.
- **On the pod, CPU is the floor.** The tier's 1850 CPU-s on 10.2 CPUs is >= 181 s, so 196 s is at it. A 24- or 32-core desk with
  free GPUs ran master's fast tier in 154-266 s at -j 10 (desk results of 11-13). There the critical path, now cut to ~30 s, and the
  GPU slots decide.

## Skip-air training: masked convs in forward, backward-data and weight gradient (2026-11-14, branch skipair2-20261113)

The user approved the masked-conv approximation of 2026-11-13 ("Empty-space skipping", below) for the live scratch2 run. `train
--skip-empty 1 [--skip-thr 0] [--skip-margin 1]` trains the masked net itself, so the approximation becomes the model rather than an
inference-time error.

**What a step computes.** Per window, the tile masks are built on the GPU from the CT channel of the device input
(`nn_skip_build16`). The raw byte threshold is mapped through the window's scan-norm z-score (ia/ib when the scan jitter is on: the
threshold is widened by 4.5|isg|). Threshold 0 (the default) marks as air only cells that hold no CT byte above 0, i.e. outside a
masked scan. Tiles are 8 x 8 x 16 cells (z, y, x) at level 0, dilated by the margin at every level. Under `--split z` only the levels
below `--split-top` are masked; each card uses its own half plus halo. The masks stay registered through the backward.
- **Forward:** the MX-fp4 conv kernel skips the main loop of an inactive tile, so the output there is the bias. The GN statistics
  include those outputs.
- **Backward-data** is gx = W^T (mask . gy). gy is staged as zero in inactive tiles. gx is computed only on tiles within one tile of
  an active one.
- **Weight gradient:** the gy records (136 B per 2 planes x 8 rows x 16 x) of inactive tiles are zeroed after the bias sums, so gb
  stays the full sum. The fp4 wgrad kernels then skip every (tile, z-chunk) item whose records are all zero. In the warp-specialised
  kernel, the counts, the producers' cursors and the consumers all step over an item alike.

This is the exact gradient of the masked net. Safeguards:
- a conv's backward is masked only if its forward was (`seen[cid]`);
- a masked backward that reaches a kernel without the mask aborts;
- the sparse 2:4 kernels are bypassed for masked convs in both directions.

The heads stay dense. Skipped air still gets the head outputs computed from the constant fill, and `--ink-air` ("no ink" in air) and
the rv losses apply there unchanged, so the fill is trained to predict air. The checkpoint header gains `"skip_empty":[thr,margin,levels]`
(written only when on). A resume keeps it unless `--skip-empty 0` is passed. `predict` (and so ueval) masks the same way by default
on such a checkpoint; `--skip-empty 0` gives the dense path.

**Tests** (`test_skip_empty` (4), on the pod RTX PRO 4000):
- With every tile active, the gradient matches the dense one within the dense run-to-run noise: |d|/|g| 1.2e-8 vs 1.3e-8. The weight
  gradients sum with atomics, so the result is not bit-identical.
- With CT masks, the gradient is finite and the masked backward-data and wgrad run on all 9 convs. The cosine to the dense gradient is
  0.55, as expected for a different net with live statistics.
- Skipping the wgrad items gives the same gradient as visiting the zeroed records.
- The header round-trips.
- A side note on gn_ema: running statistics at momentum 1 make each training pass normalise with the previous pass's statistics.
  That is why the test uses live statistics.

**scratch2's net on the pod**, single card, no split. Same widths, attention, gfilm, gn-ema, scan-norm, fstem, lat-guide 3 and all
heads (unwrap2, rv 2, ink-head / mil / air 8, fib-head), on the synthetic wind fixture (`make_wind_fixture`, CT 0 outside the scroll),
`--det 1`:
- P 768, 30 steps, L0 active 0.97: the losses track dense (step 30: 1.2233 masked vs 1.2276 dense).
- P 896 on the fixture with `FX_CT_ZCUT=0.55` (CT 0 above plane 563, labelled air), L0 active 0.51-0.66, 20 steps: median
  throughput 129 Mvox/s dense, 144 masked, 146 with the wgrad item skip (+13%). The losses match to the third digit.
- `UFSM_PROF` on the same run, last step: conv fwd 1161 -> 865 ms, bwd-data 898 -> 752, wgrad 1712 -> 1333; loss, GN and optimizer
  unchanged; 4.34 -> 3.51 s GPU (-19%). Backward-data saves least because it needs the dilated mask.
- Resume: a dense checkpoint resumed with `--skip-empty 1`, a skip checkpoint resumed with no flag (masked from the header) and with
  `--skip-empty 0` (dense) all ran. The per-step losses of masked vs dense continuation differ by < 0.002.

**Predict on a skip-trained net** (fixture, 30 steps, whole 1024^3 box, window 512): masked (the checkpoint default) vs dense
`--skip-empty 0`. On material (CT >= 64) the mean |d| is 4.4 of 255 (2.8% of the mean output), 7.6% of voxels are identical and
12.9% differ by more than 8. On air the mean |d| is 0.12. So the dense path is *not* within tolerance: the attention and gfilm
couple the fill in globally. That is why predict follows the checkpoint by default. Masked predict took 10 s, dense 17 s.

**Expected gain on scratch2.** The 2026-11-13 sampler measurement put the level-0 active share at 0.83 at threshold 40 (0.85 for the
busier split half), nearly all of the inactive share being zero-filled outside of the scan, so threshold 0 sees the same.
Scaling the fixture's conv savings (-21% of conv time at 38% inactive) to ~16% inactive gives about -8% conv time, about -6 to -8% s/step.
That is to be measured in the step-5000 swap: s/step before and after on the live run, plus `skipair/swap_check.sh` (split_finite
with the skip flags: every gradient finite, masks built on both cards, no dense fallback on a masked level).

Not done: the predict `--split z` CT-stem path (non-latent nets) does not mask. The `UFSM_SKIP_AB` per-window diagnostic reads cell
logits that the streamed-head predict path does not hold (guarded, prints the timings only).

## The next batch's label warp under the forward (2026-11-13, branch lwarp-20261113)

The P 1024 split profile (perf2, below) left ~350 ms per card a step exposed at the step boundary: upload_tail warped the next --gpu-aug
batch's label planes on the device (6 x 634 MB H2D, lw_phase / lw_ink / w4 kernels, 6 x 570 MB D2H into the pinned lbh) before its CT,
because the warp's scratch was the input buffer xb (inside gout[0] in lean 2, busy until the stem's weight gradient), and the forward
waited for all of it (ev_up). The labels are first read by head pass 0, after the whole trunk forward.
**lab_early:** the tail uploads the radial records and the CT, records ev_up (the forward's wait), then runs the label warp on the copy
stream with scratch hs_lg (35 x 8 planes x P^2 x 2 B = 587 MB >= one 570 MB plane; idle from the gradient pass to the next statistics
pass, split3's planner read) + lsc (one more plane for the winding pair, allocated at the first tail when > p3 + 768 MB is free), and
records ev_lab; head pass 0 (stream 0 and the slab-upload aux stream), the synchronous upload and the end-of-backward pinned-batch
release wait for ev_lab. Same bytes in a different order: --det losses must be identical. UFSM_LAB_EARLY=0: the old order. Startup line
"label warp: ...". **Status: built, not yet run** (desk GPUs are scratch2-only; swap-window check: /vesuvius/ufsm/perf2/lwarp_swap.sh).

## Build system: CMake + Ninja, the LLVM toolchain for everything, the Makefile removed (2026-11-13, branch buildsys-20261113)

The GNU Makefile (gcc -std=c23 + nvcc, 846 lines, one hand-written rule per test) is replaced by CMakeLists.txt + CMakePresets.json
and LLVM: clang for C23, lld, llvm-ar, compiler-rt builtins and crt files; the device code goes through nvcc with clang++ as its host
compiler (UFSM_CUDA_COMPILER=nvcc, the default: clang -x cuda works, see below, but its kernels ran 1.35x slower). Configurations stay build directories (build/, build-verify/, build86/); tests are
one ufsm_exe() line each in tests/targets.cmake (converted from the Makefile rules, the exact object lists kept: weak symbols and
tfx.c's constructor make archive-style linking change behaviour).

Profile of the old build (desk 9950X, lowprio -j8, the trainer running, no ccache): clean release 388 s wall, 2260 s CPU. nvcc 2077 s
(cicc 990, ptxas 937, host g++ 106, cudafe 40), of which lp_* 1806 s; gcc 236 s; link 0.2 s. Wall set by single TUs of up to 155 s
(lp_mx_gnbwd, lp_f4fwd_i0p: up to 8 conv_fwd_f4r_k instantiations of ~70 k SASS instructions each) scheduled last (make's order).

| desk, lowprio -j8, no ccache                     | Makefile gcc + nvcc | CMake clang + clang-cuda |
|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------:|-------------------------:|
| clean release build, wall / CPU                  |      388 s / 2260 s |            177 s / 1259 s |
| host C CPU / CUDA CPU                            |       236 / 2077 s  |              117 / 1172 s |
| edit one .cu (nn_elem.cu)                        |              3.8 s  |                     2.6 s |
| edit lp_f4fwd.cuh (~30 TUs)                      |              112 s  |                      54 s |
| edit fit.c                                       |              6.3 s  |                     3.6 s |
| edit a header (tiffw.h, 20 users)                |               26 s  |    5.6 s (exact deps; make rebuilt every object on any src/*.h) |
| verify build after release, warm ccache          |                  -  |          71 s (78 % hits) |

The verify build shares ccache with release: the ptxas wrapper is named relative to the build dir, so only the ~50 units whose
preprocessed source depends on UFSM_ALL_TYPES recompile. Slowest clang TUs: lp_f4fwd_i0p 84 s, lp_f4fwd_i0 74 s, lp_f8fwd_i0s 59 s.

What clang-cuda needed: LLVM 22 writes at most PTX ISA 9.0, the ue8m0 .scale_vec::4X mma needs 9.1 (cmake/ptxas.sh.in raises the
.version line); nvcc's host min / max overloads (src/clang_cuda_compat.cuh, force-included); CCCL 13.3's cuda/std/string_view does
not compile under clang 22 (nn_fibre's cub::DeviceScan -> an own 3-pass integer scan, identical results); device nanf is declared but
not defined by clang 22 (nn_loss: the bits nvcc gives, 0x7fc00000); clang embeds no PTX unless --cuda-include-ptx. libc++ is not
possible (CUDA's crt/host_defines.h refuses it on x86): the .cu host side keeps libstdc++.

Numerics. gcc -std=c23 does not contract a*b+c (checked: no vfmadd at -O3 -march=native; gnu23 does); clang's default would, so host
C is -ffp-contract=off. -fno-math-errno is value-neutral (replaces sample.c's gcc-only optimize attribute, which gcc had ignored
anyway: "empty declaration", it sat on an enum). Device fast math = nvcc -use_fast_math on the device side only (flush, approx
transcendentals, -fapprox-func for approx div / sqrt, contract fast; no finite-math). The byte-exact units: contract off, and
__CUDA_PREC_SQRT=1, since clang leaves libdevice's reflection at 0 and sqrtf became sqrt.approx.f32 even without fast math. Their PTX
then uses the same float instruction kinds as nvcc -fmad=false (div.rn / sqrt.rn, no fma / approx / ftz); the fast units match
nvcc -use_fast_math's kinds (div.approx.ftz, sqrt.approx.ftz, ex2.approx.ftz, fma.rn.ftz).

Caveat: clang's depfile and ccache see the host pass's includes only (checked: a header included under __CUDA_ARCH__ alone neither
rebuilds nor misses the cache); no project header is device-only today (all 165 .cu checked), and none may become one.

Suite (CPU tier on the desk, no GPU): 95 pass; test_strip segfaulted under clang: the test passed argc 19 for 17 arguments (gcc's stack
layout hid it; fixed); test_sampler_safety fails the same 3 holdout checks with the gcc build of origin/master (pre-existing).
GPU tier, clang -x cuda (desk sm_120, gpucheck-1113-1529): bench_f4conv 256 total 381.3 ms vs nvcc 281.9 ms (1.35x), single kernels
up to 5.5x slower (bdata s2 down0 5.47x, up2 fwd 1.9x, s2 wgrad, stem), 4 output hashes differ. Hence nvcc for the device code, clang++
host (needs -allow-unsupported-compiler for clang 22, and nn_common's extern __shared__ smem_raw aligned 32 everywhere: nvcc's
clang-mode front end rejects differing redeclarations). Its SASS (cuobjdump -sass, instruction lines) is byte-identical to the gcc-host
Makefile build in 164 of 165 units (nn_fibre differs: the own exact integer scan replaced CUB).

nvcc + clang++ build, desk GPU check (gpucheck-1113-1551, under the suite locks): fast suite 240 pass, 6 fail: 4 missing release-dir
helpers (the check built only ufsm into build/; the test target's test-prep builds them), test_sampler_safety (fails on gcc too),
test_predict_feather: a test bug, its CT fixture converted out-of-range doubles to uint8_t (UB; gcc wrapped mod 256, clang's
vectorised loop saturated, half the volume 0 / 255, the windows stopped disagreeing: 22 % < the 25 % gate). Through int64_t the gcc
bytes are kept and both pass (1662645 voxels blended). Predict end to end (fixture checkpoint, gcc vs cmake binary): byte-identical;
bench_f4conv output hashes identical. Fixture train (unwrap2 P 128 B 1, 40 steps): 1.74 vs 1.78 s; loss identical to step 4, then
apart (step 8 1.94 vs 2.11); a gcc-vs-gcc repeat is still to run (2 sampler workers).

Compile times with nvcc (forlindesk, -j24, no ccache), Makefile -> CMake: clean release 247 -> 245 s (UFSM_PTXAS_SPLIT=4: 242 s),
clean arch86 329 -> 325 s, edit nn_elem.cu 3.9 -> 3.0 s, lp_f4fwd.cuh 89 -> 94 s, fit.c 5.7 -> 3.0 s, tiffw.h 16.5 -> 4.3 s. The clean
build is the critical path of single nvcc units (lp_mx_gnbwd 183 s, lp_f4fwd_i0p 143 s, lp_mx_s2bwd_wide 133 s, lp_f8fwd_i0s 131 s;
clang -x cuda built everything in 87 s); what nvcc keeps of the gain: exact header deps, ccache shared by release / verify, faster host C.
Next lever: one instantiation per unit for those four.

## scratch2 at P 1024 --split z: device memory outside the planner, and a per-step leak (2026-11-13, branch s2fix-20261113)

The full scratch2 flag set (widths 256,320,384,448,288,288, attention 4 blocks with scroll PE, gn-ema, scan-norm, gfilm, ink head + MIL +
air, fibre head, rv 2, unwrap2, on-the-fly phase, fibre / ink on the GPU) planned at 11.59 GB per card but died within ~20 steps. The
fixes, by what each freed or stopped per card:

| item | per card | fix |
|---|---|---|
| fp4 gy records under the split (also wrong, see the section below) | 1.21 GB planned | no records under the split |
| head slab z 16 -> 8 (UFSM_HEAD_SLAB_Z; 4 is refused by the streamed latent head) | ~0.95 GB planned | launch env 8 |
| Muon Newton-Schulz scratch pool (one batch for all matrices) | 953 MB -> 128 MB | batched in groups, UFSM_MUON_POOL_MB (128) |
| Muon momentum beside the unused AdamW v of the matrices | 416 MB | the momentum lives in v (UFSM_MUON_MOM_ALIAS, default on); checkpoints mask both |
| peer gradient buffer (whole parameter vector) | 416 MB -> 64 MB | chunked copy + axpy |
| cuBLASLt workspace allocated on GPU 0, used from GPU 1 | crash ("cublasLtMatmul failed (14)") | per-device handle and workspace |
| split_run created two new threads per call: thread-local device caches (ink MIL backward slabs ~330 MB, GroupNorm partials, gnbwd scratch) reallocated every step | ~0.3 GB / step, OOM at step ~20 | persistent side threads |
| on-the-fly phase cache (--onfly-mb, default 2 GB on GPU 0) | 1.3 GB | --onfly-mb 768 |

Not yet moved: the EMA weights and the film ffw buffers (416 MB each). train now warns when a card's free memory falls by more
than 64 MB between log lines after step 2 (any allocator), so the next such leak shows in the log instead of as an OOM.

Bench g1 (two 5060 Ti, only the trainer on the cards, suite locks held; UFSM_HEAD_SLAB_Z=8, --onfly-mb 768, 1 slot, 6 workers, 60
steps): whole-card peaks 15.05 / 14.45 GB (gate 15.3), the trainer's own 14.93 / 14.37 GB, flat from step 14 to 60. Planner: mode MX
gradients, chunked, lean 2, shared encoder a1 offloaded, 11.59 of 13.15 GB. Step time 33 s median, sampler-bound (wait 45-93%; the
GPU part ~10 s); 18-20 s/step until a second P 1024 sampler started beside it.

Host memory: each sampler slot pins 11.8 GB at P 1024, and the trainer pins ~13.3 GB more (host offloads 3.21 GB each way per card,
label planes). 2 slots reached rss 90 GB + ~40 GB shmem and were memcg-killed at 104 GB at step 23. 1 slot: rss 50-58 GB. The
sampler is the bound: one worker thread spends its time in sym_u8 (the per-channel symmetry copies of the full-resolution label
planes in the --gpu-aug 1 CPU label path that the auxiliary heads force), 18-20 s per window against ~10 s of GPU step.

## --split z: the encoder gradient bug was the GroupNorm backward's count, plus the first step's scroll axis records (2026-11-13, branch s2fix-20261113)

Symptom: under `--split z`, encoder weight gradients differed from the one-GPU run (relative 4e-3 at enc3, 0.29 at enc0.c1). It showed
only with a scroll axis and a level width >= 64. Loss, logits, decoded inputs and decoder gradients were identical. Repro: the trainer
A/B `runs/s2fix/ab2.sh` (P 256, 32,32,64,64, `--fp4 2`, fibre sources with axis, both halves on GPU 0, UFSM_GRAD_DUMP step 1).

Bisected with the GroupNorm backward dumps (UFSM_GNB_DUMP + UFSM_GNB_TDUMP: per call the summed statistics and the x / gy tensors).
dec2's GroupNorm backward had identical x, gy and summed statistics, yet its output dy differed (3e-4) on both halves; enc3's gy
followed, then every level above it. Cause: the halves scaled the summed group sums by f = D_local / D_whole (10 / 16 at level 2),
and the apply kernels divided by the local count cpg * S_local. In exact arithmetic that equals the one-GPU AB / (cpg * S_whole), but
in fp32 it is off in the last bit. MX-fp8 rounding of the gradient flipped some of those values, and the fp4 encoder amplified the
flips. The width / axis dependence was only which values happened to flip; no halo, skip, all-gather or channel-block path was
involved. Fix: gn_group_sums_k divides by the whole window's count (gn_bwd_reduce returns its voxels per channel), and the six apply
kernels (lp_mx_gnbwd.cu, nn_common.cuh) read AB as is. Without the split, the operations and their order are unchanged.

Second bug, found on the 6-level `--split-top 3` + `--attn-pe scroll` A/B: the split path's first upload never called axr_set. The
first step's scroll RoPE therefore ran without the window's axis records ("rays along the grid rows"), and attention wo and gfilm
gradients were 0.22 / 0.13 off. From step 2 on, select_buf set them, so only step 1 was affected. Fixed.

| A/B (split vs one GPU, grad rel) | before | after | one vs rerun |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 levels 32,32,64,64, axis | 4.7e-2 | 1.35e-7 | 1.3e-7 |
| 6 levels 32,32,64,64,96,96 + attention (scroll), gfilm, gn-ema, split-top 3 | 1.4e-2 (wo 0.22, gfilm 0.13) | 1.2e-7 | - |

Third bug, in the production gradient format (MX-fp4 gradients; the A/Bs above run MX-fp8 because fp4 gradients always round
stochastically by element index, so split and whole are not comparable bit for bit). Under the split, the GroupNorm backward apply
wrote the whole layer's gy records (lp_gn_silu_bwd_apply_rec) before the caller zeroed the halo planes. The fp4 weight gradient and
its bias sums therefore read the halo voxels' gx: those planes were counted on both GPUs. Measured on enc0 / dec0 conv2 bias
gradients, split with records vs split without was 0.13 relative off; one GPU with vs without records was 0.006 (SR noise). Fix:
no gy records under the split (the weight gradient's own pre-pass reads the zeroed gy). Split with the fix vs split UFSM_GYREC=0:
8e-8. This also frees the records' 1.21 GB per GPU at P 1024 (the planner no longer counts them under the split).

Regression test `test_split_gnbwd` (fast tier): the MX GroupNorm backward of a 16-plane window in two halves (+2 halo planes) vs whole,
for C 32 / 64, MX-fp4 / fp8 x, fp32 / MX-fp8 gradients. It has one gradient voxel per channel and half, so the statistics are exact sums
on both runs (sums of many terms differ in the last bit by partition, by design). The owned gx must be bit-identical. Before the fix
6-19k of 18-37k values differed in the fp32 cases; after, 0.

## Sampler host RAM spikes: the MIL rays' CT box in z slabs, idle workers release their scratch (2026-11-13, branch hostmem-20261113)

perf2's sampler-only runs (P 1024, 2 workers, 1 slot, --ink-mil, 30 GB cap) died after ~50 batches; it looked like slow growth. With the
hostmem breakdown every 10 batches (b6558dd) and the bigalloc logger it is not: RSS sat flat at 22.8 GB, then rose to 29.7 GB in 15 s on
one 8.92 GB malloc in inkfly_rays (the face search's CT box). A window drawn at level L+1 gets its rays at level L with o and n doubled, so
the box is (2 x 1040)^3; every worker can hold one at once. Between spikes: worker big 1.07 -> 2.15 GB (the mask slice touched once),
arena in use 3.1 -> 4.0 GB, ink caches flat.

- inkfly_rays reads the box in z slabs (UFSM_INKRAY_SLAB_MB, default 256 MB a read: rows of the slab's points + the samples' reach). The
  samples keep the whole box's coordinates (tri_box_z indexes the slab rows), so the rays are byte-identical; test_ink_splat compares
  16-row slabs with the whole box.
- A worker that finds no free slot madvises its scratch (big, ttmp) away and drains its buffer pool before it sleeps (UFSM_IDLE_RELEASE=0
  off): with W > S only S workers fill at a time. test_idle_release: 3 workers on 1 slot, --det 1, the batchhash lines equal. Measured at
  P 512, W 4, S 1, 16 batches: worker scratch resident 1.08 -> 0 GB, peak RSS 14.3 vs 14.4 GB (the peak is set by the arena / onfly
  caches, not the workers, once the warps run on the device), throughput 24 vs 33 Mvox/s (noise of cold caches; no slowdown).
- Budget at P 1024 with the device warps: sampler-only W 2 S 1 flat at ~23 GB (slot 4.4 GB unsplit, ~3.5 split); the trainer adds
  ~14.5 GB pinned. S 6 W 6 ~ 37 + 5 x 3.5 + 4 x 2 = 63 GB, inside 85 GB, now that no worker holds an 8.9 GB rays box.

## Sampler host RAM at P 1024 under --lat --split z: unread targets dropped, a plane bank per slot (2026-11-13, branch hostmem-20261113)

scratch2 (92 M latent net, P 1024 split over both cards, all heads) was OOM-killed in the 104 GB train slice at WORKERS 6 SLOTS 6 (~76 GB
after 20 s, ~100 GB with the trainer's pinned buffers). Measured with `UFSM_SAMPLER_ONLY` (no GPU; `--split z` segfaulted there before:
the zero planes now come from calloc) and an LD_PRELOAD allocation logger with pagemap residency (/vesuvius/ufsm/hostmem/tools), on
scratch1 minus the on-the-fly phase sources (the CPU pair rule takes ~15 min per P 1024 window; the slot layout does not depend on it).

Why the slots were big: `--split` turns `--pack-targets` off, `sample_gpu_lwarp_ok` needs packed targets, so `--gpu-aug 3` ran as
`--gpu-aug 1` (host label warps) and each slot held every unpacked byte plane. One slot at P 1024 (1.07 GB per plane, pinned):

| plane | GB | read by the trainer |
|---|---|---|
| ct8 | 1.07 | yes |
| t (recto / sheet targets) + m (mask) | 3.22 | **no** (g_tm_unused: the unwrap2 head slabs) |
| side, w4, wcomp | 3.22 | yes; all 255 for ink / fibre windows |
| ink (the rv papyrus plane; ink bits need gpu-aug 2) | 1.07 | yes |
| aux ink, fibre H, fibre V | 3.22 | yes; at most 2 of them non-255 in any window |
| **total** | **11.8** | |

Per worker: big 3 B/vox resident (CT, warp source scratch, mask) + ttmp 2 = 5.4 GB at P 1024; the window pool ~0 once the targets'
warp is gone. Fixed: label_occupancy 2.7 GB, ink-onfly label images 5.0, ink cache <= 4 (--ink-cache-mb), ~1 other. The targets' host
warp (write_spatial_tm) took 74% of a P 1024 worker's CPU, for planes nobody reads.

Changes (both bit-identical: the batch planes the trainer reads, by hash):
- **slot_skip 4** (`sample_tm_unused`): t / m neither allocated nor written when the trainer never reads them (g_tm_unused without
  `--pack-targets`, and not the non-latent split, whose upload_slab copies t). The warped windows keep write_spatial_tm's noise draws
  (rskip, as `--gpu-aug 2` does). -3 B/vox per slot; x16 stage 515 -> 37 ms per P 512 window. UFSM_TM_SKIP4=0 off.
- **plane bank** (`sample_cfg.plane_bank`, B 1, no replays / chains / cover / validation): a slot holds K label planes, K = the most
  any eligible source fills (role_real: side / w4 / wcomp need a phase or band, aux j its prob target, the papyrus plane always);
  per window the roles point at bank planes or at one shared pinned 255 plane, whose writes the draw skips (UFSM_BANK_CHECK=1
  aborts if it changes). The trainer reads the same pointers. scratch1: 7 roles -> 4 planes, -3.2 GB per slot. UFSM_PLANE_BANK=0 off.

Slot 11.8 -> 5.4 GB (11 -> 5 B/vox; P 512 sampler-only: slots 4.43 -> 2.15 GB for 3, the 255 plane included).

Checks: sampler-only P 256 scratch2 recipe `--det 1`, base vs new: 24 + 40 batches, 520 plane hashes, 0 differ (the CPU fibre path
fails without a GPU, so no fibre windows there). tests/test_slot_planes.sh (GPU, suite): winding + fibre-only mix, old layout vs bank,
whole windows with `--gpu-aug 3` (det_cmp: batch hashes and device inputs; 2 planes for 3 roles) and the latent split on one device
(batch hashes, losses within 2%; 4 planes for 6 roles), 8 batches each, identical.

Budget (model, not run): RSS ~ 15 + T + 5.4 S + 5.4 W GB (T: the trainer's pinned label-stream / a1 offload buffers, ~11 GB est.),
W = S - 2 useful workers on two GPUs: S 6 W 4 ~ 80 GB, where the old layout fitted S 3; with the device warps below (slot ~3.5 GB)
S 8 W 6 ~ 86 GB, S 7 W 5 ~ 77 GB.

**Device label warps under the split** (ec7a98b, lead-approved: not byte-identical). `--gpu-aug 2/3` now holds under `--lat --split z`
when the unpacked targets are unused (`sample_gpu_lwarp_ok`: packed targets or slot_skip 4; UFSM_SPLIT_LWARP=0 keeps the host warps).
Warped windows keep source-grid labels in the slot, which the augz z-range builders warp on the device (nn_label_warp_z,
nn_w4runs_label_z, nn_ink_bits_z) on the copy stream inside the uploads. Tolerance: the device warp equals the CPU warp
to <= 1e-4 of the voxels per plane (test_gpu_aug), as on every non-split `--gpu-aug 2` run; the z-range builders equal the whole-window
ones byte for byte (test_aug_z). CT bytes, scanner records and radial records are unchanged (same RNG stream).
- Slot: w4 runs (-2 planes), ink bits (the papyrus plane at 1 bit), bank 4 -> 2 planes: P 256 sampler-only 3.2 B/vox, ~3.5 GB at P 1024.
- Worker: the host label warps are gone (augment stage 1063 -> 11 ms CPU per P 256 window).
- The planner already counted the split's aug staging for `--gpu-aug 2`.
- test_slot_planes: a split run with the device warps; CT bytes exact, losses within 2% of the host-warp run.

## The scratch2 step faster: profile and the first fixes (2026-11-13, branch perf2-20261113)

Goal: the 92 M net's P 1024 two-card split step (scratch2.launch) as fast as possible with equivalent training.

### The two-card P 1024 split profile (desk, 14:10-15:20, mega f16a996 + perf2)

The scratch2 command line (perf2/scratch2.cmd: 92 M, --split z --split-top 3, MX-fp4, UFSM_HEAD_SLAB_Z=8) on both 5060 Tis under the six
locks, /vesuvius/ufsm/perf2/prof2.sh (nsys over steps 4-5, UFSM_PROF, plain), tools nsplit.py / nwin.py / napi.py (per-card busy / idle,
the kernels in a window, the host threads' CUDA API time).

- **The run is sampler-bound.** Without replay the step boundary holds two idle gaps of 4.9 / 5.4 s (trainer wait 43-77 %); scratch2 try1
  logged 0.02 samples/s, wait 85 % (~50 s/step against a ~6.5 s GPU step): --sampler-slots 1 builds one window at a time. The GPU numbers
  below use --replay 8 (each window again with new device-side augmentation), which takes the sampler out.
- **GPU step, replay:** 8.1 s (2-step capture 16.26 s). Per card: kernels 6.17 s, copies not under kernels 0.57 s, idle 1.39 s.
  UFSM_PROF (both cards summed, ms per step): wgrad 3060, conv fwd 2510, loss 2270, bwd_data 1770, gn 1430.
- **The head passes ran one card at a time (1.1 s idle per card per step).** split_run hands the turn over at collectives only; a head
  slab pass has none, and its ~1300 launches (+ ~700 memsets) fill the launch queue, so the side holding the turn blocked in
  cudaLaunchKernel / cudaMemset (9.5 ms once per 20 ms slab) at its own GPU's pace while the other side, unable to enqueue, idled
  (napi.py: side 0 728 ms in launches, side 1 0.2 ms in the window). Fix: split_yield, a no-op collective at the top of every slab but the
  first (both halves run the same slab count; both passes leave the body early, so the end of the body never ran it). The op state passes
  with the turn as at any collective. **8.1 -> 6.35 s/step (-22 %)**, idle per card 1.39 -> 0.08 s; --det 1 losses identical over 5 steps
  (1.8622 1.8835 1.9184 1.7865 1.8743, yield on and off); 79-92 vs 65-74 Mvox/s. UFSM_SPLIT_YIELD=0 off.
- **Next exposed copies (per card per step):** the next batch's device label warp at the step boundary (stream 23: 6 x 634 MB H2D + 6 x
  570 MB D2H through the 2.28 GB pinned label planes, interleaved with lw_phase / lw_ink: ~350 ms with no kernel running) and the
  activation offloads (stream 27, ~180 ms not under kernels).
- **UFSM_GRAD_AR2 + UFSM_LAT_LIGHT_SPLIT:** no measurable gain at P 1024 (0.13 vs 0.13 samples/s), losses identical; AR2's H2D-done event was
  made on the source device and failed on two cards (the one-device test could not see it), fixed.
- **UFSM_PROF under --split** crashed (one global event set made on GPU 0, recorded on GPU 1): per-device event sets now.
- **NaN gradients (blocker, mega and swap1):** with these flags every step skips (non-finite gradient norm; the scale falls to 1). The step-1
  gradient (UFSM_GRAD_DUMP) is NaN on exactly enc3.c2 (18918336..24338687 = 448 x 448 x 27 + 3 x 448) and 1792 film parameters (film +3840),
  i.e. level 3, the first --split-top level; all lower levels finite. The 12:13 scratch2 binary (7ee48e2) is clean on the same flags.
  Bisect over 7ee48e2..bc6c4c7 (590b56b cherry-picked where missing; perf2/bisect_step.sh): **a054edf first bad**, the s2b fp4
  weight-streaming kernel widened to 256..448 channels (NCH 8 / 9 / 10 / 12 / 14), so down3's bwd_data (448 ch) runs it. In isolation each
  width matches the reference (test_mx4 rel err 0.167-0.170 vs dilated 0.155, 32^3), but 384 / 448 / 288 run after 256 / 320 leave the later
  "fp4 conv SR operand (32 ch)" check NaN: something outside gx is overwritten (open). The wide path is off by default now
  (UFSM_S2B_WIDE=1 / lp_set_s2b_wide on; test_mx4 keeps 256 / 320, TMX4_WIDE_ALL=1 the whole sequence): mega + this, step-1 gradient
  0 non-finite (max |g| 0.329, loss 2.77253056).
  Narrowed (UFSM_S2B_WIDE=1 with one block count excluded at a time): only the **NCH 14 (448-channel) instantiation** gives the NaN (448 skipped:
  0 non-finite; 288 or 384 skipped: still 5422144). The trainer's call is the test's shape (gy 1x448x16^3 MX-fp4 -> gx 1x448x32^3 MX-fp4,
  accumulate), which matches its reference in test_mx4 alone, so the trigger lies in the trainer's data / state, not the shape; no suite-sized
  repro. (test_mx4's five-width sequence NaN also appears with the wide path off: a test artefact, not this bug.) Gate:
  scripts/test/split_finite.sh BIN CMDFILE (desk, both cards, ~3 min): step 1 of the scratch2 command line with UFSM_GRAD_DUMP, all
  gradients finite; ok by default, FAIL (5422144) with UFSM_S2B_WIDE=1.
- **Root cause (17:00-18:00): the planner aliases gy and gx at down3.** UFSM_S2B_DUMP (the 448 call's gy, gx before / after, w per card) +
  tests/s2b_replay (the same bytes in separate buffers through nn_conv3d_bwd_data_acc): the kernel is correct on the trainer's exact inputs
  (rel 0.256 vs the dilated path, finite), yet in the trainer its output was garbage from the 4th z tile on (mean scale per 4-plane tile 115
  .. 116, then 155, 216 ...), and a second in-trainer run on a fresh gx copy was garbage everywhere: the kernel destroys its own input. The
  logged pointers: gx starts 626688 B into gy's 974848 B (both cards; the 348160 shared bytes identical in the dumps), i.e. gy's channel
  blocks ~10-13 and all its scales are gx block 0's old content. The streaming kernel reads gy tiles while writing gx; the dilated path
  converts gy first, so it never NaN'd, but with accumulate it adds gy's bytes as old gx: master's level-3 gradients (ch 0-31 of enc3's input
  gradient, z < ~21) are silently wrong on the dilated path too. UFSM_ALIAS_CHECK=1 (nn_conv3d_bwd_data_acc: abort on an overlapping gy /
  accumulated gx) fires there on master (layer 9, 448 -> 448, gy 16^3); the planner fix (the split-top whole-level gradient buffers) is open,
  with split3. Kernel side: s2b_f4 copies an overlapping gy first (1 MB at 448 ch; UFSM_S2B_NOCOPY=1 the old behaviour); test_mx4 "s2b 448 ch,
  gy overlapping gx" (the trainer's offset): streaming vs dilated rel 0.227 with the copy, 1.6e37 FAIL without. The wide path is on again:
  split_finite ok with it (max |g| 0.284); --det replay 8 steps: 82.4 vs 77.9 Mvox/s (+5.8 %), step-1 loss identical, gn 22-25 both.

**Profile before** (the archived one-card P 512 92 M run, runs/scratch-archive-20261113/prof92: nsys + UFSM_PROF=layers, 37 steady
steps): 1.61 s/step, kernel-busy 99 % (GPU-bound, no loader wait). Per step:

| part | ms |
|---|---|
| 3^3 convs (fwd fp4 150-195 TFLOP/s on enc0.c2 / dec0.c1; dec0.c1 alone 304) | ~950 |
| onfly-phase pair rule + codes decode on the training GPU (k_bg_env 151, k_ll_sub 121, k_bg_pair / xw / ll_build 25) | ~295 |
| loss / target kernels (loss_grad 26, gscale 22, lat_up4 22, lat_adj_xy 21, loss_stats 16, packed_mask 13, ...) | ~200 |
| the head's 1^3 convs (conv1_mx_t 66, conv1_to_mx_t 36, bwd_w1 57 in 2300 launches) | ~160 |
| Muon fp32 Newton-Schulz (gemm_ns_k; scratch2 runs --muon-tc 2, ~57) | 120 |
| fine stem fwd / bwd | 84 |
| down0 backward-data (the dilated fp8 path: 8x the MACs) vs its forward 26 | 69 |

The P 1024 split half is 4.25x the P 512 volume, so ~5.2 s/step per card if the split cost nothing.

**down0..down3 backward-data: the weight-streaming fp4 kernel** (trainperf WIP 417a0a4, finished here). The 256-448 channel stride-2
backward-data ran the dilated fp8 convolution on MX-fp8 copies. bwd_data_s2_f4_k with STREAM (NCH > 4) keeps one tap's weight units in
shared memory, loaded per (z tile, class, tap) from L2; the MMAs and their order are the resident kernel's. tests/bench_s2b, one 5060 Ti,
min of 4, per 32-plane slab of the P 1024 half:

| conv | gx shape | dilated path | fp4 kernel | P 1024 half, saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| down0 | 32 x 256^2 x 256 ch | 82.5 ms (11 TFLOP/s) | 10.1 ms (92) | 308 ms (136 planes) |
| down1 | 32 x 128^2 x 320 | 23.6 | 4.3 | 41 ms (68) |
| down2 | 32 x 64^2 x 384 | 8.0 | 1.6 | 7 ms (34) |
| down3 | 16 x 32^2 x 448 | 1.55 | 0.48 | 1 ms (18) |

Accuracy: test_mx4 256 / 320 ch against the fp32 reference, rel err 0.167 / 0.169 (dilated 0.155 / 0.155, TOL4). Trainer A/B (92 M,
P 256, --det 1 seed 7, step-1 summed gradient; UFSM_S2B_F4=1 is the old path): the same batch hashes, --det rerun 0, new vs old
rel 0.037 (cos 0.99932), against the SR noise floor 0.133 (`UFSM_SR_SALT=1`, new: every step's SR seed shifted, the same batches).

**The head slabs' lambda scales inside the gradient kernels** (nn_loss_grad_only_s). Under --uw every head's lambda x source weight differs
from 1, so each slab ran gscale_k over 21 logit channels after the BCE gradient (22 ms a step at P 512, ~90 per card at the P 1024 half).
The scale now multiplies the kernel's final product (one fp16 rounding instead of two). 92 M P 256 step-1 gradient vs the separate pass:
rel < 1e-5, max |d| 3e-8, the same batches.

**The latent cell head on the tensor cores.** --lat-guide 3 makes the head 160 outputs (32 task + 128 sub-cell) from dec0's 256 MX-fp4
channels; lp_conv1_fwd_mx_h16_r ran conv1_mx_t_k in 10 passes of 16 outputs, each re-reading x with 256 x 16 FFMAs a cell (P 512: 66 ms a
step at ~5 TFLOP/s). conv1_mx_tc_k does one pass: persistent blocks (one per SM) keep the fp16 weights of all outputs in shared memory
(160 x 264 halves, 84 KB), walk 128-cell tiles, decode each 32-channel MX block with its GN+SiLU in fp32 (act_ab, as before), round it to
fp16 and run m16n8k16 MMAs; the next block's x words load during the current block's MMAs. tests/test_head_tc (GN per sample and per
