slab, ranges with tails, 160 / 35 / 17 outputs) against the FFMA path: rel L2 3.9e-4, max 8.6e-4 of max |logit| (the fp16 rounding of
activations and weights, below the fp16 logits' own), bytes repeat. P 1024 half slab (4 x 256^2 cells, 256 -> 160): 2.87 -> 0.87 ms
(7.5 -> 24.6 TFLOP/s), 68 calls a step (two passes x 34 slabs): ~135 ms per card. UFSM_HEAD_TC=0: the FFMA passes. The backward-data (c1b_wh_k + conv1_to_mx_tc_k: 64 cells x 256 outputs a block, K in 32-chunks,
the MX4 epilogue through per-warp shared tiles) on the pod: rel L2 7.7e-3 against the FFMA kernel after the MX-fp4 SR (0.02 % of the
elements differ), bytes repeat; the P 1024 half slab 160 -> 256: 7.61 -> 1.12 ms (2.8 -> 19.2 TFLOP/s), 34 slabs a step: ~220 ms per
card. Default OFF (UFSM_HEAD_BTC=1 on): with it on, test_lat_head's "a second equal net" check (the same parameters and
inputs on a second unet) differs by rel 0.4 in the trunk gradients, which test_head_tc's kernel-level checks (C 32 / 96 / 256, two
samples, whole and ranges) do not reproduce. The difference is deterministic: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING changes nothing, and it shows only in
the narrow {96,64,96} config. A trace of the calls (UFSM_C1B_TRACE, not kept) shows both nets taking the same fp16 TC path (gdt 2,
whole and per range). The head's gx is therefore the same kind on both nets, and the 0.42 / 0.17 matches test_lat_head's known
narrow-level fault: "TLH_NARROW_ALL ... 0.17 on every trunk tensor, 11-09, open". BTC's slightly different gx bits seem to expose that
fault rather than cause it. The paragraph below was the first reading. One of the two nets reaches the head's backward-data with fp16
logit gradients (the TC kernel), the other with MX or bf16 ones (gdt 3 / 1: the FFMA kernel). With BTC off both use FFMA, whose fp32
sums agree whenever the values do. The TC kernel would need a gdt 3 / 1 staging to keep that equality. The 8-output comparisons
(trunk rel 0.3) are the same effect: the wide head's TC gx against the 8-output FFMA gx, where one SR flip in fp4 spreads through the
small test net. The whole-call form (lp_conv1_to_mx) now takes the same kernel as the range form,
so whole == per range holds with it on.


**The MIL backward without a sync per slab.** ink_mil_bwd_slab read its slab's (voxel, sample) pair count back with a
cudaStreamSynchronize before sizing the radix sort: 34 host syncs per ink window. Under `--split` the call runs while the GPU's thread
holds the split turn, so each sync drains that card while the other waits for the turn: the two cards serialise on every slab. Now
ink_mil_fin also queues one histogram of pairs per corner plane (no w == 0 test, so an upper bound) and its async copy to pinned memory;
the first backward slab waits for that event once per step, each slab sorts the bound of its planes (one plane of margin on each side)
with the unused tail filled by a key that sorts last, and k_runs reads the true count on the device: the sorted prefix and the sums are
the ones of the readback path. A bound exceeded on the device (not expected) is reported by the next step's first slab. tests/test_ink_mil
checks both paths byte for byte at 1 / 3 / 7 slabs, soft and hard: ok on the pod (RTX PRO 6000 MIG slice), so the plane bound is the
default (UFSM_MIL_ASYNC=0: the readback); ink_mil_set_async() for tests.

**The gradient sum in halves, both directions at once.** After each step train.c summed the two GPUs' fp32 gradients by copying
all of GPU 1's gradient to GPU 0 with cudaMemcpyPeer (no P2P on the desk, so it is staged through the host and the host blocks),
adding them, and copying the sum back: 2 x 368 MB for the 92 M net, one direction at a time, nothing overlapped. The old path also
holds a 368 MB receive buffer on GPU 0. nn_grad_allreduce2 (nn_loss.cu) instead does a reduce-scatter and then an all-gather.
GPU 0 sums [0, n/2) and GPU 1 sums [n/2, n); each then sends its summed half to the other. The data goes through double-buffered
32 MB pinned chunks, both directions in flight, with a chunk's D2H overlapping the previous chunk's H2D. It is stream-ordered
behind each device's legacy stream and the host only enqueues. Each half is y + x on one card (a + b == b + a), so the bytes are
those of the old path. Buffers: 128 MB pinned host, 64 MB of receive chunks per card. The old path's 368 MB on GPU 0 is not
allocated. tests/test_grad_ar checks both cards against the host sum byte for byte over three calls (quick: 9 M floats in 1 M
chunks; full: 92.4 M floats, timed against the old path). Default off (UFSM_GRAD_AR2=1) until that test has run on the GPUs.

**Missed derived-cache cells computed together.** On a cold cache the split benches are loader-bound at 16-23 s/step. Most of that
is the onfly pair rule: about 425 tiles per step on GPU 0, and 576 cells computed in a 6-window sampler-only check. Each missed cell
was computed on its own, with a halo of rmax + 2 codes voxels around it. That is 4.5x the cell's voxels for a 128^3 cell at rmax 40
(the scratch1 sources use rmax 20 / 40 / 41 / 48.5 / 80, so cells of 128 and 256), plus one tile's packing and launches per cell.
dc_read now claims a block of G^3 cells (G = UFSM_DC_BATCH or "cache_batch" / C, default 384 voxels: 3^3 cells of 128). The claimed
cells that are not on disk are computed as one box with one inner read (their bounding box, when they fill at least half of it), then
cut into cells. At rmax 40 the halo share drops from 4.5x to 1.8x (the onfly read tiles the box itself within its --onfly-mb budget).
A reader waits for another reader's cells only after all its own claims are settled, so there are no wait cycles. A block's
references are held until it has been copied: at most 27 cells (57 MB) plus the box (57 MB) per reading thread at C 128. Cells of 256
keep G = 1 at the default. This is only enabled for the onfly phase, whose values do not depend on the box read
(tests/test_phase_onfly.sh: byte-identical across tilings). Checks:
- On the wind fixture (cache_cell 32), the onfly phase through the cache at batch 0 / 96 / 384 is byte-identical to phase-raster
  (1.01 M known voxels, CPU), and a reopen reads all 64 cells from disk.
- tests/test_dcache_batch (CPU, fast tier): batched == cell by cell == direct values on ragged boxes, 4 threads on one cold array, and
  disk reopen. A cold whole read takes 8 inner reads instead of 64.

**One memory LRU for every onfly phase array.** Each onfly phase spec opened its own dcache LRU (`"cache_mb"`, default 1024). With
scratch1's 19 specs that allows 19 GB of host RAM. The sampler-only warm reached the 30 GB memory cap within 2 minutes, twice. All onfly
phase arrays now share dcache_pool_shared("phase"), sized by --onfly-cache-mb or UFSM_ONFLY_CACHE_MB (default 2048). A spec that sets
its own "cache_mb" keeps a private LRU, as before. The size only changes hit rates: a cell's bytes are the same from memory, from disk
or computed (test_dcache_batch, test_mesh_phase).

**Single-card profile on pod A, and the fine stem's forward.** Pod A is an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell MIG 1g.24gb slice, about 1.3-1.5x
one 5060 Ti. The run is the scratch2 92 M net and heads on the 640^3 wind fixture with ink and fibre, P 512, one card. The labels are
stored phase sets, so the onfly pair rule is not in this profile. nsys over steps 10-12 shows 1561 ms of kernels per step:

| kernel | ms/step |
|---|---|
| conv_fwd_f4_k (3^3 fp4 forward) | 399 |
| conv_bwd_w_f4ws_k (3^3 weight gradients) | 262 |
| fstem_fwd_k (the fine stem forward) | 163 |
| conv1_to_mx_t_k<192> (head backward-data; the TC path is still off) | 62 |
| lat_up4_k / lat_adj_xy_k | 53 / 39 |
| fib_head_dir_k | 52 |
| w4_events_k + w4_runs_k | 52 |
| loss_grad_k / loss_stats_k | 41 / 23 |
| conv_fwd_s2_f8_k / conv_bwd_w_s2_f8_k (stride 2) | 35 / 34 |
| conv_bwd_w1_tc_k (head weight gradients) | 33 |

Same run, 20 steady steps: 1.650 s/step; UFSM_HEAD_TC=0 1.713; UFSM_S2B_F4=1 1.695.

fstem_fwd_k ran at 100 GB/s. Lanes (l % 8, l / 8) wrote 32-byte pieces of 4 output planes at a time, with each read-modify-write
waiting on its load. Now the warps leave h of all 128 blocks of the row tile in shared memory. Thread j then projects block j (the same
sums in the same order) and updates its 4 logit pairs per output, so a warp's row is 128 contiguous bytes and the 4 loads go out
together. tests/bench_fstem (P 512, a 32-plane slab, 11 outputs): 3.68 -> 1.26 ms (306 GB/s). The output hash on random inputs is
unchanged (byte-identical). test_fstem, test_lathead, test_heads, test_predict_heads and test_fibhead_train pass on the pod. That is
about 110 ms per step at P 512 on this card, and about 4x that per card at the P 1024 split half.

## predict --seamless 2: the two-pass grid blend built in (2026-11-12, branch seamless-20261112, src/seamless.c)

The latent nets' heads carry a per-window level. inkpod ink on a 1299 corner: plane steps of 10-30 / 255 at the window seams, at halo 16
.. 256, with --gn-frozen, at levels 1 and 2, and still with the per-window dice off (inkpod-11000 / 12000). The numbers are in
branch inkcache-20261112's DESIGN section "Latent ink head: window seams". A halo or a --feather ramp (B <= halo) cannot hide a step
whose source is wider than the window, so seam-free output needs every voxel averaged over windows whose borders lie elsewhere.

Options, per output voxel at tile S:

| scheme | windows per voxel | quality |
|---|---|---|
| one pass (today) | 1 | hard steps |
| --feather B | 1 (+ the halo spill) | a B-voxel ramp, B <= halo; a 30-level step stays a visible band |
| one pass at stride S / 2 (overlap-weighted) | 8 | smooth |
| two passes, grids 0 and S / 2, sin^2 tile weights | 2 | smooth (16.9 -> 1.3 on the 1299 corner; median plane step 0.1) |

The two-pass blend is the cheapest seam-free scheme: 2x the windows against 8x for half-stride overlap. --feather at that quality
needs B ~ S / 2, i.e. windows ~2x as wide (8x the voxels).

`predict ... --seamless 2` (window - 2 halo a multiple of 256; default 544 / 16):
- the process runs the two passes as children of the same binary (UFSM_SEAM_CHILD=1, no CUDA in the parent) into `<out>/.seam/{a,b}`,
  with `--full-grid 1 --q 0 --levels 1 --shard S/2` and `--grid-origin 0,0,0` / `S/2,S/2,S/2`. Shard S / 2 keeps the shifted tiles
  aligned with the store's shards: with S-sized shards each shifted tile spans 8 shards and the planner runs 7.5x the windows (P4 inner
  17405 vs 2311); the output is byte-identical, 5 s vs 63 s on the 1299 test box;
- `--gpus A,B` runs the two passes at once, one per GPU (both desk 5060 Tis); otherwise both on `--gpu`, one after the other;
- every store of pass a (the single output, or each `--heads` store `<out>/<name>`, nested names like `fib/H` included) is blended with
  its pass-b twin by ink-blend's core (`ink_blend_run`, factored out of src/inkblend.c) into `<out>[/<name>]` with the run's --q,
  --levels and --shard; the store's attributes record `"seamless": {mode, window, halo, tile, grids}`;
- each pass's --box is moved down onto its tile grid (origin = shift mod S): predict's planner places one window per tile only when
  the box origin (rounded to shards) lies on the --grid-origin lattice, else one per shard (1667 labelled box at shard 256: 3305
  windows instead of 578; the sequential --seamless run 774 s -> 256 s: pass a 516 windows 64 s, pass b 545 windows 77 s, the rest the
  lossless writes, blend and pyramid). A pass-b origin below 0 starts at S / 2; the blend gives absent shards (that edge, occupancy
  air skipped by one pass only) weight 0 instead of averaging in zeros;
- a pass with `.seam/<p>/.done` is not rerun (resume after a blend failure); `.seam` is removed at the end (UFSM_SEAM_KEEP=1 keeps it).
  The pass logs are `.seam/{a,b}.log`.

Not with --boxes, --fit-zarr, --split or --feather. The output is always full-grid. tests/test_seamless.py runs without a GPU: a
stand-in pass (UFSM_SEAM_EXE) checks each pass's arguments and writes constant stores (100 / 200, two heads); the blend matches
(100 wa + 200 wb) / (wa + wb) within 1 at five voxels; the bad-tile error and the removal of .seam are checked too.
test_ink_blend still passes after the refactor.

Open (GPU, on the lead's say): the same 1299 corner through `--seamless 2` against u1667ink.sh's scripted blend (that one
blends q-8 passes into q 32; here lossless passes into the run's q, so close but not byte-identical); and the wall time of `--gpus 0,1` against sequential passes.

## Empty-space skipping: the opportunity on scratch2 windows, and why it cannot be exact (2026-11-13, branch skipair-20261113)

The goal was to stop computing convs in air and outside the scan. Keep a tile mask per level and fill inactive tiles with the
constant the dense net would compute there. **That constant does not exist for scratch2:**
- The input is never spatially constant. `nn_input_latc` appends 3 radial-direction channels (the unit vector to the scroll axis,
  `rad_voxel`) to the 29 latent codes. They vary everywhere, including in air and in the zero-filled outside of the scan.
- Scroll-RoPE attention at the 8^3 bottleneck and `--gfilm 1` couple every decoder voxel to the whole window.
- Air CT is noisy, not constant: per 4^3 cell, max <= 40 holds for only ~21% of cells, and max <= 64 for 39%.

So any skip changes the function. The version built here is a **masked conv**: an inactive output tile of a wide 3^3 conv holds the
conv's bias (the CTA skips its main loop; the epilogue, MX store and GroupNorm sums run as usual). GN, SiLU, attention and heads stay
dense. It is a well-defined net whose backward would be exact. Its deviation from the dense net has to be measured on papyrus voxels.

**Opportunity.** Method: `UFSM_SAMPLER_EMPTY=1` with `UFSM_SAMPLER_ONLY` on scratch2's recipe, no GPU, dev slice
(`/vesuvius/ufsm/skipair/empty_measure*.sh`).
- Data: source-grid CT bytes before the device augmentation, 24 windows. The first 7 use the full recipe, until the CPU ink / fibre
  label build hit the 40 GB memcap. The other 17 drop the ink / fibre heads so the run fits.
- Tiles: 8^3 cells (32^3 voxels at level 0). A tile is active when any voxel is > t. Margin r means dilation by r tiles of the
  same level.
- Level weights of conv FLOPs at widths 256,320,384,448,288,288: L0 75.5%, L1 20.2%, L2 3.6%, L3 0.6%.

| t | empty cells | L0 active r0 / r1 / r2 | L1 (r1) | L2 (r1) | L3 (r1) | conv FLOPs saved (r1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (outside the scan) | 0.205 | 0.803 / 0.833 / 0.860 | 0.873 | 0.932 | 0.993 | 15.4% |
| 40 | 0.213 | 0.803 / 0.833 / 0.860 | 0.873 | 0.932 | 0.993 | 15.5% |
| 64 (papyrus iso) | 0.386 | 0.773 / 0.819 / 0.849 | 0.863 | 0.926 | 0.984 | 16.7% |

- t 0 and t 40 are nearly the same, so the skippable space is almost all the zero-filled outside of the scan. Air inside the scroll
  gives few whole 32^3-voxel tiles.
- By source and level: level-0 / 1 windows are 0.93-1.00 active. Coarse windows are where the empty space is: PHerc1667 lev 2
  0.68, PHercParis4-july lev 3 0.59, PHerc1218-b3 lev 0 0.64.
- `--split z`: the busier card's half averages 0.849 active vs 0.867 for its whole windows (17 windows), so the split costs little.
- Expected: 15-17% of conv FLOPs. Convs are ~60% of a step, so at most ~9% of a step. Skipped CTAs still run their epilogue and
  stores, and the memory-bound ops stay dense, so ~6-7% is more realistic.
- Inference: `predict` already skips whole air shards and windows (`--occupancy`, air tiles), so only boundary windows gain.

**Built (predict side).**
- `src/nn_skip.cu`: `nn_skip_build` makes the per-level masks from the device CT window. `conv_fwd_f4_k` checks the mask (an output
  tile is one z / y tile and at most two x tiles) and skips the main loop.
- Scope: MX forwards only, N 1, whole-tensor outputs on a registered level grid. z-windows, z-ranges and slab outputs stay dense.
  `lp_skip_get` decides per launch.
- `predict --skip-empty 1 [--skip-thr 40] [--skip-margin 1]` on latent-grid nets: masks from `ctd` before the trunk forward, off
  after it.
- `tests/test_skip_empty` checks three things: all tiles active gives bit-identical logits, margins 2 / 3 stay within 2% / bit-identical
  on the toy net's material, and `nn_skip_off` restores the dense bits.
- Predict runs levels 0 / 1 as z-range halves (planes of a depth-yD output, read from a depth-Di input). `lp_skip_get` places
  them on their level by that depth and first plane; before that fix, only levels 1-2 were masked and the trunk was 1% faster.

**GPU results (pod B, RTX PRO 6000 MIG 1g.24gb, 2026-11-13).**
- `test_skip_empty` passes. With every tile active, the logits are bit-identical to the dense forward. On the toy net (3 levels,
  gn_ema, no attention), the material-voxel error is 4.4% at margin 1, 0.2% at margin 2, and 0 (bit-identical) at margin 3.
- Real-CT A/B (`UFSM_SKIP_AB=1`): u1 `last.ckpt` (10 M, widths 96-192, 4 levels), PHerc0343 masked scan at level 1 (17.28 um),
  box 4000,0,1536 + 512 x 1024 x 1024 (the scroll edge), windows 512^3 (128^3 cells), threshold 40.
- Speed: the trunk is 0.064 s dense vs 0.034-0.048 s masked (25-47% faster) at level-0 active shares of 0.27-0.60. The masked
  convs scale with the active share (enc0.c2 9.5 -> 4.6 ms, dec0.c1 16.9 -> 7.9 ms). down0 (6.6 ms) and the head (7.9 ms) stay dense.
- Accuracy: u1 has live GroupNorm, so the bias fill moves every window statistic. Material logits then differ by 48% (mean |d| over
  mean |logit|), so live-GN nets must not use it. `UFSM_SKIP_AB_FREEZE=1` normalises the masked pass with the dense pass's
  statistics, which is how a gn_ema net behaves; the control with every tile active under the freeze is bit-identical.
- Under the freeze, on material cells (a voxel >= 64):

| margin | trunk faster | material mean \|d\| / mean \|logit\| | material logit sign flips | bit-identical material values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 37-47% | 0.108-0.143 | 6.4-6.9% | 0-0.04% |
| 2 | 31-44% | 0.092-0.126 | - | 0-3% |
| 3 | 25-34% | 0.062-0.103 | 3.9-4.9% | 2-26% |

- Unlike the toy net, the error reaches deep into material. u1's reach is ~60 level-0 cells through its 4 levels, while the fill sits
  only 8 x margin cells from the material. The fill's error enters the coarse levels and comes back up, and a 128^3-cell window
  near the scroll edge has almost no material farther than that from the fill.
- scratch2 couples further (6 levels, attention over the whole bottleneck, gfilm), so its error would be at least this large.

**Verdict.** The masked conv runs 25-47% faster on scroll-edge windows, but changes 4-7% of the papyrus logit signs at margins 1-3.
That is not acceptable as a silent default. It stays opt-in (`predict --skip-empty 1`, default off) for previews where boundary
windows dominate. No training path: it would change what the net learns there, for at most ~6-9% of a step. Most of the skippable
space is the zero-filled outside of the scan. Keeping training windows inside the scan would recover that compute exactly.

## 2:4 sparsity mid-run: ramp, hard pruning under Muon, the scratch2 recipe (2026-11-14, branch sparse24b-20261114)

The user approved 2:4 sparsity for scratch2. Switching a dense run sparse needs three things the 11-13 version lacked: no loss jolt, an
optimizer that respects the mask, and checkpoints that resume at any point of the switch.
- `--sparse24 S --sparse24-ramp N`: from step S, the forward copy holds the pruned weights x r, with r = 1 - (step - S + 1) / N. The mask
  is the magnitude mask of the dense master, recomputed every ramp step. The ramp runs on the dense kernels.
- Hard pruning (`--sparse24-hard`, the default for modes 2 / 3) after the ramp. Before the optimizer, the step's magnitude mask is taken
  from the master and kept as one keep byte per (co, 8 ci, tap) (np / 8 bytes), and the pruned weights' gradient is zeroed, so Muon's
  momentum stays masked. After the update, the master and its Muon momentum are pruned with that same mask. A pruned weight's
  (orthogonalised, dense) update therefore can never swap it in: the mask stays fixed after the ramp, and between steps the master
  itself holds it (pruned weights are exactly +0), so a checkpoint needs no mask array.
- Checkpoint keys `sparse24_hard` and `sparse24_r` (mid-ramp; the trainer recomputes r from its flags) are written only when set.
  `UFSM_SP24=0` runs the dense kernels on the same pruned weights (identical bytes); `UFSM_SP24_REPORT=1` prints the sparse call count;
  `UFSM_SP24_CHECK=1` checks after every hard step that the master keeps all its energy under its own mask. When the mask first applies
  fully, the trainer reports the kept |w|^2 per level.
- predict loads the mode with the checkpoint, masks (idempotent on the pruned master) and runs the sparse kernel. tests/test_sp24_train.sh
  checks that its output equals the dense kernels' on the same weights.

**Pod A/B** (RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell, one card, P 512, the 92 M scratch2 widths and flags minus the split, synthetic wind fixture,
--det 1; 150 steps from a dense checkpoint at step 511, the switch at 512):

| arm | s/step (steps 580-658) | loss - dense, ramp | next 100 steps | kept |w|^2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dense | 1.099 | | | |
| mode 2, ramp 50 | 1.064 (-3.2 %) | +0.013 | +0.02 | 0.785 |
| mode 3, ramp 50 | 1.053 (-4.2 %) | +0.022 | +0.02 | 0.674 |
| mode 2, abrupt | | +0.27 at the switch | +0.025 | |

(dense loss ~1.19). The ramp removes the jolt, and mode 3 costs no more loss than mode 2 here while also sparsifying the backward-data,
so the recommendation is mode 3. On the real scratch2 step-508 weights the kept energy is 0.676 (mode 3), the same at every level: at 508
steps the weights are still close to their random init.

**Recipe for scratch2:** `--sparse24 S --sparse24-mode 3 --sparse24-ramp 500`, with S after the LR warmup (a step-0 mask is the random
init, frozen forever by hard pruning). In a swap, S = the resume step + 1. If S lies more than N steps before the resume, the prune is
abrupt. The two-card --split z path runs the same per-thread registry and masks, and the z-window and z-range of the split kernels are
byte-tested on the sparse kernel (test_sp24_conv). A two-card split_finite with the flags is the swap window's check.

## 2:4 sparse fp4 convs: the hardware pattern, the kernel, the ceiling (2026-11-13, branch sparse24-20261113)

Goal: halve the 3^3 conv MMAs of the 92 M scratch2 net with the sparse block-scaled tensor cores of the RTX 5060 Ti (sm_120a).

**Hardware.** ptxas (CUDA 13.3) lowers `mma.sp::ordered_metadata.sync.aligned.m16n8k128.row.col.kind::mxf4.block_scale.scale_vec::2X`
and `kind::mxf4nvf4 ... scale_vec::4X` (ue8m0) to `OMMA.SF.SP.168128`, and the e4m3 `m16n8k64 kind::mxf8f6f4` to `QMMA.SF.SP.16864`:
consumer Blackwell has sparse MX-fp4. For e2m1 the sparse element is the byte (two adjacent K values): the metadata (one 32-bit register
per lane, 64 bits per row for 128 K) indexes 2 of 4 bytes per 8 K, so the pattern is **pair-wise 4:8**, not element-wise 2:4. The
existing `--sparse24` (2026-10-01: element-wise 2:4, dense kernels on a masked copy) cannot use it. tests/test_sp24_mma checks the
operand / metadata / scale layout of every lane against an fp64 host reference and measures the MMA-only throughput (numbers below).

**Where the gain can come from.** Only conv_fwd_f4_k (forward, recompute, backward-data via flipped weights) can use it; the weight
gradient reduces over voxels and stays dense. The backward-data reduces over the forward's output channels, so a mask along ci is
not sparse there: only a transposable mask (mode 3) makes it sparse too. The archived prof92 trace (92 M, P 512, one card, kernel busy
time) bounds the step gain: conv_fwd_f4_k 22 % (25.6 of 115 s), the dense weight gradient conv_bwd_w_f4ws_k 15 %, k_bg_env + k_ll_sub
14 %, Muon NS 6 %. A perfect 2x on conv_fwd_f4_k saves <= 11 % of the step (mode 3) or ~7 % (mode 2, forward + recompute).

**Modes** (`--sparse24 STEP --sparse24-mode 1|2|3 --sparse24-levels 0,1,...`; SR-STE `--srste` on the dense master, the forward reads the
masked copy u->wm; prune-by-magnitude at STEP, so a dense checkpoint continues sparse; checkpoint key `sparse24` = the mode, old
checkpoints are mode 1, `sparse24_lv` written only when set):
- 1: element-wise 2:4 along ci (the old behaviour; dense kernels only);
- 2 (default): pair-wise 4:8 along ci, every stride-1 3^3 conv but the stem; the forward runs the sparse kernel, backward-data dense;
- 3: transposable 2 x 2 blocks: per (tap, 8 co x 8 ci) a 4 x 4 grid of 2 x 2 blocks keeps exactly 2 per grid row and column (max
  summed |w| over the 90 patterns), so the flipped weights are pair-wise 4:8 along co and the backward-data runs sparse as well.

**Kernel** (src/lp_sp24conv.cu): conv_fwd_f4_k's code with the tap-pair dense MMA (m16n8k64: 2 taps x 32 ci) replaced by a tap-quad
sparse MMA (m16n8k128 kind::mxf4nvf4 scale_vec::4X: 4 taps x 32 ci, A compressed to 32 B per row, the 4 taps' ue8m0 scales in one
register, one metadata register per lane): per 32-channel chunk 7 quads instead of 14 pairs, half the MMAs and the weight ldmatrix,
the same B ldmatrix (the quad's B is the two pairs' dense fragments). Staging and epilogue are conv_fwd_f4_k's, so the inputs are
staged with the same bits. The prep (prep_sp24_k) quantises each tap's 32 channels with prep_w4_k's scale and nibbles and keeps the 2
largest pairs per 8 channels, counting groups with more non-zero pairs (lp_sp24_err). Routing: unet_apply_sparse24 registers the
masked convs (per host thread), conv_fwd_tc sends MX-fp4 calls on registered weights (> 64 input channels) to the sparse kernel, and a
flip of registered mode-3 weights marks the flipped copy for the next call.

**Tests.** tests/test_sp24_conv: on exact operands (every MX block holds a +-6, so every sum is exact in any order) the sparse
kernel's MX-fp4 output bytes equal the dense kernel's on the same masked weights (MT 4 / TZ 2, MT 2 / TZ 4 and TZ 2, the gradient
path's output SR, a split input); GN + SiLU inputs (prenorm path) and random weights agree to fp32 rounding; the mode 2 mask equals
the host's, mode 3 keeps whole 2 x 2 blocks two per row and column, SR-STE touches exactly the pruned weights; mode-3 flipped
weights pass the prep without truncation; conv_fwd_tc routes registered weights to the sparse kernel and others to the dense one.

**Numbers.** MMA only (tests/test_sp24_mma, dense-equivalent TFLOP/s): 5060 Ti dense mxf4 432, sparse mxf4 865, sparse mxf4nvf4 4X
851, e4m3 dense 212 / sparse 424 (RTX PRO 6000 MIG 1g slice: 401 / 802): the sparse tensor core is a true 2x. Measured layout: the
metadata lane (g, t) holds row g + 8 (t & 1), groups 8 (t >> 1) .. + 7; scales as the dense MMA (4X: one byte per 32 K). The first
kernel used the other lane candidate (row g + 8 (t >> 1)) and failed test_sp24_conv; with the measured one every case is byte-identical
to the dense kernel, including GN inputs and random weights (the fp32 sums happen to round the same).

Conv time (tests/bench_sp24, 5060 Ti, one 32-plane slab of the P 1024 half window per level, GN + SiLU input and output statistics
for fwd, MX-fp4 gy with output SR for bdata, min of 3, prepared-weight memo on):

| level | shape | fwd dense / sparse ms | bdata dense / sparse ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 32 x 256^2 x 256 ch | 34.5 / 27.4 (1.26x) | 34.4 / 27.9 (1.23x) |
| 1 | 32 x 128^2 x 320 | 12.8 / 10.4 (1.24x) | 12.4 / 10.0 (1.24x) |
| 2 | 32 x 64^2 x 384 | 4.57 / 3.67 (1.25x) | 4.44 / 3.55 (1.25x) |
| 3 | 16 x 32^2 x 448 | 0.81 / 0.63 (1.27x) | 0.79 / 0.62 (1.29x) |

The sparse kernel reaches 270-290 TFLOP/s dense-equivalent against the dense one's ~215 (of the 432 MMA peak): halving the MMAs
gives 1.25x, because staging and the B ldmatrix (unchanged) now dominate. With conv_fwd_f4_k at 27 % of the 92 M step (perf2:
442 of 1610 ms at P 512) that is ~5 % of the step for mode 3 and ~3.5 % for mode 2, before any quality cost. More needs the staging
cost per MMA cut (a wider output tile per staged input), which the dense kernel would profit from as much.

## Split-window input builders: every --gpu-aug builder by z range, the scanner split exactly across two GPUs (2026-11-13, branch augz-20261112)

**The light statistics pass under the split (UFSM_LAT_LIGHT_SPLIT=1, untested).** For the fused head groups (the normal 7 and the
side pair), the single-card trainer counts only mask weights in the statistics pass and takes the loss sums from the gradient pass
("light"). The split turned light off because its gradient pass also covers a 4-plane halo band. On the pod, light off cost 22 ms a
step at P 512 one card (1.518 -> 1.540 s), so at the P 1024 split half it should be roughly 90 ms per card. Now:
- nn_lat_fuse_grad's loss sums take only fine planes [lo, hi) (nn_lat_fuse_sum_zwin, set from hs_keep's statistics-pass range);
- the light finalisation (nn_loss_stats_fin_light) sums only entries 1 .. 4 across the halves, because the statistics pass's
  finalisation already summed the mask weights in entry 0.
It is off by default. The pods were shut down before the same-GPU split comparison (--gpus 0,0 --split z, --det, light on vs off,
logged losses) ran.

## Muon variants for the from-scratch universal net: ten arms on the 92 M net (2026-11-13, branch muonx-20261113)

The regime: B = 1, P 512..1024 windows. Gradients are very noisy and runs are short (tens of thousands of steps). ANVIL II already tied
Muon here (section below). The user asked for fundamental algorithmic gains, so every variant below is a flag on `--opt muon`, and each
one off is Muon bit for bit (tests/test_muonx). A/B harness: `runs/muonx/abq.sh GPU`. Each arm is 1500 steps of the approved 92 M net
(widths 256,320,384,448,288,288, 4 attention blocks, scroll RoPE). Recipe: P 512 B 1, `--det 1 --seed 7`, so every arm sees the same
windows; scratch1 sources, latdino's LR probe recipe plus `--gn-ema 1 --scan-norm 1 --fib-head 1` (rfwide merged); Muon 0.01 /
AdamW 1e-3, warmup 150, WSD cooldown 0.2. Compared: training loss and per-head losses over the last 300 steps, paired step for step
against plain Muon, with a block-bootstrap CI (`absum.py`).

| flag | what | source | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--muon-ns polar` | Polar Express: per-iteration minimax quintics instead of the fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315). Derived here by greedy LP from [1e-3, 1]; the published schedule matches to ~3%. Output singular values for sigma in [1e-3, 1]: [0.887, 1.113] (fixed: [0.471, 1.202]) | Amsel, Persson, Musco & Gower 2025, arXiv 2505.16932 | built, tested |
| `--normuon 1 [--normuon-beta2 0.95]` | per-row second-moment EMA of the orthogonalised direction; rows normalised, then Frobenius-rescaled to Muon's RMS | Li et al. 2025, arXiv 2510.05491 | built, tested |
| `--muon-vr G` | MARS variance reduction: c = g + G beta/(1-beta) (g - g_prev), clipped to unit norm per matrix, then Nesterov + NS. One g_prev buffer | Yuan et al. 2024, arXiv 2411.10438 | built, tested |
| `--muon-kron 1` | order-3 Shampoo on each 3^3 conv gradient [Co][Ci][27]: factors Co x Co, Ci x Ci, 27 x 27 (EMA b2 0.99), exponent -1/6, damping 1e-3 x \|L\|_F. Roots by coupled Newton (Guo & Higham 2006), refreshed round robin every 10 steps; the preconditioned gradient feeds Muon's momentum + NS. Memory 2 (Co^2 + Ci^2 + 729) per conv | Gupta, Koren & Singer 2018 | built, tested vs dense double reference |
| `--muon-c 1` | Muon-C on attention nets: the convs per frequency, the linears on the plain direction | (existing) | attention path built |
| `--muon-cautious 1` | zero the direction's elements whose sign disagrees with g, keep the norm | Liang et al. 2024, arXiv 2411.16085 | built, tested |
| `--muon-scale spectral`, `--opt-rest sign` | Scion geometry: per-matrix sqrt(fan_out / fan_in) instead of sqrt(max(1, Co/K)); biases / norms / head on sign momentum (ell-inf LMO) instead of AdamW | Pethick et al. 2025, arXiv 2502.07529 | built |
| `--muon-ademamix A [--ademamix-b3 0.999]` | slow EMA m2 added to the Nesterov momentum, alpha ramped 0 -> A | Pagliardini et al. 2024, arXiv 2409.03137 | built |
| `--muon-qkv-split 1` | Q / K / V of every head orthogonalised separately (not the fused [3C][C]) | Kimi K2 / MuonClip practice | built; QK-clip needs a logit-max hook in the attention kernels (not yet) |
| `--muon-tc 1` | the NS products on fp16 tensor cores (wmma, fp32 accumulate) | | built; accuracy test vs fp32 |
| `--muon-tc 2` | the NS products on cuBLASLt TF32 tensor cores (one GEMM per product and matrix, fp32 buffers) | | built, tested (2.4e-3 vs fp32) |

**Evaluation.** Matched step: training loss over the last 300 steps (the WSD cooldown), paired step for step against Muon (the same
windows), block-bootstrap 95% CI (`absum.py`). Held-out: each finished arm resumed from its last.ckpt for one lr-0 step with
`--val-batches 32 --val-live 1` (`evsum.py`; the same 32 windows for every arm, hash 4221f46d; scratch1 has no holdout boxes, so they come from
the training distribution at val seed + 777). Matched wall time: the wall clock of the arm (`done in`). Converting a loss gap into steps by the
reference's loss-vs-ln(step) slope does not work here: after step ~300 the per-window training loss is dominated by window difficulty
(fitted slope over steps 200-1200: +0.017 per ln step, the wrong sign), so a variant that is slower must win at matched steps by more than
the noise, or run a wall-matched arm.

| arm | wall (x Muon) | train loss vs Muon, last 300 [CI] | val | phase | normal | wind4 | turn acc | ink | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| muon | 2805 s | 1.6002 | 1.2325 | 0.3618 | 0.2736 | 0.3581 | 0.346 | 0.5800 | reference |
| kron | 3267 s (1.16x) | -0.0013 [-0.0021, -0.0006] | -0.0016 | +0.0000 | -0.0010 | +0.0006 | -0.003 | -0.0006 | tie at matched steps (-0.1%), 16% slower: no |

(The interim kron gap at steps 411-580, -0.0056, shrank to -0.0013 by the end of the cooldown.)

**Optimizer speed** (bench_muonx, 92 M net, ms per unet_muon call on one 5060 Ti; the P 512 training step is 1.81 s): Muon fp32 NS 121
(6.7% of the step), `--muon-tc 1` (hand-written wmma fp16) 213, `--muon-tc 2` (cuBLASLt TF32) 57 (3.2%); polar 122, NorMuon 126,
MARS-VR 127, cautious 128, AdEMAMix 128, Muon-C 263, Kronecker 465 (+344 ms: the whole of kron's 16% slowdown in training, 0.472 vs 0.553
samp/s). The TF32 update differs from the fp32 one by 2.4e-3 relative over 3 steps (test_muonx), as the fp16 path's; arm `muontc2` checks
loss parity in training. CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_16BF failed on the net's shapes (dropped).

**QK-clip** (`--qk-clip TAU`, built 2026-11-13): MuonClip rescales W_q, W_k when a head's max logit exceeds tau; with our QK-norm the
projections' scale cancels, so the clip scales the head's QK-norm gains qg, kg by sqrt(tau / max). The max logit q.k / sqrt(48) per head
comes from the fp16 tensor-core flash forward (`at_set_lmax`: the row maxima it already keeps, one atomicMax per warp); multi-GPU replicas
clip by the max over all GPUs. tests/test_qkclip: the hook against a double reference (2 sequences, partial tiles, masked keys) to
2e-3 relative, the clip exact. Every training log line now carries `qk` (the max logit since the last line). Muon at step 1500 of the
92 M net: qk 7.0, far below the tau ~100 of the Kimi recipe: QK-norm already bounds the logits, so QK-clip is expected to be inactive
here unless long runs grow them.

- **Labels** (nn_label_warp_z / nn_label_sym_z / nn_w4runs_label_z / nn_ink_bits_z) write output planes [z0, z0 + nz) from source
  planes [s0, s1) only.
  - nn_aug_src_range(rad, P, z0, nz) bounds [s0, s1). The warp's source z is linear in the per-axis displaced coordinates (rotation,
    zoom, affine, symmetry; elastic is per-axis tables), so its extremes are at the corners of the box of their ranges. Measured: the
    bound is at most 4 planes wider than the corners actually read, over 12 cases.
  - Under rotation the source range is ~nz cos + P sin. At P 256 the 40 / 72 range at 30 degrees staged 3.56 nz. So the staging does
    not halve under rotation: budget ~P planes of 8-bit staging per GPU (1 GB at P 1024).
  - nn_w4runs_apply_z: the runs are per x row, so a z range needs no plane outside it (strip offsets into the run table).
- **CT channel** (nn_aug_ct_z): the scanner ops need the whole source window. Paganin's two-sided exponential and the correlated
  noise recurse along z, GIN / histogram / z-score use whole-window statistics, and the z blur reads taps. With a zcomm (two ranks),
  rank r scans its source half and exchanges:
  - the halo planes, as they are before each stencil (the z blur's reach from the plan, GIN's 1, a dropped slice's source);
  - the correlated noise's carried plane (rank 0 -> 1);
  - paganin's carried y per line: forward 0 -> 1, then rank 1's backward from P - 2, then 1 -> 0;
  - the statistics: integer sums exact, GIN's two doubles as two partial atomic sums, which are order-free anyway;
  - finally, the scanned 8-bit planes each rank's warp reads from the other.
  The fp16 work volume aliases the rank's CT channel planes, as the one-GPU path does, when P/2 + 2 halo <= nz.
  Per GPU at P 1024: CT channel 544 planes (1.14 GB) + staging <= 1 GB, against 2 + 2.23 GB for the whole window.
- **Tests** (tests/test_aug_z.c, gpu, 14 s at P 256):
  - every label builder over 4 ranges x 12 warp / symmetry cases, with poisoned host planes outside [s0, s1) and a poisoned staging
    buffer;
  - the CT channel for the 22 scanner ops alone at two strengths, a mixture and none (44 cases) x 2 range pairs: the one-GPU range
    and both split ranks, through a loopback zcomm (two host threads, one GPU, a staging slot each);
  - all byte-identical to the whole-window call. A negative control (the exchanges dropped) differs on every voxel.
  - test_gpu_aug is unchanged and passes.
- **Stored onfly codes are now dcached.** The key is the array path, zarr.json size / mtime and the poolings. Without it every read
  recomputed the pair rule (16-50 s per 512^3 window on the CPU). sources-scratch1 v3 reads june / 0139 / 0500P2 / 1667-gt phase on
  the fly from their codes; phase-onfly against the stored rasters:
  - P4 june codesA 9.6 rmax 40: 0 differing voxels;
  - 0139 A+B fused rmax 41: 0 differing voxels;
  - 0500P2: native codes rebuilt, 0 differing voxels;
  - 1667 A+B 4.8 pooled: 10384 of 805 M voxels differ;
  - P4 july: the gtjuly codesB rebuild differs on 29%, because the 10-19 codes it came from are gone, so it keeps phaseB.
- Left to the split itself (univI): the zcomm over split.c's staged peer copies, the latent input from the CT channel, the
  label-stream slabs, MIL rays.
## The from-scratch net's whole-window field: measured ERF, seams, LR probe (2026-11-13, branch rfwide-20261113)

The next universal latent net (from scratch, all heads, one 1024^3 window split across both desk cards) is nlev 6, widths
256,320,384,448 + deep levels 288,288, 4 full-attention blocks with scroll RoPE on the 8^3-cell bottleneck (~92 M params): flags
`--widths 256,320,384,448,288,288 --attn-blocks 4 --attn-pe scroll`. Planner (13.3 GB per card, the scratch1 heads): 12.35 GB at
P 1024 x Pz 512 (the split proxy) vs 12.32 GB without the deep levels / attention; 4.09 GB at P 512 on one card. Theoretical RF:
nlev 4 103 cells, nlev 5 215, nlev 6 439 (> the 256-cell window; the attention is global on the bottleneck anyway).

**Seams** (inkpod-12000 ink, 1299 box 1024^3 at level 2, windows 512 + 2 halo; y / x seam steps, interior medians 0.05-0.3):

| halo | per-window GN + z-score | GN frozen (pooled) | fixed --norm | both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 15.4 / 26.6 | 13.8 / 11.0 | 15.3 / 24.9 | 6.2 / 6.9 |
| 64 | 28.3 / 11.7 | 5.0 / 10.6 | 28.0 / 10.1 | - |
| 256 | 5.8 / 6.7 | 0.3 / 2.2 | - | 0.0 / 0.1 |

Three causes: the halo below the RF radius, GroupNorm's whole-window statistics and the per-window input z-score. Pooled frozen
statistics at inference shift the outputs (ink mean 42 -> 33): the fix belongs in training (EMA GroupNorm at all levels, a
per-scan input z-score), next on this branch.

**Measured ERF** (`UFSM_ERF=DELTA` in train, `--lat` with the streamed head: the first training window forwarded, DELTA = 1 added to
the central 4^3 cells (16^3 voxels) of the z-scored CT, forwarded again; per cell the largest |logit change| of the first 16 head
channels, by Chebyshev distance r to the block. `UFSM_ERF_GNFROZEN=1` normalises the perturbed forward with the base forward's
GroupNorm statistics (`unet_gn_freeze_train`, diagnostics only): convolution reach alone. `UFSM_ERF_REPEAT=1`: 0 change everywhere,
the forward is deterministic.) unissl sources, P 1024 (256^3 cells) unless noted:

| net | GN | centre | r 32 | r 48 | r 56 | r >= 64 | far floor / centre | r50 / r90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| u1 random | live | 0.744 | 0.498 | 0.500 | 0.225 | 0.12-0.15 | 0.18 | 94 / 120 |
| u1 trained (last.ckpt) | live | 0.448 | 0.282 | 0.268 | 0.269 | 0.25-0.27 | **0.58** | 100 / 122 |
| u1 trained | frozen | 0.446 | 0.267 | 0.156 | 0.043 | **0** | 0 | 39 / 51 |
| 92 M random, P 768 | frozen | 0.872 | 0.660 | 0.743 | 0.737 | 0.45-0.69 (to r 94) | 0.47 | 70 / 89 |
| 92 M random, P 768 | live | 0.914 | 0.666 | 0.751 | 0.745 | 0.45-0.70 | 0.45 | 70 / 89 |

- u1's convolution reach ends at r ~ 56-60 cells (the theoretical 51.5 + the block), +-230 voxels of a 1024 window: the outer
  ~40% of each axis never sees the window's centre and vice versa.
- In trained u1 the whole-window GroupNorm coupling is larger than the convolution signal: a 16^3-voxel change moves every logit of
  the window by 58% of the change at the block itself, flat to the corners. This is the window dependence behind the seams
  (and why a window's outputs change with its extent); EMA GroupNorm removes it by construction.
- The 92 M net covers the whole window by convolution + attention alone (frozen: 47% of the centre change at the corners, r 94
  at P 768); random-init ERFs are wider than trained ones, the trained number comes with the first snapshot.

**LR probe** (the 92 M net at P 512 B 1 on one card, from scratch on sources-scratch1.json, --det 1 seed 7 so every arm sees the
same windows, 300 steps, warmup 50, WSD cooldown 0.2, AdamW 1e-3, 0.60 samp/s): mean logged loss over steps 200-300 Muon 0.005
1.710, 0.01 1.719, 0.02 1.721 (per-head at 300 within 0.01 of each other); none unstable. 300 steps at B 1 do not separate the
arms (differences ~0.01, 5 logged points); the earlier voxel-net sweep (F1 0.307 / 0.296 / 0.290 at 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.05) stays the
basis: Muon 0.01, AdamW 1e-3, warmup 1000, WSD cooldown 0.2.

**fib-head + fstem** (1f881bf): `--fstem` refused `--fib-head` ("25 outputs (16 at most)"): the head pads past 16 outputs to 32
and the fine stem counted the 9 unsupervised pad channels. It now maps into the supervised voxel outputs only (phase 2, wind4 2,
ink 1, rv 2, fibre 9 = 16, the stem kernel's limit); test_fibhead_train covers --lat 4 --fstem 16 --ink-head 1 --fib-head 1.

**EMA GroupNorm at every site** (`--gn-ema 1`, unet_cfg.gn_ema; `--gn-ema-mom 0.01 --gn-ema-warm 500`): all GroupNorms (every level's
blocks, the down norms, the attention stage, the head's input) normalise with running statistics (BatchNorm-style, [mean | var] per
group in the gn_sites layout; the first warm training forwards use their own statistics, after that training forwards are constants
in forward and backward, the backward without the statistics' terms, nn_set_gn_const; inference uses the running statistics as soon
as there are any). The sites hold the constants before the convs run (ge_begin), the convs write their live statistics to twins
(ge_dst) that ge_after pools into the running set after dec[0]; the EMA weights keep their own set (unet_ema), forwards with the
EMA weights (the SSL teacher) do not update. Checkpoints: header keys `gn_ema`, `ge_n`, `ge_warm`, `ge_mom`, `ge_run` only when on
(no new parameters: an old checkpoint loads into a gn_ema net as a fresh warm-up; u1-size net 448 floats, 31 KB header). Needs
`--l0-norm gn`. Multi-GPU data parallel: each card keeps its own statistics (card 0's are saved); with --split z the cards share one
window, so their statistics agree. Tests: test_gn_ema (both a down-norm net and an attention net: the warm-up then the running blend
at every site to 1e-4; a far-corner input change leaves the logits bit-identical, live GN moves them; momentum 1 reproduces live GN,
statistics 1e-7, logits 5e-3 of 6.2; EMA-weight set; checkpoint round trip bit-identical; old checkpoint = fresh warm-up; finite
backward), test_unet~GN_EMA=1 (fp32 finite differences with down norms: worst 7.5e-5 over 60 params; tensor cores vs fp32 logits
0.061 of 6.6). Train smoke (u1 widths, P 256, warm-up 10): losses continuous across the switch to constants.

**Per-scan input normalisation** (`--scan-norm 1`, unet_cfg.scan_norm, src/scannorm.c): the CT input is (v - center) / scale with one
(center, scale) per scan and level instead of each window's mean / sd: the mean and sd of the nonzero voxels in 48 boxes of 32^3 at
the working level, centred on nonzero voxels of a coarse level (the first of L + 2 .. L + 9 with <= 2^26 voxels read whole, else the
smallest subsampled every st-th voxel) at fixed ranks: a deterministic function of the volume. The sampler computes it on the first
window per (source, level) (a source's "norm" key wins; a failure keeps the window z-score, reported once); the checkpoint keeps
`"scan_norm":1`, and predict computes the same numbers for its scan and level (`--norm MEAN,SD` overrides). Mean / sd rather than
median / MAD: inside the mask the nonzero voxels are bimodal and the MAD follows the dominant mode only (1667 level 2: median 45,
1.4826 MAD 10.4, papyrus at ~+7; mean / sd 62.9 / 37.6). On the unissl sources all 22 (source, level) pairs get statistics (center
62.9-126, scale 28-56); predict on 1667 level 2 prints 62.9 / 37.59, the sampler's. test_scan_norm (wind fixture: deterministic
across runs, in the checkpoint, predict = sampler, --norm overrides, the losses change).

Found on the way (not fixed here): with the scratch1 sources at P 1024 on one card an early `inkfly gpu: out of device memory`
falls back to the CPU and then segfaults in nn_ink_bits (cudaMemcpyAsync of an invalid host pointer, lab_upload kind 3); and
the scratch1 data path holds ~7 GB of device memory outside the planner at P 512.
## Deep levels whole on both cards: --split-top (2026-11-13, branch splitwin-20261112)

Under `--split z` the halo is 2^(nlev-1) cells. For the 6-level scratch2 net that would be 32 cells (128 voxels): halves of 640 instead
of 544 at P 1024, +18 % level-0 memory and compute. `unet_set_split_top(u, T, split_gather)` / `train --split-top T` (default 3 above 4
levels) splits only levels 0..T-1.

**Forward:**
- down[T-1]'s output is all-gathered in place (split_gather / nn_split_gather: each half's owned planes, peer copy, unpacked into the
  whole window's layout).
- Levels T.. (the attention stage included) and their decoders run on the whole window on both GPUs, with nn's split statistics off
  (sp_deep).
- dec[T]'s a2 is sliced back to the half (sp_slice) behind a stand-in block for dec[T-1]'s staged upsample. Its GN statistics are the
  window's.

**Backward:**
- The coarse up-part gradient is computed on the half and gathered.
- enc[T]'s input gradient is sliced back for the split down[T-1].
- Both cards compute identical deep parameter gradients, so side 1 zeroes its copy (sp_dedup, before film_bwd). The existing two-card
  gradient sum then stays the window's.

**Parity:** the halo is 2^T cells, so 2 planes at level T-1 and 1 at level T, which keeps the stride-2 grid. A gather at level 4 with
an 8-cell halo would break that parity, so T = 3 with 8 cells (32 voxels) is the setting that keeps today's 544-deep halves. Level 3 at
P 1024 is 32^3 cells, so the redundant deep compute is negligible.

**Attention:** the stage sees the whole window, so `--attn-pe scroll` keeps the sampler's whole-window axis record under the split.

**Trainer A/B** (scripts/test/split_lat_ab.sh, P 256, both halves on GPU 0, round to nearest, the first step's loss and summed gradient,
split vs one GPU, the scratch1 smoke sources):

| net | input | loss | gradient rel (rerun noise) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 levels | --gpu-aug 2 (CT channel per half via nn_aug_ct_z) | identical | 2.2e-7 (1.9e-7) |
| 6 levels + scroll attention, --gn-ema, --scan-norm | host-built | identical | 1.2e-7 (1.0e-7) |
| the same | --gpu-aug 2 | identical | 1.4e-7 (1.2e-7) |

The scratch1 smoke sources carry aux labels, so --gpu-aug 2 falls back to 1 there: the CT channel on the device, labels warped on the
host. The labels' _z builders are covered by test_aug_z, but not by a trainer A/B yet.

**Found while wiring this in:**
- train set `--gpu-aug 0` under any --split, silently. A latent split now keeps it: each half builds its planes, lab_upload / ct_upload
  inside a split_run job.
- The planner counted the latent split's gy records per voxel instead of per cell (77 GB at P 1024).
- The planner never counted the --gpu-aug staging for --lat. It now counts the shared staging buffer: one P^3 with --gpu-aug 3 runs
  slots, 2 P^3 otherwise.

**92 M, P 1024, --split z --split-top 3, the scratch2.launch flags** (without --ink-mil / --ink-air / --fib-head, still refused under the
split), planned for 13.3 GB per card: 12.57 of 12.80 GB.

| part | GB |
|---|---|
| network (lean 2, MX-fp4 gradients, shared encoder a1) | 5.38 |
| workspace | 0.38 |
| gy records (the deferred GN apply is off under the split) | 1.21 |
| task (label stream, head slabs at UFSM_HEAD_SLAB_Z=16, the latent batch, the aug staging) | 5.02 |
| fixed | 0.58 |

**test_split_lat:** a 6-level net (32,32,64,64,96,96) with an attention block at P 256 (local 40 cells), against one GPU. It gives the
same verdicts as the 4-level net:

| mode | owned logits | cut halo cells | gradient rel | 4-level net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp4 rn | bit-identical | identical | 6e-8 | 2e-8 |
| MX-fp8 rn | bit-identical | identical | 7e-3 (perturbed CT: 0.49) | 5e-3 |

## The U2 sampler at P 1024: where the workers wait, the codes pooling without its atan2 (2026-11-12, branch pool2fast-20261112)

(Merged 2026-11-13 into integ19 as numbers only: the code of this branch is superseded. Its pooling loop gave way to the exact host /
device bin-search pooling in codes_pool.h with the pooled tiles on the GPU (26528b9, below), and the branch-free coverage shares landed as
064fc4d. The slot / memory findings stand.)

Pod (one RTX PRO 6000, 40 CPUs, a 175 GB cgroup shared by every job), `UFSM_SAMPLER_ONLY` with U2's args (`sources-u2pod.json`: 9 band,
2 mesh, 8 ink sources; replay 3), the GPU exclusive but the CPUs not (load average ~30). What limited the sampler, in the order found:

- **`--sampler-slots` caps the builders, not `--workers`.** 24 workers on 10 slots built 9 windows at once (589 Mvox/s, 6.3 busy cores);
  the log line "N workers but M slots" says so. Slots must be workers + 2.
- **Host memory then caps the slots**: with the ink sources a slot is ~7 GB and a worker's scratch ~4 GB (12 workers / 14 slots: 135-147 GB
  RSS; 24 / 26 and 32 / 34 passed 166 GB and were stopped). On this pod no more than ~12 workers fit beside nothing else, 8 / 10 beside
  the trainer's own memory under a 130 GB cap (U2's launch).
- **The pooled-codes tiles** (levels whose phase comes "from the codes pooled 2x (on the fly)") never reach the device: the pooled codes
  are a derived array without stored chunks, so `z3_chunk_raw` fails and `codes_pool2_box` runs on the reading thread, one double atan2
  per labelled 2^3 block. Stack samples (the run as gdb's child, 10 interrupts in steady state, 12 workers / 14 slots / 4 onfly slots):
  2.6 workers inside the pooling loop, 1.5 queued in `ob_take` for a buffer set behind them. The loop now gives the same bytes without
  the atan2 in all but the near-tie blocks: runs of 8 empty blocks are skipped on two 64-bit tests per row, equal children return their
  own code (the float sums' angle is theirs within 1e-6 codes), and for mixed blocks a polynomial angle (error < 1e-4 rad = 0.004
  codes) decides the rounding wherever it lands more than 0.03 codes from a half; only the remaining near ties call the reference
  atan2. After: 0.1 workers in the pooling, 0.6 in `ob_take`. `test_phase_pool` compares it with the reference loop (`codes_pool2_ref`,
  `UFSM_POOL2_REF=1`): 64260 equal-children blocks, 30 M random blocks (spreads of 1-6 steps around a base code, wraps at 252, holes,
  conflicts) and three boxes of a synthetic 150 x 201 x 333 codes array with odd edges, 0 bytes differ.
- **The sampler-only mode capped itself**: its consuming thread computed the material / phase-known shares with a branch per voxel,
  ~1.3 s per P 1024 batch, so the mode could not report much over 0.7 batches/s (4.4 of 12 workers waited for a slot behind it once the
  pooling was fixed). Every rate measured before this commit (522-787 Mvox/s) is a floor for that reason; the shares are now taken once
  per window, branch-free per 64 k voxels (`UFSM_SAMPLER_COV=0`: none), and the per-source "windows" count new windows, not batches.
  Not re-measured: with U2 resident on the pod a full-list sampler-only run no longer fits the cgroup.
- U2 itself (8 workers / 10 slots / 4 onfly slots) logs "wait 0%" from step 200 at 0.35-0.38 samp/s beside another P 1024 training on the
  card: the step, not the sampler, is its limit.

## PHerc1299 B3 labels: the direction check, its mask, phase on the fly + one weight array (2026-11-12, branch fibd-20261111)

PHerc1299's snapped wraps (71 of 88 kept, surf-labels kept share 0.9487) failed the stored-phase guard: `phase-check` outward 0.890 over
23 558 chunks, box range 0.161..1.000. Per 128^3 cell outside the held-out band (17 383 cells): 0.36 of the voxel pairs sit in cells
>= 0.95, 0.48 in 0.80-0.95, 0.16 below; 14 cells in the whole scroll under 0.4. Mixed, not flipped.

**The raw outward share is confounded with sheet orientation.** On 500 sampled cells it correlates 0.83 with the mean |cos| between the
phase gradient and the radius: cells under 0.6 have mean |cos| 0.15 (sheets running along the radius; the sign of the radial component
is noise). Counting only voxels whose in-plane gradient lies within 45.6 degrees of the radius (|cos| > 0.7, >= 3 codes / voxel:
`phase_outward_aligned`, `phase-check --cells` / `--aligned-cos`) gives 0.9957 outward over the scroll outside the band (0.33 of the
pairs aligned), 1.000 / 0.996 in the cells whose raw score is >= 0.95 / 0.90-0.95. **Use the aligned share for future scrolls**; a 0.95
raw threshold would have discarded 64% of correct labels here. (Without the 3-code floor an azimuth-only phase, whose quantised
differences are 0 / 1 code, produced spurious aligned voxels: test_phase_check covers both.)

**Fibre gate vs outward: independent.** spirals' fiber-judge tiles (Paris 4 ramp 189..378 persistent /m) against the raw cell score:
correlation -0.09; median rate 411 / 373 / 401 /m in the < 0.8 / 0.8-0.95 / >= 0.95 bins, i.e. at or above the ramp's top everywhere
(the same miscalibration latres measured on the 8.64 um 1218 / 1447 scans). Shares of pairs outside the band:

| fibre tile | outward >= 0.95 | 0.80-0.95 | < 0.80 | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| factor 0 | 0.224 | 0.229 | 0.088 | 0.541 |
| partial | 0.105 | 0.230 | 0.060 | 0.395 |
| factor 1 | 0.022 | 0.009 | 0.001 | 0.033 |
| unjudged | 0.011 | 0.014 | 0.006 | 0.031 |

**The mask (coordinator's option B)**, `scripts/univ/b3_1299_mask.py` -> a `phase-coh --box-scale` file (first box wins), then
`ufsm phase-coh --coh 0 --papyrus 64 --pap-dilate 2` on the gated phase:
- the held-out band + guard (level-2 z < 4167): 0;
- direction-masked 128^3 cells: 0. (a) fibre factor 0 AND raw outward < 0.8: 1922 cells, 0.088 of the pairs; (b) reversed by the aligned
  test (>= 20 000 aligned pairs, ~1% of a cell, binomial sd < 0.004, of which < 0.5 outward): 314 cells, 0.021; both 0.008. Total 2113
  cells, 0.101 of the pairs; kept 0.899;
- fibre tiles: 0.5 + 0.5 x factor (floored: the ramp must not act as a mask through the weight), 1 elsewhere;
- air (CT < 64 with no CT >= 64 within 2 voxels): 0.131 of the known voxels; the gt-gate's removed cells and every surf-labels ignore are
  already unknown in the gated phase and get weight 0.
Result `/vesuvius/ufsm/univ/b3/PHerc1299/mask/weight.zarr` (1.4 GB): 0.42 of the known voxels at 0, 0.39 at 0.5-0.6, mean 0.35.

**Gate numbers with the band excluded**: the gated phase keeps 0.962 of the labelled phase's pairs outside the band (gt-gate + shard rule
remove 0.038; 0.070 of all sheet voxels including the band), aligned outward 0.9961. The band cells held 0.258 / 0.257 of the pairs of
the labelled / gated phase: the labels were built while holdouts-1299.json had the band in level-2 numbers (an empty corner, "holdout
0"), so they hold phase there; the weight, the band's holdout_reject and the sampler keep training out. surf-labels now fails on a holdout
box with no labelled voxel (test_surflabels).

**PHerc1218 rescored the same way** (its B3 gate rerun, 2026-11-12 04:16: gt-gate removed 0.179 of the sheet voxels, every gated cell for
sheet direction vs m7, 2319 shards): over the gated phase's 103 696 cells, raw outward 0.9852 (pass), 0.659 of the pairs aligned (vs
0.33 on 1299: 1218's sheets face its axis), aligned outward **0.9998**. By raw bin, the pair shares are 0.007 / 0.010 / 0.016 / 0.035 /
0.933 for < 0.6 / 0.6-0.8 / 0.8-0.9 / 0.9-0.95 / >= 0.95, with aligned outward 0.865 / 0.965 / 0.990 / 0.998 / 0.9999. By the 1299 rule
27 cells read reversed (0.0002 of the pairs): no direction mask for 1218. On the aligned share the two scrolls are comparable: 1218
0.9998, 1299 0.9961 gated (0.9957 labelled) outside its band.

**Shipped form**: phase on the fly from the kept wraps' codes (2.0 GB, `codes.zarr`, rmax 20 = surf-labels --radius 20) plus the one
weight array; no stored phase. `phase-onfly --ref (label phase) --weight (the array)` on 12 windows of 512^3: 30.4 M voxels differ from
the stored label phase overall (the label phase has surf-labels' ignored voxels blanked; the rule fills them), **0 of 587 330 312 voxels
differ under a non-zero weight**. CPU pair rule ~15 s per 512^3 window (u1 holds both GPUs). The entry `PHerc1299-b3` is in
mksources_univ.py behind B3=1 until its sampler-only band line is read in a GPU window.

## One P 1024 window across both 5060 Tis: the z split for the latent net (design, 2026-11-12, branch splitwin-20261112)

User: "if we can split one window across both gpus rather than just doing 2 separate inferences that would also be preferred" and
"more recompute is fine if we can get a bigger model with 1024 windows on the 5060tis". Design only; no code yet.

**What exists.** The spatial z split is already built for the voxel (CT) net (2026-10-01, `train --split z --gpus 0,1`,
`predict --split z`, src/split.{c,h}, test_split x5 in the slow tier). Each GPU holds its z half plus 2^(L-1-l) halo planes at
level l. Every stencil consumer needs only the innermost halo plane, so each produced tensor gets that plane from the other GPU,
and the outer halo planes are zeroed. A gradient that feeds a reduction (GN backward, weight gradient) has its halo zeroed. GN
statistics, GN-backward sums and loss sums are reduced across the GPUs (`nn_split_cfg` + the `split_reduce` callback).
Parameter gradients are summed and the weights stay replicated. Two host threads take turns, and the second to reach a collective
issues it for both. Backward halos go over a communication stream during the weight gradient. Measured then: no P2P on the
GeForce cards, staged peer copies at 14-17 GB/s, ~10 us small. Split vs one GPU matched to the rerun noise (fp16 loss within
3e-6), and split ran at 0.141 vs data parallel 0.149 Gvox/s at 512^3 (~-5..-8 %). The windows grew from 576^3 (data parallel)
to 704^3 (split).
So this is mostly porting the latent path onto that machinery. The latent path refuses --split today:
- `--lat 4: ... no --split`;
- the head-slab loss path needs `!split`;
- `--gpu-input` / `--gpu-aug` need `!split`;
- the ink head, `--fib-head`, `--count-lambda`, `--pap-head`, `--ssl`, `--attn-axis` and `predict --heads` all refuse it.

**1. Decomposition: z slabs, not a depth / pipeline split.**
- At P 1024 with u1's net (lat 4: trunk level 0 = 256^3 cells; widths 96, 128, 160, 192; MX-fp4 activations), one level-0 cell
  tensor of 96 channels is ~0.86 GB, level 1 ~0.14 GB, levels 2-3 < 0.03 GB. The full-resolution planes (CT, the target and label
  planes, ~3.2 GB uploaded per step) plus the level-0 trunk tensors are ~90 % of the 11.78 GB lean-2 plan (11.0 B a voxel; params
  + optimizer ~0.2 GB).
- A pipeline split (encoder levels on GPU 0, decoder on GPU 1) would leave both level-0 ends (stem / enc0 / skip and dec0 / head)
  on different GPUs with the skip crossing PCIe (0.86 GB a step each way). It would not halve the full-resolution planes, and one
  GPU idles in each half of the step. Spatial halves every window-sized buffer.
- Halo cost: 8 cell planes at level 0 (= 32 voxels), and the same 1/16 at every level, so +6.25 % trunk compute (3 % at 512^3
  owned depth if h0 4). The head path runs on owned voxels + 1 cell (below), < 1 %.

**2. Cross-GPU pieces.**
- *Halo exchange:* the existing split_halo / begin / end (innermost plane, staged through the peer copy). Per exchange at level 0:
  256^2 cells x 96 ch: fp4 ~3.3 MB, fp16 gradient ~12.6 MB; deeper levels smaller. ~40 exchanges a step (the 4-level trunk) is
  ~0.25 GB a step, ~15-20 ms at 14-17 GB/s, mostly overlapped (backward on the comm stream), against a 1.35-2.5 s step.
  Stage 0 re-measures P2P (cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer) and the staged bandwidth on today's driver.
- *GroupNorm:* trunk GN already reduces sum / sumsq per group across the GPUs, with the halo excluded (split_t zlo / zhi). The
  latent head's statistics (the l0 constants, `gn_const`) take the same reduce.
- *Head slab pass (head_slab_pass, streamed latent head):* each GPU runs its own z slabs (32 planes) over its owned voxels plus
  4 voxels (one cell) into the halo. Targets exist there: the label planes are uploaded with the halo. The loss value and its
  normalisers count owned voxels only, summed across GPUs; the gradient is computed on owned + 1 cell. Then each GPU's owned
  cells get their complete gradient from its own pass (the upsample and fine stem reach at most one cell). That needs no new
  collective, unlike a reverse halo add. Stencil losses (normals from the phase gradient, +-1 voxel) are covered by the 32-voxel
  CT / label halo.
- *Losses / uw / statistics:* every global sum (loss numerators, denominators, the uw log-variances' inputs, MIL / dice counts)
  goes through split_reduce, as the voxel path's side / phase losses already do.
- *MIL rays (ink):* rays along the normal can cross the cut. Assign each ray to the GPU that owns its centre voxel and give it the
  halo samples (32 voxels covers rays up to +-32: check `inkfly_rays` lengths). If any ray exceeds that, the max-over-ray needs a
  gather of a few k floats per step, which is cheap.
- *Optimizer:* weights replicated, gradients summed through the existing data-parallel allreduce (one host thread per GPU,
  2026-11-11 section). Muon's Newton-Schulz then runs identically on both GPUs (deterministic bytes needed: it already is
  under --det).
- *Inputs (`--gpu-input`, gpu-aug 2/3, on-the-fly labels):* each GPU builds its z range + halo of the same window. The warps and
  noise must be functions of global voxel coordinates and the shared per-window parameters: counter-based noise keyed by global
  index, blurs / correlated noise computed over the needed extra planes. This is the largest new piece: every nn_aug kernel
  gains a z offset and depth, and each CPU-side builder that fills whole planes (phase from codes, fibre H / V, ink targets)
  gains a z range. The sampler then delivers one window per step instead of two (data parallel), which halves the host
  label-build load. That load was the P 1024 bottleneck (23-25 s phase reads per window).
- *SSL / DINO (--ssl):* the student / teacher terms over masked cell blocks need the pooled embeddings and the centring /
  variance statistics summed across the halves (a few hundred floats). The block mask must come from one seed and be indexed by
  global cell coordinates. Stage 3.
- *predict --heads:* the trunk forward under the split, then each GPU runs its owned planes' head / fit-field / pyramid writes
  (the voxel path's psplit_job already places owned planes per shard).

**3. Cost model (estimates; stage 0 replaces them with UFSM_MEM_DRY / UFSM_MEM_REPORT numbers per GPU).**
- Memory per GPU, same net (96..192), lean 2: window-sized buffers x (0.5 + 0.03 halo) ~ 5.4-5.8 GB, plus slab-sized head
  workspace ~1 GB (does not shrink) and params ~0.2 GB. That is ~6.5-7 GB of the 13.3 GB budget instead of 11.78.
- Widest net: trunk memory is ~linear in width at level 0. At lean 2 the spare ~6 GB takes the level-0 / dec0 width from 96 to
  roughly 192 (or 96, 128, 160, 192 -> ~160, 224, 288, 352 with the deeper levels cheap). Alternatively keep the width and drop
  to a mode without the 2.45 GB host offloads each way and the recompute.
- Step time: per window, about half the one-GPU step x 1.06 (halo) + ~3-8 % sync / exchange. So per voxel ~equal to data parallel
  at the same width (data parallel does 2 windows per step) and slower per window as the net widens (compute ~linear in width).
  What it buys is width and window, not speed. On the host side it halves sampler windows per step.

**4. Tests.**
- `test_split_lat` (gpu2, slow + a quick fast variant): a lat 4 unwrap2 net with the ink and rv heads, P 128-256, B 1, and
  synthetic labels including halo-crossing structure. Split vs one GPU:
  - forward cell logits within the fp4 rounding noise (the voxel test's bounds: loss within 1e-6 relative at fp16 storage; at
    fp4 compare against two rounding seeds of one GPU);
  - every loss term and the uw statistics equal;
  - parameter gradients relative L2 within the one-GPU rerun difference.
- A central-difference check of the summed gradient on a tiny net (8 / 16 channels, fp32 verify build) at a few parameters
  next to the cut.
- predict: `--heads --split z` byte-identical outputs to one GPU on a test box. The voxel path already is; the cell path should
  be too, given deterministic sums.
- Input builders: each gpu-aug kernel with a z offset reproduces the corresponding planes of the whole-window build
  byte-identically (host reference).

**5. Staged plan (effort; GPU work only in windows).**
- S0, 0.5 day: P2P / staged-bandwidth probe (seconds); the planner (build_acts already sizes from the local depth) at P 1024 with
  split depth 512 + 32 for u1's widths and a width sweep. Gives the real "widest net" number before anything else.
- S1, 1-2 days: latent trunk + predict --heads under the split (forward only): lift the refusals, the cell-level halos (the
  existing sp_* calls already wrap the trunk's convs), head / fit planes per owned range. Test byte-identity. This is cheap and
  proves the trunk.
- S2, 3-4 days: training. Head-slab pass on owned + 1 cell, loss / uw / MIL sums reduced, gpu-input / gpu-aug / on-the-fly labels
  per z range, the gradient allreduce for the split pair, test_split_lat + FD. Then a P 1024 throughput bench vs data parallel at
  u1's width and at the widest planned width.
- S3, 1-2 days: --ssl (DINO) under the split, --fib-head, the planner's split mode in `--mem auto`, the wrapper flags.
- Total ~6-9 working days. Recommendation: S0 first (it decides whether the width gain is worth it), then S1 -> S2. Predict
  alone gains nothing from the split (an inference window already fits one GPU, and two windows on two GPUs are faster). It
  matters only once a wider net no longer fits one GPU's forward.

**S0 (measured 2026-11-12 22:00): the planner per GPU at P 1024.** UFSM_MEM_DRY=1 UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB=13.3 with the sslpair-ctrl arguments
exactly (u1 recipe + --ssl 16, --ink-head 1, --rv 2, --fstem 16, --film 2; latdino4 binary; lean 2 + shared encoder a1 picked
everywhere). The split half is proxied by a single-card --Pz 544 window (512 owned + 32 halo voxels = 136 trunk cells); the
halo exchange buffers (~0.25 GB of traffic, a few planes resident) are not in it. GB of the 13.30 budget:

| level widths | params | whole window (one card) | split half (per GPU) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 96,128,160,192 (u1) | 10.1M | 12.97 | 9.71 |
| 128,160,192,256 | 15.8M | 14.39 refused | 10.47 |
| 160,192,256,320 | 25.5M | 15.82 refused | 11.24 |
| 192,256,320,384 | 40.0M | 17.34 refused | 12.05 |
| 192 x 4 | 19.1M | 17.09 refused | 11.91 |
| 256 x 4 | 33.9M | 19.92 refused | 13.42 (just over) |
| 256,320,384,448 | 60.1M | 20.17 refused | 13.57 (just over) |

- One card tops out at u1's width; the split fits 2x u1's width at every level (40M params, 4x u1).
- The per-GPU task term barely shrinks (8.11 -> 6.81 GB). The head slabs (1.48), the gpu-aug staging (2.23) and the lat head
  slab (0.61) are sized per window, not per depth. Staging per z range (the gpu-aug builders' global z range: spec sent to univA)
  would halve the staging and fit 256 x 4 / 256-448 (~12.3-12.5 GB).
- (This binary plans the whole window at 12.97 GB; the sslpair-ctrl log's earlier start line said 11.78, from before --ssl.)
- Compute: level 0 dominates and grows with w0^2. 192-384 is ~4x u1's FLOPs per window: ~2x u1's per-card step time per window,
  ~4x fewer windows a second than u1 data parallel. The target is 192,256,320,384, with 160-320 as the fallback.

**Planner for the target net (2026-11-12 23:00).** Setup:
- every head of the run: --ink-head 1 --ink-mil 1 --ink-air 8, --fib-head 1, --rv 2, --fstem 16, --film 2;
- binary: rfwide 1f881bf (latdino);
- Pz 512 single-card proxy (nlev 6 needs Pz % 128), 13.3 GB budget, lean 2 + shared a1 chosen.

Mode-4 totals with 32-plane head slabs (default):

| net | params | GB |
|---|---|---|
| 192-384 | 40M | 13.49 |
| 256-448 | 60M | 14.92 |
| 256,320,384,448,288,288 + 4 attention | ~92M | 14.93 |
| 256,320,448,512 | — | 14.94 |

- The head slabs (2.68 GB with 32 outputs) and the gpu-aug staging (2.23) dominate the task term (8.86).
- The network term is ~linear in w0 (3.79 at 192, 5.02 at 256). The deep levels and the attention add 0.01.
- Recompute 2 is bigger than lean 2 here (16.65).

UFSM_HEAD_SLAB_Z=16 halves the head slabs (2.68 -> 1.34, lat head slab 0.71 -> 0.43). Mode-4 totals with it:

| net | GB |
|---|---|
| 92M | 13.04 |
| 288-480 + deep | 13.75 |
| 320-512 + deep | 14.47 |

Split estimate per card:
- start from the proxy;
- + 6.25 % of the level 0-3 network + workspace (the 32-voxel halo; the level-4 all-gather keeps levels 4-5 whole);
- + the planner's split halo term (0.27);
- - univA's split scanner: staging 2.23 -> ~1.0 GB, x 1 + 1/14 margin = -1.32.

| net | GB per card | headroom |
|---|---|---|
| 92M | 13.04 + 0.34 + 0.27 - 1.32 = **12.33** | 0.97 |
| 288-480 | 13.08 | 0.22 |
| 320-512 | 13.84 | refused |

So the 92M target fits with HEAD_SLAB_Z 16 and the split scanner, and w0 256 is the widest with >= 0.8 GB headroom.

**S1 / S2 order changed.** An inference forward of the 40M net at 1024 fits one card (no stored activations), so predict gains only
latency from the split. Training goes first.

**S2 implementation (branch splitwin-20261112).**
- The trunk under the split needs one change. The latent input pool (nn_input_latc / nn_input_lat, rad_full4) computes the radial
  channels of the global voxel. The record keeps the window's depth (h[2]); the spare word 7 holds this half's first plane, so
  the cube symmetries (z flip, z <-> y) and warps read the global axis centres. Whole windows: word 7 is 0, so the bytes are
  unchanged.
- unet_split_head_halo: dec[0]'s output (the head input) gets its innermost halo plane from the other GPU. The head logits of the
  halo cell next to the cut are then the window's, which the head slabs' band reads (below).
- tests/test_split_lat (gpu, 9 cases, ~1 s; both halves on one GPU when only one is free): a cin-32 latent net (32 cells, halo 8)
  vs one GPU, with a fixed smooth cell-logit gradient:
  - MX-fp8 round to nearest: the owned cells' logits are bit-identical (rel 0) under identity / z flip / z<->y, and so are the
    exchanged cut halo cells. The gradient rel is 4.9e-3, against 0.25 for a last-bit-perturbed input.
  - The fp4 preset rounding to nearest (MX-fp8 gradients): logits and cut cells identical; gradient rel 2.3e-8 (perturbed 0.82).
  - The fp4 preset with SR and MX-fp4 gradients: logits identical; gradient rel 0.68-0.72, at the seed-to-seed spread
    (0.66-0.72).
- The trainer (`train --lat 4 --split z --gpus a,b`) runs each half as a window of its own: g_Pz = g_Dl = P / 2 + 32 voxels,
  set after the sampler config, which keeps P^3 windows.
  - batch_view: the upload sees the sampler window's planes from split_z0, plus a per-buffer pinned copy of the record with word 7.
    The existing upload, label stream, planner and head-slab code then run unchanged on the half.
  - The head slabs mask the halo voxels (hs_clip). The statistics pass counts the owned voxels; the loss finalisations already
    sum across the GPUs (zs_reduce in nn_loss_stats_fin / nn_wind4_fin).
  - The gradient pass also takes the halo cell next to the cut (4 voxels). The latent upsampling is the pool4 chain: every voxel of
    cell c reads cells c-1 .. c+1 (nn_lat.cu LW), so those voxels reach the owned boundary cell, and they read the 2 innermost
    halo cells. Hence unet_split_head_halo exchanges 2 planes (split_halo_k / nn_split_halo_k, a new k-plane collective). The owned
    cells' gradient is then complete without a reverse halo add, and the halo cells' gradient is dropped (hs_zero_halo_cells,
    before the streamed head backward).
  - The first version used a 2-voxel band and a 1-plane exchange (assuming plain trilinear). The trainer A/B caught it: every cell
    plane was bit-identical except the 2 at the cut (7 % of values, rel 1.6e-2), which the backward amplified to 0.2 rel in
    enc0.c1 (3e-2 overall).
  - The fine stem's weight gradient takes the owned planes only.
  - One fstem-dropout and lat-step-jitter draw per window.
  - The light statistics pass is off: it would double-count the band in the logged loss.
- Trainer A/B (scripts/test/split_lat_ab.sh: P 256, 32-64 net, every u1 head but ssl, --fstem 16, --film 2, --uw 1, --det 1,
  round to nearest + MX-fp8 gradients via UFSM_TEST_SR_OFF / UFSM_GRAD_MX4=0; UFSM_GRAD_DUMP: the first step's loss and summed
  gradient). One GPU vs the split, both halves on GPU 0:
  - the loss is identical (2.96193621);
  - every streamed cell-gradient plane is bit-identical (UFSM_LATG_DUMP, per half .s0 / .s1);
  - the parameter gradient rel is 8.0e-8, the one-GPU rerun level (5.7e-8).
- Not yet under the split (refused): --gpu-aug (univA's z-range builders), --ssl, --ink-mil, --fib-head, --fib-normal-lambda,
  --pgrad, --count, --pap-head, --distill, --lat-guide 1 / 2, the unstreamed latent head.

## The from-scratch net's whole-window field: measured ERF, seams, LR probe (2026-11-13, branch rfwide-20261113)

The next universal latent net (from scratch, all heads, one 1024^3 window split across both desk cards) is nlev 6, widths
256,320,384,448 + deep levels 288,288, 4 full-attention blocks with scroll RoPE on the 8^3-cell bottleneck (~92 M params): flags
`--widths 256,320,384,448,288,288 --attn-blocks 4 --attn-pe scroll`. Planner (13.3 GB per card, the scratch1 heads): 12.35 GB at
P 1024 x Pz 512 (the split proxy) vs 12.32 GB without the deep levels / attention; 4.09 GB at P 512 on one card. Theoretical RF:
nlev 4 103 cells, nlev 5 215, nlev 6 439 (> the 256-cell window; the attention is global on the bottleneck anyway).

**Seams** (inkpod-12000 ink, 1299 box 1024^3 at level 2, windows 512 + 2 halo; y / x seam steps, interior medians 0.05-0.3):

| halo | per-window GN + z-score | GN frozen (pooled) | fixed --norm | both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 15.4 / 26.6 | 13.8 / 11.0 | 15.3 / 24.9 | 6.2 / 6.9 |
| 64 | 28.3 / 11.7 | 5.0 / 10.6 | 28.0 / 10.1 | - |
| 256 | 5.8 / 6.7 | 0.3 / 2.2 | - | 0.0 / 0.1 |

Three causes: the halo below the RF radius, GroupNorm's whole-window statistics and the per-window input z-score. Pooled frozen
statistics at inference shift the outputs (ink mean 42 -> 33): the fix belongs in training (EMA GroupNorm at all levels, a
per-scan input z-score), next on this branch.

**Measured ERF** (`UFSM_ERF=DELTA` in train, `--lat` with the streamed head: the first training window forwarded, DELTA = 1 added to
the central 4^3 cells (16^3 voxels) of the z-scored CT, forwarded again; per cell the largest |logit change| of the first 16 head
channels, by Chebyshev distance r to the block. `UFSM_ERF_GNFROZEN=1` normalises the perturbed forward with the base forward's
GroupNorm statistics (`unet_gn_freeze_train`, diagnostics only): convolution reach alone. `UFSM_ERF_REPEAT=1`: 0 change everywhere,
the forward is deterministic.) unissl sources, P 1024 (256^3 cells) unless noted:

| net | GN | centre | r 32 | r 48 | r 56 | r >= 64 | far floor / centre | r50 / r90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| u1 random | live | 0.744 | 0.498 | 0.500 | 0.225 | 0.12-0.15 | 0.18 | 94 / 120 |
| u1 trained (last.ckpt) | live | 0.448 | 0.282 | 0.268 | 0.269 | 0.25-0.27 | **0.58** | 100 / 122 |
| u1 trained | frozen | 0.446 | 0.267 | 0.156 | 0.043 | **0** | 0 | 39 / 51 |
| 92 M random, P 768 | frozen | 0.872 | 0.660 | 0.743 | 0.737 | 0.45-0.69 (to r 94) | 0.47 | 70 / 89 |
| 92 M random, P 768 | live | 0.914 | 0.666 | 0.751 | 0.745 | 0.45-0.70 | 0.45 | 70 / 89 |

- u1's convolution reach ends at r ~ 56-60 cells (the theoretical 51.5 + the block), +-230 voxels of a 1024 window: the outer
  ~40% of each axis never sees the window's centre and vice versa.
- In trained u1 the whole-window GroupNorm coupling is larger than the convolution signal: a 16^3-voxel change moves every logit of
  the window by 58% of the change at the block itself, flat to the corners. This is the window dependence behind the seams
  (and why a window's outputs change with its extent); EMA GroupNorm removes it by construction.
- The 92 M net covers the whole window by convolution + attention alone (frozen: 47% of the centre change at the corners, r 94
  at P 768); random-init ERFs are wider than trained ones, the trained number comes with the first snapshot.

**LR probe** (the 92 M net at P 512 B 1 on one card, from scratch on sources-scratch1.json, --det 1 seed 7 so every arm sees the
same windows, 300 steps, warmup 50, WSD cooldown 0.2, AdamW 1e-3, 0.60 samp/s): mean logged loss over steps 200-300 Muon 0.005
1.710, 0.01 1.719, 0.02 1.721 (per-head at 300 within 0.01 of each other); none unstable. 300 steps at B 1 do not separate the
arms (differences ~0.01, 5 logged points); the earlier voxel-net sweep (F1 0.307 / 0.296 / 0.290 at 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.05) stays the
basis: Muon 0.01, AdamW 1e-3, warmup 1000, WSD cooldown 0.2.

**fib-head + fstem** (1f881bf): `--fstem` refused `--fib-head` ("25 outputs (16 at most)"): the head pads past 16 outputs to 32
and the fine stem counted the 9 unsupervised pad channels. It now maps into the supervised voxel outputs only (phase 2, wind4 2,
ink 1, rv 2, fibre 9 = 16, the stem kernel's limit); test_fibhead_train covers --lat 4 --fstem 16 --ink-head 1 --fib-head 1.

**EMA GroupNorm at every site** (`--gn-ema 1`, unet_cfg.gn_ema; `--gn-ema-mom 0.01 --gn-ema-warm 500`): all GroupNorms (every level's
blocks, the down norms, the attention stage, the head's input) normalise with running statistics (BatchNorm-style, [mean | var] per
