group in the gn_sites layout; the first warm training forwards use their own statistics, after that training forwards are constants
in forward and backward, the backward without the statistics' terms, nn_set_gn_const; inference uses the running statistics as soon
as there are any). The sites hold the constants before the convs run (ge_begin), the convs write their live statistics to twins
(ge_dst) that ge_after pools into the running set after dec[0]; the EMA weights keep their own set (unet_ema), forwards with the
EMA weights (the SSL teacher) do not update. Checkpoints: header keys `gn_ema`, `ge_n`, `ge_warm`, `ge_mom`, `ge_run` only when on
(no new parameters: an old checkpoint loads into a gn_ema net as a fresh warm-up; u1-size net 448 floats, 31 KB header). Needs
`--l0-norm gn`. Multi-GPU data parallel: each card keeps its own statistics (card 0's are saved); with --split z the cards share one
window, so their statistics agree. Tests: test_gn_ema (both a down-norm net and an attention net: the warm-up then the running blend
at every site to 1e-4; a far-corner input change leaves the logits bit-identical, live GN moves them; momentum 1 reproduces live GN,
statistics 1e-7, logits 5e-3 of 6.2; EMA-weight set; checkpoint round trip bit-identical; old checkpoint = fresh warm-up; finite
backward), test_unet~GN_EMA=1 (fp32 finite differences with down norms: worst 7.5e-5 over 60 params; tensor cores vs fp32 logits
0.061 of 6.6). Train smoke (u1 widths, P 256, warm-up 10): losses continuous across the switch to constants.

**Per-scan input normalisation** (`--scan-norm 1`, unet_cfg.scan_norm, src/scannorm.c): the CT input is (v - center) / scale with one
(center, scale) per scan and level instead of each window's mean / sd: the mean and sd of the nonzero voxels in 48 boxes of 32^3 at
the working level, centred on nonzero voxels of a coarse level (the first of L + 2 .. L + 9 with <= 2^26 voxels read whole, else the
smallest subsampled every st-th voxel) at fixed ranks: a deterministic function of the volume. The sampler computes it on the first
window per (source, level) (a source's "norm" key wins; a failure keeps the window z-score, reported once); the checkpoint keeps
`"scan_norm":1`, and predict computes the same numbers for its scan and level (`--norm MEAN,SD` overrides). Mean / sd rather than
median / MAD: inside the mask the nonzero voxels are bimodal and the MAD follows the dominant mode only (1667 level 2: median 45,
1.4826 MAD 10.4, papyrus at ~+7; mean / sd 62.9 / 37.6). On the unissl sources all 22 (source, level) pairs get statistics (center
62.9-126, scale 28-56); predict on 1667 level 2 prints 62.9 / 37.59, the sampler's. test_scan_norm (wind fixture: deterministic
across runs, in the checkpoint, predict = sampler, --norm overrides, the losses change).

**Global-context FiLM** (`--gfilm 1`, unet_cfg.gfilm, branch gfilm-20261113): the user asked for an effective field of the whole 1024^3
window by construction. The 4 full-attention blocks on the 8^3 bottleneck give every token all 512; to carry that context to every decoder
level (not only up through the 288-channel deep levels), the attention stage's output tokens are averaged into g (K = the bottleneck width)
and every decoder block's output GroupNorm affine becomes gamma (1 + A_l g), beta + B_l g, composed after --film's (the forward weight
copy). A / B zero-initialised (logits bit-identical to the net without it), appended last (old checkpoints load), B 1. Cost for the
target net: 2 x 288 x (448 + 384 + 320 + 256 + 288) = 0.98 M params (+1.1%), < 1 MB activations, a few small kernels. Backward: in
the attention stage's backward (the decoders' norm gradients complete) dA / dB, the pre-gfilm affine's gradient, and dg; under --split
unet_set_gfilm_reduce sums the split decoder levels' dg share across the cards (the whole-window levels >= split_top counted once, their
A / B gradients de-duplicated on side 1). The token path (dg / S into every token's gradient) is OFF by default (UFSM_GFILM_TOKGRAD=1):
its directional check is 9% off (analytic -415 vs central differences -455 with the code frozen vs recomputed; the plain net's own
16-bit FD noise is ~6%, and attention needs the tensor-core path, so no fp32 check yet). Without it A / B still learn; the attention
is trained by the decoder path. test_gfilm: zero-init bit-identical, A / B directional derivative 0.17% (step 0.05), checkpoint round
trip bit-identical; the token check reported (GF_TOKCHECK enforces it).

Found on the way (not fixed here): with the scratch1 sources at P 1024 on one card an early `inkfly gpu: out of device memory`
falls back to the CPU and then segfaults in nn_ink_bits (cudaMemcpyAsync of an invalid host pointer, lab_upload kind 3); and
the scratch1 data path holds ~7 GB of device memory outside the planner at P 512.

## The universal net's eval: label-free quality on unseen scrolls, validated against GT (2026-11-12, branch univ-eval-20261111)

The from-scratch universal net trains on every label we have (user: "train on literally everything we have labels for ... then working
on unseen scrolls from the corpus"), so its main eval cannot use labels. `scripts/univ/ueval.sh` has two blocks: **unseen** (24 boxes of
512^3 level-0 voxels, 3 per scan on 9 corpus scans with no labels and no fits of ours: 0268, 0800, 0826, 0175B, 0306B, 0483A, 0490A,
0846A, 0343 at 8.64 / 9.36 um, placed CPU-side by `unseen_boxes.py` from the level-4 CT and the corpus axis) scored label-free by
`uqa.py` + the fibre judge; and **training-fit** (wbench core, rv eval, the 34 ink crops, the P4 fibre box: all in training now, so they
track convergence and head interference, not generalisation). `upair.py` pairs two checkpoints over the boxes.

The winding metrics come from the box's fit (fit-phase-box: frac(W) on a step-2 grid) and the CT. The wraps (W = integer) sit ~0.1-0.15
turn off the CT sheet centre on the wbench fits (C18: CT mean peaks at frac W 0.10-0.15, 85 vs 57 at 0.6), so each box's sheet phase
phi is measured (first harmonic of CT along frac W) and the band / gap / rv sides are taken relative to it; h1 = that harmonic's
amplitude / CT sd.

Validation (`uqa_validate.py`, CPU only): the metrics on the kept wbench fits of 6 checkpoints (unified-1504-a0e, inkpod-5000 / 10000,
unissl-6000, u1-13790-ssl, lat-vc384-4000-384) x 44 core boxes against the boxes' GT. "pooled" = Spearman over all 264 (tag, box)
pairs (mostly box difficulty); "within" = mean per-box Spearman across the 6 tags; "pairs" = share of same-box tag pairs (|d GT| >=
0.02) whose metric difference has the GT difference's sign, oriented by the metric's better side (0.5 = no information).

| metric | pooled vs p05x | within vs p05x | pairs vs p05x | pairs vs ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| jumps (W steps > 0.25 turn, lower) | +0.79 | +0.41 | **0.77** | 0.60 |
| gap_void (mid-gap voxels off papyrus) | +0.78 | +0.20 | 0.64 | 0.50 |
| on_pap (band voxels on papyrus) | -0.47 | +0.22 | 0.63 | 0.50 |
| h1 | +0.84 | +0.17 | 0.61 | 0.49 |
| contrast | +0.85 | +0.16 | 0.61 | 0.49 |
| nrm30 | -0.02 | +0.16 | 0.59 | 0.46 |
| sp_cv | -0.72 | -0.07 | 0.49 | 0.45 |
| nrm_deg (lower assumed better) | -0.87 | -0.38 | 0.25 | 0.38 |

Winding jumps are the one metric that ranks checkpoints on the same box like the GT does (0.77 of pairs vs p05x); the CT-alignment
metrics (h1, gap_void, on_pap, contrast) carry a weak signal (0.61-0.64) and none vs ids; nrm_deg is inverted (smoother normals go with
worse fits: over-smoothing), sp_cv carries nothing. Tiers in `upair.py`: primary jumps, secondary h1 / gap_void / on_pap / contrast,
info nrm_deg / sp_cv / nrm30 (no win count). Check on a known pair: inkpod-10000 vs unified-1504-a0e (GT p05x -0.048 [-0.068, -0.028]):
jumps +0.0039 [+0.0014, +0.0066] (worse on 30 / 44 boxes, agrees); h1 / gap_void / contrast slightly better (disagree), so a checkpoint
call rests on jumps first. Not validated yet: rv_agree, ink_air / ink_band, the fibre judge and the fit residuals (the kept fits have no
head predictions); the first GPU run of ueval on two checkpoints with wbench rows will validate them the same way.

## Latent ink head: window seams at inference, the 2-pass grid blend, 1667 scores (2026-11-12, scripts/inkgt/u1667ink.sh)

The inkpod snapshots' ink head (`predict --heads ink`, latent trunk, 4 levels) gives every predict window its own level: the 1299
inkpod-9000 renders showed a square tile grid. Measured in the raw store on a fixed 1299 corner (level 2, box 5632,2048,2048 + 1024^3,
the plane-mean step across the window seam / the median plane step, z / y / x; sched/seam/seam.tsv):

| run | halo 16 | halo 64 | halo 96 |
|---|---|---|---|
| inkpod-9000 (--ink-dice 0.25) | 2.6 / 7.2 / 30.2 | 2.0 / 27.1 / 4.9 | 1.6 / 27.5 / 13.6 |
| inkpod-11000 (dice off) | 1.4 / 15.3 / 29.5 | 2.4 / 30.3 / 12.1 | 2.6 / 23.8 / 16.1 |
| inkpod-12000 (dice off, --ink-air 8, ink share 40%) | 0.4 / 15.4 / 26.6 | | |

(median plane steps 0.07-0.5; ift3 on the same box: no step.) Window 1024 / halo 256 still 10-14; `--gn-frozen` (fresh pooled
statistics) moves the levels, not the steps; level 1 (4.8 um, the crop eval's level) 5.2 / 13.2 / 3.8. No attention stage, constant
FiLM code. Turning the per-window dice off did NOT remove the steps (11000 / 12000 as large as 9000), so the head's level depends on
context wider than 256 voxels for another reason (receptive field of the stride-4 trunk; ink never supervised in air, ~60 / 255 there).

Fix at inference: two passes, the second on a tile grid shifted by half a tile (`--grid-origin 256,256,256`), blended with sin^2 tile
weights (`ufsm ink-blend --tile 512 --grids 0,0,0:256,256,256`): on a 512^3 read across the corner the largest plane step drops from
16.9 to 1.3 (median 0.1). The shifted pass must use `--shard 256`: with 512 shards every shard needs 8 windows (P4 inner 17405 windows
vs 2311, 7.5x); with 256 shards the output is byte-identical (1299 test box) in 5 s instead of 63 s. Papyrus gate for renders only:
the same `--heads ink,c12,c13` run gives the recto / verso probabilities, gated = ink x max(c12, c13) on the rendered stripes; the
store and the scores stay ungated.

1667 u1 centre surface, inkpod-9000 blended, vs the published human labels (wrapscore, 40 um; ift3-24000 beside):

| split | coverage | inkpod-9000 ink AUC | ift3-24000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| all | 0.860 | 0.774 | 0.646 |
| validation | 0.827 | 0.528 | 0.670 |
| holdout | 0.864 | 0.560 | 0.639 |
| rest (in the ink training labels) | 0.864 | 0.832 | 0.643 |

The "all" gain is the training labels: on the unseen splits the latent head is below ift3 (-0.14 / -0.08). 20 / 80 um all: 0.776 /
0.776 (coverage 0.615 / 0.971). wrapscore: the foot-point refine's 2x2 solve is closed-form (np.linalg.solve raised on P4's grid holes).

## The 1667 unroll's ink against the human labels on our surfaces (2026-11-12, scripts/inkgt/wrapscore.py)

`ufsm ink-compare`, which the earlier unrolls ran, is label-free (CT | ink panels and statistics). wrapscore.py maps the published
labels onto our flattened stripes:
1. It samples every 8th label px of the 6 published PHerc1667 segments inside their supervision (7.79 M samples, ink 0.24) and takes
   each sample's 3-D point on the published mesh.
2. It finds the nearest vertex of our stripes (x 4 to level 0), then the foot point on that bilinear patch. The distance is the miss.
3. Within a tolerance, it reads the stripe's ink and CT renders (strip-mosaic <s>_ink.jpg / <s>_ct.jpg) at the render pixel
   (render px = grid / scale, render_core.h).

Coverage scores the surfaces. AUC and best F1 are rank-based, so the mosaic stretch doesn't change them.

Check: a published segment through a half-resolution re-grid of itself in 9.6 um voxels, with a half-size map, gives AUC 0.978 for a
perfect map (miss median 0.2 um).

u1 unroll (ift3-24000 ink, out of sample on 1667), 40 um, all samples:

| render set | coverage | median miss | ink AUC (20 / 80 um) | ink best F1 | CT AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| centre, depth 1 + fill | 0.860 | 15.1 um | 0.646 (0.645 / 0.648) | 0.435 | 0.540 |
| centre, thin +-2 | 0.860 | 15.1 um | 0.646 | 0.434 | 0.540 |
| recto face (1.5 voxels toward the axis) fill / thin | 0.848 | 16.6 um | 0.648 / 0.647 | 0.437 | 0.535 |
| verso face (1.5 voxels away from the axis) fill / thin | 0.795 | 22.4 um | 0.643 / 0.643 | 0.431 | 0.526 |

- Coverage at 20 / 80 um (centre): 0.615 / 0.971.
- The validation split runs 0.01-0.035 higher, the ink holdout boxes about 0.01 lower.
- Sign (settled 11-14, audit #20): the recto is the face toward the scroll axis. `rvside.sh` moves wraps_snap by `tifxyz-scale --normal
  +1.5 --toward AXIS` (+n oriented toward the axis), so its logs say +1.5 for wraps_in_recto and -1.5 for wraps_out_verso; this table
  earlier wrote the same shifts as -1.5 / +1.5 along the outward radius. The pub1667 comparison agrees: the published (recto) surface
  lies 4 um inward of our centre surface at the median.
- The face shift and the thin band move the ink AUC by <= 0.005. The limit is the ink model, not the render. The published meshes lie
  slightly to the recto side of our centre surface.

## Pod whole-scroll unroll queue: two lanes per card, axis check, latent ink stage (2026-11-12/13, branch podunroll-20261112)

Pod 3 (one RTX PRO 6000, 98 GB; cgroup 94 GB / 27.2 CPUs), u1-13750, RECTOSP=0, the user's smallest-first list. 13 scrolls landed
on the desk before the user cancelled the queue (01:xx 11-13): 0332, MAN5, 0009B, MANB, 0814, 1203, 0358, 1451, 0813, 0846B, 0257,
0490B, 0483B (renders in /vesuvius/ufsm/unroll/<S>-u1; logs in /vesuvius/ufsm/v2/lat/runs/podsave-20261112/pod3).
On papyrus 0.60-0.85, wrap-check dup 0-17 % (MAN5 27 %). The fields took 36-586 s and the slabs 118-1979 s per scroll.

- `scripts/pod/q.sh LANE`: 2 lanes share the card (FITLANES 2, TH 13 each); a lane claims the next scroll (flock), fetches its CT from
  the mirror (setup.sh step 6), uses the corpus box / axis (kit/S/{box.txt,axis.json}), runs pod/unroll.sh. After the 00:24 disk-full
  (500 / 500 GB, a lane spun on a failed setup because its claim file could not be written): a claim counts only when written, a failed
  setup marks the scroll failed and backs off 60 s, lanes wait below 60 GB free, rc 0 without stripimg.done is a failure.
- `scripts/pod/podpull.sh` (desk): each scroll's overview / strip_long / one ct+ink stripe / logs as soon as stripimg lands
  (temp name + rename), a sanity FLAG (on-papyrus < 0.5 or dup share > 30 %), then trims the pod (strip mesh, ink, ref-cf, CT copy).
- pod/unroll.sh: per-scroll helper dir (drv/S: two lanes' starts swapped scrolls.tsv otherwise); `INKW=576` (an auto ink window took
  1600^3 / 90 GB of a free card and spilled the other lane's fits to managed memory, ink 2 -> 260 s per window; see the winauto section).
- Axis check (`scripts/pod/axcheck.{sh,py}`, hooked into pod/unroll.sh before the run starts): the corpus axis vs the papyrus centroid
  (Otsu on level LV+3, per-z centroid, running median +-2048 L0 voxels) at 10/30/50/70/90 % of the papyrus height; off = the median of
  the 30/50/70 % offsets > 2 mm, or no papyrus within 1 mm at 50 % -> axis_centroid.json. "Any level > 2 mm" was too strict: the ends
  are tapered caps and the umbilicus is not the mass centroid (0009B 5.9 / 1.1 / 3.4 / 0.7 / 7.8 mm and 0814 3.6 / 1.3 / 0.3 / 0.6 /
  1.9 mm unrolled well on their corpus axes). PHercMANB (crushed, lens-shaped; corpus axis 3-10 mm off, median 4.1 mm): on papyrus
  0.369 -> 0.628 and dup 30 % -> 17 % with the centroid axis.
- Latent ink stage (`scripts/pod/latink.sh` as INKCMD; user 11-13 "forget about ift3"): inkB's recipe, predict --heads ink,c12,c13
  (inkpod-9000) at the run's level, window 544 halo 16, grids 0 and 256 (the 256 pass on --shard 256: on 512 shards each shard
  overlapped 8 shifted windows, ~7x the windows), ink-blend per head. strip_refill.sh (INKGATE) gates every stripe's ink render by
  max(p_recto, p_verso) and takes the contrast stretch from the gated middle stripes (ink percentiles over papyrus pixels, CT >= 80).
  Only 0841 / 0846A ran it before the cancel (0846A ink 1621 s incl. the rerun of its grid 256); no landed scroll has latent ink.

## Split-window input builders: every --gpu-aug builder by z range, the scanner split exactly across two GPUs (2026-11-13, branch augz-20261112)

For the 40 M net (widths 192..384), one P 1024 window is split in z across both 5060 Tis (univI's splitwin-20261112). Each GPU then
builds only its own output planes of the window's input and labels. The window stays the global P^3: the same record, draws and
global coordinates, so a rank's planes are byte for byte the whole-window call's planes.

- **Labels** (nn_label_warp_z / nn_label_sym_z / nn_w4runs_label_z / nn_ink_bits_z) write output planes [z0, z0 + nz) from source
  planes [s0, s1) only.
  - nn_aug_src_range(rad, P, z0, nz) bounds [s0, s1). The warp's source z is linear in the per-axis displaced coordinates (rotation,
    zoom, affine, symmetry; elastic is per-axis tables), so its extremes are at the corners of the box of their ranges. Measured: the
    bound is at most 4 planes wider than the corners actually read, over 12 cases.
  - Under rotation the source range is ~nz cos + P sin. At P 256 the 40 / 72 range at 30 degrees staged 3.56 nz. So the staging does
    not halve under rotation: budget ~P planes of 8-bit staging per GPU (1 GB at P 1024).
  - nn_w4runs_apply_z: the runs are per x row, so a z range needs no plane outside it (strip offsets into the run table).
- **CT channel** (nn_aug_ct_z): the scanner ops need the whole source window. Paganin's two-sided exponential and the correlated
  noise recurse along z, GIN / histogram / z-score use whole-window statistics, and the z blur reads taps. With a zcomm (two ranks),
  rank r scans its source half and exchanges:
  - the halo planes, as they are before each stencil (the z blur's reach from the plan, GIN's 1, a dropped slice's source);
  - the correlated noise's carried plane (rank 0 -> 1);
  - paganin's carried y per line: forward 0 -> 1, then rank 1's backward from P - 2, then 1 -> 0;
  - the statistics: integer sums exact, GIN's two doubles as two partial atomic sums, which are order-free anyway;
  - finally, the scanned 8-bit planes each rank's warp reads from the other.
  The fp16 work volume aliases the rank's CT channel planes, as the one-GPU path does, when P/2 + 2 halo <= nz.
  Per GPU at P 1024: CT channel 544 planes (1.14 GB) + staging <= 1 GB, against 2 + 2.23 GB for the whole window.
- **Tests** (tests/test_aug_z.c, gpu, 14 s at P 256):
  - every label builder over 4 ranges x 12 warp / symmetry cases, with poisoned host planes outside [s0, s1) and a poisoned staging
    buffer;
  - the CT channel for the 22 scanner ops alone at two strengths, a mixture and none (44 cases) x 2 range pairs: the one-GPU range
    and both split ranks, through a loopback zcomm (two host threads, one GPU, a staging slot each);
  - all byte-identical to the whole-window call. A negative control (the exchanges dropped) differs on every voxel.
  - test_gpu_aug is unchanged and passes.
- **Stored onfly codes are now dcached.** The key is the array path, zarr.json size / mtime and the poolings. Without it every read
  recomputed the pair rule (16-50 s per 512^3 window on the CPU). sources-scratch1 v3 reads june / 0139 / 0500P2 / 1667-gt phase on
  the fly from their codes; phase-onfly against the stored rasters:
  - P4 june codesA 9.6 rmax 40: 0 differing voxels;
  - 0139 A+B fused rmax 41: 0 differing voxels;
  - 0500P2: native codes rebuilt, 0 differing voxels;
  - 1667 A+B 4.8 pooled: 10384 of 805 M voxels differ;
  - P4 july: the gtjuly codesB rebuild differs on 29%, because the 10-19 codes it came from are gone, so it keeps phaseB.
- Left to the split itself (univI): the zcomm over split.c's staged peer copies, the latent input from the CT channel, the
  label-stream slabs, MIL rays.

## inkpod: the ink training run on a rented RTX PRO 6000; --ink-dice 0 from step 10036 (2026-11-12 / 13, branch inkpod2-20261113)

The unified run's ink head moved off the desk (user, 11-12: "do ink detection training on the rtx6000"). inkpod = the unified run's
flags (`--lat 4`, P 1024, B 1, `--ink-head 1 --ink-mil 1 --ink-smooth 0.1`, um-rungs 4.8,9.6:2,19.2, ...), init by head from the desk
unified run's step 1504, master a0eecbb, then a5520d5 from pod step ~1050. Pod: 96 GB card, 27 CPUs, cgroup memory 94 GB (`free` shows 755),
500 GB disk, glibc 2.39 (desk binaries need 2.43: built on the pod).

- Data. The desk uplink is 4.2 MB/s (2 GB in 480 s over 4 streams), so the ~220 GB label set was rebuilt on the pod where public:
  Paris 4 codes A / B / A48 and phase A (scripts/pod/p4kit.sh from the published June / July meshes; codesB 4 min and codesA48 9 min
  at full memory), PHerc0139 phase (k0139.sh: 17,035,432,659 known voxels, the desk's count exactly). Shipped: the ink GT (1.6 GB), 1667
  GT (20 GB, 1.5 h), 0500P2 phase, axes / holdouts. Paris 4 phase B (57 GB) did not fit beside the local CT: july is out of the pod sources.
- CT over HTTP from the volcomp mirror: 90-113 Mvox/s at 91-92 % loader wait (latency-bound reads). `ufsm mirror` copies at 250-400 MB/s
  (Paris 4 level 3, 12 GB, in 30 s): levels 1-5 of Paris 4 / 1667 / 0009B / MAN5 and 0139 / 0500P2 9.362 local (~235 GB), 0139 2.399 and
  0814 on HTTP + cache. Mirror CT groups need the desk's zarr.json (absolute-um scales).
- Host memory. The trainer alone peaks at ~83 GB at W6 / S6 (pinned slots 3.36 GB each, a worker ~2.2 GB); five cgroup OOM kills while
  settling. Fix: the container's cgroup root split into `main` (the trainer) and `kit` (memory.max 6G) so a label build can never make the
  OOM killer pick the trainer; rasters that need more run in a stopped-trainer window.
- The loader bottleneck was the slot count, not the workers: W5 and W8 at S4 both ran 310-430 Mvox/s at 64-73 % wait (per-thread /proc
  samples: 3 of 8 workers idle on a futex for 40 / 40 s, the others ~0.6 core), because each window holds its slot through its 3 replays.
  W5 / S7: 650-850 Mvox/s at 17-38 % wait (2.5-3.8x the desk's 226 Mvox/s), anon + shmem ~67 GB.
- Stage 2 (pod step 2010): the winding / rv sources back at 50 % of the source weight, ink 50 % (mix lines 52-54 % ink windows).
- The window-level dice. inkB found per-window ink level steps in inkpod-9000 whole-scroll predicts (5-30 / 255 across seams, 10-14 even
  at halo 256; GN frozen stats do not remove them; ift3 has none; ~60 / 255 in air). From the training side: `--ink-dice 0.25` adds a soft
  dice per window over its known voxels, normalised by the window's own ink sum (a per-window gain prior); MIL is local (per ray, +/- 10
  voxels along the face normal); ink trains at 4.8 and 9.6 (so 9.6 inference is in distribution); the ink targets label only papyrus on a
  labelled face band, so air is never supervised. inkpod restarted at step 10036 with `--ink-dice 0` (the dice version kept as
  inkpod-pre-nodice.ckpt). To measure: inkB's seam steps on the same 1299 box at +1000 / +2000, latres's 34-crop ink AUC for the cost.
  Next candidate: `--ink-air W` (air voxels of ink windows -> ink 0 at a small subsampled weight).

## predict --window auto on a shared card: UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB budget, interior cap 1024 (2026-11-12, branch winauto-20261112)

Pod 3 (one RTX PRO 6000, 98 GB), two unroll lanes: PHerc0814's ink pass (`--window auto`, feathered, halo 32) started on a nearly
free card and picked 1600^3 (interior 1536), holding 90.4 GB of device memory. The other lane's slab fits (PHercMANB) dropped to
602 MB of device each (managed-memory spill) and 0814's count-field to 1.7 GB; the ink itself slowed from ~2 s to ~260 s per window
(149 windows: ~10 h). Killing it brought the fits back to ~6 GB and seconds per slab; the rerun at 576^3 did 2293 windows at ~10 / s.

Change (`src/winauto.h`, used by predict.c; host-only test `test_winauto`):
- the budget is the device's free memory capped by `UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB` (the variable train's planner already reads), so a job
  sharing a card can be given its share; `UFSM_PRED_WINDOW_FREE` (planning for another card) still replaces the device figure and
  is capped the same way;
- candidates with an interior (window - 2 halo) above `UFSM_PRED_WINDOW_MAX` (default 1024) are never picked. That drops only the
  ink's 1600^3 (1.13 computed voxels per interior voxel; 1088^3 is 1.20, ~6 % more compute) and keeps the fields' 1152^3 (interior
  1024). Candidate 0 with copy slabs stays the always-fits fallback; the log line now prints the budget and the cap.
- pods: scripts/pod/unroll.sh on pod 3 also pins `INKW=576` (two lanes per card); with this change `--window auto` plus
  `UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB=<share>` does the same without a fixed window.

## The post-slab chain faster, same bytes: wraps, snap, join, stripimg (2026-11-12, branch postperf-20261112)

The unroll's chain after the slab fits (scripts/unroll/unroll.sh: join, check, wraps, trim, snap, strip, stripflat, stripimg) on the
Paris 4 u1 run took 2147 s: join 148, check 6, wraps 315, trim 19, snap 584, strip 58, stripflat 414 (GPU), stripimg 603 (GPU). All
changes below give byte-identical outputs (checked file by file against the u1 runs of Paris 4 and 1667; deterministic stages only).
CPU numbers at 8 threads on the loaded desk (the runs had 20).

**wraps** (97% of its time in the root search along each ray, fp64 W evaluations). Counted on a 500-row band of Paris 4: 12.9e9
evaluations, of which 69% for rays that keep no vertex: their first crossing ring lies outside the data bounds [ua, ub] (50 M rays, 129
evaluations each) or there is no crossing at all (13 M rays, 189 each). The ring scan steps dr = pitch / 4 from the hint on both sides and
only needs a side's value where its class (sign of W - k, and the side's stop at +-2) can change. A local Lipschitz bound of W along the ray
(1 / pitch + |sin| gy + |cos| gx, gy / gx the largest lattice node differences per voxel over the 3 x 3 tiles of 8 x 8 cells around the
point, per lattice z cell; fit_lip) gives a radius in which the class cannot change; those steps are not evaluated, and where a crossing
interval starts at a skipped point its value is evaluated there (the same point: the same bits). Every ring, crossing interval and
Illinois iteration is the full scan's: the same roots. A single per-plane bound was useless (outlier nodes: max 10 turns / voxel against a
median of 0.01). Evaluations 12.9e9 -> 3.0e9 (no-vertex rays 129 / 189 -> 11 / 10 each, found roots 15 -> 9). Radii are only asked for when
one could reach the next step. Idle workers now help with the rows of the tail's large wraps (each wrap's rows were on one thread).
Paris 4 whole run: 695 -> 228 s wall, 5375 -> 2177 CPU s, 191 .sfc identical; 1667: 29.1 -> 24.1 s. test_wraps_core: the skipped scan vs
the full one on 19200 random rays of a 3-slab set with outlier nodes, 0 differ (a bound 20x too tight: 1522 differ). What is left: the root
search ~45%, the .sfc encoder ~26% (the same codec is most of strip's 58 s and of snap's write), the w plane decode ~9%.

**snap** (wrap-snap: evidence along each vertex's ray, then per-wrap solves). Only the wraps the strip keeps are snapped now (trim's
--first / --last into wrap-snap; the ids just outside are still read as the neighbours that bound them, so the kept wraps are unchanged:
19% of Paris 4's vertices, 15% of 1667's not snapped). The evidence: trilinear lookups with one chunk lookup for the 8 corners and shifts
for the power-of-two chunks (they did 3 int64 divisions + 3 modulos per corner), the phase of --target mix only at candidate maxima (it was
every profile sample: half of all lookups), the per-vertex getenv out, box filters 8 lines at once (a column pass read 1 float of 16 per
cache line), only the marked volcomp substreams (16 z x 32 y slabs) of each chunk decoded, and the CT mask scan along a ray skipped where
its voxels lie in held substreams without a 0. Paris 4 wraps 300..320 (21 snapped, 237 M vertices, the run's .sfc identical): 148.5 ->
85.3 s, 1169 -> 651 CPU s (evidence 130 -> 68 s, of which the volcomp decode 36 -> 30 s); 1667 all: 71.8 -> 40.8 s (with --last 39). The
decode is now ~45% of the CPU: unroll.sh SNAPGPU (default: the first FITGPUS GPU that is not INKGPU, idle after the slabs) runs it on the
GPU decoder (UFSM_GPU_DECODE, byte-identical), to be measured in a GPU window (scripts/unroll/postperf_gpu.sh).

**join** (fit-join): the field blocks recycled their planes (the page faults and zeroing of a fresh 2.5 GB block per 128 rows were 257 of
723 CPU s), the overlap / ref cell sampling without a 64-bit division per material cell (masks of 64 cells, AVX-512 + pdep), the next
block loaded on a thread while the current block's tasks sample (3 slots, +1 block of RAM). Paris 4: 216 -> 131 s, 723 -> 513 CPU s (the
recycling and the sampling; the prefetch measured on 1667 only: 20.5 -> 14.5 s); joined/ identical. UFSM_JOIN_TIMES prints the parts.

**stripimg**: the stretch's 3 middle stripe renders ran one after another (Paris 4 3 x 28 s, 1667 26 + 15 + 10 s); now at once (SJOBS:
3 with >= 72 GB available, 2 with >= 48; each ~21 GB RSS and a 4 GB device pool on Paris 4). Independent renders: the same images, to be
confirmed in a GPU window (postperf_gpu.sh compares both schedules' files, the run's fill maps and stretch). The 19 other renders ran
with RJOBS 1 on Paris 4 (RJOBS 2 needs 64 GB available); each is ~25 s, half of it CPU (grids 4.5, fill 3.6, writes 4.5 s).

Not changed: stripflat (414 s, GPU SLIM per chunk, its job count tuned 2026-10 on 0490B), check (6 s), trim (19 s), strip (58 s: the .sfc
encode of the whole strip at 19 cores; the codec is the next lever for wraps, snap and strip together, ~2000 CPU s on Paris 4).

## Slab fits over the material only: fit --crop-material (2026-11-12, branch slabperf-20261112)

A P4 slab fit (unroll.sh lane: 96 x 3575 x 3712 cells, 12.7 GB of fields) did not fit the 16 GB card and ran from managed memory: 17-19 s
per slab, 149 slabs on 2 lanes = 1365 s (s070: load 4.5 s, phase gate 4.1, stages 0-3 1.0, unwrap 1.0 + 1.7 + 1.2, stage 4 4.6, stage 5
1.6). Most of the cross-section holds no papyrus: the y / x bounds of w != 0 over a slab's rows cover 0.52 of it (s070: y [128, 2544) x [672,
3520), 6.6 GB of fields; the chunk-level bounds over all 74 z chunk rows: 0.52 on average, 0.1 near the ends).

`fit --crop-material M` reads the box's w plane (once; the loader reuses it), takes those bounds grown by M cells, rounded out to 16 cells
(a multiple of every pooling factor and of uw_refbias's 4-cell sampling), and loads only those cells of every plane (`fit_fields_crop`;
zarr / raw). Nothing else changes: `fit_fields` / `fit_dev` carry the crop (oy ox H0 W0) and every position is the box cell's, the lattice,
knots and model are the box's, and the minibatch hash reads the box cell's linear index (`fit_box_index`; the GPU's inverse-hash
selection maps candidate box cells into the crop, `fit_crop_index`), the prior samples the box's index sequence, the pooled stages see
the same pooled cells (crop edges on pool multiples or the box edge), the counts are equal (outside cells hold no material), the phase
gate's W_ref grid starts at the crop's box position (exact sums: integer cells x integer h). The phase gate reads +-1 neighbours and its
box sums are 0 outside material, so M >= 1 keeps it exact (default 2). The model is byte-identical to the uncropped fit.

Verified on the CPU backend (the same terms: src/fit_terms.h) with the slab lane's options: P4 boxes 48x900x900 (crop 0.583, offsets in y
and x, ends at the box), 40x1875x1012 (0.406, interior ends), 96x1800x1900 (0.600): delta.f32 / model.json identical to the uncropped fit and
to the base binary; the CPU fit of the last 33.0 -> 18.4 s (gate 14.4 -> 9.1, unwrap 3.7 -> 1.7, stages 0-3 5.4 -> 1.9, 4-5 11.4 -> 5.8).
test_fit's crop case: host fields on both backends, streamed loads + stream verify on the GPU. Options whose code reads the box's arrays
otherwise (repair, two-level / msf floods, pdv, phase stretch, bend, pgrad, CT terms, fibres, emb, seed / init models, --winding / --codes
exports) turn the crop off (logged). The GPU parts (stream loader, nn_fit_loss2's selection, the GPU gate) await a GPU window:
scripts/unroll/slabperf_gpu.sh (tests, BASE / nocrop / crop / hostw / stream-verify identity on P4 s010 s070 s140 + 1667 s030, lanes).

Also: the GPU phase gate keeps W_ref on the device (`fit_set_grid_dev`: no device -> host -> device trip of 4 B per cell per block,
the scratch kept across the 16M-cell blocks; UFSM_PG_HOSTW=1 the old path), and unroll.sh's FITLOCK=1 / 2 (UFSM_FIT_GPU_LOCK, + LOCK_LATE:
the normals decoded to the host before the lock) for FITLANES=2 on one card. unroll.sh passes --crop-material $CROPM (2; 0 off).

## Self-supervision for the latent net: what the 10-21..25 DINO work showed, the plan (2026-11-12, branch latdino-20261112)

User (11-12): "revive the self supervised dino stuff for latent net". Plan only; no GPU run yet.

**What the old work (dino-train, 10-21..25; branches dino / dino-wip / dino-wip2, all merged into master) showed.** Its run
directories (/vesuvius/ufsm/dino, ~/ufsm-data/dino/runs) are gone, and no sheet-identity table (dinovol-eval, sslev.sh) was written
down, so the numbers below come from commit messages only:
- It was a separate network and trainer (a 6-level hybrid conv + attention U-Net, D 16-64 unit embeddings, `--recipe 1` = the
  upstream dinovol multi-crop DINO + iBOT with 32768 prototypes). It was never connected to a winding net and never measured on
  wbench. Its only downstream use, `fit --emb` (votes from the embedding in the slip repair), was measured on a synthetic spiral
  only (0.9707 -> 1.0000 ids).
- It was unstable. The iBOT token norm ran away (|mean| 60) and the student collapsed (fix: a parameter-free LayerNorm). Then came
  a stack of anti-collapse terms: a token variance hinge (`--ssl-ibot-zvar 10`), mean-prototype removal, a learnable logit scale,
  SIGReg, and an embedding spread hinge (`--var 30`). DESIGN notes that SupCon collapse is a stationary point.
- It was slow on the desk: the 4-level gate net took 10.5 s/step at P384.
- The pseudo-label SupCon contradicted itself. The wind96 pseudo codes are gauge-consistent per ~128^3 (0.83-0.94) but only 0.64
  box-wide, so P512 windows got contradictory long-range pairs, and the desk full run's GT SupCon loss stayed flat at 8.1 (the fix
  was a pair radius and a radial limit). On 10-24 full.sh turned DINO / iBOT / the SSL batch off by default ("DINO / SSL nixed"):
  pseudo labels + GT SupCon only. On 10-25 the work moved on to selftrain (stored-phase pseudo labels) and `train --distill`
  (dinovol PCA-64 targets). From 11-09 the latent net replaced all of it.
- So SSL was never shown to help or to hurt a winding net. It stalled on collapse and speed in a separate network, before the
  question was asked.

**Recommendation: (b), an auxiliary masked self-distillation term inside the latent trainer on unlabelled windows.**
- u1 learns from 5 scans (Paris 4, 0139, 0500P2, 1667; 8 sources). /vesuvius/ufsm/v2/ct holds 34. Under (b) the trunk sees every
  scroll, at no cost to the production schedule, and the supervised heads anchor the trunk against collapse (the 10-23 failure was
  SSL alone).
- (a), SSL pretraining and then a finetune, needs a separate multi-day run of both desk GPUs, which we do not have. Literature and
  our own history agree that SSL pretraining gains shrink once the supervised finetune is long (u1: 16k steps).
- (c), SupCon on labelled voxels, uses no unlabelled CT. The wind4 head is already a gauge-free sheet-identity loss on the same
  voxels, and SupCon is where the pseudo-pair contradictions came from.

**Loss (data2vec / iBOT in the latent cell grid).**
- Two views of one CT window, with the same geometry (cells align one to one, so no crop -> source mapping). They differ in the
  GPU appearance augmentation (ct / scan augment seeds) and the latc quantisation step (the `--lat-step-jitter` range, i.e.
  invariance to the 20x compression standard).
- The teacher is the EMA weights (`unet_use_ema`) running a forward pass on view A.
- The student sees view B with a share r of the latent input cells masked in 2^3-cell blocks (latc channels zeroed; the radial
  channels kept).
- The target is a 1^3 side head of D 16 channels on decoder level 1 (76.8 um cells, width 128), i.e. the existing distillation
  head (`cfg.emb_lev / emb_ch`, `side_head_bwd`). The teacher's outputs are unit-normalised and quantised to int8 x 127.
- The loss is `nn_distill_loss`'s cosine on the masked cells only (int8 zero = no target, already the convention), plus `dn_varreg`
  (the variance hinge from nn_dino.cu) on a 64k-cell sample of the student's head outputs.
- The full-resolution head slabs and label streams are skipped on these windows, and the task heads get no gradient from them.
- The fine stem does not reach level 1, so the voxel path cannot leak masked cells.

**Implemented (8fd3e66, 34e31e5).** Differences from the plan above:
- Unlabelled sources are the existing `"ct_only": 1` kind (the 10-25 distill plumbing), not a new "ssl" key. A GPU-free sampler-only
  run (unwrap2 --lat, P 256, 80 batches) drew windows from every one of the 37 generated volumes that had a local zarr.json, with phase
  known 0.000. The generator is `scripts/latdino/ssl-sources.sh` (PHerc0490B and PHercParis3 skipped: incomplete local copies). 0841
  has no held-out ink boxes in holdouts-ink.json yet (asked inkB).
- The mask zeroes the student's CT channel in 16^3-voxel blocks (`nn_ssl_mask`), before the latent cell transform, so the latc
  cells and the fine stem are hidden together. Each block is one 2^3 group of level-1 cells.
- The views differ by the mask and the latc quantiser step: the teacher uses the transform's own step, the student that step x
  2^(u --ssl-jit), u uniform in [-1, 1]. A second appearance augmentation is not yet in.
- Teacher targets are centred per window (the channel mean over the window's cells is subtracted) before the unit normalisation.
- The variance hinge runs on the unit rows of 64k cells through `dn_gather` / `dn_varreg` / `dn_scatter_grad` (nn_dino.cu), with
  gamma 1 / sqrt(D).
- Not yet done: unlabelled windows still run the full-resolution head slabs (with zero loss masks), and the planner does not count
  the side head and the ssl buffers (~0.3 GB at P 1024, D 16).
- Tests:
  - test_ssl: the mask in fp16 and fp32 against the host byte for byte; targets byte-identical; distinct sample indices; the
    whole loss and its gradient against double central differences.
  - test_heads (8): --ssl without a ct_only source logs exactly lat_plain's losses; with a ct_only copy at share 0.5, finite ssl
    terms and targeted shares of 10-75%; the header and a resume.
- GPU results (11-12, desk GPU 0, 5060 Ti):
  - test_ssl PASS: mask 0 bytes differ in fp16 and fp32 (24576 of 73728 voxels masked at ratio 0.4); targets 0 bytes differ (104
    of 240 cells); loss 0.843316 vs host 0.843315; gradient worst error 3.6e-9 of max 7.3e-3.
  - test_heads ok: the 7 old layouts log the reference losses, and (8) passes.
  - Fixture run (P 64, --ssl 8, share 0.5, 12 steps): 8 unlabelled windows. The targeted share equals the masked share of the CT
    channel on every check (34-47 % at mask 0.4). The ssl cosine falls 0.330 -> 0.130, the hinge 0.048 -> 0.027, and the
    per-dimension std of the unit rows stays 0.31-0.34 (gamma 0.354): no collapse at fixture scale. Labelled steps log their usual
    terms.
- Head-slab skip and planner (6a05337), checked on desk GPU 0 on 11-12:
  - test_heads ok, including (8c): with the skip the --det fixture run logs exactly the losses of the run with the slabs
    (UFSM_SSL_SLABS=1).
  - Planner, UFSM_MEM_DRY at P 1024 with the unified run's flags (--ink-dice dropped: not on this branch's base), UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB 14:
    without --ssl, mode 4 (lean 2) 11.43 GB; with --ssl 16 --ssl-share 0.25 (35 unlabelled sources = 25.0 % of the weight), the same
    mode, 11.78 GB. The +0.35 GB is network +0.13 (the side head's outputs and parameters in the dry build) + task +0.20 (targets,
    gradient, hinge points, margin) + workspace +0.01. 2.2 GB stay free on a 14 GB budget.
- `--ssl-ink W [--ssl-ink-conf C (0.3) --ssl-ink-pap 0|1 (1)]` (stage 2, written 11-12 CPU-side, GPU tests pending):
  - The EMA teacher's coarse head runs per chunk of cell planes (`unet_head_fwd_z` on its live dec[0], streamed latent head only).
    Its ink channel becomes per-cell targets round(254 p) at the cells the student sees (not in a masked block), where the teacher
    is confident (|p - 0.5| >= C) and, with --rv 2, on its papyrus (max of the rv pair's sigmoids >= 0.5); 255 = none
    (`nn_ssl_ink_targets`).
  - In the head-slab skip of an unlabelled window, the student's own coarse ink logits (the same chunks) give the soft-BCE
    gradient W x gs / N (sigmoid(z) - p_t) on the ink channel of the head's 16-bit input planes (`nn_ssl_ink_grad`, N = the gated
    cells), and the other channels stay zero.
  - Cell level only: no full-resolution slabs, and the fine stem's ink part is absent on both sides.
  - Logged as `ink-ssl L (gated % of the cells, ink % of the gated)`.
  - test_ssl (5): targets and gradient against the host. test_heads (8e): a fixture run with the ink head.
  - Not with UFSM_SSL_SLABS=1 (the term rides on the skip path).
- `--ssl-heads LIST` (11-12, user: "can we dino for all things the universal model supports"; c8eaa09) generalises `--ssl-ink` to
  every head that a self-trained target can be checked for. `--ssl-ink W` is now `ink:W`, and its log marker is ` ssl-ink`.
  - The same mechanism: the teacher's coarse head per chunk of cell planes, targets round(254 p) per enabled channel and cell
    (255 = none) at the cells the student sees, the student's soft BCE on its own coarse logits in the skip path. One target
    kernel and one gradient kernel over a per-head spec (`nn_sslh_targets` / `nn_sslh_grad`, ssl.h), replacing the ink pair.
  - Gates per head (thresholds are flags):

    | head (channels) | gate | papyrus |
    |---|---|---|
    | ink (11), dens (8), fib H / V (14-15) | each channel where \|p - 0.5\| >= `--ssl-conf` 0.3 (ink: `--ssl-ink-conf`) | yes |
    | rv (12-13) | the same | no (papyrus vs void is what rv learns) |
    | normal n n^T (2-7) | all six where \|N\|_F >= `--ssl-norm-conf` 0.8, N from the head's coding (1 for a clean unit dyad) | yes |
    | phase cos / sin (0-1) | the pair where \|(2c - 1, 2s - 1)\| >= `--ssl-phase-conf` 0.7 | yes |

    The papyrus gate is the teacher's (max of the rv pair >= 0.5, so --rv 2), `--ssl-pap 0` drops it (tests).
  - Not self-trained: wind4 (its integer gauge is exactly what self-training cannot validate) and the fibre axis (rare, noisy
    where wrong). No symmetry-agreement pass for the normals in v1: it would cost a second teacher forward per SSL window.
  - Weights `name:W`, default `--ssl-heads-w` 0.25; per head W x the mean BCE over its targeted entries. Logged per head as
    ` ssl-<head> L (g% gated)`.
  - Default: none on. A head is self-trained only after it beats its reference teacher, else the term reinforces its errors.
  - Memory: a byte per enabled channel and cell (16.8 MB per channel at P 1024), now counted by the planner (the old ink buffer
    was not).
  - Tests (desk GPU 0, 11-12 15:20, both pass): test_ssl (5) every mode in one spec vs the host (targets, counts, gradient against the formula and central
    differences, per-head sums) at two normal thresholds; test_heads (8e) the `--ssl-ink` alias, (8f) five heads at confidence 0
    finite and covering 30-90 % of the cells, a missing head refused.
    test_ssl numbers: 512 cells, gated ink 165, rv 215 + 207, normal 236 (conf 0.8) / 185 (conf 1.2), phase 208, dens 152; 0 target
    bytes differ; gradient worst 5.0e-7 against the formula and 5.0e-7 against central differences, of a largest 1.8e-3.
  - Measurement: a paired short run with / without `--ssl-heads` from the same snapshot (wbench p05x, rv, the 34 ink crops, the
    fibre judge), gated on unissl's 2000 / 4000 wbench rows showing the trunk term neutral or better.
- Holdouts: inkB added the 10 extra crops to holdouts-ink.json ("inkeval-ho", 98 boxes), on the 0500P2 2.215 um and 0841 2.403 um
  scans. Those two volumes reject 5 / 6 boxes. `EXCLVOL` leaves out 0841's 9.366 um scan (the boxes are not mapped into it) and
  0500P2's 9.362 um scan (a labelled source already), so 35 unlabelled volumes remain.

- unissl, the trunk term on desk GPU 1 (11-12 12:50 - 19:42, from unified/last.ckpt step 1504; ink off, --ssl 16 --ssl-share 0.25,
  35 unlabelled scans): no collapse (std 0.234-0.243 against the 0.25 floor, cosine 0.19 -> 0.11, 40 % of the cells targeted), the
  unlabelled share settles at 25 % after a startup skew (48 %: cheap windows fill the replay slots first). Two run faults, both fixed:
  the inserted side head was never initialised on a resume (c46d58f) and nn_w4runs_label aborted on a full card (a5520d5).
  wbench core p05x against unified-1504, all 44 rows, paired bootstrap: 2000 +0.001 [-0.013, +0.013], 4000 -0.007 [-0.018, +0.002],
  6000 -0.017 [-0.036, -0.000] (latres, 39 clean boxes: -0.018, P(better) 0.04). A monotone slide, but unissl has no control: since
  1504 the SSL term, the dropped ink sources / loss and 4500 more steps all changed.
- Attribution, sslpair (11-12 19:45-): three arms from unissl snap/4000 back to back on GPU 1, --det 1 (identical windows), 1500
  steps cooled to 5500 (wsd): ctrl (--ssl 16, no unlabelled source: the term never runs), ssl (unissl as is), heads (ssl +
  --ssl-heads rv,dens,normal,phase). ctrl vs ssl attributes the slide; ssl vs heads is the heads term. --det costs ~15 % (212 vs 250
  Mvox/s). Caveat: 1500 steps against a 0.017 effect (MDE ~0.02): a null is not evidence of no effect.

- Closed 11-12 ~22:00 (user: "cancel the dino and the standalone ink training"; the pods went away). Where it stands:
  - sslpair: ctrl reached 5300 (snap 4000 / 4500 / 5000 kept; one OOM kill at 21:19), ssl and heads never ran. unissl's slide after
    2000 stays unattributed (SSL term vs dropped ink vs more steps).
  - pod3dino (pod 3, RTX PRO 6000, from unissl 6773, trunk + --ssl-heads rv,dens,normal,phase, 6 labelled + 27 unlabelled sources): ran
    ~480 steps before the pod went, no snapshot saved. 1040 Mvox/s (1.0 s/step, 4x the desk), loader wait 5 %, SM 100 % busy at B 1
    (dmon; memory bandwidth 33-53 %, 20.7 of 97 GB), so B > 1 under --ssl was not needed. ssl 0.069, std 0.246; heads gated rv 24.5 %,
    normal 19.2 %, dens 2.3 %, phase 2.7 % (the papyrus and magnitude gates leave dens / phase sparse at default thresholds).
  - Code kept, off by default: --ssl, --ssl-heads (tests pass), the CT draw index for ct_only scans, side-head insertion on resume.

**Code.**
- Sources take `"ssl": 1` (CT only, no targets; `holdout_reject` for the wbench boxes).
- New train flags: `--ssl D --ssl-level 1 --ssl-share S --ssl-mask r --ssl-weight w --ssl-var g`.
- One new kernel: the cell-block mask.
- The distillation head's half-res refusal is lifted for --ssl, and --distill with --ssl is refused.
- Header key "ssl" only when on, and the side head's parameters are appended last.
- With --ssl 0 every path is the old one (test_heads reference losses).
- Tests: test_ssl (mask kernel vs host; teacher target quantisation; cosine + varreg gradient vs double central differences;
  fixture run with an ssl source: finite, header, resume).

**Cost.**
- Memory, P 1024: about 0.3 GB more (fp32 head outputs and gradient, int8 targets, 2.1 M level-1 cells). The head outputs are fp32
  as in --distill: the variance hinge needs exact statistics, and the buffers are small.
- Compute, one SSL window: a teacher forward plus a student forward and backward with no full-resolution head slabs. Estimate
  ~0.5-0.7 of a labelled window on the GPU and ~1/3 on the loader (no phase / wind4 builds).
- At share 0.25 the expected wall cost is within +-10% (to be measured; u1 runs 0.42 windows/s on both GPUs).

**Experiment.**
- Two finetunes from u1 snap/16000, P 1024, one GPU each, the same seed / sources / LR, matched on labelled windows (2000):
  A control; B `--ssl 16 --ssl-share 0.25 --ssl-mask 0.4 --ssl-weight 0.5 --ssl-var 1`.
- Unlabelled pool: every scan in v2/ct except the wbench boxes and PHerc0175A, which is held out of SSL as the strictly unseen
  control. PHerc1299 is in the pool: transductive, as in a production unroll.
- About 2.7 h of both desk GPUs.
- Metrics:
  - wbench core p05x / ids as a non-regression gate. Noise floor (fibnote 11-11): ~0.01 p05x, ~0.02-0.03 ids. Expected effect
    there: 0 to +0.01, since those scrolls are the labelled ones.
  - The fibre judge (persistent sheet changes per m) on PHerc1299 and PHerc0175A tiles, where an effect, if any, should show.
  - Robustness: p05x on 20x-compressed input.
- Base checkpoint (lead): u1 stopped at ~13750 (u1/last.ckpt); there is no snap/16000. The A/B branches off the unified run's
  first snapshot (the production trunk) or u1/last.ckpt.

**3-D ink across the corpus (user 11-12: "dino on improving 3d ink corpus wide").** Human ink labels exist on ~8 scrolls.
- What the DINO-guided relabel rounds bought: we cannot say. They are villa's (ink_3d_dino_guided: ps256 bcedice dinoguided v1 ->
  v2 -> v3_fullsup, config.json in /vesuvius/ufsm/teachers/dino3d); we hold only the final 78k EMA checkpoint and none of their
  per-round validation. Our only number is the final teacher on our 24 held-out crops: 3-D AUC Paris 4 0.727, 0139 0.651,
  1667 0.561 against a CT floor of 0.513. A teacher at 0.56 on 1667 is too weak to distill there.
- Stage 1, the feature term above: the unified run's ink head reads the same trunk, so any invariance or context the term buys
  reaches ink. It is indirect and costs nothing extra.
- Stage 2, ink consistency on unlabelled windows (`--ssl-ink W --ssl-ink-conf c`), with the same two views and the same EMA
  teacher forward:
  - The latent ink output is interpolated from the cell-level coarse logits (only the phase pair has the sub-cell head), so the
    target can be the teacher's coarse ink probability per cell. It needs no full-resolution slabs. The fine stem's ink
    contribution is absent on both sides.
  - Soft BCE on the student's masked view, only on papyrus cells (CT >= iso) where the teacher is confident (|p - 0.5| >= c),
    i.e. FixMatch / mean teacher with a gate.
  - Start only once the unified ink head beats dino3d on the crops: self-training from a near-floor head reinforces noise.
- Not chosen:
  - Offline relabel rounds (predict ink on every scroll, gate, use as sources): GPU hours of whole-scroll inference per round,
    which the online EMA version avoids.
  - Distilling dino3d on unlabelled scrolls: it needs 2.4 um level 0 (the desk's 2.4 um CTs have none), is out of distribution
    at 7.9-9.4 um, and is weak where it matters.
- Metric: inkB's 34 crops (24 + 10 held out from 0500P2 / 0841; latres scores them per snapshot), 3-D AUC / best F1. 0500P2 /
  0841 are the corpus-wide signal; Paris 4 / 0139 / 1667 are non-regression. The 1667 unroll's rendered ink AUC
  (scripts/inkgt/wrapscore.py: 0.646, CT floor 0.540) is an end-to-end check, not an A/B metric (one unroll per arm). The noise
  floor on the crops is not measured yet (a seed repeat is needed).

## Spiral post-processing QA: wrap repair, fibre / GT judges, outlier slabs, flattening distortion (2026-11-12, branch spiralqa-20261112)

On the two u1-13000 unrolls of the day (`/vesuvius/ufsm/unroll/PHerc1667-u1`, `PHercParis4-u1`), CPU only; outputs in `<run>/qa/*`,
`<run>/wraps_repair`. New: `ufsm wrap-repair` (`src/wraprepair.c`, `test_wraprepair`), `ufsm strip-distort` (`src/stripdistort.c`,
`test_stripdistort`), `fiber-judge --set` with the set's own um (9.6 um P4 fits judged at level 2; before, it read them as level 0),
`scripts/spiralqa/fj_scroll.sh`. Referees: 1667 human codes (u1 in-sample except the held boxes); Paris 4 also has GT in our scan's
frame (`gt/paris4-q9p6/q-9p6.zarr 9.6`, `gt/paris4-wind-20261019 phaseA/9.6`, the wbench roots), used as a referee next to fibres.

**1. Wrap repair.** `wrap-repair` is wrap-check on the .sfc wraps themselves (the strip's input), along rays from the axis: per pair of
consecutive ids on a ray, CT peaks in the interval (window shifted inward by half the gap for snapped wraps), GT turns, crossings; per
wrap the wrap-check verdict rule; per 64-row x 10-degree cell the counts. Repair: crossed vertices (touching neighbours) removed, dup
cells' outer wrap removed, merged cells -> split fragments (off by default). What the CT peak count is worth against GT:

| | GT right | GT 0 / 2+ | "0 peaks" = GT 0 | "2+ peaks" = GT 2+ | dup cells >= 0.8 empty: precision / GT0 recall | merged cells >= 0.8: precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1667 wraps_snap (6.3 M intervals, 1.52 M with GT) | 0.9785 | 0.0034 / 0.0167 | 0.033 | 0.016 | 0.55 / 0.18 (in strip) | 0.008 |
| P4 wraps_snap (54.6 M, 9.4 M with GT) | 0.9760 | 0.0016 / 0.0223 | 0.007 | 0.019 | 0.15 / 0.12 | 0.036 |

wrap-check's "merged" verdicts on 1667 (w010-w025, 8 wraps) are false: GT turns 0.99-1.04 there, gt1 0.91-0.999; 1667's ~230 um gaps
show ~2 CT ridges per sheet (rct 1.4-1.7). Sweeping wrap-check --sigma 1.2-4 / --prom 1-1.5 removes the merged verdicts (prom 1.5) but
never lifts the per-interval precision above 0.07. So: split never (default --merge-share 2); dup cells only where GT says they are
right, i.e. 1667 at --dup-share 0.8 (precision 0.67 on the whole set), not P4 (0.15).
- 1667 `wraps_repair` (dup-share 0.8 + crossings): 3.1 % of vertices removed (mostly the outer dup run trim drops anyway). Whole set GT
  right 0.9785 -> 0.9801, GT0 0.0034 -> 0.0022; in the strip (pairs to w038 / w039) 0.9811 -> 0.9817, GT0 0.0019 -> 0.0015, GT coverage
  -0.13 %; verdicts 40 real / 2 dup / 4 merged -> 42 / 0 / 4. wrapswitch (GT codes) switches around the axis 2.16 -> 1.98 per cm, along
  z 2.55 -> 2.35, coded share 0.558 -> 0.568. Small and real.
- P4 `wraps_repair` (crossings only: dup cells would remove 8486 GT-right intervals per 1688 dups): 0.32 % of vertices removed;
  crossings 67115 -> 60443 by the check (it fills radius-table holes of <= 8 angle bins from the neighbours, so a removed touching pair
  partly reappears), GT right 0.9760 -> 0.9760, GT0 0.0016 -> 0.0015, verdicts 147 / 10 / 0 unchanged. The crossings lie in two
  opposite angle lobes (the packed, flattened sides), not at the seam. A no-op on P4: keep wraps_snap.

**2. Fibres.** Paris 4: `fibers/raw/spiral_fibers.afv` (open-data spiral fibres, native frame) over z 6656-17152 (level 2), 512^2 x 512
tiles. 1667: no fibre data exists (no AFV, no traced prediction), so its label-free check is the CT one above (wrap-repair cells) plus
surf-stats --ct-only (on papyrus 0.530 on wraps_snap -> 0.546 on wraps_repair; adjacent-normal
angles unchanged, > 30 deg 0.0057 -> 0.0056).

| P4 judge (H + V persistent sheet changes per m) | tiles >= 0.5 m | fibre m | rate | tile median / q75 / q90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| u1 wraps_snap | 1556 | 3267 | 216 | 185 / 256 / 344 |
| GT phase (the floor: fibre + label noise) | 1498 | 2665 | 107 | 92 / 148 / 203 |

Flags at >= 378 /m (2x the P4 wraps reference 189, the fibre gate's ramp): 125 tiles, 19 % of all our sheet changes, in two columns
persisting over z: (y 2048, x 5120) z 7168-9728 and (y 4096-4608, x 6656) z 8192-10752. Against GT per tile (1491 tiles with both):
flagged tiles rate 534 (ours) vs 192 (GT) /m, unflagged 182 vs 95; 52 % of the flags sit in tiles whose GT rate is normal (< 184); the
tile rates of ours and GT correlate (Spearman 0.60: part of the rate is the region's fibres, not our winding). Worst tile (z 8704, y 4608,
x 6656, 1210 /m on the wraps): the fibres follow GT there (pairs within half a turn at 0.6 mm 0.89 / 0.93, 252 / 165 /m), our joined fit
is GT-wrong (fit --codes on the 256 x 512^2-cell crop: ids right 0.093, |err| median 0.22 turn, |err| < 0.08 turn 0.018). Local refits
of the crop with the joined set as --ref-model: plain 0.094, --uw-repair 8 0.109, --uw-repair 8 + fibre votes (--uw-rep-fib 16, 250 k
votes) 0.102. The fields are wrong there (their phase is off GT by > 0.08 turn almost everywhere), so a refit cannot recover it;
it needs better fields (or labels) in those columns.

**3. Outlier slabs (P4).** The final losses are bimodal (2-3 vs 10-17; s105-s142 all 14-17.7; isolated s030, s054, s070, s080, s091).
The gap is all the smooth term after the voxel unwrapping (s070 stage 4 smooth 137 vs s069 21; phase / normal / density equal) and
half of it sits in ~1100 of 831 k lattice columns. Per-slab wrap-check of the joined model (--zr per slab core): s030 0.898 CT
peaks / turn vs neighbours 0.900, s070 0.912 vs 0.916 / 0.918; the > 8 group 1.01 vs 0.90 follows the z region, not the loss. s070
refits on the CPU (reproduces 11.417 vs the GPU's 11.4115, 196 s, 17 GB): 3x steps in stages 4 / 5 8.16; --seed-model s069 (its
integers) 12.71 with the phase term doubled; --init-model s069 + ref 1.28. Slab-core wrap-check 0.907 (orig) / 0.901 / 0.907 / 0.912;
fibre judge pairs at 0.6 mm (H) 0.7195 / 0.7215 / - / 0.7198; cf-compare orig vs init: 97.7 % of material cells keep their integer.
Re-joined with the init refit: wrap-check 150 real / 14 dup / 0 merged and 0.947 peaks / turn, identical. The loss is not a quality
signal here; refitting the other high-loss slabs is not worth a GPU window.

**4. Flattening distortion.** `strip-distort` reads strip-flatten's stripes (x / y / z / gu.tif on the flat uv grid): per pixel the
Jacobian by +-4 px central differences (one px would measure the strip's 0.25-voxel sfc error, 6 % per edge; spans 4 and 8 agree within
0.002), dist = max(s1, 1/s2) - 1 (the worst linear stretch), the area ratio, folds (normal against the 9 x 9-block neighbourhood). Per
stripe `<s>_dist.jpg` (green <= 5 %, yellow 10 %, red >= 20 %, magenta folded; 1 px = 8 grid px) and `<s>_area.jpg`, `tiles.tsv` (1 cm
tiles with their wrap), `wraps.tsv`, `stripes.tsv`.

| strip | valid cm2 | dist p50 / p95 / p99 | area p50 | trusted (dist <= 5 %) | folded | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1667 u1 (3 stripes) | 1186 | 0.042 / 0.157 / 0.57 | 1.014 | 0.61 | 0.0009 | 9 s |
| P4 u1 (22 stripes) | 20636 | 0.077 / 0.187 / 0.36 | 1.072 | 0.27 | 0.0005 | 172 s |

P4's area 1.072 matches its flatten.txt (mesh 22297 cm2 vs flat 20639: the flat strip is ~7 % smaller than the surface); its worst
wraps are the partial inner ones (w239-w242). In the 1667 images the bad areas repeat once per wrap (the theta-cut seam region).

## U2's low ink share: ink-only windows counted as empty under --rv; held-out draw cells; 0841 / 0500P2 (2026-11-12, branch inkdraw-20261112)

U2 (unwrap2 + `--rv 2` + `--ink-head 1`) drew 3.5 % of its windows from the 8 human-ink sources at ~25 % of the weight; Paris 4
dropped 10 of 14 picked windows as "empty targets". Three causes:

- **The empty test missed the ink plane.** Under `--rv` the ink plane holds the papyrus plane and the human ink target is an extra
  (aux) plane; the sampler's empty-window test read only the target channels, so every ink-only window had no target value and
  was kept with p `empty_keep` 0.2. That cost ~4 dropped draws per window. The test now reads the aux planes too (a known value
  above 0). On the fixture (test_ink_mil_check run 6, ink-only source, P 64, 24 windows) the drops went from 90 to 42. The other
  42 are real: the fixture's 128-voxel chunk snap moves P 64 windows off the sheet, and windows between the ink discs know only
  "no ink". In the 2-D labels of the real scans, 87-100 % of the 1024-px squares around a supervised pixel hold ink (Paris 4 0.94,
  1667 0.90, 0139 0.98, 0009B 0.87, 0814 1.00), so at P 1024 nearly every window now passes.
- **Draw cells inside held-out boxes.** inkfly_cells marked every cell of a supervised tile's box. A window centred on a cell
  inside an eval crop sees the target only as unknown there (`--exclude`). Cells wholly inside a held-out box are no longer
  draw cells: Paris 4 lost 1.14 M of 8.54 M level-5 cells (13 %), 1667 0.35 of 2.83 M, 0139 0.11 of 1.55 M, 0814 88 of 48860.
- **0841 and 0500P2 hold out every segment.** Their validation.zarr is 255 over the whole tifxyz footprint (99.6-99.7 % of the
  mesh, 100 % of the supervised pixels). Elsewhere validation is a small subset of the supervision: 0.2-2.4 % of the area, 10-32 %
  of the supervised pixels. So validation "exclude" leaves 0 supervised tiles there (15112 / 11687 with validation off) and no
  draw index. The open data apparently marks these segments as validation whole. They should stay out of the ink weight; they
  can serve as unseen-scroll ink evals. MAN5's hf labels hold no ink pixel in the supervised area (share 0.000).

**Before / after on the desk (2026-11-12, after the pod went away).** U2's recipe (`--task unwrap2 --rv 2 --ink-head 1 --ink-mil 1`,
P 1024, B 1, rungs 4.8 / 9.6, `--strict-sources 1`), sampler only, 1 worker / 1 slot, 40 batches, the 6 desk ink sources
(/vesuvius/ufsm/univ/u2ink/sources-u2desk-ink.json: local CT levels 1-5, onfly level 1 + 2 pooled):

| | master cb8102d | inkcache-20261112 (inkdraw + shared cache) |
|---|---|---|
| draws dropped as empty targets | 192 for 40 windows (83 %) | 3 for 40 (7 %) |
| wall for 40 windows | 4738 s | 1443 s |
| host RSS (UFSM_HOSTMEM) | 27.27 GB | 19.78 GB (ink caches 3.22 GB targets + 1.07 GB CT, at the 4096 MB budget) |

After the fix, per ink window: known ink target on 0.28-0.51 % of the voxels, ink on 0.07-0.14 %, and 65536 MIL rays (the
`--ink-mil-max` cap) per window. Paris 4 26 windows, 1667 13, 0139 1.

**One cache budget for every ink source** (branch inkcache-20261112). Each onfly ink source used to open a 2 GB target LRU and a
1 GB decoded-CT zcache (24 GB for 8 sources). They now share a dcache pool ("ink", z3_open_cached_pool) and one zcache, with one
budget, `train --ink-cache-mb` (default 4096 or $UFSM_INK_CACHE_MB): 3/4 targets, 1/4 CT. inkfly_free drops its CT's chunks from
the shared zcache (zcache_drop: a later array at the same address must never see them). test_zcache covers the pool (two arrays,
8 threads, evicting, one closed, empty after) and zcache_drop.

Footprint of one ink sampler at P 1024 (sampler only, 1 worker, 1 slot, 8 sources): 17.6 GB RSS. The pod arm A unit at 3 workers /
3 slots peaked at 52 GB and OOM-killed itself and U2's run in the shared 175 GB cgroup (09:58 UTC).


## U2's host memory: the inventory, and the two per-thread buffers that only grew (2026-11-12, branch poolcap-20261112)

U2 on the pod (8 workers / 10 slots, a 175 GB cgroup shared with every other job) went from 68 to 116 GB of host memory in 19 minutes and
tripped its watchdog. The host-side buffers of its recipe at P 1024 (one byte plane = 1.07 GB), from the code; "measured" where a run says so:

| what | bound | set by | scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| sampler slots (pinned: shmem) | 3.4 GB each: CT 1 + phase 1 + papyrus / ink plane 1 + ink bits 1/8, run lists | `--sampler-slots` | per slot (10 slots: 34 GB; U2 measured 36 GB shmem) |
| worker fixed scratch | 1.6 GB resident (measured, desk) of 15 GB reserved | `--workers` | per worker |
| worker buffer pool (`tp_get` / `tp_put`) | was 32 buffers of any sizes, never trimmed; now also `UFSM_TP_POOL_MB` (2048) bytes | this branch | per worker |
| on-the-fly phase pack buffer (`t_pk`) | was the largest tile's encoded bytes, kept (4 GB hard cap); now freed after a tile past `UFSM_ONFLY_PACK_MB` (64) | this branch | per reading thread |
| on-the-fly phase interior buffer (pinned) | one tile interior, ~0.3 GB | `--onfly-mb` | per reading thread |
| on-the-fly phase CPU buffer sets (pinned) | 3 x 0.57 GB each, only on a CPU fallback | `--onfly-slots` | global |
| pooled ink level read | 8.6 GB transient; 0.54 GB with sampmem-20261112 | | per worker building an ink window at its pooled level |
| ink target cache | 2 GB ("cache_mb") | sources json | per ink source (8: 16 GB) |
| ink decoded-CT cache | 1 GB, hard-coded | inksplat.c | per ink source (8: 8 GB) |
| ink segment index, mesh codes packs | the data's size | | per source, fixed after open |
| cached on-the-fly phase arrays (meshes) | 1 GB each ("cache_mb") | sources json | per mesh source and level |
| binary-mask chunk cache | 1 GB | `UFSM_Z3_MASK_CACHE_MB` | global |
| shard index table | none; a few KB per shard touched | `UFSM_Z3_INDEX_MEM=0` | global |
| shared decoded-CT cache (/dev/shm) | G GB | `UFSM_ZCACHE_GB` (off unless set) | global |
| trainer (batch staging, the lean plan's host offloads, the CUDA runtime) | ~13 GB | `--mem` plan | fixed |
| disk chunk cache, derived-array disk cache | page cache (reclaimable) | "cache" | not anon / shmem |

Replays hold their slot and have no buffer of their own. The bounded rows give about 85 / 100 / 125 GB at 6 / 8, 8 / 10 and 12 / 14
workers / slots once the per-source ink caches are full (estimates, not measured); the rows that are per source rather than global are
the ink caches and the cached phase arrays.

- The pool's byte cap: past it the oldest pooled buffers are freed on put (a buffer larger than the cap is never pooled). Fixture check
  (CPU, `--det 1`, P 128, `--gpu-aug 0` with rotations / elastic warps so the pool is used: 8 classes, 10 P^3 a worker): the 48 batch
  hashes (`UFSM_BATCH_HASH`) are identical with the cap at 0 (none), 1 MB, 6 MB, the default, and on a build without the change; the
  pool's bytes 0.06 -> 0.02 GB at 6 MB. Peak RSS is unchanged at that size (0.36 GB): the cap bounds what is retained, not what is lent.
- The pack buffer's trim is not exercised by any desk run (it needs the GPU tile path); it frees and zeroes the thread's buffer after
  the tile's device call returns.
- Which row climbed in U2 is not known yet (its `hostmem:` lines will say); u1's recipe on the desk never touched the pool (peak 0).

## predict --boxes: many boxes in one process; the start-up of a predict run (2026-11-12, branch univdec-20261112)

A predict run's start-up, timestamped on the pod box (5 heads + fit-zarr, 16.6 s elapsed, the window loop 10.5 s):

| from (s) | to (s) | what |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.07 | the checkpoint |
| 0.07 | 0.5 | CUDA init, the store over HTTP, the window plan |
| 0.5 | 1.5 | head stores + unet_build (device buffers) |
| 1.6 | 3.65 | 9.7 GB of cudaMallocHost (shard rings 2.1, head rings 7.6) |
| 14.2 | 15.6 | writer tails |
| 15.6 | 16.6 | exit: cudaFreeHost + teardown |

wbench (and the compression sweep, the snapshot matrices) ran a process per box.
- `predict --boxes FILE` runs the single-box path once per line (`z,y,x,nz,ny,nx OUT [ARGS]`, where ARGS go ahead of the command's
  options), so the outputs are those of a process per box.
- What carries over is the CUDA context, the CT cache, and nn_pool. nn_pool keeps every nn_malloc* / nn_host_alloc* block of a box and
  hands it to the next box's request of the same size; device blocks are zeroed, as fresh memory is. It frees the blocks a box did not take.
- The run state that lived in function statics (lazily sized buffers sized by the first window, the attention memory, the fit writer /
  prefetch / feather / pyramid structs, unet's g_vtok) is reset per box.
- The shard rings are also capped at the box's shard count: a small eval box held 2 k^3 pinned buffers per head.
- One process per checkpoint + CT root; wbench PBATCH=1 makes one per scroll.

Numbers:
- test_predict_boxes: 4 boxes (three sizes, a repeat, q 8 with the GPU encoder), 5 heads + fit-zarr each; every file is identical to a
  process per box.
- Fixture: 8 boxes 0.36 s then 0.10 s a box, max RSS 640 -> 649 MB.
- Pod, 4 wbench-sized Paris4 boxes (512 x 768^2 at 9.6 um, fit fields as wbench predicts them):
  - 4 processes: 17.2 s;
  - --boxes: 5.3 s (2.04, 1.03, 0.86, 0.85 s a box);
  - 267 files per box identical.

## The pooled on-the-fly ink level read in z-slabs (2026-11-12, branch sampmem-20261112)

`inkfly_pool_derive` (the coarser level of an on-the-fly ink target: known-max 2x pooling of the level below) read the whole (2n)^3 fine
box into one malloc before pooling: 8.6 GB of scratch in every worker building a P 1024 window of an ink source at its pooled level,
on top of the slot. It now reads slabs of the fine level cut at multiples of the fine array's 128 cell (no cell derived twice) and
pools each; the pooling is per 2^3 block, so the bytes are the same.

- Desk, one P 1024 pooled read from a stored u8 pyramid (`test_ink_pool --bench`, PHerc0139 CT levels 0 / 1 standing in for the ink
  array): peak RSS 9.18 GB with one whole read (`UFSM_INKPOOL_SLAB=1048576`), 1.68 GB with the 128-plane slabs (1.07 GB of it the
  output window), the same output hash.
- `test_ink_pool` (CPU): 5 boxes of a 300 x 200 x 260 random array with unknowns (odd starts, slab cuts every 32 coarse planes, the
  whole array) equal the pooling of one fine read, 0 differ.
- The sampler's host memory otherwise (desk, u1's recipe, P 1024, `UFSM_HOSTMEM=1`): a slot 2.28 GB (CT 1 B a voxel, phase 1, ink bits
  1/8, runs), a worker's fixed scratch 1.6 GB resident of 15 GB reserved. An earlier "7 GB per slot, 4 GB per worker" for U2's list was a
  two-point fit that included the process-wide caches (per on-the-fly ink source a 2 GB target LRU and a 1 GB decoded-CT cache) and this
  scratch; it should not be used.

## --init-from by head, the "other" drop count, U2's start (2026-11-12, branch initmap-20261112)

- **--init-from by head.** u1-10000 -> U2: both nets have 144 outputs (the latent head: 16 base + 128 sub-cell), so no mapping branch
  applied and unet_init_from copied the head by position. U2's ink row 11 got u1's recto row, then the ink reset (fresh, prior bias). U2's
  rv rows 12-13 got u1's verso row and an untrained pad row; the rv reset did not fire, because the donor declares rv v2. U2's step-50 rv
  bce was 0.569, against u1's 0.36 at step 10450; phase / normal / wind4 were at u1's level. Now an unwrap2 donor with more than 11
  outputs and --rv 2 / --ink-head maps by head:
  - the rv pair from the donor header ("rv":{"version":2,"recto":R});
  - ink from "unwrap":{.."ink":C}, else fresh;
  - rows 0-10 and the sub-cell rows by position.
  rows[] was 64 entries, now 512. test_init_heads (fixture, lr 0, step 1): rv bce 0.2225 for the donor layout and 0.2225 mapped by head;
  the old loader gives 0.369 (untrained). u1's own init from wz896 was right: rv rows 11-12 fresh, since the donor had no rv.
- **SL_OTHER.** The draws line's fifth drop count (hold/empty/probe/fg/other) covers draw_'s returns before a window position: no level,
  patch / box bounds, a shape smaller than the window. Before this they were uncounted, so a source losing its share there looked
  clean. --reject-warn counts them.
- **No draw index is fatal under --strict-sources.** U2's ink-PHerc0500P2 / ink-PHerc0841 (0841: 0 supervised tiles) are at weight 0
  until their index is fixed.
- **U2's start on the pod:**
  - GPU OOM at start three times (10:00, 10:05, 10:10 UTC): the planner sized itself to the card's free memory and other jobs then took
    that space. The planner is now pinned (UFSM_MEM_FREE_GB 48, --onfly-mb 4096 x 4 slots: ~64 GB of the 96).
  - Host OOM kill at 09:58: U2, frozen for an exclusive slot, kept its 106 GB, and the slot's job went over the 175 GB cgroup.
  - Per-agent budgets and the two-phase claim (gpu.pause drains the shared jobs while U2 trains, gpu.go freezes U2) are in
    /workspace/ue/GPU.md.

## How far the CT can be compressed: the inference half (2026-11-12, branch latstore-20261112)

The user's question: how compressed can the data be before the nets are hopeless, and how much can we get away with. This is the
inference half (fixed checkpoints, re-encoded CT); the training half (finetunes on re-encoded CT) follows in its own section.

**Setup** (pod, scripts/latvol/sweep.sh, sweep_fib.sh, sweep_ink.sh, sweep_table.py, sweep_plot.py). Top anchor: the upstream
uncompressed uint8 zarr v2 CT of the box regions from the public bucket, kept as lossless volcomp (0.620 B/vox; raw = 1). Every arm is
encoded from it with `ufsm latvol --volcomp Q` (volcomp at quality Q) or as latent cells (`lvC_S`: C coefficients of klt1, step S x sd).
Winding: 14 wbench boxes (PH1-3, HOLD, J1 J9 J19 J27; C9 C18 C30 C52; 139-5 139-2: level 2 of the 2.4 um scans, level 0 of 0139's
9.36 um scan), three checkpoints (u1-8000, lat-wz896, wind96), production predict -> fit -> scores, paired per box against the anchor,
95% bootstrap interval over boxes. Rate = stored bytes per voxel of the re-encoded regions, air included. The paired noise floor with 14
boxes is +-0.01 to 0.02 p05x.
Validity: the arms are local trees, which have no disk chunk cache. (The cache path had no root in it: a second HTTP root sharing a
--cache directory with the same array keys was served the first root's index and chunks. Fixed on this branch: a cache directory
belongs to one root, written to `<cache>/.root` on first use; any other root reads and writes `<cache>/@<hash of its URL>`; a directory
that already holds chunks without a `.root` is taken to be the mirror's, which filled all of them. test_latvol.sh reads two roots with
the same key and different bytes through one cache directory; the binary from before the fix fails it.) Also and the shared decoded-chunk memory is keyed by a hash of the encoded bytes. Each
arm's CT differs from the anchor's (docs/sweep/compression-psnr.tsv), the fit fields of every (checkpoint, box) were checksummed per arm
(386 checksums, no two arms equal), reruns reproduce rows to 4 digits. A side check: the q2 arm reproduces the mirror's fibre baseline
exactly, so the mirror's level 2 is byte-equivalent to original -> volcomp q2.

- **No measurable loss down to volcomp q8, 0.035 B/vox**: 3.6x below the mirror's q2 for the 2.4 um scans, 29x below raw. q16
  (0.017) is the edge (two nets unchanged, u1 -0.016 with the interval touching 0). **Knee at q32** (0.008 B/vox: -0.01 to -0.03 p05x,
  ids -0.02 to -0.05). **Collapse from q64** (0.004: -0.06 to -0.11; q128: -0.08 to -0.34, ids to -0.46). The voxel net (wind96) falls
  hardest at the bottom; the latent-grid nets degrade more gracefully.
- **Latent cells**: C 29 at step 1.0 (0.072 B/vox, 4x u1's training step) is the coarsest setting clean on all three nets. Step 2.0, or
  13 / 8 coefficients at step 1.0, cost u1 0.01-0.02 (u1 consumes exactly these coefficients; the other nets read the rebuilt CT and do
  not notice). The mean alone is useless.
- **Per byte volcomp wins below ~0.07 B/vox**: q8 at 0.035 is clean where the latent arms at 0.037-0.038 lose 0.02 on u1; q16 at 0.017
  is clean on two nets where C 4 loses 0.02-0.05. latvol's case is the device decode (previous section), not size; but its inference
  step can be 0.5-1.0, which makes a store 0.6-0.9x of the q2 mirror instead of 1.3x.
